passages.intro_en: Read the story: to Tarim with his father. Then answer.

lines.ar: ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: Ahmad went with his father to Tarim.

lines.ar: دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْمَسْجِدَ الْكَبِيرَ وَجَلَسَ مَعَ عُمَرَ.
lines.en: Ahmad entered the big mosque and sat with ʿUmar.

lines.ar: وَسَأَلَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَخِيهِ، وَهُوَ رَجُلٌ ذُو عِلْمٍ.
lines.en: And Ahmad’s father asked about his brother, who is a man of knowledge.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: أَخُوكَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Your brother is in the ribāṭ.

lines.ar: فَذَهَبَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ وَرَأَى أَخَاهُ.
lines.en: So Ahmad’s father went to the ribāṭ and saw his brother.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَخُو أَبِيهِ لِأَحْمَدَ: هَلْ أَنْتَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ؟
lines.en: His father’s brother said to Ahmad: Are you a student of knowledge?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، أَنَا طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: Yes, I am a student of knowledge.

passages.ar: ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى تَرِيمَ. دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْمَسْجِدَ الْكَبِيرَ وَجَلَسَ مَعَ عُمَرَ. وَسَأَلَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَخِيهِ، وَهُوَ رَجُلٌ ذُو عِلْمٍ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: أَخُوكَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ. فَذَهَبَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ وَرَأَى أَخَاهُ. قَالَ أَخُو أَبِيهِ لِأَحْمَدَ: هَلْ أَنْتَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، أَنَا طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
passages.en: Ahmad went with his father to Tarim. Ahmad entered the big mosque and sat with ʿUmar. And Ahmad’s father asked about his brother, who is a man of knowledge. The Habib said: Your brother is in the ribāṭ. So Ahmad’s father went to the ribāṭ and saw his brother. His father’s brother said to Ahmad: Are you a student of knowledge? Ahmad said: Yes, I am a student of knowledge.

lines.ar: مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ

passages.ar: إِنَّمَا يَعْمُرُ مَسَٰجِدَ اللَّهِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ

lines.en: The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).

lines.ar: حَمِدَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ اللَّهَ.
lines.en: The boy’s father praised Allah.

passages.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ. حَمِدَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ اللَّهَ.
passages.en: The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm). The boy’s father praised Allah.

questions.q: Who went to Tarim, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ ذَهَبَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: Ahmad, with his father.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the big mosque, with ʿUmar.

questions.q: Who asked about his brother?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَأَلَ عَنْ أَخِيهِ؟
questions.a: Ahmad’s father (أَبُو أَحْمَدَ).

questions.q: What kind of man is the brother?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ هُوَ الْأَخُ؟
questions.a: A man of knowledge (ذُو عِلْمٍ).

questions.q: Where is the brother, according to the Habib?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ الْأَخُ؟
questions.a: In the ribāṭ.

questions.q: Who spoke to Ahmad in the ribāṭ?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ قَالَ لِأَحْمَدَ: هَلْ أَنْتَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ؟
questions.a: His father’s brother (أَخُو أَبِيهِ).

questions.q: True or false? Ahmad is a student of knowledge.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ أَحْمَدُ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
questions.a: True: نَعَمْ، أَنَا طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.

questions.q: Line 1: why does تَرِيمَ end in ـَ after إِلَى?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي «تَرِيمَ» بِفَتْحَةٍ بَعْدَ «إِلَى»؟
questions.a: Tarīm refuses tanwin and kasra, so it takes ـَ.

questions.q: Line 5: which word is a five noun in the “acted on” form?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ الْخَامِسِ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْخَمْسَةِ بِالْأَلِفِ؟
questions.a: أَخَاهُ (ـَ ا)

questions.q: Line 3: find the word that means “owner of”. Which ending shows it is not the doer?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «صَاحِبَ»؟
questions.a: ذُو (ـُ): it describes رَجُلٌ, which is ـٌ.

questions.q: Line 6: أَخُو أَبِيهِ. Say the ending of each word and why.
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَخْتَلِفُ نِهَايَةُ أَخُو وَأَبِيهِ فِي «أَخُو أَبِيهِ»؟
questions.a: أَخُو: ـُ (the doer); أَبِيهِ: ـِ (the second word of an “of” phrase).

questions.q: Which two names in the story refuse tanwin after a little word? Give the phrase.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ اسْمَيْنِ لَا يَقْبَلَانِ التَّنْوِينَ بَعْدَ حَرْفِ جَرٍّ؟
questions.a: تَرِيمَ (إِلَى تَرِيمَ) and أَحْمَدَ (لِأَحْمَدَ); also عُمَرَ (مَعَ عُمَرَ).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an: sūrat al-Tawba, verse 18 (a part of it).

questions.q: Translate the verse.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ.
questions.a: Only he keeps up the mosques of Allah, who believes in Allah and the Last Day.

questions.q: Who keeps up the mosques of Allah?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَعْمُرُ مَسَاجِدَ اللَّهِ؟
questions.a: Only the one who believes in Allah and the Last Day.

questions.q: Why does مَسَاجِدَ end in ـَ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي «مَسَاجِدَ» بِفَتْحَةٍ؟
questions.a: It is a long plural that refuses tanwin and kasra; it is the thing the verb reaches.

questions.q: In which two places does اللَّهِ have the ending ـِ, and why?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ مَوْضِعَيْنِ نِهَايَةُ «اللَّهِ» كَسْرَةٌ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: After مَسَاجِدَ (“of Allah”) and after بِ.

questions.q: ءَامَنَ is the Qur’an’s spelling of آمَنَ. What is its meaning, and what other words in this course share its root?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى «ءَامَنَ»؟ وَمَا الْكَلِمَاتُ الَّتِي لَهَا الْجَذْرُ نَفْسُهُ؟
questions.a: He believed; the root أ م ن is also in مُؤْمِن and إِيمَان.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge. The boy’s father praised Allah.

questions.q: In the first new line, which form of “father” follows لِ, and what is its ending?
questions.a: أَبِي (the ending ـِ after a preposition)

questions.q: In the second new line, which form of “father” is the one doing it, and what is its ending?
questions.a: أَبُو (the ending ـُ for the one doing it)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy’s father praised Allah.
questions.a: حَمِدَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ اللَّهَ.

translate.en: Ahmad’s father visited the ribāṭ.
Ahmad heard his brother in the mosque.

translate.ar: جَلَسَ عُمَرُ مَعَ أَخِيهِ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ.
translate.en: ʿUmar sat with his brother in the library.
Your brother has knowledge and good manners.
Did you ask your father about the lesson?
The Muslims believed in Allah.
The student praised Allah in the morning.

translate.ar: أَعْطَى أَبُو سَالِمٍ الزَّكَاةَ فِي هَذَا الشَّهْرِ.
translate.en: Salim’s father gave the zakāh this month.

translate.ar: فِي هَذِهِ السَّنَةِ ذَهَبَ أَبُو فَاطِمَةَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
translate.en: This year Fatima’s father went to Tarim.
Maryam’s father was a generous man.

translate.ar: لَمْ يَذْهَبْ أَخُو عَلِيٍّ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ أَمْسِ.
translate.en: Ali’s brother did not go to school yesterday.
Who is the father of this boy?
ʿUmar’s father’s book is new.
Sit with your brother in the circle.
The Habib said: You are a student of knowledge.

translate.ar: هَذَا مَسْجِدٌ كَبِيرٌ، وَتِلْكَ مَسَاجِدُ كَثِيرَةٌ.
translate.en: This is a big mosque, and those are many mosques.

translate.ar: ذَهَبَتْ فَاطِمَةُ مَعَ أُخْتِهَا إِلَى السُّوقِ.
translate.en: Fatima went with her sister to the market.
What did your father say to your brother?
The boy’s brother drank cold water.

translate.ar: فِي هَذَا الشَّهْرِ يَقْرَأُ أَبُوهُ الْمُصْحَفَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
translate.en: This month his father reads the muṣḥaf every day.

translate.ar: سَكَنَ أَخُو أَحْمَدَ فِي بَيْتِ أَبِيهِ.
translate.en: Ahmad’s brother lived in his father’s house.
Where is your father now?

translate.ar: ذَهَبَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ إِلَى بَيْتِ أَخِيهِ وَجَلَسَ هُنَاكَ.
translate.en: That man went to his brother’s house and sat there.

translate.ar: هَذِهِ سَنَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ وَهَذَا شَهْرٌ جَدِيدٌ.
translate.en: This is a new year and this is a new month.

translate.ar: ذَهَبَ أَبُو سَالِمٍ إِلَى السُّوقِ مَعَ أَخِيهِ. اِشْتَرَى خُبْزًا وَلَبَنًا لِلضُّيُوفِ. ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى بَيْتِ أَبِيهِ وَجَلَسَ مَعَ أُمِّهِ.
translate.en: Salim’s father went to the market with his brother. He bought bread and milk for the guests. Then he returned to his father’s house and sat with his mother.
Ahmad went with his father to the market.
translate.ar: ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى السُّوقِ.

translate.en: Salim’s father sat in the mosque.
I heard your brother.
Fatima went to Tarim with her brother.
translate.ar: ذَهَبَتْ فَاطِمَةُ إِلَى تَرِيمَ مَعَ أَخِيهَا.
alt: ذَهَبَتْ فَاطِمَةُ مَعَ أَخِيهَا إِلَى تَرِيمَ.

translate.en: Your father is a man of knowledge.
The student asked ʿUmar about the lesson.
The Muslim believed in Allah and the Last Day.
His brother did not go to the school.
This is the book of Ahmad’s father.
Salim’s brother gave Maryam a gift.
Maryam’s father was a generous man.
She sat with her father and her brother.

readings.title_en: Many: but which one?
readings.question_en: This word means “many”: which word is the one?
readings.question_ar: هَذِهِ كَلِمَةٌ لِلْكَثْرَةِ: فَمَا الْكَلِمَةُ الْوَاحِدَةُ؟

passages.intro_en: Read the story: the circle of the scholars. Then answer.
passages.cite: Course text, written for this lesson (no outside source).

lines.ar: مَسَاجِدُ تَرِيمَ كَثِيرَةٌ، وَمَجَالِسُ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِيهَا كَثِيرَةٌ.
lines.en: The mosques of Tarim are many, and the scholars’ gatherings in them are many.

lines.ar: ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ إِلَى مَجْلِسٍ كَبِيرٍ.
lines.en: Ahmad went with his father in the evening to a big gathering.

lines.ar: جَلَسَ الْعُلَمَاءُ وَالطُّلَّابُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
lines.en: The scholars and the students sat in the circle.

lines.ar: سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ دَرْسًا جَيِّدًا وَحَفِظَ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً.
lines.en: Ahmad heard a good lesson and memorised many words.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْعَالِمُ: الدُّرُوسُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَالْأَوْقَاتُ قَلِيلَةٌ.
lines.en: The scholar said: The lessons are many and the times are few.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: أَنَا أَطْلُبُ الْعِلْمَ، وَلَكِنْ لَا أَفْهَمُ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَاتِ.
lines.en: So Ahmad said: I seek knowledge, but I do not understand every word.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْعَالِمُ: اِسْأَلْ عَنْ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ، فَإِنَّ الْعِلْمَ نُورٌ.
lines.en: The scholar said: Ask about every word, for knowledge is light.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَكَتَبَ الْكَلِمَاتِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
lines.en: And Ahmad went back to the house and wrote the words in his book.

passages.ar: مَسَاجِدُ تَرِيمَ كَثِيرَةٌ، وَمَجَالِسُ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِيهَا كَثِيرَةٌ. ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ إِلَى مَجْلِسٍ كَبِيرٍ. جَلَسَ الْعُلَمَاءُ وَالطُّلَّابُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ. سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ دَرْسًا جَيِّدًا وَحَفِظَ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً. قَالَ الْعَالِمُ: الدُّرُوسُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَالْأَوْقَاتُ قَلِيلَةٌ. فَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: أَنَا أَطْلُبُ الْعِلْمَ، وَلَكِنْ لَا أَفْهَمُ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَاتِ. قَالَ الْعَالِمُ: اِسْأَلْ عَنْ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ، فَإِنَّ الْعِلْمَ نُورٌ. وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَكَتَبَ الْكَلِمَاتِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
passages.en: The mosques of Tarim are many, and the scholars’ gatherings in them are many. Ahmad went with his father in the evening to a big gathering. The scholars and the students sat in the circle. Ahmad heard a good lesson and memorised many words. The scholar said: The lessons are many and the times are few. So Ahmad said: I seek knowledge, but I do not understand every word. The scholar said: Ask about every word, for knowledge is light. And Ahmad went back to the house and wrote the words in his book.

lines.ar: يَٰأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم
lines.en: O people, We created you

lines.ar: مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ
lines.en: from a male and a female,

lines.ar: وَجَعَلْنَٰكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُواْ

passages.ar: يَٰأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَٰكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُواْ

questions.q: Where are the mosques many?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ الْمَسَاجِدُ كَثِيرَةٌ؟
questions.a: In Tarim.

questions.q: When did Ahmad go to the big gathering, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ الْكَبِيرِ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the evening, with his father.

questions.q: Who sat in the circle?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ؟
questions.a: The scholars and the students.

questions.q: What did Ahmad hear and memorise?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ وَحَفِظَ؟
questions.a: A good lesson, and many words.

questions.q: What did the scholar say about the lessons and the times?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْعَالِمُ عَنِ الدُّرُوسِ وَالْأَوْقَاتِ؟
questions.a: The lessons are many and the times are few.

questions.q: True or false? Ahmad understood every word.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ فَهِمَ أَحْمَدُ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَاتِ.
questions.a: False: he said لَا أَفْهَمُ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَاتِ.

questions.q: What did the scholar tell Ahmad to do?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْعَالِمُ لِأَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: To ask about every word.

questions.q: What did Ahmad do at the end?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ فِي النِّهَايَةِ؟
questions.a: He went back to the house and wrote the words in his book.

questions.q: Line 1: مَجَالِسُ is the plural of which single word? Which shape?
questions.q_ar: مَا مُفْرَدُ «مَجَالِسُ»؟ وَمَا وَزْنُهَا؟
questions.a: مَجْلِس; the shape mafāʿil.

questions.q: Line 5: find two plurals and give the single word of each.
questions.q_ar: جِدْ جَمْعَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْخَامِسِ وَاذْكُرْ مُفْرَدَ كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا.
questions.a: الدُّرُوسُ ← دَرْس; الْأَوْقَاتُ ← وَقْت.

questions.q: Line 1: كَثِيرَةٌ is feminine singular, though it describes plurals. Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «كَثِيرَةٌ» مُؤَنَّثَةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ؟
questions.a: The plural of things is treated as one feminine word.

questions.q: Line 3: الْعُلَمَاءُ and الطُّلَّابُ are both plurals of people. Give the single word of each.
questions.q_ar: مَا مُفْرَدُ «الْعُلَمَاءُ» وَمُفْرَدُ «الطُّلَّابُ»؟
questions.a: عَالِم (shape fuʿalāʾ) and طَالِب (another shape: طُلَّاب).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an: sūrat al-Ḥujurāt, verse 13 (a part of it).

questions.q: Translate the verse.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ.
questions.a: O people, We created you from a male and a female, and made you peoples and tribes, so that you may know one another.

questions.q: Which two words are broken plurals? Give the single word of each.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ جَمْعُ تَكْسِيرٍ؟ مَا مُفْرَدُ كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا؟
questions.a: شُعُوبًا ← شَعْب (a people); قَبَائِلَ ← قَبِيلَة (a tribe).

questions.q: Which two words in line 2 are single words, not plurals?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي مُفْرَدَتَانِ؟
questions.a: ذَكَرٍ (a male) and أُنْثَى (a female).

questions.q: Which small word at the start of line 2 means “from”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي أَوَّلِ السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي تَعْنِي «مِنْ»؟
questions.a: مِّن (the Qur’an’s spelling of مِنْ).

questions.q: شُعُوبًا has tanwin, but قَبَائِلَ has none. Why? (Lesson 40)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «شُعُوبًا» مُنَوَّنَةٌ وَ«قَبَائِلَ» غَيْرُ مُنَوَّنَةٍ؟
questions.a: قَبَائِل is a long plural that refuses tanwin and kasra; شُعُوب is an ordinary plural.

questions.q: Translate the new line into English.
questions.a: The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.

questions.q: Which two words in the new line are broken plurals?
questions.a: مَجَالِسِ and الْعُلَمَاءِ

questions.q: Guess the singular of each of them from its shape.
questions.a: مَجْلِس (a gathering) and عَالِم (a scholar)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars.
questions.a: جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ.

translate.ar: جَلَسَ الْعُلَمَاءُ فِي الْمَجَالِسِ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ.
translate.en: The scholars sat in the gatherings with the students.
The students heard the lessons in the ribāṭ.

translate.ar: حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً مِنَ الدُّرُوسِ.
translate.en: The boy memorised many words from the lessons.
The students’ work is plentiful.
The times in Tarim were beautiful.
The tribes went to the mosque.
These peoples are many.
Who wrote these letters?
The students in these schools are many.
These are new conditions.
The pillars of this mosque are big.
The scholars are happy in the gathering.
The light is in the hearts.
Write the conditions in the book.
Did the students understand the lessons?
The scholars did not attend the gathering yesterday.
The gatherings were big and beautiful.
The scholar mentioned pillars and conditions.

translate.ar: سَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ الْعُلَمَاءَ عَنِ الْأَعْمَالِ الطَّيِّبَةِ.
translate.en: The boy asked the scholars about good deeds.
Sit in the gatherings and listen to the lessons.
This man is from a large tribe.
What is in these gatherings?
These schools are new and those are old.
The times are few and the lessons are many.

translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ رَسَائِلَ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ. وَقَرَأَ الْأَصْحَابُ الرَّسَائِلَ فِي الْمَدَارِسِ. ثُمَّ سَأَلُوا الْمُعَلِّمِينَ عَنْ كَلِمَاتٍ جَدِيدَةٍ.
translate.en: Ahmad wrote letters to his companions. The companions read the letters in the schools. Then they asked the teachers about new words.
The scholars sat in the gatherings.
The students heard the lessons.
The books are many.
Ahmad wrote letters to his friend.
The times in Tarim are beautiful.
The scholars are happy.
Did the boy understand the conditions?
These mosques are old.
The tribes went to Tarim.
The student studied the lessons in the library.
The guests sat in the gatherings of the ribāṭ.
Write the conditions in your book.

readings.title_en: Who did it? Nobody says: the passive
readings.question_en: The door was opened. By whom? The sentence does not say. How does Arabic say it?
readings.question_ar: فُتِحَ الْبَابُ. مَنْ فَتَحَهُ؟ لَا تَقُولُ الْجُمْلَةُ. كَيْفَ تَقُولُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ ذَلِكَ؟

passages.intro_en: Read the story, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (written for Lesson 42)

lines.ar: سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ: أَيْنَ وُلِدَ إِمَامُ الْمَسْجِدِ؟
lines.en: Ahmad asked ʿUmar: Where was the imam of the mosque born?

lines.ar: قَالَ عُمَرُ: يُقَالُ إِنَّهُ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ، وَطَلَبَ الْعِلْمَ هُنَاكَ.
lines.en: ʿUmar said: It is said that he was born in Tarim, and that he sought knowledge there.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: وَأَيْنَ يُطْلَبُ الْعِلْمُ الْيَوْمَ؟
lines.en: Ahmad said: And where is knowledge sought today?

lines.ar: قَالَ عُمَرُ: يُطْلَبُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ وَفِي الْمَسْجِدِ، وَتُفْتَحُ أَبْوَابُ الْمَسْجِدِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
lines.en: ʿUmar said: It is sought in the ribāṭ and in the mosque, and the doors of the mosque are opened in the morning.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدَانِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ، وَسُمِعَ الذِّكْرُ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ.
lines.en: Then the two boys went to the mosque, and the dhikr was heard from far away.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: كُتِبَ هَذَا الدَّرْسُ فِي كِتَابٍ قَدِيمٍ، وَحُفِظَ فِي الْقُلُوبِ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: This lesson was written in an old book, and it was memorised in the hearts.

lines.ar: قَالَ عُمَرُ: وَقِيلَ لَنَا: اِحْفَظُوا الدَّرْسَ.
lines.en: ʿUmar said: And it was said to us: Memorise the lesson.

passages.ar: سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ: أَيْنَ وُلِدَ إِمَامُ الْمَسْجِدِ؟ قَالَ عُمَرُ: يُقَالُ إِنَّهُ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ، وَطَلَبَ الْعِلْمَ هُنَاكَ. قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: وَأَيْنَ يُطْلَبُ الْعِلْمُ الْيَوْمَ؟ قَالَ عُمَرُ: يُطْلَبُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ وَفِي الْمَسْجِدِ، وَتُفْتَحُ أَبْوَابُ الْمَسْجِدِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ. ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدَانِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ، وَسُمِعَ الذِّكْرُ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ. قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: كُتِبَ هَذَا الدَّرْسُ فِي كِتَابٍ قَدِيمٍ، وَحُفِظَ فِي الْقُلُوبِ. قَالَ عُمَرُ: وَقِيلَ لَنَا: اِحْفَظُوا الدَّرْسَ.
passages.en: Ahmad asked ʿUmar: Where was the imam of the mosque born? ʿUmar said: It is said that he was born in Tarim, and that he sought knowledge there. Ahmad said: And where is knowledge sought today? ʿUmar said: It is sought in the ribāṭ and in the mosque, and the doors of the mosque are opened in the morning. Then the two boys went to the mosque, and the dhikr was heard from far away. Ahmad said: This lesson was written in an old book, and it was memorised in the hearts. ʿUmar said: And it was said to us: Memorise the lesson.

lines.ar: يَٰأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ
lines.en: O you who believe,

lines.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ
lines.en: fasting has been prescribed for you

lines.ar: كَمَا كُتِبَ
lines.en: as it was prescribed

lines.ar: عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ
lines.en: for those before you,

lines.ar: لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
lines.en: so that you may be mindful of Allah.

glossary.en: you are mindful of Allah, you guard against wrongdoing

passages.ar: يَٰأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
passages.en: O you who believe, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may be mindful of Allah.

passages.intro_en: A line from a teaching text (Durūs al-Tawḥīd). Read it, then answer.
passages.source: Durūs al-Tawḥīd (Ḥabīb Muḥammad b. Sālim b. Ḥafīẓ)

lines.ar: عِلْمُ التَّوْحِيدِ: هُوَ عِلْمٌ يُعْرَفُ بِهِ إِثْبَاتُ الْعَقَائِدِ الدِّينِيَّةِ بِالْأَدِلَّةِ الْيَقِينِيَّةِ.
lines.en: The science of tawḥīd is a science by which the beliefs of the religion are established through certain proofs.

passages.ar: عِلْمُ التَّوْحِيدِ: هُوَ عِلْمٌ يُعْرَفُ بِهِ إِثْبَاتُ الْعَقَائِدِ الدِّينِيَّةِ بِالْأَدِلَّةِ الْيَقِينِيَّةِ.
passages.en: The science of tawḥīd is a science by which the beliefs of the religion are established through certain proofs.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 71-72 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.

lines.ar: قِيلَ لِلْوَلَدِ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ.
lines.en: It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.

passages.ar: يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ. قِيلَ لِلْوَلَدِ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ.
passages.en: It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim. It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.

glossary.en: you are mindful of Allah, you guard against wrongdoing

questions.q: Who asked a question, and what was it? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَأَلَ؟ وَمَا السُّؤَالُ؟
questions.a: Ahmad asked where the imam of the mosque was born.

questions.q: Translate the verb.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْفِعْلَ.
questions.a: was born

questions.q: Line 2: is ʿUmar sure? Which word shows it?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ عُمَرُ وَاثِقٌ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: No. يُقَالُ = “it is said”: he does not say who said it.

questions.q: Where was the imam born, and what did he do there?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ؟ وَمَاذَا فَعَلَ هُنَاكَ؟
questions.a: In Tarim; he sought knowledge.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: Knowledge is sought.

questions.q: When are the doors of the mosque opened? Who opens them?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى تُفْتَحُ الْأَبْوَابُ؟ مَنْ يَفْتَحُهَا؟
questions.a: In the morning. The text does not say who.

questions.q: What was heard from far away?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سُمِعَ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ؟
questions.a: The dhikr (الذِّكْرُ).

questions.q: True or false: the text says who wrote the old book.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَذْكُرُ النَّصُّ كَاتِبَ الْكِتَابِ الْقَدِيمِ.
questions.a: False. كُتِبَ = “was written”: the writer is not named.

questions.q: Why does line 4 say تُفْتَحُ (with تُـ), not يُفْتَحُ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «تُفْتَحُ» وَلَيْسَ «يُفْتَحُ»؟
questions.a: What the verb is about, أَبْوَابُ (doors), is a plural of things: the verb is feminine singular.

questions.q: Find the two passive verbs in line 6 and say what they mean.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْفِعْلَيْنِ الْمَجْهُولَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ السَّادِسِ وَقُلْ مَعْنَاهُمَا.
questions.a: كُتِبَ (was written) and حُفِظَ (was memorised).

questions.q: Line 7: قِيلَ names no speaker. Why might the story not say who spoke?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَا تَذْكُرُ الْقِصَّةُ مَنْ قَالَ؟
questions.a: Open answer: what was said matters more than who said it (for example the teachers of the ribāṭ).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and which sūra is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيِّ سُورَةٍ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an, Sūrat al-Baqara (2:183).

questions.q: Who is spoken to?
questions.q_ar: لِمَنْ هَذَا الْخِطَابُ؟
questions.a: Those who believe (الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ).

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: Fasting is prescribed for you (literally: “was written upon you”).

questions.q: What is prescribed? Which word says it?
questions.q_ar: مَا الَّذِي كُتِبَ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: Fasting: الصِّيَامُ.

questions.q: How many times does كُتِبَ occur? Does the word name who prescribed it?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً جَاءَ «كُتِبَ»؟ هَلْ يَذْكُرُ الْفَاعِلَ؟
questions.a: Twice. No: the verb leaves the doer out.

questions.q: The verse compares two groups. Which two?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْجَمَاعَتَانِ فِي الْآيَةِ؟
questions.a: You (the believers) and those before you.

questions.q: Why does الصِّيَامُ end with ḍamma?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا انْتَهَتْ «الصِّيَامُ» بِالضَّمَّةِ؟
questions.a: It is what was prescribed: it stepped into the doer’s place, so it is in the ḍamma state.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A short definition from a teaching text on tawḥīd: Durūs al-Tawḥīd.

questions.q: What is being defined?
questions.q_ar: مَا اسْمُ هَذَا الْعِلْمِ؟
questions.a: The science of tawḥīd.

questions.q: Find the passive verb.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْفِعْلَ الْمَجْهُولَ.
questions.a: يُعْرَفُ (“is known”).

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: is known by it

questions.q: What is established by this science?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا نَعْرِفُ بِهَذَا الْعِلْمِ؟
questions.a: The beliefs of the religion (إِثْبَاتُ الْعَقَائِدِ).

questions.q: Write the active verb (he knows) that يُعْرَفُ comes from.
questions.q_ar: اُكْتُبِ الْفِعْلَ الْمَعْلُومَ.
questions.a: يَعْرِفُ

questions.q: Say in your own words what the science of tawḥīd does.
questions.q_ar: قُلْ بِكَلِمَاتِكَ: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ عِلْمُ التَّوْحِيدِ؟
questions.a: Open answer: it shows, with sure proofs, that the beliefs of the religion are true.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim. It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.

questions.q: Which two words in the new lines are passive (the doer is not named)?
questions.a: يُقَالُ and قِيلَ (and also وُلِدَ: “he was born”)

questions.q: In the first new line, who says it? Does the sentence tell us?
questions.a: No. A passive verb leaves the speaker out: “it is said”.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
questions.a: قِيلَ لِلْوَلَدِ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ.

translate.en: The door of the ribāṭ was opened in the morning.

translate.ar: كُتِبَ هَذَا الْكِتَابُ فِي مَدِينَةِ تَرِيمَ.
translate.en: This book was written in the city of Tarim.

translate.ar: يُقْرَأُ الْوِرْدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
translate.en: The wird is read in the mosque in the evening.
The lesson was heard in the circle.
Fatima was born in an old house.
It is said that the lesson is easy.
It was said to the guests: Enter the majlis.
The word was kept (memorised) in the heart.
The teacher was thanked because he is generous.
The library was opened yesterday.
The name of the mosque was written on the door.
The lessons are memorised in the ribāṭ.

translate.ar: يُطْلَبُ الْعِلْمُ فِي الْمَسَاءِ وَيُحْفَظُ فِي الْقَلْبِ.
translate.en: Knowledge is sought in the evening and kept in the heart.

translate.ar: يُذْكَرُ اللَّهُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَفِي الْمَسَاءِ.
translate.en: Allah is remembered in the mosque in the morning and in the evening.
My brother was born in a beautiful house.

translate.ar: يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ قَدِيمٌ وَإِنَّهُ كَبِيرٌ.
translate.en: It is said that the mosque is old and that it is big.
The lesson was written, then memorised.

translate.ar: سَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ: أَيْنَ كُتِبَ هَذَا الْكِتَابُ؟ قَالَ الْمُعَلِّمُ: يُقَالُ إِنَّهُ كُتِبَ فِي تَرِيمَ، وَلَكِنْ لَا يُعْرَفُ مَنْ كَتَبَهُ.
translate.en: The boy asked: Where was this book written? The teacher said: It is said that it was written in Tarim, but it is not known who wrote it.
The door was opened.
The lesson was written in the book.
The dhikr is heard in the mosque.
Ahmad was born in Tarim.
It is said that the Habib is in the ribāṭ.
The letter was written yesterday.
Knowledge is sought in the majlis.
It was said to the boy: “Read the lesson.”
The word was heard in the circle.
Maryam was born in a big house.
The lessons are memorised in the ribāṭ.
The muṣḥaf was opened in the mosque.

lines.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: In the evening Ahmad sat in the Habib’s circle.

lines.ar: سَلَّمَ أَحْمَدُ عَلَى الْحَبِيبِ، وَسَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ عَلَيْهِ.
lines.en: Ahmad greeted the Habib, and the Habib greeted him.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ ذَكَّرَ الْحَبِيبُ الطُّلَّابَ بِالْأَدَبِ.
lines.en: Then the Habib reminded the students of good manners.

lines.ar: وَعَلَّمَ أَحْمَدَ صَلَاةً عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
lines.en: And he taught Ahmad a ṣalāt on the Prophet ﷺ.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: قُلْ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمْ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Say: O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him.

lines.ar: فَقَالَهَا أَحْمَدُ، وَكَبَّرَ الطُّلَّابُ وَسَبَّحُوا اللَّهَ.
lines.en: Ahmad said it, and the students said “Allāhu akbar” and glorified Allah.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ دَرَّسَ الْحَبِيبُ الدَّرْسَ، وَفَهَّمَ الطُّلَّابَ الْكَلِمَاتِ الْجَدِيدَةَ.
lines.en: Then the Habib taught the lesson and made the students understand the new words.

lines.ar: وَقَدَّمَتْ مَرْيَمُ الطَّعَامَ لِلضُّيُوفِ، وَنَظَّفَ عُمَرُ الْمَسْجِدَ.
lines.en: And Maryam served the food to the guests, and ʿUmar cleaned the mosque.

lines.ar: فَذَكَّرَ أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ بِالصَّلَاةِ، لِأَنَّ الْوَقْتَ قَرِيبٌ.
lines.en: So Ahmad reminded ʿUmar of the prayer, because the time was near.

passages.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ. سَلَّمَ أَحْمَدُ عَلَى الْحَبِيبِ، وَسَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ عَلَيْهِ. ثُمَّ ذَكَّرَ الْحَبِيبُ الطُّلَّابَ بِالْأَدَبِ. وَعَلَّمَ أَحْمَدَ صَلَاةً عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: قُلْ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمْ. فَقَالَهَا أَحْمَدُ، وَكَبَّرَ الطُّلَّابُ وَسَبَّحُوا اللَّهَ. ثُمَّ دَرَّسَ الْحَبِيبُ الدَّرْسَ، وَفَهَّمَ الطُّلَّابَ الْكَلِمَاتِ الْجَدِيدَةَ. وَقَدَّمَتْ مَرْيَمُ الطَّعَامَ لِلضُّيُوفِ، وَنَظَّفَ عُمَرُ الْمَسْجِدَ. فَذَكَّرَ أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ بِالصَّلَاةِ، لِأَنَّ الْوَقْتَ قَرِيبٌ.
passages.en: In the evening Ahmad sat in the Habib’s circle. Ahmad greeted the Habib, and the Habib greeted him. Then the Habib reminded the students of good manners. And he taught Ahmad a ṣalāt on the Prophet ﷺ. The Habib said: Say: O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him. Ahmad said it, and the students said “Allāhu akbar” and glorified Allah. Then the Habib taught the lesson and made the students understand the new words. And Maryam served the food to the guests, and ʿUmar cleaned the mosque. So Ahmad reminded ʿUmar of the prayer, because the time was near.

passages.ar: مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَيَّ صَلَاةً صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ بِهَا عَشْرًا

lines.en: O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him.

passages.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمْ
passages.en: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad, O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him.
