lines.ar: عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
lines.en: The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.

lines.ar: ذَكَّرَ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ بِالصَّلَاةِ.
lines.en: The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.

passages.ar: عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ. ذَكَّرَ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ بِالصَّلَاةِ.
passages.en: The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ. The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and when?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: In the Habib’s circle, in the evening.

questions.q: Who greeted whom in line 2?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَلَّمَ عَلَى مَنْ؟
questions.a: Ahmad greeted the Habib, and the Habib greeted him.

questions.q: Translate the verb.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْفِعْلَ.
questions.a: he greeted (he said salām)

questions.q: What did the Habib remind the students of? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: بِمَاذَا ذَكَّرَ الْحَبِيبُ الطُّلَّابَ؟
questions.a: Of good manners (الْأَدَبِ).

questions.q: What did the Habib teach Ahmad? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: A ṣalāt (a prayer for blessings) on the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: What did the Habib tell Ahmad to say? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ أَنْ يَقُولَ؟
questions.a: O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him.

questions.q: What did the students do in line 6?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي السَّطْرِ السَّادِسِ؟
questions.a: They said “Allāhu akbar” and glorified Allah (كَبَّرَ، سَبَّحُوا).

questions.q: Line 7: find the two Form II verbs that say what the Habib did.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْفِعْلَيْنِ مِنَ الْوَزْنِ الثَّانِي فِي السَّطْرِ السَّابِعِ.
questions.a: دَرَّسَ (he taught the lesson) and فَهَّمَ (he made them understand).

questions.q: Who served the food, and who cleaned the mosque?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ قَدَّمَ الطَّعَامَ؟ وَمَنْ نَظَّفَ الْمَسْجِدَ؟
questions.a: Maryam served the food; ʿUmar cleaned the mosque.

questions.q: Why did Ahmad remind ʿUmar of the prayer? Which word shows the reason?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا ذَكَّرَ أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى السَّبَبِ؟
questions.a: Because the time was near. لِأَنَّ = because.

questions.q: Which of عَلِمَ and عَلَّمَ means “taught”? What is different in the letters?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّهُمَا بِمَعْنَى «teach»؟ مَا الْفَرْقُ فِي الْحُرُوفِ؟
questions.a: عَلَّمَ: the middle letter is doubled.

questions.q: Why is كَبَّرَ singular but سَبَّحُوا plural in line 6?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «كَبَّرَ» مُفْرَدٌ وَ«سَبَّحُوا» جَمْعٌ؟
questions.a: كَبَّرَ comes before its doer (الطُّلَّابُ), so it stays singular; سَبَّحُوا has no doer after it, so its ending shows “they”.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A saying of the Prophet ﷺ (a ḥadīth), from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 384.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: Whoever sends blessings upon me

questions.q: How many times does the verb صَلَّى occur?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً جَاءَ الْفِعْلُ «صَلَّى»؟
questions.a: Twice.

questions.q: In the second part, who sends blessings?
questions.q_ar: فِي الْجُزْءِ الثَّانِي: مَنْ يُصَلِّي؟
questions.a: Allah (اللَّهُ).

questions.q: How many blessings does Allah send for each one?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ صَلَاةً يُصَلِّي اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ صَلَّى مَرَّةً؟
questions.a: Ten (عَشْرًا).

questions.q: Which word in the line is the noun from the same root as the verb? Write it.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ اسْمٍ فِي السَّطْرِ مِنْ جَذْرِ الْفِعْلِ؟ اُكْتُبْهُ.
questions.a: صَلَاةً

questions.q: The verb is the same twice. How does its meaning differ between the believer and Allah?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ مَعْنَى الْفِعْلِ وَاحِدٌ فِي الْمَوْضِعَيْنِ؟
questions.a: The believer asks for blessings upon the Prophet; Allah answers with ten blessings upon the believer.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A saying of the Prophet ﷺ (a ḥadīth), from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 406.

questions.q: Is قُولُوا said to one person or to many? How can you tell?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ «قُولُوا» لِوَاحِدٍ أَمْ لِجَمَاعَةٍ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: To many: the ending is the plural ending of a command.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad

questions.q: Who else is named after Muḥammad? Which word means “family”?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ ذُكِرَ بَعْدَ مُحَمَّدٍ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ مَعْنَاهَا «family»؟
questions.a: His family: آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ (آلِ = family of).

questions.q: Which word is the command? Which Form is it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ الْأَمْرُ؟ مِنْ أَيِّ وَزْنٍ؟
questions.a: صَلِّ: a command, Form II.

questions.q: Compare this line with the Rātib line اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمْ. What is the same, and what is added?
questions.q_ar: اُنْظُرْ إِلَى هَذَا السَّطْرِ وَسَطْرِ الرَّاتِبِ. مَا الْمُشْتَرَكُ؟ وَمَا الزِّيَادَةُ؟
questions.a: The same command صَلِّ; the Rātib line adds وَسَلِّمْ (“and grant peace”).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A dhikr: the ṣalāt on the Prophet ﷺ, from the Rātib of Imam al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him

questions.q: Find the two Form II commands in the two lines.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْأَمْرَيْنِ مِنَ الْوَزْنِ الثَّانِي فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ.
questions.a: صَلِّ and سَلِّمْ

questions.q: Who is the ـهِ in عَلَيْهِ?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْهَاءُ فِي «عَلَيْهِ»؟
questions.a: Muḥammad, the Prophet ﷺ (named in line 1).

questions.q: Which word in the lines is the first word of both, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي أَوَّلِ السَّطْرَيْنِ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: اللَّهُمَّ: “O Allah”.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ. The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.

questions.q: What does the doubled middle letter in عَلَّمَ do to the meaning of عَلِمَ (he knew)?
questions.a: It makes another know: he taught.

questions.q: Which two commands in the first new line have a doubled middle letter?
questions.a: صَلِّ and سَلِّمْ

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
questions.a: ذَكَّرَ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ بِالصَّلَاةِ.

translate.ar: سَلَّمَ الْوَلَدُ عَلَى الْمُعَلِّمِ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: The boy greeted the teacher in the mosque.
The Habib taught the students a new word.
The imam reminded the people of Allah.
The imam said “Allāhu akbar”, then the people prostrated.
The students glorify Allah in the evening.
The teacher teaches the boy how to read.

translate.ar: فَهَّمَ الْمُعَلِّمُ الْوَلَدَ الدَّرْسَ، فَفَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ.
translate.en: The teacher made the boy understand the lesson, so the boy understood.
Fatima served the food to the guests.
ʿUmar cleaned the room and the kitchen.

translate.ar: يُدَرِّسُ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
translate.en: The Habib teaches in the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Greet the teacher.
Fatima taught Maryam a word.

translate.ar: سَلَّمَ الضُّيُوفُ عَلَى الْحَبِيبِ، وَقَدَّمَ لَهُمْ أَحْمَدُ اللَّبَنَ.
translate.en: The guests greeted the Habib, and Ahmad served them milk.
The boy said “Allāhu akbar” and glorified Allah, then sat down.
The teacher reminds the students of the lesson.

translate.ar: سَلَّمَ الطَّالِبُ عَلَى الْمُعَلِّمِ. وَعَلَّمَهُ الْمُعَلِّمُ كَلِمَةً جَدِيدَةً. ثُمَّ ذَكَّرَهُ بِالدَّرْسِ الْقَدِيمِ.
translate.en: The student greeted the teacher. The teacher taught him a new word. Then he reminded him of the old lesson.
The boy greeted the Habib.
The teacher taught the boy.
The Habib reminded the students of the lesson.
The imam said “Allāhu akbar”.
The students glorify Allah in the mosque.
Maryam served the food to the guests.
ʿUmar cleaned the mosque.
The teacher made the student understand the word.
The Habib teaches in the ribāṭ.
Say: “O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him.”
Ahmad reminded ʿUmar of the prayer.
The guests greeted the Habib.

readings.title_en: Reading day 1: the formulas of the Rātib and where they come from
readings.question_en: I know these words by ear. Can I read them, understand them and say where they come from?
readings.question_ar: أَعْرِفُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ بِالسَّمْعِ. هَلْ أَقْرَؤُهَا وَأَفْهَمُهَا وَأَعْرِفُ مِنْ أَيْنَ جَاءَتْ؟

passages.intro_en: Read the six formulas of the Rātib aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Rātib al-Ḥaddād, six of its dhikrs (each said three times)
passages.cite: al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, Rātib (Sabīl al-Saʿāda wa-l-Falāḥ fī Adhkār al-Masāʾ wa-l-Ṣabāḥ); numbering of the dhikrs and pages after ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad Bā Sawdān, Dhakhīrat al-Maʿād bi-Sharḥ Rātib al-Ḥaddād, Cairo, 1378 H / 1959 (4th dhikr p. 83, 5th p. 91, 9th p. 114, 10th p. 115); vowelled for learners following the vowelled ḥadīth wording. Sources of the lines: (1) Muslim 2691, al-Tirmidhī 3474; (2) Muslim 2137; (3) Muslim 2694, al-Bukhārī 6406; (4) Muslim 2708; (5) Abū Dāwūd 5088; (6) Muslim 1884.

lines.ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
lines.en: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things.

lines.ar: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَاللهُ أَكْبَرُ
lines.en: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest.

lines.ar: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللهِ الْعَظِيمِ
lines.en: Glory be to Allah and with His praise; glory be to Allah, the Tremendous.

lines.ar: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
lines.en: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created.

lines.ar: بِسْمِ اللهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
lines.en: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

lines.ar: رَضِينَا بِاللهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
lines.en: We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad as Prophet.

passages.ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَاللهُ أَكْبَرُ سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللهِ الْعَظِيمِ أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ بِسْمِ اللهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ رَضِينَا بِاللهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
passages.en: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things. Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest. Glory be to Allah and with His praise; glory be to Allah, the Tremendous. I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created. In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad as Prophet.

passages.intro_en: Behind the formulas: two clauses of ḥadīth from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. Read, then answer.
passages.cite: Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Dār al-Jīl + Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut, vowelled print (Shamela 1786; the card gives no year), 6/172 (Dār al-Jīl no. 5724); ʿAbd al-Bāqī numbering: ed. Muḥammad Fuʾād ʿAbd al-Bāqī, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Beirut (Shamela 1785), no. 2137, 3/1685  ||  Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Dār al-Jīl + Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut, vowelled print (Shamela 1786; the card gives no year), 6/37 (Dār al-Jīl no. 4987); ʿAbd al-Bāqī numbering: ed. Muḥammad Fuʾād ʿAbd al-Bāqī, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Beirut (Shamela 1785), no. 1884, 3/1501

lines.ar: أَحَبُّ الْكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
lines.en: “The dearest words to Allah are four: glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest.”

lines.ar: مَنْ رَضِيَ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
lines.en: “Whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad as Prophet, the Garden becomes his due.”

passages.ar: أَحَبُّ الْكَلَامِ إِلَى اللَّهِ أَرْبَعٌ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ مَنْ رَضِيَ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
passages.en: “The dearest words to Allah are four: glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest.” “Whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad as Prophet, the Garden becomes his due.”

passages.intro_en: A night in the ribāṭ. You have not seen this text. Read it aloud, then answer. (Word: أَسْتَغْفِرُ = I ask forgiveness.)

lines.ar: فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
lines.en: At night Ahmad sat with the students in the ribāṭ.

lines.ar: فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ الْكِتَابَ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
lines.en: The Habib opened the book and read the Rātib.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الطُّلَّابُ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ.
lines.en: And the students said: There is no god but Allah.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ سَبَّحَ أَحْمَدُ وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَكَبَّرَ.
lines.en: Then Ahmad glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ.
lines.en: And he said: I ask Allah for forgiveness.

lines.ar: سَمِعَ الضُّيُوفُ الذِّكْرَ، وَكَانَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ سَعِيدَةً.
lines.en: The guests heard the dhikr, and their hearts were happy.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الذِّكْرُ نُورٌ لِلْقَلْبِ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Dhikr is a light for the heart.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَنَامَ.
lines.en: And Ahmad returned to the house and slept.

passages.ar: فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ فِي الرِّبَاطِ. فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ الْكِتَابَ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ. وَقَالَ الطُّلَّابُ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ. ثُمَّ سَبَّحَ أَحْمَدُ وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَكَبَّرَ. وَقَالَ: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ. سَمِعَ الضُّيُوفُ الذِّكْرَ، وَكَانَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ سَعِيدَةً. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الذِّكْرُ نُورٌ لِلْقَلْبِ. وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَنَامَ.
passages.en: At night Ahmad sat with the students in the ribāṭ. The Habib opened the book and read the Rātib. And the students said: There is no god but Allah. Then Ahmad glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar. And he said: I ask Allah for forgiveness. The guests heard the dhikr, and their hearts were happy. The Habib said: Dhikr is a light for the heart. And Ahmad returned to the house and slept.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 75-76 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
lines.en: At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.

lines.ar: قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
lines.en: They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.

passages.ar: فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ. قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
passages.en: At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib. They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Short dhikr formulas from the Rātib of Imam ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād; each one is also found in a ḥadīth.

questions.q: Line 1: whose is the dominion, and whose is the praise?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ وَلِمَنِ الْحَمْدُ؟
questions.a: Allah’s: “His is the dominion and His the praise”.

questions.q: Line 1: which word means “alone”?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ مَعْنَاهَا «مُنْفَرِدًا»؟
questions.a: وَحْدَهُ

questions.q: Line 2 joins four short formulas with وَ. Say the first and the last.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: يَجْمَعُ أَرْبَعَةَ أَذْكَارٍ. اُذْكُرِ الْأَوَّلَ وَالْأَخِيرَ.
questions.a: The first: Glory be to Allah. The last: Allah is greatest.

questions.q: Line 3: translate it.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: تَرْجِمْهُ.
questions.a: Glory be to Allah and with His praise; glory be to Allah, the Tremendous.

questions.q: True or false? Line 3 says that Allah is small.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ السَّطْرُ ٣ يَقُولُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ صَغِيرٌ.
questions.a: False. It says الْعَظِيمِ, “the Tremendous”.

questions.q: Line 4: from the evil of what? In whose perfect words do we seek refuge?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: مِنْ شَرِّ مَاذَا؟ وَبِكَلِمَاتِ مَنْ نَعُوذُ؟
questions.a: From the evil of what He created; in the perfect words of Allah.

questions.q: Which line speaks about the earth and the sky?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ يَذْكُرُ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّمَاءَ؟
questions.a: Line 5.

questions.q: Line 5: two names of Allah end the line. Which two?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٥: يَنْتَهِي بِاسْمَيْنِ لِلَّهِ. مَا هُمَا؟
questions.a: السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ: the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

questions.q: Line 6: with what are we pleased? Name the three.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٦: بِمَاذَا نَرْضَى؟ اُذْكُرِ الثَّلَاثَةَ.
questions.a: With Allah as Lord, Islam as religion and Muḥammad as Prophet.

questions.q: True or false? Every one of the six lines names Allah.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ فِي كُلِّ سَطْرٍ مِنَ الْأَسْطُرِ السِّتَّةِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ.
questions.a: True: every line contains the name Allāh.

questions.q: Line 6: these three words end in the same way. What is the ending, and what does it tell you?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٦: لِهَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ الثَّلَاثِ النِّهَايَةُ نَفْسُهَا. مَا هِيَ؟ وَمَاذَا تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: Tanwīn with fatḥa (ـًا). The three words play the same part: each says what we are pleased with.

questions.q: Line 1 has two verbs side by side with opposite meanings. What are they, and what do they say about Allah?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: فِعْلَانِ مُتَقَابِلَانِ. مَا هُمَا؟ وَمَاذَا يَقُولَانِ عَنِ اللَّهِ؟
questions.a: He gives life and He causes death: all life and death are in His hand.

questions.q: How many words does clause 1 call “the dearest to Allah”?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ كَلِمَةً يَذْكُرُ السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ؟
questions.a: Four.

questions.q: List the four in clause 1.
questions.q_ar: اُذْكُرِ الْأَرْبَعَةَ.
questions.a: Glory be to Allah; praise belongs to Allah; there is no god but Allah; Allah is greatest.

questions.q: Which line of the Rātib (lines 1–6) gives these four words together?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ مِنَ الرَّاتِبِ يَجْمَعُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ؟
questions.a: Line 2.

questions.q: Clause 2 begins with مَنْ. What does مَنْ mean here?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ الثَّانِي يَبْدَأُ بِـ «مَنْ». مَا مَعْنَاهَا هُنَا؟
questions.a: “Whoever”.

questions.q: With what is the person pleased in clause 2? Name the three.
questions.q_ar: بِمَاذَا يَرْضَى الْإِنْسَانُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muḥammad as Prophet.

questions.q: True or false? The Rātib says رَضِيَ (“whoever is pleased”) in line 6, exactly as in the ḥadīth.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ يَقُولُ الرَّاتِبُ «رَضِيَ» كَمَا فِي الْحَدِيثِ.
questions.a: False. The Rātib says رَضِينَا, “we are pleased”.

questions.q: Find the word that means “dearest”.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي مَعْنَاهَا «الْأَكْثَرُ مَحَبَّةً».
questions.a: أَحَبُّ

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ النَّصِّ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth (the words of the Prophet ﷺ), from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, nos. 2137 and 1884.

questions.q: The words أَكْبَرُ and أَحَبُّ both begin with أَ and mean “most …”. What do they have in common?
questions.q_ar: فِي كَلِمَتَيْ «أَكْبَرُ» وَ«أَحَبُّ» وَزْنٌ وَاحِدٌ. مَا هُوَ؟
questions.a: Both are on the same pattern, the one that means “more …” or “most …” (greatest, dearest).

questions.q: Clause 1 of the ḥadīth and line 2 of the Rātib give the same four words. Is the order the same?
questions.q_ar: هَلِ التَّرْتِيبُ هُوَ نَفْسُهُ؟
questions.a: Yes, the same order.

questions.q: Who sat with the students, and where?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَلَسَ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ؟ وَأَيْنَ؟
questions.a: Ahmad, in the ribāṭ.

questions.q: What did the Habib read?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ؟
questions.a: The Rātib.

questions.q: What did the students say in line 3?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣؟
questions.a: There is no god but Allah.

questions.q: Put in order: (a) Ahmad glorified Allah (b) the Habib read the Rātib (c) Ahmad returned to the house.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) سَبَّحَ أَحْمَدُ (ب) قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الرَّاتِبَ (ج) رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
questions.a: b, a, c

questions.q: Line 4 has three verbs. What did Ahmad do?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٤ ثَلَاثَةُ أَفْعَالٍ. مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: He glorified Allah, praised Him and said Allāhu akbar.

questions.q: Which verb in line 4 comes from the root ك ب ر, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ٤ مِنَ الْجَذْرِ «ك ب ر»؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهُ؟
questions.a: وَكَبَّرَ: he said “Allāhu akbar”.

questions.q: How were the hearts of the guests?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ كَانَتْ قُلُوبُ الضُّيُوفِ؟
questions.a: Happy (سَعِيدَةً).

questions.q: True or false? The Habib said that dhikr is a light for the heart.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ إِنَّ الذِّكْرَ نُورٌ لِلْقَلْبِ.
questions.a: True.

questions.q: Line 6: why does the verb كَانَتْ (she-form) go with “hearts”?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٦: لِمَاذَا جَاءَ الْفِعْلُ «كَانَتْ» مَعَ «قُلُوبُهُمْ»؟
questions.a: A plural of things (not of people) takes a feminine singular verb.

questions.q: Why do you think the Habib calls dhikr “a light for the heart”? Answer in one sentence.
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يُسَمِّي الْحَبِيبُ الذِّكْرَ «نُورًا لِلْقَلْبِ»؟ أَجِبْ بِجُمْلَةٍ.
questions.a: Any sensible answer, e.g. because the heart that remembers Allah is clear and calm.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib. They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.

questions.q: In the second new line, which word means “praise”?
questions.a: الْحَمْدُ (with وَ in front)

questions.q: Which word means “greater” (Allāhu akbar)?
questions.a: أَكْبَرُ

questions.q: Write in Arabic: Glory be to Allah.
questions.a: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ.

translate.en: The imam glorified Allah and said Allāhu akbar, then gave the salām.
Praise belongs to Allah, who created mankind.

translate.ar: اللَّهُ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ.
translate.en: Allah is the All-Merciful, the Most Merciful, and He has power over all things.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ الرَّاتِبَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ فِي اللَّيْلِ.
translate.en: The students read the Rātib in the ribāṭ at night.
The dominion is not the people’s; the dominion is Allah’s.
This sea is big, and Allah is greater.

translate.ar: ذَكَرَ أَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ فِي قَلْبِهِ وَسَبَّحَهُ.
translate.en: Ahmad remembered Allah in his heart and glorified Him.
The Habib reminded the students of Allah.

translate.ar: وَلَدٌ سَعِيدٌ يَقْرَأُ الرَّاتِبَ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
translate.en: A happy boy reads the Rātib with his father.

translate.ar: هَلْ سَمِعْتَ الرَّاتِبَ فِي اللَّيْلِ؟ نَعَمْ، سَمِعْتُهُ مَعَ الضُّيُوفِ.
translate.en: Did you hear the Rātib at night? Yes, I heard it with the guests.

translate.ar: جَلَسَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. وَسَبَّحَ وَكَبَّرَ. ثُمَّ قَالَ: اللَّهُ عَظِيمٌ.
translate.en: The Habib sat in the mosque. He glorified Allah and said Allāhu akbar. Then he said: Allah is great.
The mosque is light, and dhikr is a light for the heart.
Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah.
Allah is greatest, and there is no god but Allah.
translate.ar: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ.

translate.en: The students read the Rātib in the ribāṭ at night.
translate.ar: قَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ الرَّاتِبَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ فِي اللَّيْلِ.

translate.en: Ahmad glorified Allah and praised Him.
The Habib said: Allah is All-Merciful and Most Merciful.
The dominion is Allah’s, and the praise is Allah’s.
His mother heard him in the house, and she was happy.
translate.ar: سَمِعَتْهُ أُمُّهُ فِي الْبَيْتِ وَكَانَتْ سَعِيدَةً.
alt: سَمِعَتْهُ أُمُّهُ فِي الْبَيْتِ وَهِيَ سَعِيدَةٌ.

translate.en: Allah is great and all-powerful.

readings.title_en: An alif after the first letter, or a hamza before it: Forms III and IV
readings.title_ar: أَلِفٌ بَعْدَ الْحَرْفِ الْأَوَّلِ أَوْ هَمْزَةٌ قَبْلَهُ
readings.question_en: Why do some verbs have an alif after the first letter (سَافَرَ) and others a hamza before it (أَرْسَلَ)?
readings.question_ar: لِمَاذَا فِي بَعْضِ الْأَفْعَالِ أَلِفٌ بَعْدَ الْحَرْفِ الْأَوَّلِ (سَافَرَ)، وَفِي بَعْضِهَا هَمْزَةٌ قَبْلَهُ (أَرْسَلَ)؟

passages.intro_en: A counsel of Imam al-Ḥaddād. Read aloud, then answer.
passages.source: al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya of Imam ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād
passages.cite: al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya wa-l-Waṣāyā al-Īmāniyya (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, 1), Dār al-Ḥāwī, 1st ed. 1413 H, 2nd ed. 1418 H (title page of the Shamela copy; SSD Master Library [184250]), p. 1/304 (the copy's page column; the two sentences are consecutive on p. 1/304)

lines.ar: فَإِذَا أَحَبَّ الْإِنْسَانُ الْإِنْسَانَ وَأَلِفَهُ وَصَاحَبَهُ لِأَنَّهُ يُحِبُّ اللهَ وَيَعْمَلُ بِطَاعَتِهِ
lines.en: If a person loves another, grows fond of him and keeps his company because he loves Allah and acts in obedience to Him,

lines.ar: كَانَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْمَحَبَّةِ فِي اللهِ تَعَالَى.
lines.en: that is love for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.

lines.ar: وَإِذَا أَحَبَّهُ وَصَحِبَهُ لِأَنَّهُ يُعِينُهُ عَلَى دِينِهِ وَيُسَاعِدُهُ عَلَى طَاعَةِ رَبِّهِ
lines.en: And if he loves him and keeps his company because he helps him in his religion and assists him in obedience to his Lord,

lines.ar: فَقَدْ أَحَبَّهُ فِي اللهِ.
lines.en: he has loved him for Allah’s sake.

passages.ar: فَإِذَا أَحَبَّ الْإِنْسَانُ الْإِنْسَانَ وَأَلِفَهُ وَصَاحَبَهُ لِأَنَّهُ يُحِبُّ اللهَ وَيَعْمَلُ بِطَاعَتِهِ كَانَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْمَحَبَّةِ فِي اللهِ تَعَالَى. وَإِذَا أَحَبَّهُ وَصَحِبَهُ لِأَنَّهُ يُعِينُهُ عَلَى دِينِهِ وَيُسَاعِدُهُ عَلَى طَاعَةِ رَبِّهِ فَقَدْ أَحَبَّهُ فِي اللهِ.
passages.en: If a person loves another, grows fond of him and keeps his company because he loves Allah and acts in obedience to Him, that is love for the sake of Allah, the Exalted. And if he loves him and keeps his company because he helps him in his religion and assists him in obedience to his Lord, he has loved him for Allah’s sake.

passages.intro_en: A verse of the Qur’an: sūrat al-Qadr, 97:1. Read aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Qur’an 97:1, Madīna mushaf text, extracted by program from quran.json (Quran_Verify) and spelled in ordinary vowelled orthography.

lines.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ
lines.en: Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of al-Qadr.

passages.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ
passages.en: Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of al-Qadr.

passages.intro_en: The Night of al-Qadr in the mosque. You have not seen this text. Read it aloud, then answer.

lines.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: On the Night of al-Qadr Ahmad went with his father to the mosque.

lines.ar: كَانَ الْمَسْجِدُ كَبِيرًا، وَكَانَ فِيهِ نَاسٌ كَثِيرُونَ.
lines.en: The mosque was big, and there were many people in it.

lines.ar: سَافَرَ كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ لِأَنَّهُمْ يُحِبُّونَ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ.
lines.en: Many of them travelled from a far place because they love this night.

lines.ar: أَكْرَمَ الْحَبِيبُ الضُّيُوفَ، وَسَاعَدَهُمْ أَحْمَدُ.
lines.en: The Habib honoured the guests, and Ahmad helped them.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ جَلَسَ النَّاسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ وَسَمِعُوا الدَّرْسَ.
lines.en: Then the people sat in the circle and heard the lesson.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ كِتَابَهُ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Allah sent down His book in this night.

lines.ar: وَفِي الصَّبَاحِ أَرْسَلَ أَحْمَدُ رِسَالَةً إِلَى أُمِّهِ.
lines.en: And in the morning Ahmad sent a letter to his mother.

lines.ar: فَشَكَرَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَقَالَتْ: أَنْتَ وَلَدٌ جَيِّدٌ.
lines.en: His mother thanked him and said: You are a good boy.

passages.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ. كَانَ الْمَسْجِدُ كَبِيرًا، وَكَانَ فِيهِ نَاسٌ كَثِيرُونَ. سَافَرَ كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ لِأَنَّهُمْ يُحِبُّونَ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ. أَكْرَمَ الْحَبِيبُ الضُّيُوفَ، وَسَاعَدَهُمْ أَحْمَدُ. ثُمَّ جَلَسَ النَّاسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ وَسَمِعُوا الدَّرْسَ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ كِتَابَهُ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ. وَفِي الصَّبَاحِ أَرْسَلَ أَحْمَدُ رِسَالَةً إِلَى أُمِّهِ. فَشَكَرَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَقَالَتْ: أَنْتَ وَلَدٌ جَيِّدٌ.
passages.en: On the Night of al-Qadr Ahmad went with his father to the mosque. The mosque was big, and there were many people in it. Many of them travelled from a far place because they love this night. The Habib honoured the guests, and Ahmad helped them. Then the people sat in the circle and heard the lesson. The Habib said: Allah sent down His book in this night. And in the morning Ahmad sent a letter to his mother. His mother thanked him and said: You are a good boy.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 77-78 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
lines.en: On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.

lines.ar: سَاعَدَ الْوَلَدُ الضُّيُوفَ وَأَكْرَمَهُمْ.
lines.en: The boy helped the guests and honoured them.

passages.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ. سَاعَدَ الْوَلَدُ الضُّيُوفَ وَأَكْرَمَهُمْ.
passages.en: On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father. The boy helped the guests and honoured them.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A counsel (advice) from al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya of Imam ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: Line 1: when is a person’s love for another “love for Allah’s sake”? (first case)
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَتَى تَكُونُ مَحَبَّةُ الْإِنْسَانِ لِغَيْرِهِ فِي اللَّهِ؟
questions.a: When he loves him because he loves Allah and acts in obedience to Him.

questions.q: Which verb in line 1 means “he loved”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ١ مَعْنَاهُ «he loved»؟
questions.a: أَحَبَّ

questions.q: Which verb in line 1 means “and he kept his company”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ١ مَعْنَاهُ «and he kept his company»؟
questions.a: وَصَاحَبَهُ

questions.q: Line 1: why does he love him? What does the person himself love?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: لِمَاذَا يُحِبُّهُ؟
questions.a: Because he loves Allah (لِأَنَّهُ يُحِبُّ اللهَ).

questions.q: Line 3: in what does he help him?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: فِي مَاذَا يُعِينُهُ؟
questions.a: In his religion, and in obedience to his Lord.

questions.q: True or false? Line 4 says that he has loved him for Allah’s sake.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ السَّطْرُ ٤ يَقُولُ إِنَّهُ أَحَبَّهُ فِي اللهِ.
questions.a: True.

questions.q: Find a Form III verb in line 3. What is its root?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ فِعْلًا مِنْ بَابِ فَاعَلَ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣. مَا جَذْرُهُ؟
questions.a: وَيُسَاعِدُهُ (he helps him), root س ع د.

questions.q: Find a Form IV verb in line 4. How do you know it is Form IV?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ فِعْلًا مِنْ بَابِ أَفْعَلَ فِي السَّطْرِ ٤. كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: أَحَبَّهُ: there is a hamza before the first letter (the present is يُحِبُّ).

questions.q: Which word in line 1 is the present of أَحَبَّ?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ١ هِيَ مُضَارِعُ أَحَبَّ؟
questions.a: يُحِبُّ

questions.q: The verbs أَحَبَّ and يُحِبُّ and the noun الْمَحَبَّةِ share a root. Which?
questions.q_ar: الْفِعْلَانِ أَحَبَّ وَيُحِبُّ وَالِاسْمُ الْمَحَبَّةُ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ. مَا هُوَ؟
questions.a: ح ب ب (love).

questions.q: Lines 2 and 4 both have فِي اللهِ. What does فِي mean here?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ٢ وَ٤ عِبَارَةُ «فِي اللهِ». مَا مَعْنَى «فِي» هُنَا؟
questions.a: “For the sake of”: the love is for Allah, not for a worldly gain.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A verse of the Qur’an: sūrat al-Qadr, 97:1.

questions.q: Translate the verse.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ.
questions.a: Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of al-Qadr.

questions.q: Which word means “night”? Which means “the Decree”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ مَعْنَاهَا «night»؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ مَعْنَاهَا «the Decree»؟
questions.a: لَيْلَةِ; الْقَدْرِ

questions.q: Which verb means “We sent down”? What is its root?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ مَعْنَاهُ «We sent down»؟ مَا جَذْرُهُ؟
questions.a: أَنزَلْنَٰهُ; root ن ز ل.

questions.q: Is the verb Form III or IV? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: هَلِ الْفِعْلُ مِنْ بَابِ فَاعَلَ أَوْ أَفْعَلَ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: Form IV: a hamza before the first letter.

questions.q: Who is “We” in the verse?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ هُوَ «نَحْنُ» فِي الْآيَةِ؟
questions.a: Allah (He speaks of Himself as “We”).

questions.q: What does the hamza add to نَزَلَ (he came down) in أَنْزَلَ?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا زَادَتِ الْهَمْزَةُ عَلَى نَزَلَ فِي أَنْزَلَ؟
questions.a: It makes it “cause to come down”: He sent it down.

questions.q: Why does لَيْلَةِ end in ـِ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي لَيْلَةِ بِكَسْرَةٍ؟
questions.a: It comes after فِي.

questions.q: On which night did Ahmad go to the mosque, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ لَيْلَةٍ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: On the Night of al-Qadr, with his father.

questions.q: Why did many people travel from a far place?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا سَافَرَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ؟
questions.a: Because they love this night.

questions.q: Who honoured the guests, and who helped them?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ أَكْرَمَ الضُّيُوفَ؟ وَمَنْ سَاعَدَهُمْ؟
questions.a: The Habib honoured them; Ahmad helped them.

questions.q: What did the people do in line 5?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ النَّاسُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٥؟
questions.a: They sat in the circle and heard the lesson.

questions.q: What did the Habib say in line 6?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٦؟
questions.a: Allah sent down His book in this night.

questions.q: What did Ahmad send in the morning, and to whom?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا أَرْسَلَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟ وَإِلَى مَنْ؟
questions.a: A letter, to his mother.

questions.q: True or false? Line 2 says the mosque was small.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ السَّطْرُ ٢ يَقُولُ إِنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ كَانَ صَغِيرًا.
questions.a: False. The mosque was big (كَبِيرًا).

questions.q: Put in order: (a) the Habib said that Allah sent down His book (b) Ahmad sent a letter (c) the people sat in the circle.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ كِتَابَهُ (ب) أَرْسَلَ أَحْمَدُ رِسَالَةً (ج) جَلَسَ النَّاسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
questions.a: c, a, b

questions.q: Line 3: is سَافَرَ Form III or IV? What is its root and its meaning?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: هَلْ سَافَرَ مِنْ بَابِ فَاعَلَ أَوْ أَفْعَلَ؟ مَا جَذْرُهُ وَمَعْنَاهُ؟
questions.a: Form III (alif after the first letter); root س ف ر; he travelled.

questions.q: Why does the mother thank him? What do you think he wrote in the letter? Answer in one sentence.
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا شَكَرَتْهُ أُمُّهُ؟ مَاذَا كَتَبَ فِي الرِّسَالَةِ فِي رَأْيِكَ؟ أَجِبْ بِجُمْلَةٍ.
questions.a: Any sensible answer, e.g. he told her about the night and thanked her for sending him.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father. The boy helped the guests and honoured them.

questions.q: Which verb has an alif after the first letter (Form III)?
questions.a: سَاعَدَ (he helped)

questions.q: Which verb has a hamza before the first letter (Form IV)?
questions.a: أَكْرَمَ (he honoured)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy helped the guests.
questions.a: سَاعَدَ الْوَلَدُ الضُّيُوفَ.

translate.ar: سَافَرَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَأَرْسَلَ رِسَالَةً.
translate.en: The father of Ahmad travelled to the city and sent a letter.
The boy helps his mother in the kitchen.
The Habib honoured the guests and thanked them.

translate.ar: لَمْ يُسَافِرْ عُمَرُ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ حَزِينًا.
translate.en: Umar did not travel because he was sad.

translate.ar: أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ كِتَابَهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ.
translate.en: Allah sent down His book in the Night of al-Qadr.

translate.ar: جَاهَدَ الطَّالِبُ فِي الدَّرْسِ وَحَفِظَ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
translate.en: The student strove in the lesson and memorised every word.

translate.ar: هَلْ أَرْسَلْتَ الرِّسَالَةَ؟ نَعَمْ، أَرْسَلْتُهَا أَمْسِ.
translate.en: Did you send the letter? Yes, I sent it yesterday.
The student loves his teacher because he helps him.

translate.ar: صَاحَبَ أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ وَسَاعَدَهُ فِي الدَّرْسِ.
translate.en: Ahmad kept company with Umar at school and helped him in the lesson.

translate.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ سَافَرَ النَّاسُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ. أَكْرَمَهُمُ الْحَبِيبُ وَسَاعَدَهُمْ أَحْمَدُ. وَجَلَسُوا حَتَّى الصَّبَاحِ.
translate.en: The people travelled to the mosque on the Night of al-Qadr. The Habib honoured them and Ahmad helped them. They sat until the morning.

translate.ar: أَسْلَمَ الرَّجُلُ وَكَانَ سَعِيدًا فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ.
translate.en: The man became a Muslim and was happy on that day.

translate.ar: سَافَرَتْ فَاطِمَةُ مَعَ بِنْتِهَا إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
translate.en: Fatima travelled with her daughter to Tarim.
The boy travelled to Tarim with his father.
translate.ar: سَافَرَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.

translate.en: Umar helped his friend in the lesson.
Ahmad sent a letter to his mother.
The Habib honoured the guests in the ribāṭ.
Allah sent down the book on the Night of al-Qadr.
translate.ar: أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ الْكِتَابَ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ.
alt: أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ كِتَابَهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ.

translate.en: The students strive in the lesson every day.
translate.ar: يُجَاهِدُ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الدَّرْسِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.

translate.en: I helped my sister in the kitchen.
He did not travel yesterday.
The man became a Muslim in the mosque.
The student loves his teacher, and the teacher helps him.

readings.title_en: تَـ at the front: Forms V and VI
readings.question_en: Why does this verb begin with تَـ?
readings.question_ar: لِمَاذَا يَبْدَأُ هَذَا الْفِعْلُ بِتَاءٍ؟

passages.intro_en: A ḥadīth. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 54 (Abū Hurayra): the Prophet ﷺ says it
passages.cite: Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Dār al-Jīl + Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut, vowelled print (Shamela 1786), 1/53 (Dār al-Jīl no. 203); ʿAbd al-Bāqī numbering: ed. Muḥammad Fuʾād ʿAbd al-Bāqī, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Beirut (Shamela 1785), no. 54, 1/74. Only the first sentence is printed; the ḥadīth continues “Shall I not guide you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among you.” Vowels as in the print; the line is split at the comma for reading.

lines.ar: لَا تَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا،
lines.en: “You will not enter the Garden until you believe,

lines.ar: وَلَا تُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى تَحَابُّوا.
lines.en: and you will not believe until you love one another.”

passages.ar: لَا تَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى تُؤْمِنُوا، وَلَا تُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى تَحَابُّوا.
passages.en: “You will not enter the Garden until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another.”

passages.intro_en: A short story. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (Lesson 46)

lines.ar: فِي صَبَاحِ يَوْمٍ جَدِيدٍ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ وَعُمَرُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ.
lines.en: On the morning of a new day Ahmad and Umar went to the ribāṭ.

lines.ar: كَانَ الدَّرْسُ طَوِيلًا، وَكَانَتِ الْكُتُبُ كَثِيرَةً.
lines.en: The lesson was long, and the books were many.

lines.ar: تَعَاوَنَ الْوَلَدَانِ: حَمَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْكُتُبَ، وَفَتَحَ عُمَرُ الْبَابَ.
lines.en: The two boys cooperated: Ahmad carried the books, and Umar opened the door.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ الْحَبِيبُ الرِّبَاطَ، وَجَلَسَ الطُّلَّابُ.
lines.en: Then the Habib entered the ribāṭ, and the students sat.

lines.ar: تَكَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ، وَتَوَاضَعَ لَهُمْ.
lines.en: The Habib spoke with the students, and was humble with them.

lines.ar: سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ، فَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْهُ دَرْسًا جَيِّدًا.
lines.en: Ahmad asked the Habib, and learned a good lesson from him.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ الْوَلَدَانِ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، وَكَانَا سَعِيدَيْنِ.
lines.en: And the two boys returned to the house, and they were happy.

passages.ar: فِي صَبَاحِ يَوْمٍ جَدِيدٍ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ وَعُمَرُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ. كَانَ الدَّرْسُ طَوِيلًا، وَكَانَتِ الْكُتُبُ كَثِيرَةً. تَعَاوَنَ الْوَلَدَانِ: حَمَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْكُتُبَ، وَفَتَحَ عُمَرُ الْبَابَ. ثُمَّ دَخَلَ الْحَبِيبُ الرِّبَاطَ، وَجَلَسَ الطُّلَّابُ. تَكَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ، وَتَوَاضَعَ لَهُمْ. سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ، فَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْهُ دَرْسًا جَيِّدًا. وَرَجَعَ الْوَلَدَانِ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، وَكَانَا سَعِيدَيْنِ.
passages.en: On the morning of a new day Ahmad and Umar went to the ribāṭ. The lesson was long, and the books were many. The two boys cooperated: Ahmad carried the books, and Umar opened the door. Then the Habib entered the ribāṭ, and the students sat. The Habib spoke with the students, and was humble with them. Ahmad asked the Habib, and learned a good lesson from him. And the two boys returned to the house, and they were happy.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 79-80 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: تَعَاوَنَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
lines.en: The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.

lines.ar: تَوَاضَعَ الْوَلَدُ وَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْهُمْ.
lines.en: The boy was humble and learned from them.

passages.ar: تَعَاوَنَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ. تَوَاضَعَ الْوَلَدُ وَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْهُمْ.
passages.en: The students helped one another in the ribāṭ. The boy was humble and learned from them.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth, from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 54 (Abū Hurayra).

questions.q: Who is speaking? Look at the source line.
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟
questions.a: The Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: You will not enter the Garden until you believe.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And you will not believe until you love one another.

questions.q: Find the word that means “the Garden”.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي مَعْنَاهَا «the Garden».
questions.a: الْجَنَّةَ (line 1).

questions.q: What must a person do before entering the Garden?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ الْإِنْسَانُ قَبْلَ دُخُولِ الْجَنَّةِ؟
questions.a: Believe (تُؤْمِنُوا).

questions.q: What must happen before a person truly believes?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَكُونُ قَبْلَ الْإِيمَانِ؟
questions.a: They love one another (تَحَابُّوا).

questions.q: Which earlier verb is this a form of? Root?
questions.q_ar: مِنْ أَيِّ فِعْلٍ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ؟ مَا الْجَذْرُ؟
questions.a: آمَنَ (Lesson 40); root أ م ن.

questions.q: Is this Form V or Form VI? How can you tell?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ هَذَا الْفِعْلُ مِنَ الْبَابِ الْخَامِسِ أَوِ السَّادِسِ؟
questions.a: Form VI: تَـ at the front and a long ā after the first root letter.

questions.q: How many people are needed to love one another (Form VI)?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ شَخْصًا يَلْزَمُ؟
questions.a: At least two.

questions.q: Put in order, first to last: believe · enter the Garden · love one another.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبْ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ.
questions.a: Love one another, believe, enter the Garden.

questions.q: True or false? The text says people enter the Garden and then believe.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. First they believe, then they enter.

questions.q: The root of تَحَابُّوا has a doubled letter (ح ب ب). Where is it, and why do you see only one ب?
questions.q_ar: جَذْرُ تَحَابُّوا فِيهِ حَرْفٌ مُكَرَّرٌ. أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The root is ح ب ب: the two ب are joined into one letter with a shadda (بُّ).

questions.q: Who is spoken to, and what ending shows it?
questions.q_ar: لِمَنِ الْكَلَامُ؟ وَمَا النِّهَايَةُ الَّتِي تَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: “You” (plural): the ending -ūna.

questions.q: Who went to the ribāṭ, and when?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ ذَهَبَ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: Ahmad and Umar, in the morning of a new day.

questions.q: Was the lesson short? What else does line 2 say?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ كَانَ الدَّرْسُ قَصِيرًا؟
questions.a: No, it was long; and the books were many.

questions.q: Which Form is تَعَاوَنَ? What did each boy do?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ كُلُّ وَلَدٍ؟
questions.a: Form VI. Ahmad carried the books; Umar opened the door.

questions.q: Who entered the ribāṭ, and who sat?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ دَخَلَ؟ وَمَنْ جَلَسَ؟
questions.a: The Habib entered; the students sat.

questions.q: Translate. Who is “them”?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ. مَنْ «هُمْ»؟
questions.a: and was humble with them: the students.

questions.q: Why did Ahmad ask the Habib? What happened after?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا حَدَثَ بَعْدَ السُّؤَالِ؟
questions.a: To learn; he learned a good lesson from him.

questions.q: Is this Form V or VI? Does Ahmad teach, or learn?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ أَحْمَدُ يُعَلِّمُ أَمْ يَتَعَلَّمُ؟
questions.a: Form V; Ahmad learns.

questions.q: True or false? The two boys were sad when they returned.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. They were happy (سَعِيدَيْنِ).

questions.q: Find two verbs in the story that start with تَـ. Which is Form V and which is VI?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ فِعْلَيْنِ يَبْدَآنِ بِتَاءٍ. أَيُّهُمَا مِنَ الْبَابِ الْخَامِسِ؟
questions.a: تَكَلَّمَ (V) and تَعَاوَنَ (VI); also تَوَاضَعَ (VI) and تَعَلَّمَ (V).

questions.q: Who is كَانَا? Why the ending ـَا?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ «كَانَا»؟ لِمَاذَا النِّهَايَةُ ـَا؟
questions.a: The two boys: ـَا means “the two of them”.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The students helped one another in the ribāṭ. The boy was humble and learned from them.

questions.q: Which verb means doing it together, with one another (Form VI)?
questions.a: تَعَاوَنَ (also تَوَاضَعَ is Form VI)

questions.q: Which verb means “he learned” (Form V: the doubled middle letter, تَـ in front)?
questions.a: تَعَلَّمَ

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
questions.a: تَعَاوَنَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.

translate.en: Ahmad learned the lesson from the Habib.

translate.ar: عَلَّمَ الْمُعَلِّمُ الْوَلَدَ، وَتَذَكَّرَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
translate.en: The teacher taught the boy, and the boy remembered every word.
The students cooperate in the work of the ribāṭ.
The Habib was humble toward the guests, and honoured them.

translate.ar: لَمْ يَتَكَلَّمِ الطَّالِبُ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ حَزِينًا.
translate.en: The student did not speak because he was sad.

translate.ar: تَصَدَّقَ أَبِي بِمَالٍ، ثُمَّ تَكَلَّمَ مَعَ الْجَارِ.
translate.en: My father gave charity, then spoke with the neighbour.

translate.ar: كَانَ الْوَلَدَانِ يَتَذَكَّرَانِ الدَّرْسَ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ.
translate.en: The two boys were going over the lesson in the library.

translate.ar: دَخَلَ الْحَبِيبُ الْمَسْجِدَ، وَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ. تَعَاوَنَ الطُّلَّابُ، وَتَعَلَّمُوا مِنْهُ دَرْسًا جَدِيدًا. ثُمَّ تَصَدَّقُوا بِمَالٍ وَرَجَعُوا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
translate.en: The Habib entered the mosque and spoke with the students. The students cooperated, and learned a new lesson from him. Then they gave money in charity and returned to the house.
The students learned the lesson in the library.
The Habib taught the boy, and the boy remembered the lesson.
translate.ar: عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ، فَتَذَكَّرَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ.
alt: عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ وَتَذَكَّرَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ.

translate.en: The boy was humble before his teacher.
The men cooperate in the work of the mosque.
My father gave charity, and he spoke with the guests.
Fatima did not speak in the majlis.
The students and the teacher helped one another.
Ahmad remembered the Habib’s word in the night.
translate.ar: تَذَكَّرَ أَحْمَدُ كَلِمَةَ الْحَبِيبِ فِي اللَّيْلِ.

readings.title_en: Extra letters at the front: Forms VII, VIII and X
readings.title_ar: حُرُوفٌ زَائِدَةٌ فِي أَوَّلِ الْفِعْلِ: اِنْـ، ـتـ، اِسْتَـ
readings.question_en: What are the extra letters before the root of this verb?
readings.question_ar: مَا هَذِهِ الْحُرُوفُ الزَّائِدَةُ قَبْلَ جَذْرِ الْفِعْلِ؟

passages.intro_en: A line of the Rātib. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Rātib al-Ḥaddād, the istighfār dhikr (said three times)
passages.cite: Rātib al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, called Sabīl al-Saʿāda wa-l-Falāḥ fī Adhkār al-Masāʾ wa-l-Ṣabāḥ, in the Shamela copy ‘Awrād wa-Aḥzāb’ (SSD Master Library [184180], from the loose .bok file; printed edition not identified), part 2, p. 2/3; commented in ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad Bā Sawdān, Dhakhīrat al-Maʿād bi-Sharḥ Rātib al-Ḥaddād, Cairo, 1378 H / 1959, the dhikr on istighfār (the 20th dhikr), around pp. 161–162. Vowelled for learners.

lines.ar: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ رَبَّ الْبَرَايَا،
lines.en: I ask Allah, Lord of the creatures, for forgiveness;

lines.ar: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ مِنَ الْخَطَايَا
lines.en: I ask Allah for forgiveness from my sins.

passages.ar: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ رَبَّ الْبَرَايَا، أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ مِنَ الْخَطَايَا
passages.en: I ask Allah, Lord of the creatures, for forgiveness; I ask Allah for forgiveness from my sins.

passages.intro_en: A verse. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Qur’an, sūrat al-Fātiḥa 1:5 (text produced by program from quran.json)

lines.ar: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ
lines.en: You alone we worship,

lines.ar: وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ
lines.en: and You alone we ask for help.

passages.ar: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ
passages.en: You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.

passages.intro_en: A ḥadīth, the beginning of a longer one. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 591 (Thawbān): a clause of the ḥadīth
passages.cite: Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Dār al-Jīl + Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut, vowelled print (Shamela 1786), 2/94 (Dār al-Jīl no. 1362); ʿAbd al-Bāqī numbering: ed. Muḥammad Fuʾād ʿAbd al-Bāqī, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Beirut (Shamela 1785), no. 591, 1/414. The ḥadīth continues “O Allah, You are Peace ...”; only this first clause is printed here. Vowels as in the print.

lines.ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذَا انْصَرَفَ مِنْ صَلَاتِهِ اسْتَغْفَرَ ثَلَاثًا
lines.en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he turned away from his prayer, asked for forgiveness three times ...

passages.ar: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ إِذَا انْصَرَفَ مِنْ صَلَاتِهِ اسْتَغْفَرَ ثَلَاثًا
passages.en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he turned away from his prayer, asked for forgiveness three times ...

passages.intro_en: A short story. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (Lesson 47)

lines.ar: فِي الصَّبَاحِ اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: In the morning the students gathered in the mosque.

lines.ar: اِنْتَظَرُوا الْحَبِيبَ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
lines.en: They waited for the Habib in the circle.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ الْحَبِيبُ، فَاسْتَقْبَلَهُ الْوَلَدُ.
lines.en: Then the Habib entered, and the boy welcomed him.

lines.ar: اِسْتَمَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى كَلِمَةِ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: Ahmad listened to the Habib’s word.

lines.ar: وَاسْتَغْفَرَ الْحَبِيبُ وَالطُّلَّابُ.
lines.en: And the Habib and the students asked for forgiveness.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ اِنْصَرَفَ الطُّلَّابُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
lines.en: Then the students left for school.

lines.ar: وَانْطَلَقَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، لِأَنَّ أُمَّهُ كَانَتْ تَنْتَظِرُهُ.
lines.en: And Ahmad set off for home, because his mother was waiting for him.

passages.ar: فِي الصَّبَاحِ اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. اِنْتَظَرُوا الْحَبِيبَ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ. ثُمَّ دَخَلَ الْحَبِيبُ، فَاسْتَقْبَلَهُ الْوَلَدُ. اِسْتَمَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى كَلِمَةِ الْحَبِيبِ. وَاسْتَغْفَرَ الْحَبِيبُ وَالطُّلَّابُ. ثُمَّ اِنْصَرَفَ الطُّلَّابُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. وَانْطَلَقَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، لِأَنَّ أُمَّهُ كَانَتْ تَنْتَظِرُهُ.
passages.en: In the morning the students gathered in the mosque. They waited for the Habib in the circle. Then the Habib entered, and the boy welcomed him. Ahmad listened to the Habib’s word. And the Habib and the students asked for forgiveness. Then the students left for school. And Ahmad set off for home, because his mother was waiting for him.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 81-82 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.

lines.ar: اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.

passages.ar: اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ. اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
passages.en: The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque. The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A line of the Rātib of Imam al-Ḥaddād: the istighfār dhikr, said three times.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: I ask Allah, Lord of the creatures, for forgiveness.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: I ask Allah for forgiveness from my sins.

questions.q: Find the verb. Which Form is it?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْفِعْلَ. مِنْ أَيِّ بَابٍ هُوَ؟
questions.a: أَسْتَغْفِرُ: Form X.

questions.q: Who is the doer? Which letter tells you?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْفَاعِلُ؟ أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: “I”: the أَـ at the front.

questions.q: Which verb in the vocabulary is the past form of this verb?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ هُوَ الْمَاضِي مِنْ هَذَا الْفِعْلِ؟
questions.a: اِسْتَغْفَرَ (he asked forgiveness).

questions.q: Find the word that means “Lord”.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي مَعْنَاهَا «Lord».
questions.a: رَبَّ (line 1).

questions.q: Find the word that means “the sins”. In which line is it?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي مَعْنَاهَا «the sins».
questions.a: الْخَطَايَا (line 2).

questions.q: True or false? The text asks forgiveness from people.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. It asks Allah for forgiveness (اللهَ).

questions.q: What does مِنْ show here?
questions.q_ar: عَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ «مِنْ» هُنَا؟
questions.a: “From”: what the forgiveness is asked for.

questions.q: The root is غ ف ر. Which letters are extra, and what does each tell you?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الْحُرُوفِ زَائِدَةٌ؟ وَعَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ كُلٌّ مِنْهَا؟
questions.a: أَ = “I”; س ت = the Form X letters (asking for).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an: sūrat al-Fātiḥa, verse 5.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: You alone we worship.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And You alone we ask for help.

questions.q: Which verb in line 2 is Form X?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي مِنَ الْبَابِ الْعَاشِرِ؟
questions.a: نَسْتَعِينُ.

questions.q: Who is speaking? Which letter at the front shows it?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟ أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: “We”: the نَـ.

questions.q: Is this a longer Form, or a plain verb? Which earlier verb is it from?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ هُوَ فِعْلٌ مَزِيدٌ أَمْ بَسِيطٌ؟ مِنْ أَيِّ فِعْلٍ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A plain verb, from عَبَدَ (he worshipped).

questions.q: True or false? The verse says we ask help from anyone.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. We ask help from Him alone.

questions.q: The root is ع و ن. Which verb of Lesson 46 has the same root?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي الدَّرْسِ ٤٦ لَهُ الْجَذْرُ نَفْسُهُ؟
questions.a: تَعَاوَنَ (he cooperated).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth, from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 591 (Thawbān).

questions.q: Who is the text about?
questions.q_ar: عَنْ مَنْ هَذَا النَّصُّ؟
questions.a: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

questions.q: When did he ask for forgiveness?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى اِسْتَغْفَرَ؟
questions.a: When he turned away from (finished) his prayer.

questions.q: What did he do after he turned away from the prayer?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ بَعْدَ اِنْصِرَافِهِ؟
questions.a: He asked for forgiveness (اسْتَغْفَرَ).

questions.q: How many times did he ask for forgiveness?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً اِسْتَغْفَرَ؟
questions.a: Three times (ثَلَاثًا).

questions.q: Which Form is this verb, and what is its present with “I”?
questions.q_ar: مِنْ أَيِّ بَابٍ هُوَ؟ وَمَا مُضَارِعُهُ مَعَ «أَنَا»؟
questions.a: Form X; أَسْتَغْفِرُ.

questions.q: Form VII: which two letters are at the front? Did somebody turn him away, or did he turn away of himself?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفَيْنِ فِي أَوَّلِهِ؟ هَلْ صَرَفَهُ أَحَدٌ أَمِ اِنْصَرَفَ بِنَفْسِهِ؟
questions.a: ا ن. Nobody turned him: Form VII says the action happens by itself; he turned away (from the prayer).

questions.q: Who gathered, and where?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ اِجْتَمَعَ؟ وَأَيْنَ؟
questions.a: The students, in the mosque.

questions.q: Who did they wait for? Where?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ اِنْتَظَرُوا؟ وَأَيْنَ؟
questions.a: The Habib, in the circle.

questions.q: Translate. Who is ـهُ?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ. مَنْ «هُوَ»؟
questions.a: and the boy welcomed him: the Habib.

questions.q: Who listened to the Habib’s word?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ اِسْتَمَعَ؟
questions.a: Ahmad.

questions.q: Who asked for forgiveness?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ اِسْتَغْفَرَ؟
questions.a: The Habib and the students.

questions.q: Where did the students go after that?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ الطُّلَّابُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: To school.

questions.q: Why did Ahmad set off for home?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا اِنْطَلَقَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ؟
questions.a: Because his mother was waiting for him.

questions.q: True or false? The Habib did not enter the circle.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. He entered, and the boy welcomed him.

questions.q: Find three verbs of Form VIII or Form X in the story.
questions.q_ar: جِدْ ثَلَاثَةَ أَفْعَالٍ مِنَ الْبَابِ الثَّامِنِ أَوِ الْعَاشِرِ.
questions.a: اِجْتَمَعَ، اِنْتَظَرُوا، اِسْتَمَعَ (VIII); اِسْتَقْبَلَ، اِسْتَغْفَرَ (X).

questions.q: What is the Form of تَنْتَظِرُ? Why is كَانَتْ feminine?
questions.q_ar: مَا بَابُ «تَنْتَظِرُ»؟ لِمَاذَا جَاءَ «كَانَتْ» بِالتَّاءِ؟
questions.a: Form VIII (present). Because it is about his mother (أُمّ).

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque. The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.

questions.q: Which verbs have اِ in front and a ـتـ after the first letter (Form VIII)?
questions.a: اِنْتَظَرَ (root ن ظ ر) and اِجْتَمَعَ (root ج م ع)

questions.q: Which verb starts with three extra letters (Form X)? What is its root?
questions.a: اِسْتَمَعَ (root س م ع)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy listened to the Habib.
questions.a: اِسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.

translate.ar: فِي الصَّبَاحِ اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
translate.en: In the morning the students gathered in the ribāṭ.
The boy waited for the Habib in front of the door.
The guests listen to the teacher’s word.

translate.ar: اِنْكَسَرَ قَلَمُ الْوَلَدِ، فَطَلَبَ قَلَمًا جَدِيدًا.
translate.en: The boy’s pen broke, so he asked for a new pen.

translate.ar: اِسْتَغْفَرَ الرَّجُلُ فِي اللَّيْلِ، ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: The man asked for forgiveness at night, then went to the mosque.

translate.ar: اِنْصَرَفَ الضُّيُوفُ مِنَ الرِّبَاطِ، وَاسْتَقْبَلَ الْوَلَدُ ضَيْفًا جَدِيدًا.
translate.en: The guests left the ribāṭ, and the boy welcomed a new guest.

translate.ar: لَمْ يَنْطَلِقِ الطُّلَّابُ لِأَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ كَانَ جَالِسًا.
translate.en: The students did not set off, because the teacher was sitting.

translate.ar: كَانَ أَبِي يَجْلِسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ وَيَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
translate.en: My father used to sit in the circle and listen to the Habib.

translate.ar: اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَانْتَظَرُوا الْحَبِيبَ. ثُمَّ دَخَلَ الْحَبِيبُ، فَاسْتَقْبَلَهُ الْوَلَدُ. وَاسْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ إِلَى كَلِمَتِهِ، ثُمَّ اِسْتَغْفَرُوا.
translate.en: The students gathered in the mosque and waited for the Habib. Then the Habib entered, and the boy welcomed him. The students listened to his word, and then asked for forgiveness.
The students gathered in the mosque in the morning.
translate.ar: اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
alt: فِي الصَّبَاحِ اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.

translate.en: Ahmad waited for the Habib.
The boy listened to the teacher.
I ask Allah for forgiveness.
The pen broke.
The guests left, and the boy set off for the house.
translate.ar: اِنْصَرَفَ الضُّيُوفُ، وَانْطَلَقَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
alt: اِنْصَرَفَ الضُّيُوفُ وَانْطَلَقَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.

translate.en: The students did not wait for the teacher.
The boy welcomed the guests in the house.

readings.title_en: A letter that doubles, a hamza that hides
readings.question_en: This verb has a shadda, and that one has lost its hamza. Where did the letters go?
readings.question_ar: أَيْنَ ذَهَبَتِ الْحُرُوفُ؟ هَذَا الْفِعْلُ فِيهِ شَدَّةٌ، وَذَاكَ سَقَطَتْ هَمْزَتُهُ.

passages.intro_en: Read the verses aloud, then answer. The two ★ rows are for adults.
passages.cite: Qur’an, sūrat al-ʿAlaq (96), verses 1–3; text extracted by program from the Madīna muṣḥaf data (quran.json) with quran_util.Q

lines.ar: اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ
lines.en: Read in the name of your Lord who created,

lines.ar: خَلَقَ الْإِنسَٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ
lines.en: created the human being from a clinging clot.

lines.ar: اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ
lines.en: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.

passages.ar: اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ خَلَقَ الْإِنسَٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ
passages.en: Read in the name of your Lord who created, created the human being from a clinging clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.

passages.intro_en: Read the story, then answer. The two ★ rows are for adults.
passages.cite: Course text, written for Lesson 48 (the boy’s father returns from the pilgrimage)

lines.ar: حَجَّ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ هَذِهِ السَّنَةَ.
lines.en: Ahmad’s father made the pilgrimage to Mecca this year.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ الْحَاجُّ إِلَى تَرِيمَ فِي آخِرِ الشَّهْرِ.
lines.en: The pilgrim returned to Tarim at the end of the month.

lines.ar: كَانَ فِي الْبَيْتِ ضُيُوفٌ كَثِيرُونَ، وَكَانَ أَحْمَدُ سَعِيدًا.
lines.en: There were many guests in the house, and Ahmad was happy.

lines.ar: مَدَّ أَحْمَدُ يَدَهُ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى أَبِيهِ.
lines.en: Ahmad stretched out his hand and greeted his father.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الْأَبُ لِأَحْمَدَ: كُلِ التَّمْرَ وَاشْرَبِ الْقَهْوَةَ.
lines.en: And the father said to Ahmad: Eat the dates and drink the coffee.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ الْأَبُ هَدِيَّةً وَقَالَ: خُذْ هَذِهِ الْهَدِيَّةَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ.
lines.en: Then the father took a gift and said: Take this gift to your mother.

lines.ar: ظَنَّ أَحْمَدُ أَنَّ الْحَجَّ سَهْلٌ، فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُوهُ: لَا، الْحَجُّ صَعْبٌ.
lines.en: Ahmad thought the pilgrimage was easy, but his father said to him: No, the pilgrimage is difficult.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الْأَبُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، رَدَّنِي اللَّهُ إِلَى بَيْتِي وَأَهْلِي.
lines.en: And the father said: Praise be to God. God returned me to my house and my family.

passages.ar: حَجَّ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ هَذِهِ السَّنَةَ. وَرَجَعَ الْحَاجُّ إِلَى تَرِيمَ فِي آخِرِ الشَّهْرِ. كَانَ فِي الْبَيْتِ ضُيُوفٌ كَثِيرُونَ، وَكَانَ أَحْمَدُ سَعِيدًا. مَدَّ أَحْمَدُ يَدَهُ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى أَبِيهِ. وَقَالَ الْأَبُ لِأَحْمَدَ: كُلِ التَّمْرَ وَاشْرَبِ الْقَهْوَةَ. ثُمَّ أَخَذَ الْأَبُ هَدِيَّةً وَقَالَ: خُذْ هَذِهِ الْهَدِيَّةَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ. ظَنَّ أَحْمَدُ أَنَّ الْحَجَّ سَهْلٌ، فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُوهُ: لَا، الْحَجُّ صَعْبٌ. وَقَالَ الْأَبُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، رَدَّنِي اللَّهُ إِلَى بَيْتِي وَأَهْلِي.
passages.en: Ahmad’s father made the pilgrimage to Mecca this year. The pilgrim returned to Tarim at the end of the month. There were many guests in the house, and Ahmad was happy. Ahmad stretched out his hand and greeted his father. And the father said to Ahmad: Eat the dates and drink the coffee. Then the father took a gift and said: Take this gift to your mother. Ahmad thought the pilgrimage was easy, but his father said to him: No, the pilgrimage is difficult. And the father said: Praise be to God. God returned me to my house and my family.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 83-84 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
lines.en: The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.

lines.ar: أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
lines.en: The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.

passages.ar: حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ. أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
passages.en: The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca. The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.

questions.q: Translate verse 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ ١.
questions.a: Read in the name of your Lord who created.

questions.q: Translate verse 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ ٢.
questions.a: He created the human being from a clinging clot.

questions.q: Translate verse 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ ٣.
questions.a: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.

questions.q: What kind of word is it, and what does it tell you to do?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ الْكَلِمَةِ؟ وَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُ؟
questions.a: A verb in the command form (from قَرَأَ): read!

questions.q: Root?
questions.a: خ ل ق

questions.q: Which word in verse 1 means “who”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي الْآيَةِ ١ مَعْنَاهَا «who»؟
questions.a: الَّذِي

questions.q: Whom did He create, and from what? (verse 2)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ خَلَقَ رَبُّكَ؟ وَمِمَّ خَلَقَهُ؟
questions.a: The human being (الْإِنْسَانَ), from a clinging clot (عَلَقٍ).

questions.q: True or false: the verb اِقْرَأْ is in verse 1 and in verse 3.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: «اِقْرَأْ» فِي الْآيَةِ ١ وَفِي الْآيَةِ ٣؟
questions.a: True.

questions.q: Which word in verse 3 comes from the same root as أَكْرَمَ (he honoured)?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي الْآيَةِ ٣ مِنْ جَذْرِ «أَكْرَمَ»؟
questions.a: الْأَكْرَمُ (root ك ر م).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an: Sūrat al-ʿAlaq (96), verses 1–3.

questions.q: Which verb of Lesson 1 has the same root as اِقْرَأْ? Does the command lose its hamza like خُذْ?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي الدَّرْسِ ١ مِنْ جَذْرِ «اِقْرَأْ»؟ هَلْ تَسْقُطُ هَمْزَتُهُ كَمَا فِي «خُذْ»؟
questions.a: قَرَأَ (he read). No: the hamza is the last letter of the root and it stays.

questions.q: Who made the pilgrimage, and where did he go?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ حَجَّ؟ وَإِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ؟
questions.a: Ahmad’s father; to Mecca.

questions.q: When did the pilgrim return to Tarim?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى رَجَعَ الْحَاجُّ إِلَى تَرِيمَ؟
questions.a: At the end of the month.

questions.q: Root?
questions.a: ح ج ج

questions.q: Who was in the house?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ كَانَ فِي الْبَيْتِ؟
questions.a: Many guests.

questions.q: What did Ahmad do when he met his father? Which verb means “stretched”?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟ أَيُّ فِعْلٍ مَعْنَاهُ «stretched»؟
questions.a: He stretched out his hand and greeted his father. مَدَّ (root م د د).

questions.q: What did the father tell Ahmad to eat and to drink?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا أَمَرَ الْأَبُ أَحْمَدَ؟ مَاذَا يَأْكُلُ وَمَاذَا يَشْرَبُ؟
questions.a: Dates and coffee.

questions.q: Which verb is this the command of, and what is its root?
questions.q_ar: أَمْرُ أَيِّ فِعْلٍ هَذَا؟ مَا جَذْرُهُ؟
questions.a: أَكَلَ; root أ ك ل.

questions.q: Who is the gift for?
questions.q_ar: لِمَنِ الْهَدِيَّةُ؟
questions.a: For Ahmad’s mother.

questions.q: True or false: Ahmad thought the pilgrimage was difficult.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: ظَنَّ أَحْمَدُ أَنَّ الْحَجَّ صَعْبٌ؟
questions.a: False. He thought it was easy; his father said it is difficult.

questions.q: In the last line, which verb means “returned (me)”? Find its root and say who the doer is.
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَخِيرِ أَيُّ فِعْلٍ مَعْنَاهُ «returned me»؟ مَا جَذْرُهُ؟ مَنِ الْفَاعِلُ؟
questions.a: رَدَّنِي: root ر د د; the doer is Allah (اللَّهُ) and ـنِي = me.

questions.q: What does the father say in the last line? Who does he thank?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْأَبُ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَخِيرِ؟ مَنْ شَكَرَ الْأَبُ؟
questions.a: He says الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ (praise be to God): he thanks Allah.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca. The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.

questions.q: Which verb in the first new line is a doubled verb? Give its root.
questions.a: حَجَّ (root ح ج ج)

questions.q: Which verb in the second new line starts with a hamza that is a root letter? Give its root.
questions.a: أَخَذَ (root أ خ ذ)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy’s father made the pilgrimage.
questions.a: حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ.

translate.en: I returned the book to the library yesterday.
The teacher stretched out his hand and took the pen.

translate.ar: ظَنَنْتُ أَنَّ الدَّرْسَ سَهْلٌ ثُمَّ فَهِمْتُ أَنَّهُ صَعْبٌ.
translate.en: I thought the lesson was easy, then I understood that it was difficult.
The teacher told the boy to read, and he read the lesson.
Take this pen and write your name.

translate.ar: شَدَّ الْأَبُ يَدَ الْوَلَدِ وَدَخَلَ الْمَسْجِدَ.
translate.en: The father held the boy’s hand firmly and entered the mosque.

translate.ar: يَحُجُّ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ.
translate.en: Many people make the pilgrimage every year.
The teacher gave the pen back to the girl.

translate.ar: هَلْ أَخَذْتَ كِتَابِي؟ لَا، الْوَلَدُ لَمْ يَأْخُذْ كِتَابَكَ.
translate.en: Did you take my book? No, the boy did not take your book.

translate.ar: سَأَلَ الْأَبُ أَحْمَدَ: أَيْنَ الْكِتَابُ؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: رَدَدْتُهُ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ. قَالَ الْأَبُ: جَيِّدٌ، خُذْ كِتَابًا جَدِيدًا وَاِقْرَأْ.
translate.en: The father asked Ahmad: Where is the book? Ahmad said: I returned it to the library. The father said: Good, take a new book and read.
I returned the book to the teacher yesterday.
Ahmad’s father made the pilgrimage this year.
Take the pen and write your name.
Eat the dates and drink the milk.
The father told the boy to read, and the boy read the lesson.
translate.ar: أَمَرَ الْأَبُ الْوَلَدَ فَقَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ.

translate.en: I thought the question was easy.
The teacher stretched out his hand and took the book.
Maryam gripped her mother’s hand.

readings.question_en: Where does the chain end, and where do the words begin?
readings.question_ar: أَيْنَ يَنْتَهِي السَّنَدُ، وَأَيْنَ يَبْدَأُ الْمَتْنُ؟

passages.intro_en: Read the ḥadīth with its chain aloud, then answer. The two ★ rows are for adults.

lines.ar: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ بْنِ قَعْنَبٍ
lines.en: ʿAbd Allāh b. Maslama b. Qaʿnab told us:

lines.ar: حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكٌ
lines.en: Mālik told us,

lines.ar: عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ
lines.en: from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, from Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm,

lines.ar: عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ وَقَّاصٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ قَالَ:
lines.en: from ʿAlqama b. Waqqāṣ, from ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, who said:

lines.ar: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّةِ وَإِنَّمَا لِامْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
lines.en: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Deeds are by intention, and each person has only what he intended.”

passages.ar: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ بْنِ قَعْنَبٍ حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكٌ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ وَقَّاصٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّةِ وَإِنَّمَا لِامْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى
passages.en: ʿAbd Allāh b. Maslama b. Qaʿnab told us: Mālik told us, from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, from Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama b. Waqqāṣ, from ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Deeds are by intention, and each person has only what he intended.”

passages.intro_en: Read the story, then answer. The two ★ rows are for adults.
passages.cite: Course text, written for Lesson 49 (the boy hears his first ḥadīth with a chain)

lines.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ.
lines.en: Ahmad sat in the majlis with the students.

lines.ar: وَقَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ حَدِيثًا مِنْ كِتَابٍ كَبِيرٍ.
lines.en: And the Habib read a ḥadīth from a big book.

lines.ar: سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً: حَدَّثَنَا، أَخْبَرَنَا، عَنْ، عَنْ.
lines.en: Ahmad heard many words: “told us”, “informed us”, “from”, “from”.

lines.ar: سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: مَاذَا فِي هَذَا السَّنَدِ؟
lines.en: Ahmad asked: What is in this chain?

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: فِيهِ اسْمُ كُلِّ رَجُلٍ سَمِعَ الْحَدِيثَ.
lines.en: The Habib said: In it is the name of every man who heard the ḥadīth.

lines.ar: السَّنَدُ مِنَ الْمُعَلِّمِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ.
lines.en: The chain goes from the teacher to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

lines.ar: فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: هَذَا سَنَدٌ، وَهَذَا مَتْنٌ.
lines.en: So Ahmad wrote in his book: This is a chain, and this is a matn.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ الْحَدِيثَ لِأُمِّهِ.
lines.en: Then he went home and read the ḥadīth to his mother.

passages.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ. وَقَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ حَدِيثًا مِنْ كِتَابٍ كَبِيرٍ. سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً: حَدَّثَنَا، أَخْبَرَنَا، عَنْ، عَنْ. سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: مَاذَا فِي هَذَا السَّنَدِ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: فِيهِ اسْمُ كُلِّ رَجُلٍ سَمِعَ الْحَدِيثَ. السَّنَدُ مِنَ الْمُعَلِّمِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ. فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: هَذَا سَنَدٌ، وَهَذَا مَتْنٌ. ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ الْحَدِيثَ لِأُمِّهِ.
passages.en: Ahmad sat in the majlis with the students. And the Habib read a ḥadīth from a big book. Ahmad heard many words: “told us”, “informed us”, “from”, “from”. Ahmad asked: What is in this chain? The Habib said: In it is the name of every man who heard the ḥadīth. The chain goes from the teacher to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So Ahmad wrote in his book: This is a chain, and this is a matn. Then he went home and read the ḥadīth to his mother.

passages.intro_en: A second ḥadīth opens with a one-name chain. Read, then answer.
