The Muslim print reads «بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ» (no «جُلُوسٌ»); the Arbaʿīn has «جُلُوسٌ». This text follows the Arbaʿīn and cites Muslim for the rest of the sentence.

lines.ar: عَنْ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا قَالَ:
lines.en: From ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, also, who said:

lines.ar: بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ جُلُوسٌ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ
lines.en: “While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day,

passages.ar: عَنْ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا قَالَ: بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ جُلُوسٌ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ
passages.en: From ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, also, who said: “While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day,

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 85-86 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ حَدِيثًا بِسَنَدِهِ.
lines.en: The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.

lines.ar: قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
lines.en: The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.

passages.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ حَدِيثًا بِسَنَدِهِ. قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
passages.en: The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain. The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.

questions.q: Translate the last line (the words of the Prophet ﷺ).
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَخِيرَ.
questions.a: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Deeds are only by intention, and each person has only what he intended.”

questions.q: How many times does حَدَّثَنَا appear? Who is “us”?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً جَاءَتْ «حَدَّثَنَا»؟ مَنْ «نَا»؟
questions.a: Twice (lines 1 and 2). “Us” is the narrator and the others who heard it with him.

questions.q: Which word joins one name to the next in lines 3 and 4?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَرْبِطُ اسْمًا بِاسْمٍ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ٣ وَ٤؟
questions.a: عَنْ (“from”).

questions.q: Root?
questions.a: ح د ث

questions.q: Who is the last name in the chain, and what is he called?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ آخِرُ اسْمٍ فِي السَّنَدِ؟ وَمَاذَا يُسَمَّى؟
questions.a: ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb: a Companion (from الصَّحَابَة).

questions.q: The word قَالَ appears twice. Who says it the first time (end of line 4), and who the second time (line 5)?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقُولُ «قَالَ» الْأُولَى؟ وَمَنْ يَقُولُ الثَّانِيَةَ؟
questions.a: The first: ʿUmar speaks (عُمَرَ). The second: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (رَسُولُ اللَّهِ) speaks.

questions.q: Where is the chain, and where is the matn?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ السَّنَدُ؟ وَأَيْنَ الْمَتْنُ؟
questions.a: The chain: lines 1–4 and the start of line 5 (قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ). The matn: إِنَّمَا … نَوَى.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.a: Deeds are only by intention.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.a: And each person has only what he intended.

questions.q: Root?
questions.a: ن و ي

questions.q: Translate.
questions.a: from ʿAlqama, son of Waqqāṣ

questions.q: What does this word mean in a name?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَعْنِي هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ فِي الِاسْمِ؟
questions.a: “son of”: ʿAbd Allāh, son of Maslama.

questions.q: Which narrator is named in line 2 with no “son of”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ رَاوٍ ذُكِرَ فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ بِلَا «بْنِ»؟
questions.a: Mālik (مَالِكٌ).

questions.q: How many narrators are named in the whole chain?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ رَاوِيًا فِي السَّنَدِ كُلِّهِ؟
questions.a: Six: ʿAbd Allāh, Mālik, Yaḥyā, Muḥammad, ʿAlqama and ʿUmar.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth with its chain, in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (no. 1907). The same ḥadīth opens al-Arbaʿīn al-Nawawiyya (no. 1).

questions.q: The Arbaʿīn has بِالنِّيَّاتِ and لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ, but this Muslim text has بِالنِّيَّةِ and لِامْرِئٍ. What does that teach you about quoting a ḥadīth?
questions.q_ar: فِي الْأَرْبَعِينَ «بِالنِّيَّاتِ» وَ«لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ»، وَفِي مُسْلِمٍ «بِالنِّيَّةِ» وَ«لِامْرِئٍ». مَاذَا تَتَعَلَّمُ؟
questions.a: Books can give the same ḥadīth with small differences of wording. Always say which book you are quoting from.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the majlis, with the students.

questions.q: What did the Habib read, and from what?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth, from a big book.

questions.q: Meaning?
questions.a: he told us

questions.q: Which link word did Ahmad hear twice (line 3)?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ سَمِعَهَا أَحْمَدُ مَرَّتَيْنِ؟
questions.a: عَنْ (“from”).

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: What is in this chain?

questions.q: What is in a chain, according to the Habib?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فِي السَّنَدِ؟
questions.a: The name of every man who heard the ḥadīth.

questions.q: From whom to whom does the chain go?
questions.q_ar: مِمَّنْ إِلَى مَنْ يَذْهَبُ السَّنَدُ؟
questions.a: From the teacher to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

questions.q: What two things did Ahmad write in his book?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ؟
questions.a: This is a chain, and this is a matn.

questions.q: True or false: Ahmad kept the ḥadīth to himself.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: بَقِيَ الْحَدِيثُ عِنْدَ أَحْمَدَ وَحْدَهُ؟
questions.a: False. He read it to his mother.

questions.q: In line 3 the same word, عَنْ, appears twice. What does that tell you about the chain?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٣ كَلِمَةُ «عَنْ» مَرَّتَانِ. مَاذَا يَدُلُّ ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: The chain has more than one link: each عَنْ joins one narrator to the next.

questions.q: Why must the chain go all the way to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? What if it stopped at the teacher?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَصِلُ السَّنَدُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ؟ مَاذَا لَوْ وَقَفَ عِنْدَ الْمُعَلِّمِ؟
questions.a: The ḥadīth is the words of the Prophet ﷺ, so the chain must connect us to him. A chain that stops earlier does not reach the one who spoke.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ ١.
questions.a: From ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, also, who said:

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ ٢.
questions.a: While we were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day,

questions.q: How many names are in the chain of line 1? Who is he?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ اسْمًا فِي سَنَدِ السَّطْرِ ١؟ مَنْ هُوَ؟
questions.a: One: ʿUmar, a Companion.

questions.q: Which word in line 1 ends the chain?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ١ يَنْتَهِي بِهَا السَّنَدُ؟
questions.a: قَالَ

questions.q: Meaning?
questions.a: at, with (beside)

questions.q: Who is the “we” in line 2?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ «نَحْنُ» فِي السَّطْرِ ٢؟
questions.a: The Companions, sitting with the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain. The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.

questions.q: Which two words belong to the chain (the sanad)?
questions.a: حَدَّثَنَا and أَخْبَرَنَا (they introduce the narrators)

questions.q: Where do the words of the Prophet ﷺ (the matn) begin?
questions.a: After قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: they begin with إِنَّمَا.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
questions.a: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ حَدِيثًا بِسَنَدِهِ.

translate.ar: حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: رَجَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
translate.en: Ahmad told us, from his father, who said: The boy returned to the house.

translate.ar: أَخْبَرَنَا سَالِمٌ أَنَّ الْأَبَ رَجَعَ مِنَ الْحَجِّ.
translate.en: Salim informed us that the father returned from the pilgrimage.
This book is only for Ahmad.
Every student has a good intention.

translate.ar: كَانَتِ الْهِجْرَةُ مِنْ مَكَّةَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ.
translate.en: The emigration was from Mecca to the city (Medina).

translate.ar: سَمِعَ الطُّلَّابُ حَدِيثًا مِنَ الْمُعَلِّمِ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
translate.en: The students heard a ḥadīth from the teacher in the majlis.
The Habib tells the students every night.

translate.ar: هَذَا السَّنَدُ طَوِيلٌ وَهَذَا الْمَتْنُ قَصِيرٌ.
translate.en: This chain is long and this matn is short.

translate.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ حَدِيثًا فِي الْمَجْلِسِ. قَالَ لَهُ الْمُعَلِّمُ: هَلْ كَتَبْتَ السَّنَدَ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ، وَكَتَبْتُ الْمَتْنَ.
translate.en: The boy heard a ḥadīth in the majlis. The teacher said to him: Did you write the chain? He said: Yes, and I wrote the matn.
Ahmad told us from his father.
Umar informed us, from Salim, who said: The boy went to the mosque.
translate.ar: أَخْبَرَنَا عُمَرُ عَنْ سَالِمٍ قَالَ: ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.

translate.en: The students heard a ḥadīth in the majlis.
Every human being has an intention.
The boy wrote the chain, then he wrote the matn.
translate.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ السَّنَدَ ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْمَتْنَ.

translate.en: My father made the pilgrimage and returned to Tarim.
This book is only for the students.
Salim returned the book to the library.

Muḥammad Fuʾād ʿAbd al-Bāqī, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Beirut (Shamela 1785), no. 38, 1/65. Text copied from the print (checked with ./sh verify: EXACT). The Muslim print reads فَاسْتَقِمْ; the wording ثُمَّ اسْتَقِمْ is that of al-Arbaʿīn al-Nawawiyya no. 21 (Shamela copy [26390], p. 74, “narrated by Muslim”). Only the lam-alif mark is the print’s own.

lines.ar: قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قُلْ لِي فِي الْإِسْلَامِ قَوْلًا لَا أَسْأَلُ عَنْهُ أَحَدًا بَعْدَكَ.
lines.en: I said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, tell me something about Islam that I shall not ask anyone about after you.”

lines.ar: قَالَ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
lines.en: He said: “Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.”

passages.ar: قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قُلْ لِي فِي الْإِسْلَامِ قَوْلًا لَا أَسْأَلُ عَنْهُ أَحَدًا بَعْدَكَ. قَالَ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
passages.en: I said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, tell me something about Islam that I shall not ask anyone about after you.” He said: “Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.”

passages.intro_en: Read the story aloud. Then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (written for Lesson 50 in the register of the story strip; no source).

lines.ar: زَارَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
lines.en: Ahmad visited the Habib in the ribāṭ in the evening.

lines.ar: قَامَ أَحْمَدُ لِلْحَبِيبِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ.
lines.en: Ahmad stood for the Habib and greeted him.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: هَلْ صُمْتَ الْيَوْمَ؟
lines.en: The Habib said: Did you fast today?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، صُمْتُ الْيَوْمَ وَقَرَأْتُ فِي الْمُصْحَفِ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: Yes, I fasted today and read in the muṣḥaf.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: كُنْ كَرِيمًا مَعَ الضُّيُوفِ وَقُمْ لَهُمْ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Be generous with the guests and stand for them.

lines.ar: وَجَاءَ عُمَرُ وَقَالَ: خِفْتُ أَمْسِ لِأَنَّ اللَّيْلَ كَانَ طَوِيلًا.
lines.en: And Umar came and said: I was afraid yesterday, because the night was long.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: يَقُولُ النَّاسُ: الطَّالِبُ يَخْدُمُ ثُمَّ يَتَعَلَّمُ.
lines.en: The Habib said: People say: The student serves, and then learns.

passages.ar: زَارَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ. قَامَ أَحْمَدُ لِلْحَبِيبِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: هَلْ صُمْتَ الْيَوْمَ؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، صُمْتُ الْيَوْمَ وَقَرَأْتُ فِي الْمُصْحَفِ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: كُنْ كَرِيمًا مَعَ الضُّيُوفِ وَقُمْ لَهُمْ. وَجَاءَ عُمَرُ وَقَالَ: خِفْتُ أَمْسِ لِأَنَّ اللَّيْلَ كَانَ طَوِيلًا. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: يَقُولُ النَّاسُ: الطَّالِبُ يَخْدُمُ ثُمَّ يَتَعَلَّمُ.
passages.en: Ahmad visited the Habib in the ribāṭ in the evening. Ahmad stood for the Habib and greeted him. The Habib said: Did you fast today? Ahmad said: Yes, I fasted today and read in the muṣḥaf. The Habib said: Be generous with the guests and stand for them. And Umar came and said: I was afraid yesterday, because the night was long. The Habib said: People say: The student serves, and then learns.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 87-88 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
lines.en: The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.

lines.ar: قَامَ الْوَلَدُ وَقَالَ: آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ.
lines.en: The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.

passages.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ. قَامَ الْوَلَدُ وَقَالَ: آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ.
passages.en: The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright. The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: I said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, tell me something about Islam that I shall not ask anyone about after you.”

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: He said: “Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.”

questions.q: Who is speaking in line 1, and whom is he speaking to?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: A Companion (Sufyān) speaks to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

questions.q: What does the man want? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُرِيدُ الرَّجُلُ؟
questions.a: A saying about Islam that is enough for him, so that he need not ask anyone after the Messenger ﷺ.

questions.q: Which letter is hidden in the middle of this verb? What is the root?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَخْتَفِي فِي وَسَطِ هَذَا الْفِعْلِ؟ مَا الْجَذْرُ؟
questions.a: The letter و. Root ق و ل (the present is يَقُولُ).

questions.q: Is قُلْ in line 1 said by the same person as قُلْ in line 2?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ قَائِلُ «قُلْ» فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ هُوَ قَائِلُهَا فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: No. In line 1 the man says it to the Prophet ﷺ: “tell me”. In line 2 the Prophet ﷺ says it to the man: “say”.

questions.q: Who is the doer of قَالَ in line 2?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ فَاعِلُ «قَالَ» فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

questions.q: What two things does the Prophet ﷺ tell him to do?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ أَنْ يَفْعَلَ؟
questions.a: To say “I believe in Allah” and then to be upright.

questions.q: What does the small فَـ at the front do? Is the verb a command?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ فَـ فِي أَوَّلِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟ هَلِ الْفِعْلُ أَمْرٌ؟
questions.a: It joins: “and (so)”. Yes, a command: be upright.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth, from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 38 (the Companion Sufyān b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Thaqafī).

questions.q: Why is the و of قُلْ not written? Which other form of the same verb shows it?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَا تَظْهَرُ الْوَاوُ فِي «قُلْ»؟ أَيُّ صِيغَةٍ تُظْهِرُهَا؟
questions.a: In the command the long middle letter drops out. The present يَقُولُ shows it: ق و ل.

questions.q: The same ḥadīth in al-Nawawī’s Arbaʿīn (no. 21) has ثُمَّ اسْتَقِمْ. What does ثُمَّ add?
questions.q_ar: فِي الْأَرْبَعِينَ «ثُمَّ اسْتَقِمْ». مَاذَا تَزِيدُ ثُمَّ؟
questions.a: “Then (later)”: believe first, and after that be upright.

questions.q: Who visited the Habib, and where?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ زَارَ الْحَبِيبَ؟ وَأَيْنَ؟
questions.a: Ahmad visited the Habib in the ribāṭ.

questions.q: Who stood up, and for whom? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ قَامَ؟ وَلِمَنْ؟
questions.a: Ahmad stood up for the Habib.

questions.q: What did the Habib ask Ahmad? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: Did you fast today?

questions.q: True or false? Ahmad did not fast today.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ مَا صَامَ أَحْمَدُ الْيَوْمَ.
questions.a: False: he said he fasted (صُمْتُ).

questions.q: What else did Ahmad do today, besides fasting? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ أَيْضًا؟
questions.a: He read in the muṣḥaf.

questions.q: What does the Habib tell Ahmad to do in line 5?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ أَنْ يَفْعَلَ فِي السَّطْرِ الْخَامِسِ؟
questions.a: To be generous with the guests and to stand for them.

questions.q: Find the verb that means “I was afraid”. What is its root?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْفِعْلَ الَّذِي مَعْنَاهُ «I was afraid». مَا جَذْرُهُ؟
questions.a: خِفْتُ (line 6). Root خ و ف.

questions.q: Why was Umar afraid?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا خَافَ عُمَرُ؟
questions.a: Because the night was long.

questions.q: Which two forms of the verb قَامَ are in the story?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ صِيغَتَيْنِ مِنَ الْفِعْلِ «قَامَ» فِي الْقِصَّةِ؟
questions.a: قَامَ (line 2) and قُمْ (line 5).

questions.q: Which two verbs in line 4 end in ـتُ (“I”)?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الرَّابِعِ آخِرُهُمَا ـتُ؟
questions.a: صُمْتُ and قَرَأْتُ.

questions.q: Who said the words in line 6, and who is the doer of وَقَالَ?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ قَالَ كَلَامَ السَّطْرِ السَّادِسِ؟
questions.a: Umar. He came and said it.

questions.q: The root of كُنْ is ك و ن. Which form of the same verb is in line 6, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: جَذْرُ «كُنْ» هُوَ ك و ن. أَيُّ صِيغَةٍ مِنْهُ فِي السَّطْرِ السَّادِسِ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: كَانَ: “it was”.

questions.q: Is يَخْدُمُ a hollow verb? Explain.
questions.q_ar: هَلْ «يَخْدُمُ» فِعْلٌ أَجْوَفُ؟ اِشْرَحْ.
questions.a: No. Its middle letter د is a strong letter and stays (root خ د م).

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright. The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.

questions.q: Which command in the first new line comes from the hollow verb قَالَ? Which letter is hidden in it?
questions.a: قُلْ; the hidden middle letter is و (root ق و ل)

questions.q: Which hollow verb in the second new line means “he stood”? Give its root.
questions.a: قَامَ (root ق و م)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
questions.a: قَامَ الْوَلَدُ وَقَالَ: آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ.

translate.en: The students stood and greeted the Habib.
I said to my father: I fasted today.
The Habib was generous with the guests.

translate.ar: يَبِيعُ أَبُو سَالِمٍ الْخُبْزَ فِي السُّوقِ.
translate.en: Salim’s father sells bread in the market.

translate.ar: خَافَ الْوَلَدُ أَمْسِ، وَالْيَوْمَ هُوَ سَعِيدٌ.
translate.en: The boy was afraid yesterday, and today he is happy.

translate.ar: زُرْتُ الْمُعَلِّمَ فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ ثُمَّ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
translate.en: I visited the teacher at the school, then I went to the house.

translate.ar: نَامَ الضَّيْفُ فِي الْغُرْفَةِ، وَقَامَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
translate.en: The guest slept in the room, and got up in the morning.

translate.ar: يَقُولُ الْمُعَلِّمُ: كُنْ كَرِيمًا وَقُلْ كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً.
translate.en: The teacher says: Be generous and say a good word.
What did you say to the Habib?

translate.ar: هَلْ صُمْتَ أَمْسِ؟ نَعَمْ، صُمْتُ وَنِمْتُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: Did you fast yesterday? Yes, I fasted and slept in the mosque.

translate.ar: قَامَ أَحْمَدُ مِنَ الْمَجْلِسِ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِعُمَرَ: كُنْتُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ أَمْسِ. وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: وَأَنَا زُرْتُ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
translate.en: Ahmad got up from the majlis, then said to Umar: I was in the mosque yesterday. And Umar said: And I visited the Habib in the ribāṭ.

translate.ar: بَاعَ الرَّجُلُ كِتَابَهُ، وَقَالَ: كَانَ الْكِتَابُ قَدِيمًا.
translate.en: The man sold his book, and said: The book was old.
My father fasts and stands (in prayer) at night.

translate.ar: قُمْ، يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ، وَاذْهَبْ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: “Get up,” says the Habib, “and go to the mosque.”
I said to the teacher (f): I was in the library.

translate.ar: زَارَ الرَّجُلُ الْحَبِيبَ وَقَامَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ.
translate.en: The man visited the Habib, and the Habib stood for him.

translate.ar: يَخَافُ الْوَلَدُ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَلَا يَنَامُ.
translate.en: The boy is afraid at night and does not sleep.
I fasted today and visited the mosque.
The student stood up and said: “Yes.”
I said to the teacher: “I understood the lesson.”
The man sells bread in the market.
Yesterday I visited the Habib in the ribāṭ.
Be generous and stand for the guest.
The boy was afraid because the night was long.
translate.ar: خَافَ الْوَلَدُ لِأَنَّ اللَّيْلَ كَانَ طَوِيلًا.

translate.en: My father fasted in this month.
I slept in the room, and he slept in the mosque.
translate.ar: نِمْتُ فِي الْغُرْفَةِ وَنَامَ هُوَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
alt: نِمْتُ فِي الْغُرْفَةِ وَنَامَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.

translate.en: What does the Habib say today?
The Habib stood and said: “Be generous.”
Yesterday I was afraid, and today I am happy.
I was a student, and now I am a teacher.

readings.title_en: A weak first or last letter
readings.question_en: Why does the first letter vanish in يَجِدُ and the last letter change in دَعَوْتُ?
readings.question_ar: لِمَاذَا يَسْقُطُ الْحَرْفُ الْأَوَّلُ فِي «يَجِدُ» وَيَتَغَيَّرُ الْحَرْفُ الْأَخِيرُ فِي «دَعَوْتُ»؟

passages.intro_en: Read the duʿāʾ aloud. Then answer.
passages.source: the Rātib of Imam ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād (the 14th and the 11th dhikrs)
passages.cite: Rātib al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, called Sabīl al-Saʿāda wa-l-Falāḥ fī Adhkār al-Masāʾ wa-l-Ṣabāḥ, in the Shamela copy 'Awrād wa-Aḥzāb' (SSD Master Library [184180]; printed edition not identified), part 2, p. 2/3 (line 1 of this text, the 14th dhikr) and p. 2/2 (line 2, the 11th dhikr); Dhakhīrat al-Maʿād: ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad Bā Sawdān al-Dawʿanī al-Ḥaḍramī, Dhakhīrat al-Maʿād bi-Sharḥ Rātib al-Ḥaddād, al-Ṭabʿa al-ūlā, Cairo, 1378 H / 1959 (TLNOOR 190, a lead only). Consonants checked EXACT against [184180]; the source is only partly vowelled: the rest is vowelled for learners. Line 2 is traced to Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1884 (see Lesson 44). These are the Imam’s own invocations: no ḥadīth is claimed for line 1.

lines.ar: يَا رَبَّنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، وَامْحُ الَّذِي كَانَ مِنَّا
lines.en: O our Lord, pardon us and wipe away what we have done;

lines.ar: رَضِينَا بِاللهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
lines.en: we are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad ﷺ as Prophet.

passages.ar: يَا رَبَّنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، وَامْحُ الَّذِي كَانَ مِنَّا رَضِينَا بِاللهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيًّا
passages.en: O our Lord, pardon us and wipe away what we have done; we are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad ﷺ as Prophet.

passages.intro_en: Read the verse aloud. Then answer.
passages.cite: Qur’an 1:6, copied by program from quran.json (quran_util.Q).

lines.ar: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَٰطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
lines.en: Guide us to the straight path.

passages.ar: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَٰطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
passages.en: Guide us to the straight path.

passages.intro_en: Read the words of the verse aloud. Then answer.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ
lines.en: And your Lord said: “Call on Me, and I will answer you.”

passages.ar: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ
passages.en: And your Lord said: “Call on Me, and I will answer you.”

passages.intro_en: Read the story aloud. Then answer.

lines.ar: مَشَى أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
lines.en: Ahmad walked with his father to the ziyāra.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَبُوهُ: لَا يَنْسَى الطَّالِبُ الْأَدَبَ.
lines.en: His father said: The student does not forget good manners.

lines.ar: وَوَصَلَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ بَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ.
lines.en: And Ahmad arrived at the ribāṭ after an hour.

lines.ar: وَجَدَ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُ.
lines.en: He found the Habib in the majlis and sat with him.

lines.ar: دَعَا الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ وَلِأَبِيهِ.
lines.en: The Habib made duʿāʾ for Ahmad and for his father.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنَا.
lines.en: And Ahmad said: O Allah, guide us.

lines.ar: رَضِيَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ.
lines.en: The Habib was pleased with Ahmad.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، وَكَانَ سَعِيدًا.
lines.en: And Ahmad returned to the house, and he was happy.

passages.ar: مَشَى أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ. قَالَ أَبُوهُ: لَا يَنْسَى الطَّالِبُ الْأَدَبَ. وَوَصَلَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ بَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ. وَجَدَ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُ. دَعَا الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ وَلِأَبِيهِ. وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنَا. رَضِيَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ. وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، وَكَانَ سَعِيدًا.
passages.en: Ahmad walked with his father to the ziyāra. His father said: The student does not forget good manners. And Ahmad arrived at the ribāṭ after an hour. He found the Habib in the majlis and sat with him. The Habib made duʿāʾ for Ahmad and for his father. And Ahmad said: O Allah, guide us. The Habib was pleased with Ahmad. And Ahmad returned to the house, and he was happy.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 89-90 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
lines.en: The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.

lines.ar: دَعَا الْوَلَدُ: اللَّهُمَّ اِهْدِنَا.
lines.en: The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.

passages.ar: مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ. دَعَا الْوَلَدُ: اللَّهُمَّ اِهْدِنَا.
passages.en: The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening. The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: O our Lord, pardon us and wipe away what we have done.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muḥammad ﷺ as Prophet.

questions.q: Whom is the speaker calling in line 1?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يُنَادِي الْقَائِلُ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟
questions.a: His Lord: “our Lord” (رَبَّنَا).

questions.q: Which two words in line 1 are commands? What do they ask for?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ أَمْرٌ؟ مَاذَا تَطْلُبَانِ؟
questions.a: وَاعْفُ and وَامْحُ: to pardon us and to wipe away what we have done.

questions.q: Who is speaking in line 2? Which ending tells you?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْمُتَكَلِّمُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟ أَيُّ نِهَايَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: “We”: the ending ـنَا.

questions.q: With what three things are they pleased?
questions.q_ar: بِأَيِّ ثَلَاثَةِ أَشْيَاءَ رَضُوا؟
questions.a: Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, Muḥammad ﷺ as Prophet.

questions.q: Which verb in the vocabulary list is this? Write its “he” form and its present.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ هَذَا؟ اُكْتُبْ صِيغَةَ «هُوَ» وَالْمُضَارِعَ.
questions.a: رَضِيَ, يَرْضَى (root ر ض ي).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A duʿāʾ and a dhikr from the Rātib of Imam ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād, which is read after ʿIshāʾ.

questions.q: The root of this command is ع ف و. Which letter is missing at the end of وَاعْفُ, and why?
questions.q_ar: جَذْرُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ هُوَ ع ف و. أَيُّ حَرْفٍ سَقَطَ مِنْ آخِرِ «وَاعْفُ»؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: The و. In the command the last weak letter drops.

questions.q: In line 2 the three nouns رَبًّا، دِينًا، نَبِيًّا each end in ـًا. What do you think this shows? (Look at the verb رَضِينَا.)
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي ثَلَاثَةُ أَسْمَاءٍ آخِرُهَا ـًا. مَاذَا تَظُنُّ أَنَّهَا تُبَيِّنُ؟
questions.a: They say “as what” they are pleased: with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, with Muḥammad ﷺ as Prophet.

questions.q: Translate the verse.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ.
questions.a: Guide us to the straight path.

questions.q: Is اِهْدِنَا a statement, a question or a command?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ «اِهْدِنَا»: خَبَرٌ أَمْ سُؤَالٌ أَمْ أَمْرٌ؟
questions.a: A command (a request: “guide us”).

questions.q: What does the ending ـنَا stand for?
questions.q_ar: عَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ ـنَا؟
questions.a: “us”.

questions.q: What is the root, and what is the “he” past form?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْجَذْرُ؟ وَمَا صِيغَةُ «هُوَ» فِي الْمَاضِي؟
questions.a: ه د ي; هَدَى.

questions.q: What is asked for?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُطْلَبُ؟
questions.a: Guidance to the straight path.

questions.q: In which sūra is this verse, and what is its number?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ سُورَةٍ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ؟ وَمَا رَقْمُهَا؟
questions.a: Sūrat al-Fātiḥa, verse 6.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: And your Lord said: “Call on Me, and I will answer you.”

questions.q: Who is speaking?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْقَائِلُ؟
questions.a: Your Lord (رَبُّكُمُ).

questions.q: What is the command, and what does the small ـنِي at its end mean?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْأَمْرُ؟ وَمَاذَا تَعْنِي ـنِي فِي آخِرِهِ؟
questions.a: “Call on Me”. ـنِي = “me”.

questions.q: What is the root of اُدْعُونِي, and which form of the same verb ends in ـتُ?
questions.q_ar: مَا جَذْرُ «اُدْعُونِي»؟ وَأَيُّ صِيغَةٍ مِنْهُ آخِرُهَا ـتُ؟
questions.a: د ع و; دَعَوْتُ.

questions.q: What is promised?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا وُعِدُوا؟
questions.a: An answer: “I will answer you” (أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ).

questions.q: In which sūra is this verse, and what is its number?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ سُورَةٍ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ؟ وَمَا رَقْمُهَا؟
questions.a: Sūrat Ghāfir, verse 60.

questions.q: Who walked, and with whom? Where to?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ مَشَى؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟ وَإِلَى أَيْنَ؟
questions.a: Ahmad walked with his father to the ziyāra.

questions.q: What did his father say? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ أَبُوهُ؟
questions.a: The student does not forget good manners.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad arrive, and when?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ وَصَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: At the ribāṭ, after an hour.

questions.q: Whom did Ahmad find, and where?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ وَجَدَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَأَيْنَ؟
questions.a: The Habib, in the majlis.

questions.q: Who made duʿāʾ, and for whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ دَعَا؟ وَلِمَنْ؟
questions.a: The Habib made duʿāʾ for Ahmad and for his father.

questions.q: What did Ahmad say in his duʿāʾ?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: O Allah, guide us.

questions.q: True or false? The Habib was angry with Ahmad.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ كَانَ الْحَبِيبُ غَاضِبًا مِنْ أَحْمَدَ.
questions.a: False: the Habib was pleased with him (رَضِيَ).

questions.q: Put the events in order: (a) Ahmad returned home; (b) he arrived at the ribāṭ; (c) he walked; (d) the Habib made duʿāʾ.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (a) رَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ (b) وَصَلَ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ (c) مَشَى (d) دَعَا الْحَبِيبُ.
questions.a: c, b, d, a.

questions.q: Write the present “he” form of وَجَدَ, and say which letter drops.
questions.q_ar: اُكْتُبْ مُضَارِعَ «وَجَدَ». أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَسْقُطُ؟
questions.a: يَجِدُ; the و drops.

questions.q: Line 2 has يَنْسَى. Is it a past or a present form? What is its past?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي «يَنْسَى». أَمَاضٍ هُوَ أَمْ مُضَارِعٌ؟ وَمَا مَاضِيهِ؟
questions.a: Present. The past is نَسِيَ (root ن س ي).

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening. The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.

questions.q: Which verb ends in a weak letter (written ـى) and means “he walked”? Give its present.
questions.a: مَشَى; its present is يَمْشِي

questions.q: Which verb has a weak first letter و (root و ص ل)? What does it mean?
questions.a: وَصَلَ: he arrived

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra.
questions.a: مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.

translate.ar: مَشَى أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: Ahmad walked with his father to the mosque.
I found a new book in the library.

translate.ar: وَصَلَ الضُّيُوفُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
translate.en: The guests arrived at the ribāṭ in the evening.
The teacher promised the students a new lesson.

translate.ar: نَسِيتُ كِتَابِي فِي الْبَيْتِ، وَلَكِنْ وَجَدْتُ مُصْحَفًا هُنَا.
translate.en: I forgot my book at the house, but I found a muṣḥaf here.
The Habib makes duʿāʾ for the students every day.
I called on Allah and prayed in the mosque.

translate.ar: رَضِيَ الْأَبُ عَنِ الْوَلَدِ لِأَنَّهُ طَالِبٌ جَيِّدٌ.
translate.en: The father was pleased with the boy because he is a good student.

translate.ar: يَمْشِي الطَّالِبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ وَلَا يَنْسَى كِتَابَهُ.
translate.en: The student walks to school and does not forget his book.
Call on Allah and say: O Allah, guide us.

translate.ar: مَشَى أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ، وَمَشَى عُمَرُ مَعَهُ. وَصَلَ أَحْمَدُ بَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ وَوَجَدَ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ. فَدَعَا لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ.
translate.en: Ahmad walked to the Habib, and Umar walked with him. Ahmad arrived after an hour and found the Habib in the majlis. And the Habib made duʿāʾ for him.
I promised the teacher: I will memorise the lesson.

translate.ar: يَصِلُ أَبِي إِلَى الْبَيْتِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
translate.en: My father arrives at the house in the evening.

translate.ar: يُصَلِّي الْحَبِيبُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَيَدْعُو بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ.
translate.en: The Habib prays in the mosque and makes duʿāʾ after the prayer.
The student forgot the lesson, so he asked the teacher.

translate.ar: وَصَلْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ فِي اللَّيْلِ وَصَلَّيْتُ.
translate.en: I arrived at the house at night and prayed.
I promised my father: I will go to the mosque.

translate.ar: يَرْضَى الْمُعَلِّمُ عَنِ الطَّالِبِ الَّذِي يَقْرَأُ.
translate.en: The teacher is pleased with the student who reads.
The boy walked to the mosque with his father.
translate.ar: مَشَى الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.

translate.en: I found the book in the library.
The guests arrived in the evening.
I forgot my book at home.
Call on Allah in the night.
The Habib made duʿāʾ for the students.
The father was pleased with Ahmad.
I prayed in the mosque, then I walked to the house.
translate.ar: صَلَّيْتُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ ثُمَّ مَشَيْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
alt: صَلَّيْتُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ، ثُمَّ مَشَيْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.

translate.en: The teacher promised the students a new lesson.
O Allah, guide us.
The student forgot the lesson, so he asked the teacher.
I arrived at the house, then I prayed.

readings.title_en: Odd ones: verbs that break the pattern
readings.question_en: What do I do with the verbs that do not follow the usual shape?
readings.question_ar: مَاذَا أَفْعَلُ بِالْأَفْعَالِ الَّتِي لَا تَسِيرُ عَلَى الْقَاعِدَةِ؟

passages.intro_en: A saying of Imam al-Ḥaddād. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: al-Ḥikam al-Ḥaddādiyya (Kitāb al-Ḥikam of Imam al-Ḥaddād)
passages.cite: al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād (1044–1132 H), Kitāb al-Ḥikam (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, 8), Dār al-Ḥāwī, 1st ed. 1413 H, 2nd ed. 1418 H (title page of the Shamela copy; SSD Master Library [184340]), p. 1/16 of the copy. Consonants checked against the copy; vowelled for learners.

lines.ar: مَنْ نَظَرَ إِلَى الدُّنْيَا بِعَيْنَيْ رَأْسِهِ رَأَى غُرُورًا وَزُورًا،
lines.en: Whoever looks at the world with the two eyes of his head sees delusion and falsehood;

lines.ar: وَمَنْ نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا بِعَيْنَيْ قَلْبِهِ رَأَى هَبَاءً مَنْثُورًا.
lines.en: and whoever looks at it with the two eyes of his heart sees scattered dust.

passages.ar: مَنْ نَظَرَ إِلَى الدُّنْيَا بِعَيْنَيْ رَأْسِهِ رَأَى غُرُورًا وَزُورًا، وَمَنْ نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا بِعَيْنَيْ قَلْبِهِ رَأَى هَبَاءً مَنْثُورًا.
passages.en: Whoever looks at the world with the two eyes of his head sees delusion and falsehood; and whoever looks at it with the two eyes of his heart sees scattered dust.

passages.intro_en: A verse: sūrat al-Zalzala, 99:1. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Qurʾān 99:1, text extracted by program from quran.json (Tanzil, Uthmani text), as in all lessons.

lines.ar: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا
lines.en: When the earth is shaken with its (great) shaking,

passages.ar: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا
passages.en: When the earth is shaken with its (great) shaking,

passages.intro_en: A short text: the majlis. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: جَاءَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
lines.en: Ahmad came to the ribāṭ with his father.

lines.ar: وَرَأَى فِي الْمَجْلِسِ نَاسًا كَثِيرِينَ.
lines.en: And he saw many people in the majlis.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
lines.en: Ahmad said: How beautiful this majlis is!

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: نِعْمَ الْمَجْلِسُ مَجْلِسُ الذِّكْرِ.
lines.en: And the Habib said: How excellent is the gathering of remembrance.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ جَاءَ عُمَرُ وَجَلَسَ مَعَ أَحْمَدَ.
lines.en: Then Umar came and sat with Ahmad.

lines.ar: وَتَرْجَمَ الْحَبِيبُ لَهُمْ كَلِمَةً جَدِيدَةً.
lines.en: And the Habib translated a new word for them.

lines.ar: وَلَيْسَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا، بَلْ هُوَ سَهْلٌ.
lines.en: The lesson is not difficult; rather, it is easy.

lines.ar: رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ مِنَ الْمَجْلِسِ، وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
lines.en: Ahmad returned to the house and said to his mother: I came from the majlis, and I saw the Habib.

passages.ar: جَاءَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ. وَرَأَى فِي الْمَجْلِسِ نَاسًا كَثِيرِينَ. قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ! وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: نِعْمَ الْمَجْلِسُ مَجْلِسُ الذِّكْرِ. ثُمَّ جَاءَ عُمَرُ وَجَلَسَ مَعَ أَحْمَدَ. وَتَرْجَمَ الْحَبِيبُ لَهُمْ كَلِمَةً جَدِيدَةً. وَلَيْسَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا، بَلْ هُوَ سَهْلٌ. رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ مِنَ الْمَجْلِسِ، وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
passages.en: Ahmad came to the ribāṭ with his father. And he saw many people in the majlis. Ahmad said: How beautiful this majlis is! And the Habib said: How excellent is the gathering of remembrance. Then Umar came and sat with Ahmad. And the Habib translated a new word for them. The lesson is not difficult; rather, it is easy. Ahmad returned to the house and said to his mother: I came from the majlis, and I saw the Habib.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 91-92 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
lines.en: The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!

lines.ar: قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
lines.en: He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.

passages.ar: جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ! قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
passages.en: The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is! He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.

questions.q: Translate the first line.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Whoever looks at the world with the two eyes of his head sees delusion and falsehood.

questions.q: Translate the second line.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And whoever looks at it with the two eyes of his heart sees scattered dust.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A wise saying (ḥikma) of Imam al-Ḥaddād, from his book of sayings (al-Ḥikam).

questions.q: Which odd verb is in both lines? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ غَرِيبٍ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهُ؟
questions.a: رَأَى: he saw (present يَرَى).

questions.q: With what does the first man look at the world?
questions.q_ar: بِمَاذَا يَنْظُرُ الْأَوَّلُ إِلَى الدُّنْيَا؟
questions.a: With the eyes of his head (بِعَيْنَيْ رَأْسِهِ).

questions.q: What does the second man see?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَرَى الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: Scattered dust (هَبَاءً مَنْثُورًا).

questions.q: True or false: the verb نَظَرَ is an odd verb.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: نَظَرَ فِعْلٌ غَرِيبٌ.
questions.a: False. نَظَرَ is a regular three-letter verb (root ن ظ ر).

questions.q: Find the word that means “the world”. What is the word for “heart” in line 2?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «الْعَالَمَ»؟ وَمَا كَلِمَةُ «الْقَلْبِ» فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: الدُّنْيَا; قَلْبِهِ (his heart).

questions.q: What does عَيْنَيْ mean? Why is it not عَيْنَانِ?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى عَيْنَيْ؟ لِمَاذَا لَيْسَتْ عَيْنَانِ؟
questions.a: Two eyes (of). After بِ the dual ends in ـَيْ (not ـَانِ), and joined to the next word (“his head”) it loses its ن.

questions.q: Why does the saying set “the eyes of the head” against “the eyes of the heart”?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يُقَابِلُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيِ الرَّأْسِ وَعَيْنَيِ الْقَلْبِ؟
questions.a: The head’s eyes see only the outside of the world; the heart’s eyes see what it is worth.

questions.q: Translate the verse.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ.
questions.a: When the earth is shaken with its (great) shaking,

questions.q: This verb comes from زَلْزَلَ. What does زَلْزَلَ mean, and how many root letters has it?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى زَلْزَلَ؟ وَكَمْ حَرْفًا فِي جَذْرِهِ؟
questions.a: He shook; four root letters (ز ل ز ل).

questions.q: What is shaken?
questions.q_ar: مَا الَّذِي زُلْزِلَ؟
questions.a: The earth (الْأَرْضُ).

questions.q: Which small word starts the verse, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ تَبْدَأُ بِهَا الْآيَةُ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: إِذَا: when, if.

questions.q: The sentence does not end in this verse. Why does it feel unfinished?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَبْدُو الْجُمْلَةُ غَيْرَ تَامَّةٍ؟
questions.a: “When …” needs an answer: what happens then. It continues in the next verse.

questions.q: Who came to the ribāṭ, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: Ahmad, with his father.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: Ahmad said: How beautiful this majlis is!

questions.q: Is مَا أَحْسَنَ a question here? What does it say?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ هَذَا سُؤَالٌ؟ مَاذَا يَقُولُ؟
questions.a: No. It is an exclamation: How beautiful …!

questions.q: What did the Habib say about the majlis?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ؟
questions.a: How excellent is the gathering of remembrance (نِعْمَ الْمَجْلِسُ مَجْلِسُ الذِّكْرِ).

questions.q: Who came after Ahmad, and what did he do?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَاءَ بَعْدَ أَحْمَدَ؟ وَمَاذَا فَعَلَ؟
questions.a: Umar came and sat with Ahmad.

questions.q: Find the four-letter verb. What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ رُبَاعِيٌّ فِي النَّصِّ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهُ؟
questions.a: تَرْجَمَ: he translated.

questions.q: True or false: the lesson was difficult.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: كَانَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا.
questions.a: False. لَيْسَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا: it was easy.

questions.q: Who says رَأَيْتُ, and to whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقُولُ رَأَيْتُ؟ وَلِمَنْ؟
questions.a: Ahmad (“I saw”), to his mother.

questions.q: Find the three forms of جَاءَ in the text. Which one is “I”?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ صُوَرَ جَاءَ الثَّلَاثَ فِي النَّصِّ. أَيُّهَا لِلْمُتَكَلِّمِ؟
questions.a: جَاءَ (line 1, Ahmad), جَاءَ (line 5, Umar), جِئْتُ (line 8, “I came”).

questions.q: Why does جِئْتُ look so different from جَاءَ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَخْتَلِفُ صُورَةُ جِئْتُ عَنْ جَاءَ؟
questions.a: Before the ending ـتُ the long alif is dropped and the first letter takes kasra (جَاءَ → جِئْتُ).

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is! He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.

questions.q: Which words make the exclamation “how beautiful …!”?
questions.a: مَا أَحْسَنَ

questions.q: Which verbs mean “I came” and “I saw”?
questions.a: جِئْتُ (from جَاءَ) and رَأَيْتُ (from رَأَى)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: How beautiful this majlis is!
questions.a: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!

translate.en: The boy saw the Habib in the ribāṭ.

translate.ar: جَاءَ الضُّيُوفُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ.
translate.en: The guests came to the majlis with the imam.
How beautiful the new mosque is!
The book is an excellent companion.
How bad is a gathering without good manners.
The student translated the letter for his mother.
The Habib is not in the mosque now.

translate.ar: جِئْتُ إِلَى تَرِيمَ مَعَ أَبِي، وَرَأَيْتُ الْمَسْجِدَ الْكَبِيرَ. مَا أَحْسَنَ الْمَسَاجِدَ هُنَاكَ! وَأَتَيْتُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ مَعَ عُمَرَ.
translate.en: I came to Tarim with my father, and I saw the big mosque. How beautiful the mosques are there! And I came to the ribāṭ with Umar.
The boy saw his teacher in the mosque.
I came to the ribāṭ yesterday.
How beautiful the majlis is!
The student translated a new word.
The door is not open.
His father comes from the market tomorrow.
The gathering of the Habib is an excellent gathering.
Umar saw the sea and the mountain.

readings.title_en: One root, one family of words
readings.question_en: How do I tell the doer, the one done-to and the action name of one root?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أُمَيِّزُ الْفَاعِلَ وَالْمَفْعُولَ وَالْمَصْدَرَ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ؟

passages.intro_en: Word families. Read each line aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: ع ل م: عَلِمَ، عِلْم، عَالِم، مَعْلُوم، عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّم، مُعَلَّم، تَعْلِيم، تَعَلَّمَ، تَعَلُّم
lines.en: he knew, knowledge, scholar, known, he taught, teacher, one taught, teaching, he learned, learning

lines.ar: غ ف ر: غَفَرَ، مَغْفِرَة، اِسْتَغْفَرَ، مُسْتَغْفِر، اِسْتِغْفَار
lines.en: he forgave, forgiveness, he asked forgiveness, one who asks forgiveness, asking forgiveness

lines.ar: س ل م: سَلَام، مُسْلِم، أَسْلَمَ، إِسْلَام، سَلَّمَ
lines.en: peace, Muslim, he became Muslim, Islam, he greeted

lines.ar: أ م ن: آمَنَ، مُؤْمِن، إِيمَان
lines.en: he believed, believer, faith

lines.ar: س ف ر: سَافَرَ، مُسَافِر، سَفَر
lines.en: he travelled, traveller, journey

lines.ar: ج م ع: جَمَعَ، اِجْتَمَعَ، اِجْتِمَاع
lines.en: he collected, he gathered, gathering

lines.ar: س ب ح: سَبَّحَ، تَسْبِيح، سُبْحَان
lines.en: he glorified, glorifying, glory be to

lines.ar: ر س ل: أَرْسَلَ، إِرْسَال، رَسُول، رِسَالَة
lines.en: he sent, sending, messenger, letter

passages.ar: ع ل م: عَلِمَ، عِلْم، عَالِم، مَعْلُوم، عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّم، مُعَلَّم، تَعْلِيم، تَعَلَّمَ، تَعَلُّم غ ف ر: غَفَرَ، مَغْفِرَة، اِسْتَغْفَرَ، مُسْتَغْفِر، اِسْتِغْفَار س ل م: سَلَام، مُسْلِم، أَسْلَمَ، إِسْلَام، سَلَّمَ أ م ن: آمَنَ، مُؤْمِن، إِيمَان س ف ر: سَافَرَ، مُسَافِر، سَفَر ج م ع: جَمَعَ، اِجْتَمَعَ، اِجْتِمَاع س ب ح: سَبَّحَ، تَسْبِيح، سُبْحَان ر س ل: أَرْسَلَ، إِرْسَال، رَسُول، رِسَالَة
passages.en: he knew, knowledge, scholar, known, he taught, teacher, one taught, teaching, he learned, learning he forgave, forgiveness, he asked forgiveness, one who asks forgiveness, asking forgiveness peace, Muslim, he became Muslim, Islam, he greeted he believed, believer, faith he travelled, traveller, journey he collected, he gathered, gathering he glorified, glorifying, glory be to he sent, sending, messenger, letter

passages.intro_en: A short text: the tree of words. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ وَكَتَبَ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً.
lines.en: Ahmad sat in the library and wrote many words.

lines.ar: وَرَأَى أَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ وَالْمُعَلَّمَ وَالتَّعْلِيمَ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.
lines.en: And he saw that the teacher, the one taught and the teaching are from one root.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ لِصَدِيقِهِ عُمَرَ: الْمُسَافِرُ وَالسَّفَرُ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ، وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرُ وَالِاسْتِغْفَارُ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.
lines.en: And he said to his friend Umar: The traveller and the journey are from one root, and the one who asks forgiveness and asking forgiveness are from one root.

lines.ar: قَالَ عُمَرُ: وَالْمُسْلِمُ وَالْإِسْلَامُ؟
lines.en: Umar said: And the Muslim and Islam?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، هُمَا مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: Yes, they are from one root.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ جَاءَ الْحَبِيبُ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْكَلِمَاتِ.
lines.en: Then the Habib came and looked at the words.

lines.ar: قَالَ: نِعْمَ الْعَمَلُ هَذَا.
lines.en: He said: How excellent this work is.

lines.ar: فَرَسَمَ أَحْمَدُ شَجَرَةً كَبِيرَةً: الْجَذْرُ تَحْتَ وَالْكَلِمَاتُ فَوْقَ.
lines.en: So Ahmad drew a big tree: the root below and the words above.

passages.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ وَكَتَبَ كَلِمَاتٍ كَثِيرَةً. وَرَأَى أَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ وَالْمُعَلَّمَ وَالتَّعْلِيمَ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ. وَقَالَ لِصَدِيقِهِ عُمَرَ: الْمُسَافِرُ وَالسَّفَرُ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ، وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرُ وَالِاسْتِغْفَارُ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ. قَالَ عُمَرُ: وَالْمُسْلِمُ وَالْإِسْلَامُ؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، هُمَا مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ. ثُمَّ جَاءَ الْحَبِيبُ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْكَلِمَاتِ. قَالَ: نِعْمَ الْعَمَلُ هَذَا. فَرَسَمَ أَحْمَدُ شَجَرَةً كَبِيرَةً: الْجَذْرُ تَحْتَ وَالْكَلِمَاتُ فَوْقَ.
passages.en: Ahmad sat in the library and wrote many words. And he saw that the teacher, the one taught and the teaching are from one root. And he said to his friend Umar: The traveller and the journey are from one root, and the one who asks forgiveness and asking forgiveness are from one root. Umar said: And the Muslim and Islam? Ahmad said: Yes, they are from one root. Then the Habib came and looked at the words. He said: How excellent this work is. So Ahmad drew a big tree: the root below and the words above.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 93-94 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
lines.en: The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.

lines.ar: وَكَتَبَ: سَافَرَ، مُسَافِرٌ، سَفَرٌ.
lines.en: And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.

passages.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ. وَكَتَبَ: سَافَرَ، مُسَافِرٌ، سَفَرٌ.
passages.en: The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm. And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.

questions.q: How is each line arranged?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ رُتِّبَ كُلُّ سَطْرٍ؟
questions.a: The three root letters first, then a colon, then the words of that family.

questions.q: In line 1: which word means “teacher” and which means “one taught”?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ١: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «الْمُعَلِّمَ»؟ وَأَيُّهَا «الَّذِي يُعَلَّمُ»؟
questions.a: مُعَلِّم (teacher) and مُعَلَّم (one taught).

questions.q: In line 1: which word means “teaching” and which means “learning”?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ١: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «التَّدْرِيسَ»؟ وَأَيُّهَا «التَّعَلُّمَ»؟
questions.a: تَعْلِيم (teaching) and تَعَلُّم (learning).

questions.q: Which line has the word for “one who asks forgiveness”? Write the word.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ فِيهِ كَلِمَةُ «مَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُ»؟ اُكْتُبْهَا.
questions.a: Line 2: مُسْتَغْفِر.

questions.q: Which two words in line 3 are the person and the name of the religion?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣ لِلشَّخْصِ وَلِاسْمِ الدِّينِ؟
questions.a: مُسْلِم (Muslim) and إِسْلَام (Islam).

questions.q: True or false: مُسَافِر and سَفَر have the same root.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: لِمُسَافِر وَسَفَر جَذْرٌ وَاحِدٌ.
questions.a: True: س ف ر.

questions.q: True or false: رَسُول and إِرْسَال come from different roots.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: رَسُول وَإِرْسَال مِنْ جَذْرَيْنِ.
questions.a: False: both are from ر س ل.

questions.q: Which line is about believing? Write its three words.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ عَنِ الْإِيمَانِ؟ اُكْتُبْ كَلِمَاتِهِ الثَّلَاثَ.
questions.a: Line 4: آمَنَ، مُؤْمِن، إِيمَان.

questions.q: سُبْحَان looks very different from تَسْبِيح. Why is it in the same line?
questions.q_ar: شَكْلُ سُبْحَان يُخَالِفُ تَسْبِيح. لِمَاذَا هُمَا فِي سَطْرٍ وَاحِدٍ؟
questions.a: The shape is different, but the three root letters س ب ح are the same.

questions.q: Which words in line 1 have no extra letters at all?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ١ لَيْسَ فِيهَا حَرْفٌ زَائِدٌ؟
questions.a: عَلِمَ (he knew) and عِلْم (knowledge): just the three root letters with vowels.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and what did he do?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَاذَا فَعَلَ؟
questions.a: In the library; he wrote many words.

questions.q: What did Ahmad see about the teacher, the one taught and the teaching?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا رَأَى أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمُعَلِّمِ وَالْمُعَلَّمِ وَالتَّعْلِيمِ؟
questions.a: That they are from one root.

questions.q: To whom did Ahmad speak? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَعَ مَنْ تَكَلَّمَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: To his friend Umar.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: Umar said: And the Muslim and Islam? Ahmad said: Yes, they are from one root.

questions.q: Who came, and what did he do? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَاءَ؟ وَمَاذَا فَعَلَ؟
questions.a: The Habib came and looked at the words.

questions.q: What did the Habib say about the work?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنِ الْعَمَلِ؟
questions.a: How excellent this work is.

questions.q: What did Ahmad draw? What is below and what is above?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا رَسَمَ أَحْمَدُ؟ مَا الَّذِي تَحْتَ وَمَا الَّذِي فَوْقَ؟
questions.a: A big tree: the root below, the words above.

questions.q: True or false: Ahmad wrote only one word.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ كَلِمَةً وَاحِدَةً فَقَطْ.
questions.a: False: he wrote many words.

questions.q: In line 3, which word is a doer and which is an action name?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فَاعِلٌ؟ وَأَيُّهَا مَصْدَرٌ؟
questions.a: الْمُسْتَغْفِرُ is the doer; الِاسْتِغْفَارُ is the action name.

questions.q: Why is a tree a good picture for a family of words?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا الشَّجَرَةُ صُورَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِأُسْرَةِ الْكَلِمَاتِ؟
questions.a: The root (three letters) is under the ground and all the words grow from it.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy wrote words from one root: he taught, teacher, teaching. And he wrote: he travelled, traveller, journey.

questions.q: What is the root of عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ?
questions.a: ع ل م

questions.q: In the first family, which word is the doer and which is the action-name?
questions.a: مُعَلِّمٌ is the doer (the teacher); تَعْلِيمٌ is the action-name (teaching).

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy wrote words from one root.
questions.a: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.

translate.en: The teacher teaches the students in the ribāṭ.

translate.ar: كَانَ الْمُسَافِرُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ السَّفَرَ كَانَ سَهْلًا.
translate.en: The traveller was happy because the journey was easy.

translate.ar: اِجْتَمَعَ الضُّيُوفُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ، وَكَانَ الِاجْتِمَاعُ كَبِيرًا.
translate.en: The guests gathered in the majlis, and the gathering was big.
The boy glorifies Allah, and glorifying is remembrance.
The sending of the letter was easy.
The man became Muslim, and he is now a Muslim.
Learning in the morning is easy.

translate.ar: تَعَلَّمَ أَحْمَدُ الدَّرْسَ مِنَ الْمُعَلِّمِ. وَكَانَ التَّعَلُّمُ سَهْلًا وَكَانَ التَّعْلِيمُ كَرِيمًا. فَشَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْمُعَلِّمَ.
translate.en: Ahmad learned the lesson from the teacher. The learning was easy and the teaching was generous. So the boy thanked the teacher.
The traveller came from the market.
The teacher teaches the boy.
Teaching is a noble work.
The students gathered in the mosque.
The boy asked forgiveness and glorified Allah.
The journey was long, and the traveller was happy.
translate.ar: كَانَ السَّفَرُ طَوِيلًا، وَكَانَ الْمُسَافِرُ سَعِيدًا.

translate.en: The boy learned the lesson.
The sending of the letter was easy.

readings.title_en: Noun shapes: five jobs
readings.question_en: What does the shape of a noun tell me before I know the word?
readings.question_ar: مَاذَا يُخْبِرُنِي شَكْلُ الِاسْمِ قَبْلَ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ مَعْنَاهُ؟

passages.intro_en: A real text: the mosques of Tarim. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Idām al-Qūt fī Dhikr Buldān Ḥaḍramawt (al-Saqqāf), the entry on Tarim
passages.cite: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. Muḥsin al-Saqqāf, Idām al-Qūt fī Dhikr Buldān Ḥaḍramawt (Shamela copy 'Maʿjam buldān Ḥaḍramawt', SSD Master Library [173760]; printed edition not identified), p. 1/589 of the copy. The text is cut and the line about who first built the mosque is left out (the author himself notes a difference of view). TLNOOR 702 is a scan of the same work (not read for this entry). Course cut: only the first and the third clause are printed; the middle clause (on the renewal of the building) is left out and marked with “...”, so the two clauses are shown in the order of the source. Vowelled for learners (the consonants are the source’s).

lines.ar: وَأَشْهَرُ مَسَاجِدِ تَرِيمَ: مَسْجِدُ آلِ أَحْمَدَ، ...
lines.en: The most famous mosques of Tarim: the mosque of Āl Aḥmad, ...

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْهِ أَوْقَافٌ كَثِيرَةٌ ...
lines.en: and it has many endowments ...

passages.ar: وَأَشْهَرُ مَسَاجِدِ تَرِيمَ: مَسْجِدُ آلِ أَحْمَدَ، ... وَعَلَيْهِ أَوْقَافٌ كَثِيرَةٌ ...
passages.en: The most famous mosques of Tarim: the mosque of Āl Aḥmad, ... and it has many endowments ...

passages.intro_en: A short text: in the mosque. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ الْمَسْجِدَ الْكَبِيرَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: Ahmad entered the big mosque in Tarim with his father.

lines.ar: فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مِنْبَرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَمِحْرَابٌ قَدِيمٌ.
lines.en: In the mosque there is a beautiful minbar and an old miḥrāb.

lines.ar: وَعِنْدَ الْمَدْخَلِ مِصْبَاحٌ كَبِيرٌ.
lines.en: And at the entrance there is a big lamp.

lines.ar: جَلَسَ وُلَيْدٌ بَيْنَ الرِّجَالِ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ، وَكَانَ أَصْغَرَ الطُّلَّابِ.
lines.en: A little boy sat among the men in the circle, and he was the youngest of the students.

lines.ar: وَكَانَ الْحَبِيبُ تَرِيمِيًّا، وَكَانَ أَعْلَمَ الرِّجَالِ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
lines.en: The Habib was from Tarim, and he was the most knowledgeable of the men in the majlis.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ فَتَحَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ بَابَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ بِالْمِفْتَاحِ.
lines.en: Then Ahmad’s father opened the library door with the key.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: الْمَكْتَبَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
lines.en: And Ahmad said: The library is bigger than the school.

lines.ar: وَقَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ الْحَضْرَمِيُّونَ كُتُبًا كَثِيرَةً.
lines.en: And the Ḥaḍramī students read many books.

passages.ar: دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ الْمَسْجِدَ الْكَبِيرَ فِي تَرِيمَ. فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مِنْبَرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَمِحْرَابٌ قَدِيمٌ. وَعِنْدَ الْمَدْخَلِ مِصْبَاحٌ كَبِيرٌ. جَلَسَ وُلَيْدٌ بَيْنَ الرِّجَالِ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ، وَكَانَ أَصْغَرَ الطُّلَّابِ. وَكَانَ الْحَبِيبُ تَرِيمِيًّا، وَكَانَ أَعْلَمَ الرِّجَالِ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ. ثُمَّ فَتَحَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ بَابَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ بِالْمِفْتَاحِ. وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: الْمَكْتَبَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ. وَقَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ الْحَضْرَمِيُّونَ كُتُبًا كَثِيرَةً.
passages.en: Ahmad entered the big mosque in Tarim with his father. In the mosque there is a beautiful minbar and an old miḥrāb. And at the entrance there is a big lamp. A little boy sat among the men in the circle, and he was the youngest of the students. The Habib was from Tarim, and he was the most knowledgeable of the men in the majlis. Then Ahmad’s father opened the library door with the key. And Ahmad said: The library is bigger than the school. And the Ḥaḍramī students read many books.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 95-96 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
lines.en: The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.

passages.ar: نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ. قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
passages.en: The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb. The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: The most famous mosques of Tarim: the mosque of Āl Aḥmad, ...

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: ... and it has many endowments ...

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A history of the towns of Ḥaḍramawt: Idām al-Qūt by al-Saqqāf, the entry on Tarim.

questions.q: Which mosque does line 1 name?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ مَسْجِدٍ يَذْكُرُ السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ؟
questions.a: The mosque of Āl Aḥmad (مَسْجِدُ آلِ أَحْمَدَ).

questions.q: What does the mosque have, according to line 2? Which word means “many”?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا لِلْمَسْجِدِ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «كَثِيرًا»؟
questions.a: Many endowments (أَوْقَاف); كَثِيرَةٌ means “many”.

questions.q: True or false?
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. The text speaks of “the most famous mosques” (many).

questions.q: Root hunt: find two words in the text built on the root س ج د. What does each name?
questions.q_ar: ابْحَثْ عَنْ كَلِمَتَيْنِ جَذْرُهُمَا س ج د. عَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ الْكَلِمَتَانِ؟
questions.a: مَسَاجِدِ (mosques) and مَسْجِدُ (mosque): the place of prostrating.

questions.q: This word is on the “more” shape. Why is it not أَشْهَرٌ with tanwīn? What does the shape add to the idea “famous”?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَيْسَتْ «أَشْهَرٌ» بِتَنْوِينٍ؟ مَاذَا يَزِيدُ الشَّكْلُ عَلَى مَعْنَى «شَهِير»؟
questions.a: A “more” word takes no tanwīn (it ends in ـُ here). The shape adds “most”: the most famous.

questions.q: Why does تَرِيمَ end in ـَ although it follows “of” (the mosques of …)?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي «تَرِيمَ» بِفَتْحَةٍ مَعَ أَنَّهَا بَعْدَ «مَسَاجِدِ»؟
questions.a: Tarim is a name that takes no tanwīn and no kasra (Lesson 40): it keeps ـَ.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad and his father go?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ وَأَبُوهُ؟
questions.a: Into the big mosque in Tarim.

questions.q: What is in the mosque? Name two things.
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ؟ اُذْكُرْ شَيْئَيْنِ.
questions.a: A beautiful minbar and an old miḥrāb.

questions.q: Where is the big lamp?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ الْمِصْبَاحُ الْكَبِيرُ؟
questions.a: At the entrance (عِنْدَ الْمَدْخَلِ).

questions.q: Who sat among the men? What does the shape of his word tell you?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَلَسَ بَيْنَ الرِّجَالِ؟ مَاذَا يَقُولُ شَكْلُ كَلِمَتِهِ؟
questions.a: A little boy. The little shape says “little”.

questions.q: Who was the most knowledgeable? Which word says “most knowing”, and what is its root?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ كَانَ أَعْلَمَ الرِّجَالِ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ؟ وَمَا جَذْرُهَا؟
questions.a: The Habib. أَعْلَمَ: root ع ل م.

questions.q: True or false?
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. Ahmad said the library is bigger (أَكْبَرُ) than the school.

questions.q: Put in order: (a) Ahmad’s father opened the library door; (b) Ahmad entered the mosque; (c) Ahmad said the library is bigger than the school.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (a) فَتَحَ الْأَبُ بَابَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ (b) دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْمَسْجِدَ (c) قَالَ أَحْمَدُ إِنَّ الْمَكْتَبَةَ أَكْبَرُ.
questions.a: b, a, c

questions.q: Root hunt: find three words built on the root ك ب ر. Which one means “more”?
questions.q_ar: ابْحَثْ عَنْ ثَلَاثِ كَلِمَاتٍ جَذْرُهَا ك ب ر. أَيُّهَا تَعْنِي «أَكْثَر»؟
questions.a: الْكَبِيرَ (line 1), كَبِيرٌ (line 3), أَكْبَرُ (line 7). أَكْبَرُ means “bigger”.

questions.q: In line 5, why does تَرِيمِيًّا end in ـًا, while الْحَضْرَمِيُّونَ in line 8 has the plural ending “-ūn”?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي «تَرِيمِيًّا» بِـ ـًا وَ«الْحَضْرَمِيُّونَ» بِـ ـُونَ؟
questions.a: تَرِيمِيًّا is what is said about the Habib after كَانَ (ـًا). الْحَضْرَمِيُّونَ describes the doer (الطُّلَّابُ), so it takes the doer’s ending: the plural of people (“-ūn”).

questions.q: Why does أَصْغَرَ end in ـَ and not in tanwīn? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي «أَصْغَرَ» بِفَتْحَةٍ دُونَ تَنْوِينٍ؟
questions.a: A “more” word takes no tanwīn; and after كَانَ the thing said ends in ـَ.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb. The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.

questions.q: مِنْبَر and مِحْرَاب are two things in the mosque. What does each one name?
questions.a: مِنْبَر: the pulpit; مِحْرَاب: the prayer niche. Their shape (مِـ in front) often names a tool or a place.

questions.q: What does the ending ـِيّ in حَضْرَمِيٌّ show?
questions.a: Belonging: from Ḥaḍramawt.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: I am from Tarim.
questions.a: أَنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ.

translate.en: The boy opened the school door with the key.
Our mosque is bigger than our school.
The lamp was near the minbar.
The little boy sat between his father and his brother.
This is a new Arabic book.
Allah knows best.
The Habib is from Tarim and his companions are Ḥaḍramīs.

translate.ar: دَخَلْتُ الْمَسْجِدَ مَعَ أَبِي. فِيهِ مِنْبَرٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمِحْرَابٌ جَمِيلٌ. وَجَلَسَ وُلَيْدٌ قُرْبَ الْمِحْرَابِ، وَهُوَ أَصْغَرُ مِنِّي.
translate.en: I entered the mosque with my father. In it are a big minbar and a beautiful miḥrāb. And a little boy sat near the miḥrāb; he is smaller than I am.
The mosque is bigger than the house.
The key is in the library.
There is a beautiful minbar in the mosque.
A little boy sat in the circle.
The Habib is from Tarim.
Umar is nearer to the door than Ahmad.
translate.ar: عُمَرُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَى الْبَابِ مِنْ أَحْمَدَ.

translate.en: The teacher knows more than the student.
He opened the door with the key.
This is the biggest mosque in the city.

readings.title_en: The dictionary: finding any word
readings.question_en: How do I find a word I do not know in a dictionary?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَجِدُ كَلِمَةً لَا أَعْرِفُهَا فِي الْمُعْجَمِ؟

passages.intro_en: A short text: a word Ahmad did not know. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ وَقَرَأَ كِتَابًا قَدِيمًا.
lines.en: In the evening Ahmad sat in the library and read an old book.

lines.ar: وَجَدَ فِيهِ كَلِمَةً جَدِيدَةً: الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ.
lines.en: He found in it a new word: al-mustamiʿūn.

lines.ar: لَمْ يَسْأَلْ أَبَاهُ، بَلْ فَتَحَ الْمُعْجَمَ.
lines.en: He did not ask his father; rather, he opened the dictionary.

lines.ar: قَالَ لِنَفْسِهِ: هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ مِنْ جَذْرِ سَمِعَ، فَأَنْظُرُ فِي بَابِ السِّينِ.
lines.en: He said to himself: This word is from the root of سَمِعَ (“he heard”), so I will look in the chapter of the letter sīn.

lines.ar: وَوَجَدَ الْمَعْنَى: الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ هُمُ الَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
lines.en: And he found the meaning: the listeners are those who hear the Habib in the majlis.

lines.ar: وَكَتَبَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
lines.en: And he wrote the meaning of the word in his book.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَبِيهِ وَقَالَ: فَهِمْتُ الْكَلِمَةَ وَحْدِي.
lines.en: Then he went back to his father and said: I understood the word by myself.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَبُوهُ: أَنْتَ الْآنَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
lines.en: His father said: You are now a seeker of knowledge.

passages.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ وَقَرَأَ كِتَابًا قَدِيمًا. وَجَدَ فِيهِ كَلِمَةً جَدِيدَةً: الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ. لَمْ يَسْأَلْ أَبَاهُ، بَلْ فَتَحَ الْمُعْجَمَ. قَالَ لِنَفْسِهِ: هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ مِنْ جَذْرِ سَمِعَ، فَأَنْظُرُ فِي بَابِ السِّينِ. وَوَجَدَ الْمَعْنَى: الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ هُمُ الَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ الْحَبِيبَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ. وَكَتَبَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ فِي كِتَابِهِ. ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَبِيهِ وَقَالَ: فَهِمْتُ الْكَلِمَةَ وَحْدِي. قَالَ أَبُوهُ: أَنْتَ الْآنَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
passages.en: In the evening Ahmad sat in the library and read an old book. He found in it a new word: al-mustamiʿūn. He did not ask his father; rather, he opened the dictionary. He said to himself: This word is from the root of سَمِعَ (“he heard”), so I will look in the chapter of the letter sīn. And he found the meaning: the listeners are those who hear the Habib in the majlis. And he wrote the meaning of the word in his book. Then he went back to his father and said: I understood the word by myself. His father said: You are now a seeker of knowledge.

passages.intro_en: A page of a dictionary. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text: entries written for the course in the style of a school dictionary, in root order; no printed source.

lines.ar: خَدَمَ، يَخْدُمُ، خِدْمَةً: عَمِلَ لِلنَّاسِ.
lines.en: to serve: he worked for people.

lines.ar: سَأَلَ، يَسْأَلُ، سُؤَالًا: طَلَبَ جَوَابًا.
lines.en: to ask: he asked for an answer.

lines.ar: سَكَنَ، يَسْكُنُ: جَلَسَ فِي بَيْتٍ وَقْتًا طَوِيلًا.
lines.en: to live (in a place): he sat in a house for a long time.

lines.ar: الْمَسْكَنُ: بَيْتٌ يَسْكُنُ فِيهِ النَّاسُ.
lines.en: the dwelling: a house where people live.

lines.ar: عَمِلَ، يَعْمَلُ، عَمَلًا: فَعَلَ شَيْئًا.
lines.en: to do, to work: he did something.

lines.ar: الْمِفْتَاحُ: شَيْءٌ نَفْتَحُ بِهِ الْبَابَ.
lines.en: the key: a thing we open the door with.

passages.ar: خَدَمَ، يَخْدُمُ، خِدْمَةً: عَمِلَ لِلنَّاسِ. سَأَلَ، يَسْأَلُ، سُؤَالًا: طَلَبَ جَوَابًا. سَكَنَ، يَسْكُنُ: جَلَسَ فِي بَيْتٍ وَقْتًا طَوِيلًا. الْمَسْكَنُ: بَيْتٌ يَسْكُنُ فِيهِ النَّاسُ. عَمِلَ، يَعْمَلُ، عَمَلًا: فَعَلَ شَيْئًا. الْمِفْتَاحُ: شَيْءٌ نَفْتَحُ بِهِ الْبَابَ.
passages.en: to serve: he worked for people. to ask: he asked for an answer. to live (in a place): he sat in a house for a long time. the dwelling: a house where people live. to do, to work: he did something. the key: a thing we open the door with.
