passages.cite: al-Ḥikam al-Ḥaddādiyya, al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād (1044–1132 H), Kitāb al-Ḥikam (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, 8), Dār al-Ḥāwī, 1st ed. 1413 H, 2nd ed. 1418 H (title page of the Shamela copy; SSD Master Library [184340]), p. 1/31; al-Ḥikam al-Ḥaddādiyya, p. 1/22; al-Ḥikam al-Ḥaddādiyya, p. 1/30. Consonants checked against the copy; vowelled for learners.

lines.ar: مَنْ حَفِظَ الْفُؤَادَ حُفِظَ مِنَ الْفَسَادِ.
lines.en: Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.

lines.ar: مَنْ أَصْلَحَ نِيَّتَهُ بَلَغَ أُمْنِيَّتَهُ.
lines.en: Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.

lines.ar: الْعِلْمُ عَلَيْكَ حَتَّى تَعْمَلَ بِهِ، فَإِذَا عَمِلْتَ بِهِ كَانَ الْعِلْمُ لَكَ.
lines.en: Knowledge is against you until you act on it; when you act on it, it is for you.

passages.ar: مَنْ حَفِظَ الْفُؤَادَ حُفِظَ مِنَ الْفَسَادِ. مَنْ أَصْلَحَ نِيَّتَهُ بَلَغَ أُمْنِيَّتَهُ. الْعِلْمُ عَلَيْكَ حَتَّى تَعْمَلَ بِهِ، فَإِذَا عَمِلْتَ بِهِ كَانَ الْعِلْمُ لَكَ.
passages.en: Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption. Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish. Knowledge is against you until you act on it; when you act on it, it is for you.

passages.intro_en: Unseen lines (2): a ḥadīth clause and two lines of prayer. Read them aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; the Rātib of Imam al-Ḥaddād; al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa
passages.cite: Line 1: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2699: Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Dār al-Jīl + Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut, vowelled print (Shamela 1786; the card gives no year), 8/71 (Dār al-Jīl no. 7028); ʿAbd al-Bāqī numbering: ed. Muḥammad Fuʾād ʿAbd al-Bāqī, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Beirut (Shamela 1785), no. 2699, 4/2074 (a clause of the ḥadīth «مَنْ نَفَّسَ عَنْ مُؤْمِنٍ كُرْبَةً ...»; the same clause opens the Risāla al-Jāmiʿa after «طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ»)  Line 2: Rātib al-Ḥaddād, 15th dhikr (said seven times): Rātib al-Imām ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, called Sabīl al-Saʿāda wa-l-Falāḥ fī Adhkār al-Masāʾ wa-l-Ṣabāḥ, in the Shamela copy 'Awrād wa-Aḥzāb' (SSD Master Library [184180], from the loose .bok file; printed edition not identified), part 2, p. 2/3; Dhakhīrat al-Maʿād p. 137 (heading seen on the page image)  Line 3: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa, Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī al-ʿAlawī (1069–1145 H), al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa, Dār Maqām al-Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr wa-l-Tawzīʿ, Ḥawṭat Aḥmad b. Zayn, Ḥaḍramawt (title page of the Shamela copy; no year given; SSD Master Library [182670]), p. 1/2 (the opening doxology) Course cut: line 3 is cut after رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ and marked with “...”.

lines.ar: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
lines.en: Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah makes easy for him a path to the Garden.

lines.ar: يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ، أَمِتْنَا عَلَى دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ
lines.en: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, make us die in the religion of Islam.

lines.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ...
lines.en: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds ...

passages.ar: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ، أَمِتْنَا عَلَى دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ...
passages.en: Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah makes easy for him a path to the Garden. O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, make us die in the religion of Islam. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds ...

passages.intro_en: Use this dictionary page to answer.
passages.cite: Course text: entries written for the course in the style of a school dictionary, in root order; no printed source.

lines.ar: حَفِظَ، يَحْفَظُ، حِفْظًا: جَعَلَ الْكَلِمَاتِ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
lines.en: to memorise: he put the words in his heart.

lines.ar: رَجَعَ، يَرْجِعُ: ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي جَاءَ مِنْهُ.
lines.en: to return: he went to the place he came from.

lines.ar: زَارَ، يَزُورُ، زِيَارَةً: ذَهَبَ إِلَى صَدِيقٍ وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُ.
lines.en: to visit: he went to a friend and sat with him.

lines.ar: عَبَدَ، يَعْبُدُ: صَلَّى وَسَجَدَ لِلَّهِ.
lines.en: to worship: he prayed and prostrated to Allah.

lines.ar: نَظَرَ، يَنْظُرُ، نَظَرًا: رَأَى بِعَيْنِهِ.
lines.en: to look: he saw with his eye.

passages.ar: حَفِظَ، يَحْفَظُ، حِفْظًا: جَعَلَ الْكَلِمَاتِ فِي قَلْبِهِ. رَجَعَ، يَرْجِعُ: ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي جَاءَ مِنْهُ. زَارَ، يَزُورُ، زِيَارَةً: ذَهَبَ إِلَى صَدِيقٍ وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُ. عَبَدَ، يَعْبُدُ: صَلَّى وَسَجَدَ لِلَّهِ. نَظَرَ، يَنْظُرُ، نَظَرًا: رَأَى بِعَيْنِهِ.
passages.en: to memorise: he put the words in his heart. to return: he went to the place he came from. to visit: he went to a friend and sat with him. to worship: he prayed and prostrated to Allah. to look: he saw with his eye.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 97-98 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
lines.en: The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
lines.en: Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.

passages.ar: نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ. ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
passages.en: The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word. Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and what did he read?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَاذَا قَرَأَ؟
questions.a: In the library; an old book.

questions.q: What new word did he find?
questions.q_ar: أَيَّةَ كَلِمَةٍ جَدِيدَةٍ وَجَدَ؟
questions.a: الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ (the listeners).

questions.q: Did he ask his father? What did he do instead?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ سَأَلَ أَبَاهُ؟ مَاذَا فَعَلَ؟
questions.a: No. He opened the dictionary.

questions.q: Which verb is the word from? Under which letter did he look?
questions.q_ar: الْكَلِمَةُ مِنْ أَيِّ فِعْلٍ؟ تَحْتَ أَيِّ حَرْفٍ نَظَرَ؟
questions.a: From سَمِعَ, under sīn (س), the first letter of the root.

questions.q: True or false?
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. He looked in the chapter of sīn (not ʿayn).

questions.q: What did he write in his book?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَتَبَ فِي كِتَابِهِ؟
questions.a: The meaning of the word.

questions.q: Root hunt: find the words in lines 4 and 5 that share the root س م ع with الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ.
questions.q_ar: ابْحَثْ عَنْ كَلِمَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ٤ وَ٥ لَهُمَا الْجَذْرُ نَفْسُهُ فِي «الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ»: س م ع.
questions.a: سَمِعَ (line 4) and يَسْمَعُونَ (line 5).

questions.q: Why did Ahmad not look under م, the first letter of الْمُسْتَمِعُونَ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَمْ يَنْظُرْ أَحْمَدُ تَحْتَ الْمِيمِ؟
questions.a: Because the م belongs to the shape (the doer prefix), not to the root. A dictionary is in root order: س م ع.

questions.q: What does his father mean by “You are now a seeker of knowledge”?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقْصِدُ أَبُوهُ بِقَوْلِهِ «أَنْتَ الْآنَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ»؟
questions.a: He sees that Ahmad found the meaning by himself, the way a student of knowledge works.

questions.q: What kind of text is this?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟
questions.a: A page of a dictionary: entries in root order, with the past, the present and the meaning.

questions.q: Translate the first entry.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْمَادَّةَ الْأُولَى.
questions.a: to serve: he worked for people.

questions.q: Under which entry would you find سُؤَال (“a question”)? Which root?
questions.q_ar: تَحْتَ أَيِّ مَادَّةٍ تَجِدُ «سُؤَالًا»؟ مَا جَذْرُهَا؟
questions.a: Under سَأَلَ (he asked): root س أ ل.

questions.q: What is a مِفْتَاح, according to the page?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي هَذِهِ الصَّفْحَةِ؟
questions.a: A thing we open the door with.

questions.q: Which two verbs are entered under the letter س? Which one comes first, and why?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلَيْنِ تَحْتَ السِّينِ؟ أَيُّهُمَا أَوَّلًا؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: سَأَلَ (س أ ل) comes before سَكَنَ (س ك ن): the second letter decides: أ comes before ك.

questions.q: True or false?
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. عَمِلَ: he did something.

questions.q: Root hunt: which word on the page shares its root with the verb سَكَنَ?
questions.q_ar: ابْحَثْ عَنْ كَلِمَةٍ فِي الصَّفْحَةِ جَذْرُهَا مِثْلُ سَكَنَ.
questions.a: الْمَسْكَنُ (the dwelling).

questions.q: The entry الْمَسْكَنُ stands right under the verb سَكَنَ. Why is a noun listed under a verb?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَأْتِي الِاسْمُ «الْمَسْكَنُ» تَحْتَ الْفِعْلِ «سَكَنَ»؟
questions.a: Both come from the root س ك ن; the dictionary keeps a whole root family together.

questions.q: Each verb entry gives the present as well as the past. What does the present show that the past does not?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَذْكُرُ الْمُعْجَمُ الْمُضَارِعَ مَعَ الْمَاضِي؟
questions.a: The vowel on the middle root letter in the present (ـَ in يَسْأَلُ and يَعْمَلُ, ـُ in يَخْدُمُ): the past does not tell you which it is.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Whoever guards the heart is guarded from corruption.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: Whoever mends his intention reaches his wish.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Wise sayings (ḥikam) of Imam al-Ḥaddād, from his book al-Ḥikam.

questions.q: In line 3, what is “against you” until you act on it?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ: مَاذَا يَكُونُ «عَلَيْكَ» حَتَّى تَعْمَلَ بِهِ؟
questions.a: Knowledge (الْعِلْمُ).

questions.q: In line 1, how is حُفِظَ different from حَفِظَ?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ: مَا الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَ حُفِظَ وَحَفِظَ؟
questions.a: It is the passive (Lesson 42): “is guarded”; the guard is not named. حَفِظَ = he guarded, he memorised.

questions.q: Root hunt: line 3 has two verbs built on the root ع م ل. Find them.
questions.q_ar: ابْحَثْ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ عَنْ فِعْلَيْنِ جَذْرُهُمَا ع م ل.
questions.a: تَعْمَلَ and عَمِلْتَ.

questions.q: أَصْلَحَ is on the shape of Form IV. What idea in the root ص ل ح (as in صَالِح) does it make into an action?
questions.q_ar: أَصْلَحَ عَلَى شَكْلِ أَفْعَلَ. مَا فِكْرَةُ الْجَذْرِ ص ل ح (كَمَا فِي صَالِح)؟
questions.a: Goodness, rightness: أَصْلَحَ = he made it right, he mended it.

questions.q: Line 3 sets “against you” against “for you”. What turns the knowledge from one into the other?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُحَوِّلُ الْعِلْمَ مِنْ «عَلَيْكَ» إِلَى «لَكَ»؟
questions.a: Acting on it (عَمِلْتَ بِهِ). Knowledge that is not acted on is a proof against its owner; acted on, it is for him.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah makes easy for him a path to the Garden.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, make us die in the religion of Islam.

questions.q: The three lines are of three kinds: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ, a prayer, and the opening of a book. Which is which?
questions.q_ar: الْأَسْطُرُ الثَّلَاثَةُ ثَلَاثَةُ أَنْوَاعٍ: حَدِيثٌ وَدُعَاءٌ وَبِدَايَةُ كِتَابٍ. أَيُّ سَطْرٍ مِنْ أَيِّ نَوْعٍ؟
questions.a: Line 1: the Prophet’s ﷺ saying (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim). Line 2: a prayer (from the Rātib). Line 3: the opening praise of a book (al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa).

questions.q: In line 1, what does Allah make easy, and for whom?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ: مَاذَا يُسَهِّلُ اللَّهُ؟ وَلِمَنْ؟
questions.a: A path to the Garden, for whoever follows a path seeking knowledge.

questions.q: Root hunt: يَلْتَمِسُ is on the shape of Form VIII (like اِجْتَمَعَ). What is its root?
questions.q_ar: ابْحَثْ عَنْ جَذْرِ يَلْتَمِسُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى شَكْلِ اِجْتَمَعَ.
questions.a: ل م س (the verb is اِلْتَمَسَ: he sought).

questions.q: In line 3, what is the praise addressed to?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ: لِمَنِ الْحَمْدُ؟
questions.a: To Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

questions.q: The word طَرِيقًا is in line 1 twice. How does the second “path” differ from the first?
questions.q_ar: جَاءَتْ كَلِمَةُ «طَرِيقًا» مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ. بِمَ يَخْتَلِفُ الثَّانِي عَنِ الْأَوَّلِ؟
questions.a: The first is the way the man walks (his seeking); the second is the path Allah makes easy for him, to the Garden.

questions.q: Where else have you read the words الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ? What does that tell you about the opening of a book?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ قَرَأْتَ «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ» مِنْ قَبْلُ؟ وَمَاذَا يُخْبِرُكَ ذَلِكَ عَنْ بِدَايَةِ الْكِتَابِ؟
questions.a: In sūrat al-Fātiḥa. A book often opens with praise, as the Qur’an does.

questions.q: Look up this word: take off وَ and the ending. Which entry is it? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: اِبْحَثْ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ: أَيَّةُ مَادَّةٍ هِيَ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: حَفِظَ (ح ف ظ): he put the words in his heart. “And we memorised.”

questions.q: Which entry is it? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيَّةُ مَادَّةٍ هِيَ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: رَجَعَ (ر ج ع): he went to the place he came from. “We returned.”

questions.q: Root? What does the verb زَارَ mean on the page?
questions.q_ar: مَا جَذْرُهَا؟ وَمَا مَعْنَى الْفِعْلِ «زَارَ»؟
questions.a: ز و ر; he went to a friend and sat with him: so “their visit”.

questions.q: Which entry is it? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيَّةُ مَادَّةٍ هِيَ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: عَبَدَ (ع ب د): he prayed and prostrated to Allah. “And they worshipped.”

questions.q: Which entry is it? Translate the word.
questions.q_ar: أَيَّةُ مَادَّةٍ هِيَ؟ تَرْجِمِ الْكَلِمَةَ.
questions.a: نَظَرَ (ن ظ ر): he saw with his eye. “I looked.”

questions.q: True or false?
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. رَجَعَ: he went to the place he came from.

questions.q: Which entry comes first on the page, زَارَ or رَجَعَ? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ مَادَّةٍ أَوَّلًا: زَارَ أَمْ رَجَعَ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: رَجَعَ: the root letter ر comes before ز.

questions.q: Which entry has a word that means “prayed”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ مَادَّةٍ فِيهَا كَلِمَةٌ تَعْنِي «صَلَّى»؟
questions.a: عَبَدَ: صَلَّى وَسَجَدَ لِلَّهِ.

questions.q: The page has five entries. In what order are the first root letters?
questions.q_ar: بِأَيِّ تَرْتِيبٍ جَاءَتِ الْحُرُوفُ الْأُولَى لِلْجُذُورِ؟
questions.a: ح، ر، ز، ع، ن: the order of the alphabet.

questions.q: Is مَسْجِد on this page? Where would you find it?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ «مَسْجِد» فِي هَذِهِ الصَّفْحَةِ؟ أَيْنَ تَجِدُهُ؟
questions.a: No. Under س ج د (the root of سَجَدَ), on another page.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word. Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.

questions.q: To find a word in the dictionary, what must you find first?
questions.a: Its root: strip the extra letters and the pattern, then look up the root.

questions.q: In the first new line, which verb means “he found”? Give its root.
questions.a: وَجَدَ (root و ج د)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy found the meaning of the word.
questions.a: وَجَدَ الْوَلَدُ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.

translate.ar: نَظَرَ الطَّالِبُ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
translate.en: The student looked in the dictionary and found the meaning of the word.

translate.ar: الْمُعْجَمُ كِتَابٌ فِيهِ كَلِمَاتٌ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمَعْنَى كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ.
translate.en: The dictionary is a book with many words and the meaning of every word.

translate.ar: لَمْ يَسْأَلْ أَحْمَدُ أَبَاهُ بَلْ فَتَحَ الْمُعْجَمَ.
translate.en: Ahmad did not ask his father; rather, he opened the dictionary.

translate.ar: سَلَكَ الْمُسَافِرُ طَرِيقًا طَوِيلًا إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
translate.en: The traveller took a long road to Tarim.

translate.ar: اِلْتَمَسَ الطُّلَّابُ الْعِلْمَ وَاسْتَمَعُوا إِلَى الْمُعَلِّمِ.
translate.en: The students sought knowledge and listened to the teacher.
The boy mended the door with his hand.
The Habib’s mosque is nearer than our house.

translate.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ وَفَتَحَ مُعْجَمًا قَدِيمًا. نَظَرَ فِي بَابِ الْعَيْنِ وَقَرَأَ: عَلِمَ، يَعْلَمُ: عَرَفَ. ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
translate.en: Ahmad sat in the library and opened an old dictionary. He looked in the chapter of ʿayn and read: “ʿalima, yaʿlamu: he knew.” Then he wrote the meaning in his book.
Ahmad opened the dictionary.
The student looked for the word in the dictionary.
He wrote the meaning of the word in his book.
The mosque is nearer than the library.
The dictionary is a big book.
The traveller listened to the teacher.
He did not ask his father; he opened the dictionary.
translate.ar: لَمْ يَسْأَلْ أَبَاهُ، بَلْ فَتَحَ الْمُعْجَمَ.

translate.en: This word comes from the verb “he heard”.

readings.title_en: Words that change the ending
readings.question_en: Which small words change the ending of the words after them?
readings.question_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ صَغِيرَةٍ تُغَيِّرُ آخِرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا؟

passages.intro_en: A creed: the first lines of a short matn. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa of Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī (1069–1145 AH)
passages.cite: Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī, al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa, Dār Maqām al-Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr, Ḥawṭat Aḥmad b. Zayn, Ḥaḍramawt (year not given on the title page); Shamela Master Library copy 'الرسالة الجامعة' (Bafaqih Sufi library, 491.mdb; same work as TLNOOR 712, an epub), pp. 2–3 of the copy (9 pp; the copy's own page counter, printed pagination not given). Lines 1, 3, 4 and 5 of the text, in the source spelling (letters unchanged). The source is only partly vowelled: the missing vowels and case endings were added by the course (vowelled for learners). Two misprints of the source corrected: الإِيَمَانِ → الإِيمَانِ, القُرَآنَ → القُرْآنَ.

lines.ar: وَأَصْلُ الْإِيمَانِ: أَنْ تَعْتَقِدَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى مَوْجُودٌ، وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى وَاحِدٌ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَلَا مِثْلَ لَهُ، وَلَا شِبْهَ لَهُ
lines.en: The root of faith: that you believe that God Most High exists, and that He is One, with no partner, no equal and no likeness.

lines.ar: وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى بَعَثَ سَيِّدَنَا مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدَهُ وَرَسُولَهُ إِلَى جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ
lines.en: And that He, Most High, sent our master Muḥammad ﷺ, His servant and messenger, to all creation.

lines.ar: وَأَنَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ صَادِقٌ فِي جَمِيعِ مَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ عَنِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
lines.en: And that he, upon him be blessings and peace, is truthful in all that he reported from God Most High.

lines.ar: وَأَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ وَجَمِيعَ كُتُبِ اللَّهِ الْمُنَزَّلَةِ حَقٌّ، وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ حَقٌّ، وَالْجَنَّةُ حَقٌّ، وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ
lines.en: And that the Qur’an and all the books God sent down are true, the angels are true, Paradise is true and the Fire is true.

passages.ar: وَأَصْلُ الْإِيمَانِ: أَنْ تَعْتَقِدَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى مَوْجُودٌ، وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى وَاحِدٌ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَلَا مِثْلَ لَهُ، وَلَا شِبْهَ لَهُ وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى بَعَثَ سَيِّدَنَا مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدَهُ وَرَسُولَهُ إِلَى جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ وَأَنَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ صَادِقٌ فِي جَمِيعِ مَا أَخْبَرَ بِهِ عَنِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَأَنَّ الْقُرْآنَ وَجَمِيعَ كُتُبِ اللَّهِ الْمُنَزَّلَةِ حَقٌّ، وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ حَقٌّ، وَالْجَنَّةُ حَقٌّ، وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ
passages.en: The root of faith: that you believe that God Most High exists, and that He is One, with no partner, no equal and no likeness. And that He, Most High, sent our master Muḥammad ﷺ, His servant and messenger, to all creation. And that he, upon him be blessings and peace, is truthful in all that he reported from God Most High. And that the Qur’an and all the books God sent down are true, the angels are true, Paradise is true and the Fire is true.

passages.intro_en: A counsel: one line with كَانَ. Read it, then answer.
passages.source: Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād

Vowelled for learners: the source is only partly vowelled; the missing vowels were added by the course, letters unchanged.

lines.ar: كَانَ ثَوَابُهُ عَلَى اللهِ، وَكَانَ مُنْقَلَبُهُ إِلَى رِضْوَانِ اللهِ وَجَنَّتِهِ
lines.en: His reward was with God, and his return was to God’s good pleasure and His Garden.

passages.ar: كَانَ ثَوَابُهُ عَلَى اللهِ، وَكَانَ مُنْقَلَبُهُ إِلَى رِضْوَانِ اللهِ وَجَنَّتِهِ
passages.en: His reward was with God, and his return was to God’s good pleasure and His Garden.

passages.intro_en: A short story: the evening in the ribāṭ. Read it, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (course-made short story, in the register of the story strip)

lines.ar: كَانَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ قَبْلَ الرَّاتِبِ.
lines.en: Ahmad was in the ribāṭ before the Rātib.

lines.ar: أَمْسَى الْمَسْجِدُ مَفْتُوحًا لِلنَّاسِ.
lines.en: In the evening the mosque was open to the people.

lines.ar: بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ جَلَسَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
lines.en: After the Rātib the Habib sat in the circle.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: لَيْتَ الْمَجْلِسَ طَوِيلٌ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: If only the majlis were long.

lines.ar: لَكِنَّ الْوَقْتَ قَصِيرٌ، وَمَا زَالَ الطُّلَّابُ جَالِسِينَ.
lines.en: But the time is short, and the students are still sitting.

lines.ar: لَعَلَّ الْحَبِيبَ يَسْمَعُ السُّؤَالَ.
lines.en: Perhaps the Habib will hear the question.

lines.ar: صَارَ أَحْمَدُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ الْحَبِيبَ سَمِعَ السُّؤَالَ.
lines.en: Ahmad became happy because the Habib heard the question.

lines.ar: كَأَنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ بَيْتُ الْعِلْمِ.
lines.en: As if the mosque were the house of knowledge.

passages.ar: كَانَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ قَبْلَ الرَّاتِبِ. أَمْسَى الْمَسْجِدُ مَفْتُوحًا لِلنَّاسِ. بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ جَلَسَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ. قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: لَيْتَ الْمَجْلِسَ طَوِيلٌ. لَكِنَّ الْوَقْتَ قَصِيرٌ، وَمَا زَالَ الطُّلَّابُ جَالِسِينَ. لَعَلَّ الْحَبِيبَ يَسْمَعُ السُّؤَالَ. صَارَ أَحْمَدُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ الْحَبِيبَ سَمِعَ السُّؤَالَ. كَأَنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ بَيْتُ الْعِلْمِ.
passages.en: Ahmad was in the ribāṭ before the Rātib. In the evening the mosque was open to the people. After the Rātib the Habib sat in the circle. Ahmad said: If only the majlis were long. But the time is short, and the students are still sitting. Perhaps the Habib will hear the question. Ahmad became happy because the Habib heard the question. As if the mosque were the house of knowledge.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 99-100 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
lines.en: The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.

lines.ar: أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
lines.en: The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا. أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
passages.en: The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib. The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A statement of belief (a creed), from al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa of Imam Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī.

questions.q: Line 1: what is said to exist?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَوْجُودٌ؟
questions.a: God Most High (اللهُ تَعَالَى).

questions.q: Line 1: find the word that means “one”.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي مَعْنَاهَا «one».
questions.a: وَاحِدٌ

questions.q: Line 1: God has no partner, no equal and no …?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: لَيْسَ لِلَّهِ شَرِيكٌ وَلَا مِثْلٌ وَلَا …؟
questions.a: No likeness (شِبْه).

questions.q: Line 2: whom did God send, and to whom?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَنْ أَرْسَلَ اللَّهُ؟ وَإِلَى مَنْ؟
questions.a: Our master Muḥammad ﷺ, His servant and messenger, to all creation.

questions.q: Line 3: which word says that he is truthful?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَقُولُ إِنَّهُ صَادِقٌ؟
questions.a: صَادِقٌ

questions.q: Line 3: how far does his truthfulness reach?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: إِلَى أَيِّ حَدٍّ صِدْقُهُ؟
questions.a: In all that he reported from God Most High.

questions.q: Line 4: name the four things said to be true (حَقٌّ).
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: اُذْكُرِ الْأَشْيَاءَ الْأَرْبَعَةَ الَّتِي قِيلَ إِنَّهَا حَقٌّ.
questions.a: The Qur’an and the books God sent down; the angels; Paradise; the Fire.

questions.q: True or false? The text says that God has a partner.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ يَقُولُ النَّصُّ إِنَّ لِلَّهِ شَرِيكًا.
questions.a: False: it says He has none.

questions.q: True or false? The Prophet ﷺ was sent only to one people.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ أُرْسِلَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إِلَى قَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ فَقَطْ.
questions.a: False: to all creation (جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ).

questions.q: The word جَمِيع ends in ـِ in line 2 and in ـَ in line 4. Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا آخِرُ «جَمِيع» ـِ فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ وَـَ فِي السَّطْرِ ٤؟
questions.a: Line 2: it follows إِلَى (a preposition), so ـِ. Line 4: it is joined to الْقُرْآنَ, which follows أَنَّ, so ـَ.

questions.q: What do اللهَ (line 1) and الْقُرْآنَ (line 4) have in common after أَنَّ?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَجْمَعُ «اللهَ» وَ«الْقُرْآنَ» بَعْدَ «أَنَّ»؟
questions.a: Both end in ـَ: أَنَّ is a sister of إِنَّ and puts the topic in ـَ.

questions.q: Find the word كَانَ. How many times does it occur?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ «كَانَ»؟ وَكَمْ مَرَّةً جَاءَتْ؟
questions.a: كَانَ, twice (كَانَ ثَوَابُهُ … وَكَانَ مُنْقَلَبُهُ).

questions.q: With whom is his reward?
questions.q_ar: عِنْدَ مَنْ ثَوَابُهُ؟
questions.a: With God.

questions.q: Where is his return to?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ مُنْقَلَبُهُ؟
questions.a: To God’s good pleasure and His Garden.

questions.q: Where was Ahmad before the Rātib?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ كَانَ أَحْمَدُ قَبْلَ الرَّاتِبِ؟
questions.a: In the ribāṭ.

questions.q: What happened to the mosque in the evening?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا حَدَثَ لِلْمَسْجِدِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ؟
questions.a: It was open to the people.

questions.q: What did the Habib do after the Rātib?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ الْحَبِيبُ بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ؟
questions.a: He sat in the circle.

questions.q: What did Ahmad wish for?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَمَنَّى أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: That the majlis were long.

questions.q: Which word in line 4 shows a wish?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ٤ تُظْهِرُ التَّمَنِّيَ؟
questions.a: لَيْتَ

questions.q: Why did he wish it?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَمَنَّى ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: Because the time is short.

questions.q: Who is still sitting?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ مَا زَالَ جَالِسًا؟
questions.a: The students.

questions.q: Why did Ahmad become happy?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا صَارَ أَحْمَدُ سَعِيدًا؟
questions.a: Because the Habib heard the question.

questions.q: True or false? The time is long.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ الْوَقْتُ طَوِيلٌ.
questions.a: False: it is short.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy read a small matn with the Habib. The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.

questions.q: In the second new line, which word is a sister of كَانَ, and what ending does the word after the noun take?
questions.a: أَصْبَحَ (became); سَهْلًا takes ـًا.

questions.q: Which word is a sister of إِنَّ, and what ending does the noun after it take?
questions.a: لَكِنَّ (but); الدَّرْسَ takes ـَ.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The matn became easy.
questions.a: أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا.

translate.en: The boy became happy after the lesson.

translate.ar: مَا زَالَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ.
translate.en: The students are still in the mosque after the Rātib.

translate.ar: لَعَلَّ الْحَبِيبَ يَجْلِسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ.
translate.en: Perhaps the Habib will sit in the circle after the prayer.
The house is far, but the ribāṭ is near.
As if the muṣḥaf were a light in the mosque.
The guests were happy in the ribāṭ that evening.

translate.ar: لَيْسَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا لَكِنَّ الْوَقْتَ قَصِيرٌ.
translate.en: The lesson is not difficult, but the time is short.
The students are still remembering God.
Ahmad was a student and became a teacher.

translate.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
translate.en: Thus God makes His signs clear to you, so that you may be guided.

translate.ar: أَصْبَحْنَا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ ، وَعَلَى كَلِمَةِ الْإِخْلَاصِ  فَأَبْشِرْ ؛ فَإِنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَبْسُطُ لَكَ أَجْنِحَتَهَا إِذَا مَشَيْتَ
translate.en: We have entered the morning on the natural way of Islam and on the word of sincerity. Rejoice! For the angels spread their wings for you when you walk.
The student became a teacher in the school.
I know that God Most High is One.
The student became a scholar.
Perhaps God will guide us.
If only knowledge were near.
The Habib is still in the ribāṭ after the Rātib.
translate.ar: مَا زَالَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ.

translate.en: Knowledge is a light, but the lesson is difficult.
We entered the evening in the mosque.
We entered the morning happy before the lesson.

readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقُولُ فِي أَيِّ حَالٍ فَعَلَ؟

lines.ar: ثُمَّ اجْلِسْ لِلْوُضُوءِ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ عَلَى مَوْضِعٍ مُرْتَفِعٍ
lines.en: Then sit for the ablution, facing the qibla, on a raised place.

lines.ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَرِحْنِي رَائِحَةَ الْجَنَّةِ وَأَنْتَ عَنِّي رَاضٍ
lines.en: O God, let me smell the fragrance of Paradise while You are pleased with me.

lines.ar: فَتَأَدَّبْ أَيُّهَا الْمِسْكِينُ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللهِ تَعَالَى
lines.en: So be courteous, poor soul, outwardly and inwardly, before God Most High.

glossary.en: let me smell (grant me the scent)
the two hands of (بَيْنَ يَدَيِ = before)

passages.ar: ثُمَّ اجْلِسْ لِلْوُضُوءِ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ عَلَى مَوْضِعٍ مُرْتَفِعٍ اللَّهُمَّ أَرِحْنِي رَائِحَةَ الْجَنَّةِ وَأَنْتَ عَنِّي رَاضٍ فَتَأَدَّبْ أَيُّهَا الْمِسْكِينُ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللهِ تَعَالَى
passages.en: Then sit for the ablution, facing the qibla, on a raised place. O God, let me smell the fragrance of Paradise while You are pleased with me. So be courteous, poor soul, outwardly and inwardly, before God Most High.

lines.ar: جَاءَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ مُسْرِعًا.
lines.en: Ahmad came to the ribāṭ hurrying.

lines.ar: كَانَ الْحَبِيبُ جَالِسًا فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
lines.en: The Habib was sitting in the circle.

lines.ar: دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ وَهُوَ يُسَلِّمُ.
lines.en: Ahmad entered, giving salām.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِمَاذَا جِئْتَ مُسْرِعًا؟
lines.en: The Habib said: Why did you come hurrying?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: كَانَ الْوَقْتُ قَصِيرًا.
lines.en: Ahmad said: The time was short.

lines.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ قَبْلَ الدَّرْسِ وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ.
lines.en: Ahmad sat before the lesson, happy.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ خَرَجَ رَاضِيًا.
lines.en: And after the lesson he left, pleased.

passages.ar: جَاءَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ مُسْرِعًا. كَانَ الْحَبِيبُ جَالِسًا فِي الْحَلْقَةِ. دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ وَهُوَ يُسَلِّمُ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِمَاذَا جِئْتَ مُسْرِعًا؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: كَانَ الْوَقْتُ قَصِيرًا. جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ قَبْلَ الدَّرْسِ وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ. وَبَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ خَرَجَ رَاضِيًا.
passages.en: Ahmad came to the ribāṭ hurrying. The Habib was sitting in the circle. Ahmad entered, giving salām. The Habib said: Why did you come hurrying? Ahmad said: The time was short. Ahmad sat before the lesson, happy. And after the lesson he left, pleased.

passages.en: The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla. And the Habib was pleased with him.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Guidance for the ablution, with a supplication (duʿāʾ), from Bidāyat al-Hidāya of Imam al-Ghazālī.

questions.q: Line 1: what is the reader told to sit for?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: لِمَاذَا يَجْلِسُ؟
questions.a: The ablution (لِلْوُضُوءِ).

questions.q: Line 1: which way does he face?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: إِلَى أَيِّ جِهَةٍ يَتَّجِهُ؟
questions.a: The qibla.

questions.q: Line 1: which word tells in what state he sits?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُبَيِّنُ حَالَهُ؟
questions.a: مُسْتَقْبِلَ (facing).

questions.q: Line 1: on what kind of place does he sit?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: عَلَى أَيِّ مَوْضِعٍ يَجْلِسُ؟
questions.a: On a raised place (مَوْضِعٍ مُرْتَفِعٍ).

questions.q: Line 2: what does he ask for?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَاذَا يَطْلُبُ؟
questions.a: The fragrance of Paradise (رَائِحَةَ الْجَنَّةِ).

questions.q: Line 2: in what state does he ask to smell it?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: فِي أَيِّ حَالٍ يَطْلُبُ ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: While God is pleased with him (وَأَنْتَ عَنِّي رَاضٍ).

questions.q: Line 3: which two words are states (ḥāl) and say how he should be courteous?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ هُمَا حَالَانِ تُبَيِّنَانِ كَيْفَ يَتَأَدَّبُ؟
questions.a: ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا (outwardly and inwardly).

questions.q: True or false? The text tells him to stand for the ablution.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ يَقُولُ النَّصُّ: قُمْ لِلْوُضُوءِ.
questions.a: False: he sits.

questions.q: وَأَنْتَ عَنِّي رَاضٍ is a ḥāl clause. What does it add to the sentence?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَزِيدُ جُمْلَةُ «وَأَنْتَ عَنِّي رَاضٍ» عَلَى الْجُمْلَةِ؟
questions.a: It says in what state: “while You are pleased with me”. A ḥāl clause is وَ + a pronoun + a statement.

questions.q: Why does مُسْتَقْبِلَ end in ـَ, and why does الْقِبْلَةِ after it end in ـِ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا آخِرُ «مُسْتَقْبِلَ» ـَ وَآخِرُ «الْقِبْلَةِ» ـِ؟
questions.a: مُسْتَقْبِلَ is a ḥāl, so ـَ. الْقِبْلَةِ is the “of” partner of مُسْتَقْبِلَ (as in an iḍāfa), so ـِ.

questions.q: How did Ahmad come to the ribāṭ?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ جَاءَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ؟
questions.a: Hurrying.

questions.q: What was the Habib doing?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَانَ الْحَبِيبُ يَفْعَلُ؟
questions.a: Sitting in the circle.

questions.q: Line 3: in what state did Ahmad enter?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: فِي أَيِّ حَالٍ دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: While giving salām (greeting).

questions.q: What did the Habib ask?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ؟
questions.a: Why he had come hurrying.

questions.q: What was Ahmad’s answer?
questions.q_ar: مَا جَوَابُ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: The time was short.

questions.q: Line 6: in what state did Ahmad sit?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٦: فِي أَيِّ حَالٍ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: Happy (وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ).

questions.q: Line 7: which word tells how he left?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٧: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُبَيِّنُ كَيْفَ خَرَجَ؟
questions.a: رَاضِيًا (pleased).

questions.q: Which two lines contain a ḥāl clause with وَ + a pronoun?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرَيْنِ فِيهِمَا جُمْلَةُ حَالٍ بِالْوَاوِ وَالضَّمِيرِ؟
questions.a: Lines 3 and 6.

questions.q: In line 1 مُسْرِعًا is a ḥāl, but in line 2 جَالِسًا is not. Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «مُسْرِعًا» حَالٌ فِي السَّطْرِ ١ وَ«جَالِسًا» لَيْسَ حَالًا فِي السَّطْرِ ٢؟
questions.a: In line 2 it is the statement after كَانَ: the sentence is not complete without it. In line 1 it only says the state.

questions.q: After وَهُوَ in line 3 and in line 6: what kind of word comes?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَأْتِي بَعْدَ «وَهُوَ» فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ٣ وَ٦؟
questions.a: Line 3: a verb (يُسَلِّمُ). Line 6: a noun (سَعِيدٌ), the statement.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla. And the Habib was pleased with him.

questions.q: Which words tell the boy’s state (the ḥāl) in the first new line?
questions.a: مُسْرِعًا (hurrying) and مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ (facing the qibla)

questions.q: What ending does a ḥāl take?
questions.a: The accusative ending: ـًا or ـَ.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy came hurrying.
questions.a: جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ مُسْرِعًا.

translate.en: The student came to the lesson hurrying.
The imam prayed standing in the mosque.

translate.ar: خَرَجَ الْحَبِيبُ مِنَ الرِّبَاطِ وَهُوَ يَذْكُرُ اللهَ.
translate.en: The Habib left the ribāṭ remembering God.

translate.ar: جَاءَ الْأَبُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ رَاكِبًا وَرَجَعَ رَاضِيًا.
translate.en: The father came home riding and went back pleased.

translate.ar: دَخَلَتِ الْبِنْتُ الْمَدْرَسَةَ وَهِيَ تَحْمِلُ كِتَابًا.
translate.en: The girl entered the school carrying a book.

translate.ar: جَلَسَ الطُّلَّابُ بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ وَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ.
translate.en: The students sat after the Rātib, listening.

translate.ar: رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ الْحَبِيبَ كَانَ رَاضِيًا.
translate.en: Ahmad returned happy because the Habib was pleased.
Perhaps the student will come hurrying.

translate.ar: جَاءَ الطُّلَّابُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ مُسْرِعِينَ وَرَجَعُوا رَاضِينَ.
translate.en: The students came to the ribāṭ hurrying and went back pleased.
So he left it, afraid and watching.

translate.ar: ثُمَّ اجْلِسْ لِلْوُضُوءِ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ عَلَى مَوْضِعٍ مُرْتَفِعٍ  اللَّهُمَّ أَرِحْنِي رَائِحَةَ الْجَنَّةِ وَأَنْتَ عَنِّي رَاضٍ
translate.en: Then sit for the ablution, facing the qibla, on a raised place.  O God, let me smell the fragrance of Paradise while You are pleased with me.

translate.ar: وَمَنْ تَابَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ وَهُوَ مُصِرٌّ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ عَازِمٌ عَلَى الْعَوْدِ إِلَيْهِ فَلَا تَوْبَةَ لَهُ
translate.en: Whoever repents of some sin while still persisting in it, or intending to return to it, has not truly repented.

translate.ar: وَقَدْ كَانَتِ الْأُمَمُ السَّالِفَةُ يُبْعَثُ فِيهِمُ النَّبِيُّ عَلَى إِثْرِ النَّبِيِّ مُجَدِّدًا لِمَا انْدَرَسَ مِنْ دِينِهِمْ
translate.en: The earlier nations had a prophet sent among them after each prophet, renewing what had faded of their religion.
The student came to the lesson hurrying.
The imam prayed standing.
The Habib left the mosque remembering God.
translate.ar: خَرَجَ الْحَبِيبُ مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ وَهُوَ يَذْكُرُ اللهَ.

translate.en: The boy returned to the house pleased.
alt: رَجَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَهُوَ رَاضٍ.

translate.en: The students came carrying the books.
Ahmad came to the ribāṭ riding.
The girl left the house laughing.
The guest came while the Habib was sitting.

readings.title_en: How much, how, why?
readings.question_en: Some words ending in ـًا are not the doer or the thing acted on. What are they telling me?
readings.question_ar: كَلِمَاتٌ تَنْتَهِي بِتَنْوِينِ فَتْحٍ وَلَيْسَتْ فَاعِلًا وَلَا مَفْعُولًا بِهِ. مَاذَا تَقُولُ لِي؟

passages.intro_en: A short text: a morning of dhikr. Read it aloud, then answer.

lines.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: After the prayer Ahmad sat in the mosque and remembered God a great deal.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.
lines.en: And he said: Glory be to God and praise be to God.

lines.ar: وَسَأَلَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: كَمْ مَرَّةً ذَكَرْتَ اللَّهَ؟
lines.en: And the Habib asked him: How many times did you remember God?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: ذَكَرْتُ اللَّهَ عِشْرِينَ مَرَّةً.
lines.en: Ahmad said: I remembered God twenty times.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُذْكُرِ اللَّهَ خَوْفًا مِنْهُ وَمَحَبَّةً لَهُ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Remember God out of fear of Him and love for Him.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
lines.en: Then Ahmad went to the rawḥa, seeking knowledge.

lines.ar: وَقَرَأَ هُنَاكَ عِشْرِينَ صَفْحَةً مِنَ الْكِتَابِ.
lines.en: And there he read twenty pages of the book.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا، وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ حَمْدًا كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: And he returned to the house happy, and said to his mother: Praise be to God, much praise.

passages.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا. وَقَالَ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. وَسَأَلَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: كَمْ مَرَّةً ذَكَرْتَ اللَّهَ؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: ذَكَرْتُ اللَّهَ عِشْرِينَ مَرَّةً. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُذْكُرِ اللَّهَ خَوْفًا مِنْهُ وَمَحَبَّةً لَهُ. ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ. وَقَرَأَ هُنَاكَ عِشْرِينَ صَفْحَةً مِنَ الْكِتَابِ. وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا، وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ حَمْدًا كَثِيرًا.
passages.en: After the prayer Ahmad sat in the mosque and remembered God a great deal. And he said: Glory be to God and praise be to God. And the Habib asked him: How many times did you remember God? Ahmad said: I remembered God twenty times. The Habib said: Remember God out of fear of Him and love for Him. Then Ahmad went to the rawḥa, seeking knowledge. And there he read twenty pages of the book. And he returned to the house happy, and said to his mother: Praise be to God, much praise.

lines.en: O you who believe, remember God with much remembrance.

passages.ar: يَٰأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اذْكُرُواْ اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا
passages.en: O you who believe, remember God with much remembrance.

lines.ar: مِنْ وَاجِبٍ لِلهِ عِشْرُونَ صِفَهْ

lines.ar: ثُمَّ اغْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ ثَلَاثًا قَبْلَ أَنْ تُدْخِلَهُمَا الْإِنَاءَ

passages.ar: ثُمَّ اغْسِلْ يَدَيْكَ ثَلَاثًا قَبْلَ أَنْ تُدْخِلَهُمَا الْإِنَاءَ ثُمَّ خُذْ غَرْفَةً لِفَمِكَ وَتَمَضْمَضْ بِهَا ثَلَاثًا

lines.ar: ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
lines.en: The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
