passages.ar: ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا. قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
passages.en: The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times. The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.

questions.q: Who sat in the mosque after the prayer?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ؟
questions.a: Ahmad.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And he said: Glory be to God and praise be to God.

questions.q: What does the Habib ask in line 3?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَسْأَلُ الْحَبِيبُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ؟
questions.a: How many times he remembered God.

questions.q: How many times did Ahmad remember God?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً ذَكَرَ أَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ؟
questions.a: Twenty times (عِشْرِينَ مَرَّةً).

questions.q: In line 1, which words say how much he remembered God?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ، أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَقُولَانِ كَمْ ذَكَرَ اللَّهَ؟
questions.a: ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا: a great deal.

questions.q: Why does the Habib say to remember God? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ «اُذْكُرِ اللَّهَ»؟
questions.a: Out of fear of Him and love for Him (خَوْفًا مِنْهُ وَمَحَبَّةً لَهُ).

questions.q: Why did Ahmad go to the rawḥa? Which word says why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى السَّبَبِ؟
questions.a: To seek knowledge. طَلَبًا.

questions.q: True or false: Ahmad read three pages at the rawḥa.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ ثَلَاثَ صَفَحَاتٍ.
questions.a: False. He read twenty pages (عِشْرِينَ صَفْحَةً).

questions.q: Put in order: (a) he read twenty pages; (b) he sat in the mosque; (c) he went home.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) قَرَأَ عِشْرِينَ صَفْحَةً (ب) جَلَسَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ (ج) رَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
questions.a: b, a, c

questions.q: Find the word that means “happy”. Is it the doer or a state (ḥāl)?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «happy». هَلْ هِيَ الْفَاعِلُ أَمْ حَالٌ؟
questions.a: سَعِيدًا: a state (ḥāl): he came back happy.

questions.q: From which verb does ذِكْرًا come? What does it add to the sentence?
questions.q_ar: مِنْ أَيِّ فِعْلٍ ذِكْرًا؟ مَاذَا تُضِيفُ إِلَى الْجُمْلَةِ؟
questions.a: From ذَكَرَ. The verb’s own noun with كَثِيرًا says how much.

questions.q: Why is it صَفْحَةً (singular) and not صَفَحَاتٍ after عِشْرِينَ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا صَفْحَةً مُفْرَدَةٌ بَعْدَ عِشْرِينَ؟
questions.a: After twenty the counted noun is singular and accusative (tamyīz).

questions.q: Translate the verse.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ.
questions.a: O you who believe, remember God with much remembrance.

questions.q: Which two words say how much? From which verb?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَقُولَانِ كَمْ؟ مِنْ أَيِّ فِعْلٍ؟
questions.a: ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا: much remembrance; from اُذْكُرُوا (ذَكَرَ).

questions.q: Who is spoken to?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْمُخَاطَبُونَ؟
questions.a: Those who believe.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A verse of the Qur’an, sūrat al-Aḥzāb (33:41).

questions.q: In the verse, this word describes ذِكْرًا. How does it end, and why?
questions.q_ar: هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ تَصِفُ ذِكْرًا. كَيْفَ تَنْتَهِي وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: Like ذِكْرًا: ـًا, accusative.

questions.q: Translate the verse.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْبَيْتَ.
questions.a: And now, know that it is obligatory to know: of what is due to God, twenty attributes.

questions.q: How many attributes are due to God?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ صِفَةً وَاجِبَةً لِلَّهِ؟
questions.a: Twenty.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A verse of a creed (a short matn) by al-Marzūqī: ʿAqīdat al-ʿAwāmm.

questions.q: What does وَبَعْدُ mean, and where do we often meet it?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى وَبَعْدُ؟ وَأَيْنَ نَلْقَاهَا غَالِبًا؟
questions.a: “And now (after this)”. It begins the main part of a book or letter.

questions.q: The noun after عِشْرُونَ is صِفَهْ (singular). What is it called? Why is it spelled with ـهْ and not ـةٌ?
questions.q_ar: مَا اسْمُ الْكَلِمَةِ الَّتِي بَعْدَ «عِشْرُونَ»؟ لِمَاذَا تُكْتَبُ بِـ ـهْ؟
questions.a: The tamyīz (what is counted). The verse is spelled as it is pronounced at the end of a line, with a stop.

questions.q: Translate the first line.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Then wash your hands three times before putting them into the vessel.

questions.q: How many times must the hands be washed? Which word says so?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً تُغْسَلُ الْيَدَانِ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: Three times: ثَلَاثًا.

questions.q: What is washed in line 1? What is rinsed in line 2?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُغْسَلُ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟ وَمَاذَا يُمَضْمَضُ فِي الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: The hands (يَدَيْكَ); the mouth (فَمِكَ).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Practical counsel (steps of ablution) from Bidāyat al-Hidāya of al-Ghazālī.

questions.q: ثَلَاثًا is not “three” (a number to count with). What is it here?
questions.q_ar: ثَلَاثًا هُنَا لَيْسَتْ عَدَدًا لِلْمَعْدُودِ. مَا هِيَ؟
questions.a: The absolute object of number: “three times”, how often.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times. The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.

questions.q: Which words tell how many times?
questions.a: ثَلَاثًا (three times) and مَرَّتَيْنِ (twice)

questions.q: Which word gives the reason in the second new line? What ending does it have?
questions.a: طَلَبًا (seeking): ـًا

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy remembered Allah a great deal.
questions.a: ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ عِشْرِينَ صَفْحَةً فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
translate.en: The boy read twenty pages in the ribāṭ.

translate.ar: ذَكَرَ الطُّلَّابُ اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ.
translate.en: The students remembered God a great deal after the prayer.
How many times did you visit the Habib?

translate.ar: جَاءَ عُمَرُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
translate.en: Umar came to the majlis seeking knowledge.
She is better than me in character.

translate.ar: سَبَّحَ أَحْمَدُ ثَلَاثًا وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ مَرَّتَيْنِ.
translate.en: Ahmad glorified God three times and praised God twice.

translate.ar: صَبَرَ الرَّجُلُ صَبْرًا جَمِيلًا خَوْفًا مِنَ اللَّهِ.
translate.en: The man was patient, with a fine patience, out of fear of God.

translate.ar: غَسَلَ الْوَلَدُ فَمَهُ وَيَدَيْهِ ثَلَاثًا قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ.
translate.en: The boy washed his mouth and his hands three times before the prayer.
The prayer is obligatory for every Muslim.

translate.ar: عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا فِي الْحَلْقَةِ. ذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا، ثُمَّ قَرَأُوا الدَّرْسَ.
translate.en: Twenty students are in the circle. They remembered God a great deal, then they read the lesson.
Ahmad read twenty pages in the library.
translate.ar: قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ عِشْرِينَ صَفْحَةً فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ.

translate.en: The student remembered God a great deal.
How many times did you read the lesson?
Umar went to the mosque seeking knowledge.
translate.ar: ذَهَبَ عُمَرُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
alt: ذَهَبَ عُمَرُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ ابْتِغَاءَ الْعِلْمِ.

translate.en: The Habib said: Remember God out of love for Him.
translate.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُذْكُرِ اللَّهَ مَحَبَّةً لَهُ.

translate.en: The boy glorified God three times.
The boy washed his hands three times.
She is better than me in character.
I praised God twice and thanked my mother twenty times.
translate.ar: حَمِدْتُ اللَّهَ مَرَّتَيْنِ وَشَكَرْتُ أُمِّي عِشْرِينَ مَرَّةً.

readings.title_en: Two objects; “no … at all”
readings.question_en: Some verbs act on two things at once. And what does لَا do before a noun, as in لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ?
readings.question_ar: بَعْضُ الْأَفْعَالِ يَقَعُ عَلَى شَيْئَيْنِ. وَمَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «لَا» قَبْلَ الِاسْمِ فِي «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ»؟

passages.intro_en: A short text: the Habib’s book. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: بَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ أَعْطَى الْحَبِيبُ أَحْمَدَ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا.
lines.en: After the lesson the Habib gave Ahmad a small book.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ لَهُ: خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِيَمِينِكَ.
lines.en: And he said to him: Take the book with your right hand.

lines.ar: ظَنَّ أَحْمَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا.
lines.en: Ahmad thought the book difficult.

lines.ar: فَقَرَأَهُ وَوَجَدَهُ سَهْلًا.
lines.en: So he read it and found it easy.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ: لَا شَكَّ، هَذَا كِتَابٌ جَيِّدٌ.
lines.en: And he said: There is no doubt, this is a good book.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَظُنَّ الْعِلْمَ صَعْبًا، فَاللَّهُ يَجْعَلُ الْعِلْمَ سَهْلًا لِمَنْ طَلَبَهُ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Do not think knowledge difficult; God makes knowledge easy for whoever seeks it.

lines.ar: وَلَا كِتَابَ عِنْدَ عُمَرَ، فَقَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَهُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ.
lines.en: And Umar had no book, so Ahmad read with him in the library.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا.
lines.en: And Ahmad returned to the house happy.

passages.ar: بَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ أَعْطَى الْحَبِيبُ أَحْمَدَ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا. وَقَالَ لَهُ: خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِيَمِينِكَ. ظَنَّ أَحْمَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا. فَقَرَأَهُ وَوَجَدَهُ سَهْلًا. وَقَالَ: لَا شَكَّ، هَذَا كِتَابٌ جَيِّدٌ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَظُنَّ الْعِلْمَ صَعْبًا، فَاللَّهُ يَجْعَلُ الْعِلْمَ سَهْلًا لِمَنْ طَلَبَهُ. وَلَا كِتَابَ عِنْدَ عُمَرَ، فَقَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَهُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ. وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا.
passages.en: After the lesson the Habib gave Ahmad a small book. And he said to him: Take the book with your right hand. Ahmad thought the book difficult. So he read it and found it easy. And he said: There is no doubt, this is a good book. The Habib said: Do not think knowledge difficult; God makes knowledge easy for whoever seeks it. And Umar had no book, so Ahmad read with him in the library. And Ahmad returned to the house happy.

passages.intro_en: A verse: Qur’an 47:19 (the first words). Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Qurʾān 47:19, words 1–6, text extracted by program from quran.json (Tanzil, Uthmani text), as in all lessons.

lines.ar: فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
lines.en: So know that there is no god but God.

passages.ar: فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ
passages.en: So know that there is no god but God.

passages.intro_en: A ḥadīth: a word from a treasure of Paradise (three lines of a short dialogue). Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: al-Bukhārī, al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Fatḥ al-Bārī numbering, Dār al-Shaʿb, Cairo, 1st ed. 1407/1987, 9 vols (Shamela 1782), vol. 5 p. 170; ./sh verify 1782: EXACT (p. 5/170 for the lines of the dialogue; the last line also occurs at 1/159 and elsewhere in the print: it is the end of this same ḥadīth at 5/170); vowels as in the source, orthography normalised (لاَ → لَا، إِلاَّ → إِلَّا). Lines 3, 4 and 5 of the record are shown (the opening address, lines 1–2, is not used).

lines.ar: قَالَ : أَلَا أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى كَلِمَةٍ مِنْ كَنْزٍ مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْجَنَّةِ ؟
lines.en: He said: “Shall I not guide you to a word from a treasure of the treasures of Paradise?”

lines.ar: قُلْتُ : بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فِدَاكَ أَبِي وَأُمِّي
lines.en: I said: “Yes, O Messenger of God ﷺ, may my father and mother be your ransom.”

lines.ar: قَالَ : لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
lines.en: He said: “There is no power and no might except through God.”

passages.ar: قَالَ : أَلَا أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى كَلِمَةٍ مِنْ كَنْزٍ مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْجَنَّةِ ؟ قُلْتُ : بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فِدَاكَ أَبِي وَأُمِّي قَالَ : لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
passages.en: He said: “Shall I not guide you to a word from a treasure of the treasures of Paradise?” I said: “Yes, O Messenger of God ﷺ, may my father and mother be your ransom.” He said: “There is no power and no might except through God.”

passages.intro_en: A line from the Imam’s letter: God gave … Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād (Jāmiʿ al-Mukātabāt wa-l-Waṣāyā wa-l-Kalimāt wa-l-Qaṣāʾid), vol. 1
passages.cite: al-Ḥaddād, Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, al-musammāt Jāmiʿ al-Mukātabāt wa-l-Waṣāyā wa-l-Kalimāt wa-l-Qaṣāʾid …, vol. 1, Dār al-Sanābil / Dār al-Ḥāwī (collated edition; year not seen on the title page); scan on the Extreme SSD (Ba_Alawi_Hadrami_Collection/Authors/Imam_Abdallah_al-Haddad/works-by/مكاتبات الإمام الحداد 1.pdf), p. 38 of the print, read from the page images; vowelled for learners.

lines.ar: فَأَعْطَى اللهُ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةَ الْكَرِيمَةَ عَلَيْهِ بِكَرَامَةِ نَبِيِّهَا ﷺ أَنْ يَبْعَثَ لَهَا
lines.en: So God gave this community, honoured by Him for the sake of its Prophet, peace be upon him, that He would raise up for it …

passages.ar: فَأَعْطَى اللهُ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةَ الْكَرِيمَةَ عَلَيْهِ بِكَرَامَةِ نَبِيِّهَا ﷺ أَنْ يَبْعَثَ لَهَا
passages.en: So God gave this community, honoured by Him for the sake of its Prophet, peace be upon him, that He would raise up for it …

passages.intro_en: A duʿāʾ with two things acted on. Read it, then answer.
passages.cite: Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī, Bidāyat al-Hidāya; Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, 53.mdb), the same text as Shamela 3.28 id 5285 (whose card says it is auto-numbered and does not match the print): so the page is the digital page of this copy, p. 32, not a printed page; edition not identified. Consonants checked against the copy (./sh verify 5285: EXACT p. 3); vowelled for learners.

lines.ar: وَقُلْ عِنْدَ غَسْلِ الْيَدِ الْيُمْنَى : أَعْطِنِي كِتَابِي بِيَمِينِي
lines.en: And say when washing the right hand: “Give me my book in my right hand.”

passages.ar: وَقُلْ عِنْدَ غَسْلِ الْيَدِ الْيُمْنَى : أَعْطِنِي كِتَابِي بِيَمِينِي
passages.en: And say when washing the right hand: “Give me my book in my right hand.”

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 105-106 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: أَعْطَى الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا.
lines.en: The Habib gave the boy a small book.

lines.ar: ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
lines.en: The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.

passages.ar: أَعْطَى الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا. ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
passages.en: The Habib gave the boy a small book. The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.

questions.q: What did the Habib give Ahmad, and to whom?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا أَعْطَى الْحَبِيبُ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: A small book, to Ahmad.

questions.q: How should Ahmad take the book? Which word says so?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يَأْخُذُ أَحْمَدُ الْكِتَابَ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: With his right hand: بِيَمِينِكَ.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: Ahmad thought the book difficult.

questions.q: What did Ahmad find when he read the book?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا وَجَدَ أَحْمَدُ حِينَ قَرَأَ الْكِتَابَ؟
questions.a: That it was easy (وَجَدَهُ سَهْلًا).

questions.q: What does لَا شَكَّ mean? Who says it?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى لَا شَكَّ؟ مَنْ يَقُولُهَا؟
questions.a: “There is no doubt.” Ahmad says it.

questions.q: What does the Habib tell Ahmad not to think?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ بَعْدَ «لَا تَظُنَّ»؟
questions.a: That knowledge is difficult.

questions.q: Who makes knowledge easy, and for whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَجْعَلُ الْعِلْمَ سَهْلًا؟ وَلِمَنْ؟
questions.a: God, for whoever seeks it.

questions.q: True or false: Umar had a book.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: عِنْدَ عُمَرَ كِتَابٌ.
questions.a: False. لَا كِتَابَ عِنْدَ عُمَرَ: he had no book.

questions.q: What did Ahmad do with Umar? Where?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ؟ وَأَيْنَ؟
questions.a: He read with him, in the library.

questions.q: Which verbs in lines 1–6 act on two things? Name three.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي السُّطُورِ ١–٦ يَقَعُ عَلَى شَيْئَيْنِ؟ اُذْكُرْ ثَلَاثَةً.
questions.a: أَعْطَى، ظَنَّ، وَجَدَ، يَجْعَلُ (any three).

questions.q: What small sentence is hidden in الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا? How did its endings change?
questions.q_ar: أَيَّةُ جُمْلَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ فِي «الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا»؟ كَيْفَ تَغَيَّرَتْ نِهَايَتَاهَا؟
questions.a: الْكِتَابُ صَعْبٌ: ـُ became ـَ, and ـٌ became ـًا.

questions.q: Why is it لَا كِتَابَ and not لَا كِتَابٌ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا نَقُولُ «لَا كِتَابَ» وَلَا نَقُولُ «لَا كِتَابٌ»؟
questions.a: After لَا that denies the whole kind the noun has fatḥa and no tanwīn.

questions.q: Translate the words.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْكَلِمَاتِ.
questions.a: So know that there is no god but God.

questions.q: Which word is the لَا of the whole kind? What ending does the noun after it have?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ «لَا» الَّتِي تَنْفِي الْجِنْسَ؟ كَيْفَ يَنْتَهِي الِاسْمُ بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: لَا; the noun إِلَٰهَ ends in fatḥa, with no tanwīn.

questions.q: What kind of word is this first word, and what does it say?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟ مَاذَا تَقُولُ؟
questions.a: A command (from عَلِمَ): so know!

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A verse of the Qur’an, sūrat Muḥammad (47:19).

questions.q: What does this word do after the denial لَا إِلَٰهَ?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ بَعْدَ نَفْيِ لَا إِلَهَ؟
questions.a: It says who is left out of the denial: nothing is a god except God.

questions.q: Translate the first line.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: He said: “Shall I not guide you to a word from a treasure of the treasures of Paradise?”

questions.q: What does كَنْز mean? Find it in the first line.
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى كَنْز؟ جِدْهُ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ.
questions.a: Treasure.

questions.q: Which words are the nouns after لَا? What ending do they have?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ بَعْدَ لَا؟ كَيْفَ تَنْتَهِيَانِ؟
questions.a: حَوْلَ and قُوَّةَ: fatḥa, no tanwīn.
questions.ref_ar: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ

questions.q: What is the “word from the treasure”? Translate it.
questions.q_ar: مَا الْكَلِمَةُ مِنَ الْكَنْزِ؟ تَرْجِمْهَا.
questions.a: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ: There is no power and no might except through God.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth (a short dialogue), from Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, no. 4205.

questions.q: Line 2: what does the Companion answer?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَاذَا يُجِيبُ الصَّحَابِيُّ؟
questions.a: “Yes, O Messenger of God ﷺ”, and he offers his parents as a ransom (فِدَاكَ أَبِي وَأُمِّي): a way of showing love and eagerness.

questions.q: Who says line 1, and who says line 2?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقُولُ السَّطْرَ ١؟ وَمَنْ يَقُولُ السَّطْرَ ٢؟
questions.a: Line 1: the Prophet ﷺ speaks. Line 2: the Companion answers. Line 3: the Prophet ﷺ gives the word.

questions.q: Translate the line (the glosses help).
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ.
questions.a: So God gave this community, honoured by Him for the sake of its Prophet, peace be upon him, that He would raise up for it …

questions.q: Who gave? Who received?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ أَعْطَى؟ مَنْ أَخَذَ؟
questions.a: God gave; this community (الْأُمَّةَ) received.

questions.q: Why does الْأُمَّةَ end in fatḥa?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي الْأُمَّةَ بِفَتْحَةٍ؟
questions.a: It is acted on by أَعْطَى (the one who receives).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A letter (mukātaba) of Imam al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: What does the ending ـهَا in نَبِيِّهَا stand for?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ ـهَا فِي نَبِيِّهَا؟
questions.a: The community (“its Prophet”).

questions.q: Translate the line (the glosses help).
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ.
questions.a: And say when washing the right hand: “Give me my book in my right hand.”

questions.q: Which two things does أَعْطِنِي act on? Say who and what.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ شَيْئَيْنِ يَقَعُ عَلَيْهِمَا أَعْطِنِي؟
questions.a: ـنِي (me, the one who receives) and كِتَابِي (my book, the thing given).

questions.q: What does يَمِين mean here, and what do you say it with?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى يَمِين؟ وَبِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: Right hand: “give me my book in my right hand”.

questions.q: When is this said, and what kind of text is it?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى تُقَالُ هَذِهِ الدَّعْوَةُ؟ وَمَا نَوْعُ النَّصِّ؟
questions.a: When washing the right hand in wuḍūʾ; a short duʿāʾ in al-Ghazālī’s Bidāyat al-Hidāya.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib gave the boy a small book. The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.

questions.q: In the first new line, which two words are acted on (both take ـَ / ـًا)?
questions.a: الْوَلَدَ (the boy) and كِتَابًا (a book)

questions.q: In لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ, what does لَا do, and what ending do حَوْلَ and قُوَّةَ have?
questions.a: It denies the whole kind: no power at all, no strength at all. The endings are ـَ.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The Habib gave the boy a small book.
questions.a: أَعْطَى الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا.

translate.en: The teacher gave the student a new pen.

translate.ar: ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْمَسْجِدَ بَعِيدًا، لَكِنَّهُ وَجَدَهُ قَرِيبًا.
translate.en: The boy thought the mosque far, but he found it near.
There is no one in the mosque now.
The teacher made the lesson easy for the students.

translate.ar: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
translate.en: There is no power and no strength except through God.
The father gave my brother a gift.

translate.ar: لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَلَا مِثْلَ لَهُ.
translate.en: He has no partner and nothing is like Him.

translate.ar: أَعْطَى الْحَبِيبُ أَحْمَدَ كِتَابًا. ظَنَّهُ صَعْبًا، فَوَجَدَهُ سَهْلًا. وَلَا شَكَّ أَنَّهُ كِتَابٌ جَيِّدٌ.
translate.en: The Habib gave Ahmad a book. He thought it difficult, and found it easy. And there is no doubt that it is a good book.
The Habib gave the student a book.
Ahmad thought the lesson difficult.
He found the book easy.
There is no doubt.
There is no man in the house.
There is no god but God.
God made the sun a light.
There is no book on the desk, so Ahmad gave Umar a book.
translate.ar: لَا كِتَابَ عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ، فَأَعْطَى أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ كِتَابًا.
alt: لَا كِتَابَ عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ فَأَعْطَى أَحْمَدُ عُمَرَ كِتَابًا.

readings.title_en: Reading day 4: a list page
readings.question_en: A page that lists things: what is being counted, and which is the first, the second, the third?
readings.question_ar: مَاذَا تَعُدُّ هَذِهِ الصَّفْحَةُ؟ وَمَا الْأَوَّلُ وَمَا الثَّانِي وَمَا الثَّالِثُ؟

passages.intro_en: Read the list page: the obligations of ablution. Read it aloud once, then answer.
passages.source: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa of Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī (1069–1145 AH)
passages.cite: Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī, al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa, Dār Maqām al-Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr, Ḥawṭat Aḥmad b. Zayn, Ḥaḍramawt (year not given on the title page); Shamela Master Library copy 'الرسالة الجامعة' (Bafaqih Sufi library, 491.mdb; same work as TLNOOR 712, an epub), pp. 2–3 of the copy (9 pp; the copy's own page counter, printed pagination not given). Abridged (the first line, the pillars of Islam, is omitted). The source is partly vowelled; vowelled for learners, every letter as in the copy (copy misprint فُرُوضِ corrected to فُرُوضُ).

lines.ar: فُرُوضُ الْوُضُوءِ سِتَّةٌ
lines.en: The obligations of ablution are six:

lines.ar: الْأَوَّلُ : النِّيَّةُ
lines.en: The first: the intention.

lines.ar: الثَّانِي: غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ
lines.en: The second: washing the face.

lines.ar: الثَّالِثُ: غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ إِلَى الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ
lines.en: The third: washing the hands up to the elbows.

lines.ar: الرَّابِعُ: مَسْحُ شَيْءٍ مِنْ بَشَرَةِ الرَّأْسِ أَوْ شَعَرٍ فِي حَدِّهِ
lines.en: The fourth: wiping something of the skin of the head or of the hair within its limit.

lines.ar: الْخَامِسُ: غَسْلُ الرِّجْلَيْنِ مَعَ الْكَعْبَيْنِ
lines.en: The fifth: washing the feet up to the ankles.

lines.ar: السَّادِسُ: التَّرْتِيبُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْكَيْفِيَّةِ
lines.en: The sixth: the order, in this manner.

passages.ar: فُرُوضُ الْوُضُوءِ سِتَّةٌ الْأَوَّلُ : النِّيَّةُ الثَّانِي: غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ الثَّالِثُ: غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ إِلَى الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ الرَّابِعُ: مَسْحُ شَيْءٍ مِنْ بَشَرَةِ الرَّأْسِ أَوْ شَعَرٍ فِي حَدِّهِ الْخَامِسُ: غَسْلُ الرِّجْلَيْنِ مَعَ الْكَعْبَيْنِ السَّادِسُ: التَّرْتِيبُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْكَيْفِيَّةِ
passages.en: The obligations of ablution are six: The first: the intention. The second: washing the face. The third: washing the hands up to the elbows. The fourth: wiping something of the skin of the head or of the hair within its limit. The fifth: washing the feet up to the ankles. The sixth: the order, in this manner.

passages.intro_en: A list on one line. Read it, then answer.
passages.source: Matn Safīnat al-Najā of Sālim b. Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī
passages.cite: Sālim b. ʿAbdallāh b. Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī, Matn Safīnat al-Najā (with Matn Safīnat al-Ṣalāt), Shamela 3.28 id 4059 (the card gives no publisher, editor or year) and the identical Hodeidah 3.64 copy read here, p. 2 of the digital text (not print pagination); TLNOOR 713 is an epub of the same matn. Vowelled for learners.

lines.ar: فُرُوضُ الْغُسْلِ اثْنَانِ : النِّيَّةُ ، وَتَعْمِيمُ الْبَدَنِ بِالْمَاءِ
lines.en: The obligations of the full wash are two: the intention, and covering the whole body with water.

passages.ar: فُرُوضُ الْغُسْلِ اثْنَانِ : النِّيَّةُ ، وَتَعْمِيمُ الْبَدَنِ بِالْمَاءِ
passages.en: The obligations of the full wash are two: the intention, and covering the whole body with water.

passages.intro_en: A story: the notebook. Read it aloud, then answer. (Words to help: الشَّهَادَة = the testimony of faith · دَفْتَر = notebook.)

lines.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: After the prayer Ahmad sat in the majlis with the Habib.

lines.ar: فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا وَقَرَأَ: أَرْكَانُ الْإِسْلَامِ خَمْسَةٌ.
lines.en: The Habib opened a small book and read: The pillars of Islam are five.

lines.ar: الْأَوَّلُ: الشَّهَادَةُ.
lines.en: The first: the testimony.

lines.ar: الثَّانِي: الصَّلَاةُ.
lines.en: The second: the prayer.

lines.ar: الثَّالِثُ: الزَّكَاةُ.
lines.en: The third: the zakat.

lines.ar: الرَّابِعُ: الصِّيَامُ.
lines.en: The fourth: fasting.

lines.ar: الْخَامِسُ: الْحَجُّ.
lines.en: The fifth: the pilgrimage.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُكْتُبْ هَذِهِ الْخَمْسَةَ فِي دَفْتَرِكَ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Write these five in your notebook.

lines.ar: فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ الْخَمْسَةَ بِالْقَلَمِ وَقَرَأَهَا ثَلَاثًا.
lines.en: So Ahmad wrote the five with the pen and read them three times.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ سَأَلَ: كَمْ فُرُوضُ الْوُضُوءِ؟
lines.en: Then he asked: How many are the obligations of ablution?

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: سِتَّةٌ، وَغَدًا نَقْرَأُ الْفُرُوضَ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Six; and tomorrow we read the obligations.

lines.ar: رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ الْخَمْسَةَ لِأُمِّهِ.
lines.en: Ahmad returned home and read the five to his mother.

lines.ar: قَالَتْ أُمُّهُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ!
lines.en: His mother said: Praise be to God!

lines.ar: أَنْتَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ جَيِّدٌ.
lines.en: You are a good student of knowledge.

passages.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ. فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا وَقَرَأَ: أَرْكَانُ الْإِسْلَامِ خَمْسَةٌ. الْأَوَّلُ: الشَّهَادَةُ. الثَّانِي: الصَّلَاةُ. الثَّالِثُ: الزَّكَاةُ. الرَّابِعُ: الصِّيَامُ. الْخَامِسُ: الْحَجُّ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُكْتُبْ هَذِهِ الْخَمْسَةَ فِي دَفْتَرِكَ. فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ الْخَمْسَةَ بِالْقَلَمِ وَقَرَأَهَا ثَلَاثًا. ثُمَّ سَأَلَ: كَمْ فُرُوضُ الْوُضُوءِ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: سِتَّةٌ، وَغَدًا نَقْرَأُ الْفُرُوضَ. رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ الْخَمْسَةَ لِأُمِّهِ. قَالَتْ أُمُّهُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ! أَنْتَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ جَيِّدٌ.
passages.en: After the prayer Ahmad sat in the majlis with the Habib. The Habib opened a small book and read: The pillars of Islam are five. The first: the testimony. The second: the prayer. The third: the zakat. The fourth: fasting. The fifth: the pilgrimage. The Habib said: Write these five in your notebook. So Ahmad wrote the five with the pen and read them three times. Then he asked: How many are the obligations of ablution? The Habib said: Six; and tomorrow we read the obligations. Ahmad returned home and read the five to his mother. His mother said: Praise be to God! You are a good student of knowledge.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 107-108 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
lines.en: The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.

lines.ar: وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
lines.en: And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.

passages.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ. وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
passages.en: The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face. And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.

questions.q: What is being counted in this list, and how many?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَعُدُّ الْقَائِمَةُ؟ وَكَمْ؟
questions.a: The obligations of ablution (فُرُوضُ الْوُضُوءِ); six.

questions.q: What is the first obligation?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْفَرْضُ الْأَوَّلُ؟
questions.a: The intention (النِّيَّةُ).

questions.q: What is the second obligation?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْفَرْضُ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: Washing the face (غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ).

questions.q: What is the third? Which word says “the third”?
questions.q_ar: مَا الثَّالِثُ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى «الثَّالِثِ»؟
questions.a: Washing the hands up to the elbows; the word is الثَّالِثُ.

questions.q: The fourth item is the longest. Which two things may be wiped?
questions.q_ar: الْبَنْدُ الرَّابِعُ هُوَ الْأَطْوَلُ. مَاذَا يُمْسَحُ؟
questions.a: Something of the skin of the head, or hair that is within its limit.

questions.q: In the fifth item, what is washed and up to where?
questions.q_ar: فِي الْبَنْدِ الْخَامِسِ: مَاذَا يُغْسَلُ وَإِلَى أَيْنَ؟
questions.a: The feet, up to the ankles (مَعَ الْكَعْبَيْنِ).

questions.q: What is the sixth item? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْبَنْدُ السَّادِسُ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهُ؟
questions.a: التَّرْتِيبُ: doing the parts in this order.

questions.q: Count the items after the heading. Does the count match the number in the heading?
questions.q_ar: عُدَّ الْبُنُودَ بَعْدَ الْعُنْوَانِ. هَلْ تُطَابِقُ الْعَدَدَ؟
questions.a: Six items; yes, it matches سِتَّةٌ.

questions.q: True or false? The second and the third items both begin with the same word.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ يَبْدَأُ الثَّانِي وَالثَّالِثُ بِالْكَلِمَةِ نَفْسِهَا.
questions.a: True: both begin with غَسْلُ (“washing of”); so do the second, third and fifth.

questions.q: What is the difference between the first item and the other items?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَ الْبَنْدِ الْأَوَّلِ وَبَقِيَّةِ الْبُنُودِ؟
questions.a: The first is one word (النِّيَّةُ, the intention); items 2–5 are “washing of …” or “wiping of …” (an action on a part of the body).

questions.q: Items 2, 3 and 5 begin with غَسْلُ. What kind of word is it, and what does it name?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ كَلِمَةِ «غَسْلُ»؟ وَعَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ؟
questions.a: An action-name (verbal noun) of the verb غَسَلَ: “the washing of …”.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A short summary of religious knowledge (a matn-style list) from al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa of Imam Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī.

questions.q: What is counted, and how many?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَعُدُّ الْقَائِمَةُ؟ وَكَمْ؟
questions.a: The obligations of the full wash (فُرُوضُ الْغُسْلِ); two.

questions.q: What is the first of the two?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْأَوَّلُ؟
questions.a: The intention (النِّيَّةُ).

questions.q: What is the second of the two?
questions.q_ar: مَا الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: Covering the whole body with water.

questions.q: Which word means “the body”? Is it in the first item or the second?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ كَلِمَةُ «الْبَدَنِ»؟
questions.a: الْبَدَنِ; in the second.

questions.q: How does this list differ from the list in A?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَ هَذِهِ الْقَائِمَةِ وَقَائِمَةِ الْوُضُوءِ؟
questions.a: The items are on one line, separated by a comma and وَ; there is no “the first, the second”.

questions.q: Which word joins the second item to the first? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَرْبِطُ الثَّانِيَ بِالْأَوَّلِ؟
questions.a: وَ (in وَتَعْمِيمُ): “and”.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the majlis, with the Habib.

questions.q: What did the Habib read? How many does the heading say?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ؟ وَكَمْ يَقُولُ الْعُنْوَانُ؟
questions.a: “The pillars of Islam are five.”

questions.q: What is the third pillar in the list?
questions.q_ar: مَا الرُّكْنُ الثَّالِثُ؟
questions.a: The zakat (الزَّكَاةُ).

questions.q: Which word means “the fifth”, and what is the fifth pillar?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «الْخَامِسَ»؟ وَمَا هُوَ؟
questions.a: الْخَامِسُ; the pilgrimage.

questions.q: Count the items in lines 3 and 4. Do they match the heading?
questions.q_ar: عُدَّ الْبُنُودَ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ٣ وَ٤. هَلْ تُطَابِقُ الْعُنْوَانَ؟
questions.a: Five items; yes.

questions.q: What did the Habib tell Ahmad to do?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ أَنْ يَفْعَلَ؟
questions.a: To write the five in his notebook.

questions.q: How many times did Ahmad read the five?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ الْخَمْسَةَ؟
questions.a: Three times (ثَلَاثًا).

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask next, and what was the answer?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ؟ وَمَا الْجَوَابُ؟
questions.a: How many are the obligations of ablution; six.

questions.q: When will they read the obligations?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى يَقْرَؤُونَ الْفُرُوضَ؟
questions.a: Tomorrow (غَدًا).

questions.q: To whom did Ahmad read the five at home?
questions.q_ar: لِمَنْ قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ الْخَمْسَةَ فِي الْبَيْتِ؟
questions.a: To his mother.

questions.q: The verb نَقْرَأُ is in the present (“we read”). Which word shows that the time is tomorrow?
questions.q_ar: الْفِعْلُ «نَقْرَأُ» مُضَارِعٌ. أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الْغَدِ؟
questions.a: غَدًا (tomorrow).

questions.q: Why does the mother call him طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ جَيِّدٌ? Give one reason from the story.
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَقُولُ الْأُمُّ إِنَّهُ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ جَيِّدٌ؟
questions.a: He wrote the five, read them three times and read them to her.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; the second, washing the face; the third, washing the hands; the fourth, wiping part of the head.

questions.q: How many pillars has he written so far?
questions.a: Four.

questions.q: Which words count the list (the ordinals)?
questions.a: الْأَوَّلُ، الثَّانِي، الثَّالِثُ، الرَّابِعُ

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The first is the intention.
questions.a: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ.

translate.en: Ablution is a condition for the prayer.
The second: washing the face with water.

translate.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
translate.en: After the prayer the boy sat with the Habib in the circle.

translate.ar: أَوْقَاتُ الصَّلَاةِ خَمْسَةٌ، وَلِكُلِّ وَقْتٍ صَلَاةٌ.
translate.en: The times of prayer are five, and every time has a prayer.

translate.ar: قَبْلَ الْوُضُوءِ اُنْظُرْ إِلَى الْمَاءِ: هَلْ هُوَ نَظِيفٌ؟
translate.en: Before ablution look at the water: is it clean?

translate.ar: اِقْرَأِ الْأَوَّلَ ثُمَّ الثَّانِيَ ثُمَّ الثَّالِثَ.
translate.en: Read the first, then the second, then the third.

translate.ar: فُرُوضُ الْوُضُوءِ سِتَّةٌ: الْأَوَّلُ: النِّيَّةُ. الثَّانِي: غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ. الثَّالِثُ: غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ.
translate.en: The obligations of ablution are six. The first: the intention. The second: washing the face. The third: washing the hands.

translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ الْخَمْسَةَ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَقَرَأَهَا لِأُمِّهِ.
translate.en: Ahmad wrote the five in his book and read them to his mother.
The prayer is one of the pillars of Islam.
Remembrance of God after the prayer is a sunna.
The pillars of Islam are five.
The obligations of the full wash are two.
The first: the intention. The second: washing the face.
The third: washing the hands.
Ablution is a condition for the prayer.
The times of prayer are five.
The sixth: the order.
The doors of the mosque are three: the first is big, the second is small, the third is new.
translate.ar: أَبْوَابُ الْمَسْجِدِ ثَلَاثَةٌ: الْأَوَّلُ كَبِيرٌ، وَالثَّانِي صَغِيرٌ، وَالثَّالِثُ جَدِيدٌ.

translate.en: The lessons of the circle are four.
Washing the face is the second; wiping the head is the fourth.
translate.ar: غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ هُوَ الثَّانِي، وَمَسْحُ الرَّأْسِ هُوَ الرَّابِعُ.

readings.title_en: Calling and exclaiming
readings.question_en: How do I read “O …!” and “By God!”: who is being called, and what happens to the word?
readings.question_ar: مَنِ الَّذِي يُنَادَى؟ وَمَاذَا يَحْدُثُ لِلْكَلِمَةِ بَعْدَ «يَا»؟

passages.intro_en: A call in the Qur’an. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: The Qur’an, Sūrat al-Baqara, 2:21 (Madinah muṣḥaf text, extracted by program).

lines.ar: يَٰأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
lines.en: O people, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, so that you may become mindful of God.

glossary.en: you guard yourselves, you become mindful

passages.ar: يَٰأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
passages.en: O people, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, so that you may become mindful of God.

passages.intro_en: A morning prayer: from the Wird al-Laṭīf. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: al-Ḥaddād, al-Wird al-Laṭīf, as given in 'Awrād wa-aḥzāb' (Master Library copy 'أوراد و أحزاب', loose .bok from the 01 BOOKS 'sameelh haddad' folder); edition not stated; p. 2 of the digital text; the source is only partly vowelled. Vowelled for learners.

lines.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَصْبَحْتُ مِنْكَ فِي نِعْمَةٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ وَسِتْرٍ ، فَأَتْمِمْ نِعْمَتَكَ عَلَيَّ وَعَافِيَتَكَ وَسِتْرَكَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
lines.en: O God, I have entered the morning with You in blessing, well-being and protection; so complete Your blessing upon me, and Your well-being and protection, in this world and the next.

passages.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَصْبَحْتُ مِنْكَ فِي نِعْمَةٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ وَسِتْرٍ ، فَأَتْمِمْ نِعْمَتَكَ عَلَيَّ وَعَافِيَتَكَ وَسِتْرَكَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
passages.en: O God, I have entered the morning with You in blessing, well-being and protection; so complete Your blessing upon me, and Your well-being and protection, in this world and the next.

passages.intro_en: A prayer of praise: from al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa of Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī (1069–1145 AH)
passages.cite: Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī, al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa, Dār Maqām al-Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr, Ḥawṭat Aḥmad b. Zayn, Ḥaḍramawt (year not given on the title page); Shamela Master Library copy 'الرسالة الجامعة' (Bafaqih Sufi library, 491.mdb; same work as TLNOOR 712, an epub), p. 11 of the copy (9 pp; the copy's own page counter, printed pagination not given). Abridged (the second line of the qunūt only). The source is partly vowelled; vowelled for learners, every letter as in the copy.

lines.ar: تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا وَتَعَالَيْتَ ، لَكَ الْحَمْدُ عَلَى مَا قَضَيْتَ ، نَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَنَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ
lines.en: Blessed and exalted are You, our Lord; Yours is the praise for what You have decreed; we ask Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.

passages.ar: تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا وَتَعَالَيْتَ ، لَكَ الْحَمْدُ عَلَى مَا قَضَيْتَ ، نَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَنَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ
passages.en: Blessed and exalted are You, our Lord; Yours is the praise for what You have decreed; we ask Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.

passages.intro_en: A story: the morning in the mosque. Read it aloud, then answer.

lines.ar: فِي الصَّبَاحِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: In the morning Ahmad sat with his father in the mosque.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَبُوهُ: يَا بُنَيَّ، اِقْرَأْ وِرْدَ الصَّبَاحِ.
lines.en: His father said: My son, read the morning wird.

lines.ar: فَقَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ: اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ، يَا رَبِّ، عَلَى كُلِّ نِعْمَةٍ.
lines.en: So Ahmad read: O God, to You be praise, O my Lord, for every blessing.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ أَبُوهُ: آمِينَ.
lines.en: And his father said: Amen.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ عُمَرُ الْمَسْجِدَ وَقَالَ: يَا أَحْمَدُ، أَيْنَ كِتَابِي؟
lines.en: Then ʿUmar entered the mosque and said: Ahmad, where is my book?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: وَاللَّهِ لَمْ أَفْتَحْ كِتَابَكَ يَا أَخِي.
lines.en: Ahmad said: By Allah, I did not open your book, my brother.

lines.ar: فَنَظَرَ عُمَرُ تَحْتَ الْمَكْتَبِ وَقَالَ: وَجَدْتُهُ!
lines.en: ʿUmar looked under the desk and said: I found it!

lines.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.
lines.en: Praise be to God.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ جَاءَ الْحَبِيبُ وَقَالَ: يَا أَيُّهَا الطُّلَّابُ، اِجْلِسُوا.
lines.en: Then the Habib came and said: O students, sit down.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ لِأَحْمَدَ: يَا طَالِبَ الْعِلْمِ، اِسْمَعِ الدَّرْسَ.
lines.en: And he said to Ahmad: O student of knowledge, listen to the lesson.

lines.ar: فَجَلَسَ الطُّلَّابُ وَسَمِعُوا الدَّرْسَ.
lines.en: So the students sat and heard the lesson.

passages.ar: فِي الصَّبَاحِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. قَالَ أَبُوهُ: يَا بُنَيَّ، اِقْرَأْ وِرْدَ الصَّبَاحِ. فَقَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ: اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ، يَا رَبِّ، عَلَى كُلِّ نِعْمَةٍ. وَقَالَ أَبُوهُ: آمِينَ. ثُمَّ دَخَلَ عُمَرُ الْمَسْجِدَ وَقَالَ: يَا أَحْمَدُ، أَيْنَ كِتَابِي؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: وَاللَّهِ لَمْ أَفْتَحْ كِتَابَكَ يَا أَخِي. فَنَظَرَ عُمَرُ تَحْتَ الْمَكْتَبِ وَقَالَ: وَجَدْتُهُ! الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. ثُمَّ جَاءَ الْحَبِيبُ وَقَالَ: يَا أَيُّهَا الطُّلَّابُ، اِجْلِسُوا. وَقَالَ لِأَحْمَدَ: يَا طَالِبَ الْعِلْمِ، اِسْمَعِ الدَّرْسَ. فَجَلَسَ الطُّلَّابُ وَسَمِعُوا الدَّرْسَ.
passages.en: In the morning Ahmad sat with his father in the mosque. His father said: My son, read the morning wird. So Ahmad read: O God, to You be praise, O my Lord, for every blessing. And his father said: Amen. Then ʿUmar entered the mosque and said: Ahmad, where is my book? Ahmad said: By Allah, I did not open your book, my brother. ʿUmar looked under the desk and said: I found it! Praise be to God. Then the Habib came and said: O students, sit down. And he said to Ahmad: O student of knowledge, listen to the lesson. So the students sat and heard the lesson.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 109-110 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْوِرْدَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
lines.en: The boy read the wird in the morning.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
lines.en: Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْوِرْدَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ. ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
passages.en: The boy read the wird in the morning. Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.

glossary.en: you guard yourselves, you become mindful

questions.q: Who is being called?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْمُنَادَى؟
questions.a: The people (النَّاسُ).

questions.q: Which words make the call? What do they mean together?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَصْنَعُ النِّدَاءَ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: يَا أَيُّهَا (here joined in one word as in the muṣḥaf): “O …”.

questions.q: What are the people told to do?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُقَالُ لِلنَّاسِ أَنْ يَفْعَلُوا؟
questions.a: To worship their Lord.

questions.q: Who is “your Lord” described as? (the part after الَّذِي)
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ وُصِفَ «رَبُّكُمْ»؟
questions.a: The One who created you and those before you.

questions.q: Which two parts make this word?
questions.q_ar: مِنْ أَيِّ جُزْأَيْنِ تَتَكَوَّنُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ؟
questions.a: رَبَّ (Lord) + كُمْ (your, for many).

questions.q: Which word means “perhaps you” and which means “before you”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «لَعَلَّكُمْ»؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «قَبْلِكُمْ»؟
questions.a: لَعَلَّكُمْ = perhaps you; قَبْلِكُمْ = before you.

questions.q: The called word النَّاسُ ends in ـُ. Why not النَّاسَ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَنْتَهِي «النَّاسُ» بِالضَّمَّةِ؟
questions.a: After يَا أَيُّهَا the noun with ال keeps ـُ (it is not part of an “of” phrase).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an, sūrat al-Baqara, verse 21.

questions.q: Who is calling, and who is called?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْمُنَادِي؟ وَمَنِ الْمُنَادَى؟
questions.a: The worshipper calls God (اللَّهُمَّ).

questions.q: What time of day has the speaker entered? Which verb says it?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ وَقْتٍ دَخَلَ الْمُتَكَلِّمُ؟ أَيُّ فِعْلٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: The morning; أَصْبَحْتُ.

questions.q: With whom is the speaker, and in what three things? (Words: سِتْر = protection)
questions.q_ar: مَعَ مَنْ؟ وَفِي أَيِّ ثَلَاثَةِ أَشْيَاءَ؟
questions.a: With God; in blessing, well-being and protection.

questions.q: Which three words are the three gifts asked to be completed?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ ثَلَاثِ كَلِمَاتٍ يُطْلَبُ إِتْمَامُهَا؟
questions.a: نِعْمَتَكَ, عَافِيَتَكَ, سِتْرَكَ.

questions.q: Where should they be complete?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ؟
questions.a: In this world and in the next.

questions.q: What does the letter فَـ add at the start?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَزِيدُ الْفَاءُ؟
questions.a: “so”: the request follows from what was said.

questions.q: What does عَلَيَّ mean? What are its two parts?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى «عَلَيَّ»؟
questions.a: “upon me”: عَلَى + ـيَّ (me).

questions.q: The line has no يَا. Which word does the calling, and what does it stand for?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُنَادِي؟
questions.a: اللَّهُمَّ: it stands for يَا اللَّهُ.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and from which book?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيِّ كِتَابٍ؟
questions.a: A supplication (duʿāʾ) from the Wird al-Laṭīf of Imam al-Ḥaddād, said in the morning.

questions.q: Who is called in this line?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْمُنَادَى فِي هَذَا السَّطْرِ؟
questions.a: Our Lord (رَبَّنَا).

questions.q: What belongs to God (لَكَ)?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَكُونُ لِلَّهِ؟
questions.a: The praise (الْحَمْدُ).

questions.q: Which verb says “we ask Your forgiveness”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ يَعْنِي «نَطْلُبُ مَغْفِرَتَكَ»؟
questions.a: نَسْتَغْفِرُكَ.

questions.q: Which verb says “we turn in repentance”? To whom?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ يَعْنِي «نَرْجِعُ»؟ وَإِلَى مَنْ؟
questions.a: نَتُوبُ; to Him (إِلَيْكَ).

questions.q: What does the letter وَ do here?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ الْوَاوُ؟
questions.a: It joins: “and we turn”.

questions.q: Why رَبَّنَا with ـَ, and not رَبُّنَا?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «رَبَّنَا» بِالْفَتْحَةِ؟
questions.a: It is the called word with “our”: a call with the يَا left out takes ـَ.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A supplication (duʿāʾ) from al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa of Imam Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī.

questions.q: With whom did Ahmad sit in the mosque?
questions.q_ar: مَعَ مَنْ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: With his father.

questions.q: What does the father call Ahmad (line 2), and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: بِمَاذَا يُنَادِي الْأَبُ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: يَا بُنَيَّ: “my son”.

questions.q: What does the father say at the end of Ahmad’s prayer?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الْأَبُ فِي آخِرِ الدُّعَاءِ؟
questions.a: آمِينَ: “amen”.

questions.q: Who does ʿUmar call, and what is he looking for?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يُنَادِي عُمَرُ؟ وَعَمَّا يَبْحَثُ؟
questions.a: Ahmad; his book.

questions.q: What does Ahmad swear? Which word is the oath?
questions.q_ar: عَلَى مَاذَا يُقْسِمُ أَحْمَدُ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ الْقَسَمُ؟
questions.a: That he did not open ʿUmar’s book; وَاللَّهِ.

questions.q: Who says يَا أَخِي, to whom, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقُولُ «يَا أَخِي»؟ وَلِمَنْ؟
questions.a: Ahmad, to ʿUmar: “my brother”.

questions.q: Where did ʿUmar find the book?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ وَجَدَ عُمَرُ الْكِتَابَ؟
questions.a: Under the desk.

questions.q: Which two words call the students in line 8?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تُنَادِيَانِ الطُّلَّابَ فِي السَّطْرِ ٨؟
questions.a: يَا أَيُّهَا.

questions.q: What is Ahmad called in line 9? Why does طَالِبَ end in ـَ?
questions.q_ar: بِمَاذَا يُنَادَى أَحْمَدُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٩؟ لِمَاذَا «طَالِبَ» بِالْفَتْحَةِ؟
questions.a: يَا طَالِبَ الْعِلْمِ; because it is the first word of an “of” phrase in a call.

questions.q: The و in وَاللَّهِ is not “and”. How can you tell?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ نَعْرِفُ أَنَّ الْوَاوَ فِي «وَاللَّهِ» لَيْسَتْ لِلْعَطْفِ؟
questions.a: It stands at the start of the speech and swears by Allah; nothing before it can be joined.

questions.q: In line 3 two calls come in one sentence (اللَّهُمَّ and يَا رَبِّ). Who is called in both?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٣ نِدَاءَانِ. مَنِ الْمُنَادَى فِيهِمَا؟
questions.a: God.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy read the wird in the morning. Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.

questions.q: Which word calls on Allah (the calling word)?
questions.a: يَا (O)

questions.q: What does آمِينَ mean at the end of a duʿāʾ?
questions.a: Amen: may it be so.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: O Allah, guide us.
questions.a: اللَّهُمَّ اِهْدِنَا.

translate.en: O boy, open the door.
By Allah, the mosque is big.

translate.ar: يَا رَبِّ، لَكَ الْحَمْدُ عَلَى الْعَافِيَةِ.
translate.en: O my Lord, to You be praise for well-being.
O God, forgive my father and my mother.
O poor one, take the bread.

translate.ar: قَالَ أَبِي: يَا بُنَيَّ، الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ.
translate.en: My father said: My son, knowledge is light.

translate.ar: قَالَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: يَا أَحْمَدُ، اُدْخُلِ الْبَيْتَ. قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: وَاللَّهِ دَخَلْتُ يَا أُمِّي. قَالَتْ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.
translate.en: Fatima said: Ahmad, come into the house. Ahmad said: By Allah, I came in, Mother. She said: Praise be to God.

translate.ar: اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ، آمِينَ يَا رَبِّ.
translate.en: O God, to You be praise. Amen, O my Lord.
My father, are you here?
O God, to You be praise for the blessing.
O God, forgive us.
O my Lord, to You be praise.
O students, listen to the lesson.
O student of knowledge, read the book.
By Allah, I did not open the door.
O my son, sit with me in the mosque.
translate.ar: يَا بُنَيَّ، اِجْلِسْ مَعِي فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.

translate.en: O God, we ask You for well-being. Amen.
O my brother, praise be to God.
O ʿUmar, where is your book?
O God, we thank You for the blessing.

readings.title_en: Except: taking one out
readings.question_en: Which word takes someone out of a sentence, and what happens to the word after it?
readings.question_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُخْرِجُ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْجُمْلَةِ؟ وَمَاذَا يَحْدُثُ لِآخِرِ الْكَلِمَةِ بَعْدَهَا؟

passages.intro_en: Text 1: the water, and the first line of faith. Read it aloud, then answer.

lines.ar: وَالْمَاءُ الْكَثِيرُ لَا يَتَنَجَّسُ إِلَّا إِذَا تَغَيَّرَ طَعْمُهُ أَوْ لَوْنُهُ أَوْ رِيحُهُ
lines.en: Plentiful water does not become impure unless its taste, colour or smell changes.

lines.ar: وَمَعْنَى لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ : لَا مَعْبُودَ بِحَقٍّ فِي الْوُجُودِ إِلَّا اللهُ
lines.en: And the meaning of "there is no god but God": no one in existence is worshipped in truth except God.

passages.ar: وَالْمَاءُ الْكَثِيرُ لَا يَتَنَجَّسُ إِلَّا إِذَا تَغَيَّرَ طَعْمُهُ أَوْ لَوْنُهُ أَوْ رِيحُهُ وَمَعْنَى لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ : لَا مَعْبُودَ بِحَقٍّ فِي الْوُجُودِ إِلَّا اللهُ
passages.en: Plentiful water does not become impure unless its taste, colour or smell changes. And the meaning of "there is no god but God": no one in existence is worshipped in truth except God.

passages.intro_en: Text 2: the same rule in verse. Read it aloud (each line is half a verse), then answer.

passages.cite: Abū Fawzī Muḥammad Maʿṣūm b. Sirāj al-Sharbūnī, Nayl al-Rajā (naẓm Safīnat al-Najā), as printed with Aḥmad Sahl b. Abī Hāshim al-Hājīnī, Fayḍ al-Ḥijā ʿalā Nayl al-Rajā; Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, 1023.mdb); publisher and year not given; p. 22 of the digital text. NB TLNOOR 938 is a different book (al-Shāṭirī's prose Nayl al-Rajā); vowels as in the source copy

lines.ar: لَا يَتَنَجَّسُ الْكَثِيْرُ بِاعْتِرَا
lines.en: Plentiful water is not made impure by the falling of

lines.ar: نَجْسٍ لَهُ إِلَّا إِذَا تَغَيَّرَا
lines.en: an impurity into it, unless it changes —

lines.ar: طَعْمٌ لَهُ أَوْ لَوْنٌ أَوْ رِيْحٌ جَلَا
lines.en: its taste, or colour, or smell, clearly;

lines.ar: وَيَتَنَجَّسُ الْقَلِيْلُ مُسْجَلَا
lines.en: but small amounts become impure, without exception.

glossary.en: the falling (بِاعْتِرَا = by the falling of)

passages.ar: لَا يَتَنَجَّسُ الْكَثِيْرُ بِاعْتِرَا نَجْسٍ لَهُ إِلَّا إِذَا تَغَيَّرَا طَعْمٌ لَهُ أَوْ لَوْنٌ أَوْ رِيْحٌ جَلَا وَيَتَنَجَّسُ الْقَلِيْلُ مُسْجَلَا
passages.en: Plentiful water is not made impure by the falling of an impurity into it, unless it changes — its taste, or colour, or smell, clearly; but small amounts become impure, without exception.

passages.intro_en: Text 3: سِوَى and إِلَّا in a counsel text. Read it aloud, then answer.

passages.cite: Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī, al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa, Dār Maqām al-Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr, Ḥawṭat Aḥmad b. Zayn, Ḥaḍramawt (year not given on the title page); Shamela Master Library copy 'الرسالة الجامعة' (Bafaqih Sufi library, 491.mdb; same work as TLNOOR 712, an epub), pp. 5–8 of the copy (9 pp; the copy's own page counter, printed pagination not given). Abridged (lines 1–2 of the three-line entry). The source is partly vowelled; vowelled for learners, every letter as in the copy (copy misprints corrected by the course: فَلَيسَ → فَلَيْسَ, فِيَما → فِيمَا).

lines.ar: أَرْكَانُ الْعُمْرَةِ: هِيَ أَرْكَانُ الْحَجِّ إِلَّا الْوُقُوفَ فَلَيْسَ مِنْهَا
lines.en: The pillars of the ʿumra are the pillars of the pilgrimage, except the standing at ʿArafa, which is not one of them.

lines.ar: فَلَا زَكَاةَ فِيمَا سِوَى النَّعَمِ السَّائِمَةِ
lines.en: So there is no zakāt on anything other than grazing livestock.

passages.ar: أَرْكَانُ الْعُمْرَةِ: هِيَ أَرْكَانُ الْحَجِّ إِلَّا الْوُقُوفَ فَلَيْسَ مِنْهَا فَلَا زَكَاةَ فِيمَا سِوَى النَّعَمِ السَّائِمَةِ
passages.en: The pillars of the ʿumra are the pillars of the pilgrimage, except the standing at ʿArafa, which is not one of them. So there is no zakāt on anything other than grazing livestock.

passages.intro_en: Qur’an 103:3, read aloud. The verse before it (103:2) says: إِنَّ الْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ (“mankind is in loss”).
passages.cite: Qur’an, sūrat al-ʿAṣr 103:3 (copied by program from the course Qur’an text, quran.json)

lines.ar: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِالصَّبْرِ
lines.en: except those who believe, and do righteous deeds, and urge one another to the truth, and urge one another to patience.

passages.ar: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِالصَّبْرِ
passages.en: except those who believe, and do righteous deeds, and urge one another to the truth, and urge one another to patience.

passages.intro_en: Qur’an 26:89, read aloud. The verse before it says that on that day neither wealth nor children will help.
passages.cite: Qur’an, sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:89 (copied by program from the course Qur’an text, quran.json); the same clause is quoted by Imām al-Ḥaddād in Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd (SOURCES, L62 adab_illa)

lines.ar: إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
lines.en: except one who comes to God with a sound heart.

passages.ar: إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
passages.en: except one who comes to God with a sound heart.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 111-112 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
lines.en: The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.

lines.ar: لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ لَوْنُهُ وَلَا طَعْمُهُ.
lines.en: Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.

passages.ar: شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا. لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ لَوْنُهُ وَلَا طَعْمُهُ.
passages.en: The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water. Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.

glossary.en: the falling (بِاعْتِرَا = by the falling of)

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A short book of Islamic law that students learn (a matn): Matn Safīnat al-Najā of Sālim ibn Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī.

questions.q: Line 1: what is it about?
questions.q_ar: عَنْ مَاذَا السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ؟
questions.a: Water: plentiful water, and when it becomes impure.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: And plentiful water does not become impure.

questions.q: What does إِلَّا إِذَا add? Translate it.
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تُضِيفُ إِلَّا إِذَا؟
questions.a: “Unless”: the one case in which the water does become impure.

questions.q: Line 1: which three things may change? Write them in Arabic.
questions.q_ar: مَا الْأَشْيَاءُ الثَّلَاثَةُ الَّتِي قَدْ تَتَغَيَّرُ؟ اُكْتُبْهَا.
questions.a: طَعْمُهُ (its taste), لَوْنُهُ (its colour), رِيحُهُ (its smell).

questions.q: What does this small word do between the three?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ بَيْنَ الثَّلَاثَةِ؟
questions.a: It joins them: “or”.

questions.q: What does the ending ـهُ point to?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ ـهُ؟
questions.a: The water (الْمَاءُ).

questions.q: True or false? “Plentiful water becomes impure whenever anything falls into it.”
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ «يَتَنَجَّسُ الْمَاءُ الْكَثِيرُ كُلَّمَا وَقَعَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ».
questions.a: False. The text says it does not become impure unless its taste, colour or smell changes.

questions.q: Translate (line 2, after the colon).
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْجُمْلَةَ بَعْدَ النُّقْطَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي.
questions.a: No one in existence is worshipped in truth except God.
questions.ref_ar: لَا مَعْبُودَ بِحَقٍّ فِي الْوُجُودِ إِلَّا اللهُ

questions.q: In لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ the last word ends in ـُ, not in ـَ. Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَنْتَهِي آخِرُ «اللهُ» بِضَمَّةٍ لَا بِفَتْحَةٍ؟
questions.a: It stands in place of the word after لَا (“no god”), so it has that word’s ending (ـُ). The ـَ belongs to a full positive sentence.

questions.q: In line 1 a whole clause follows إِلَّا (إِذَا تَغَيَّرَ …); in line 2 one word follows it. Which line gives a condition, and which gives one name?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ السَّطْرَيْنِ يُعْطِي شَرْطًا؟ وَأَيُّهُمَا يُعْطِي اسْمًا وَاحِدًا؟
questions.a: Line 1 gives a condition (“unless it changes”); line 2 gives one name (God).

questions.q: Is this prose or verse? How can you tell?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ هَذَا نَثْرٌ أَمْ شِعْرٌ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: Verse (naẓm): the lines are in two halves, and all four halves end in the same long ā.

questions.q: Which line of Text 1 says the same as lines 1–3 here?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ فِي النَّصِّ ١ يَقُولُ مَا تَقُولُهُ الْأَسْطُرُ ١–٣ هُنَا؟
questions.a: Line 1 of Text 1 (the rule about plentiful water).

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: unless it changes

questions.q: Which word in line 2 means “impurity”? (root ن ج س)
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي بِمَعْنَى «impurity»؟ (الْجَذْرُ ن ج س)
questions.a: نَجْسٍ

questions.q: Line 4 says something the first three lines do not. What?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ السَّطْرُ الرَّابِعُ مِمَّا لَمْ يَقُلْهُ مَا قَبْلَهُ؟
questions.a: Small amounts of water become impure (whenever impurity falls in), without exception.

questions.q: Which word in line 1 is the opposite of this word?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ ضِدُّ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟
questions.a: الْكَثِيْرُ (plentiful)

questions.q: The word نَجْسٍ ends in ـٍ. Why? (Look at the word before it.)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَنْتَهِي نَجْسٍ بِكَسْرَةٍ؟ اُنْظُرْ إِلَى الْكَلِمَةِ قَبْلَهُ.
questions.a: It is the “of” word after اعْتِرَا: “by the falling of an impurity”.

questions.q: Text 1 writes تَغَيَّرَ and the verse writes تَغَيَّرَا. Why the difference?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا كُتِبَ تَغَيَّرَ فِي النَّصِّ ١ وَتَغَيَّرَا فِي النَّظْمِ؟
questions.a: The poet lengthens the vowel to match the rhyme (the long ā). It is the same word.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A short teaching text, al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa of Imām Aḥmad ibn Zayn al-Ḥabashī.

questions.q: Line 1: which two sets of pillars does it compare?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُقَارِنُ السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ؟
questions.a: The pillars of the ʿumra and the pillars of the pilgrimage (الْحَجّ).

questions.q: Which word takes out? What is taken out?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُخْرِجُ؟ وَمَاذَا يَخْرُجُ؟
questions.a: إِلَّا takes out الْوُقُوفَ (the standing).

questions.q: What ending has the word after إِلَّا here, and why?
questions.q_ar: مَا آخِرُ الْكَلِمَةِ بَعْدَ إِلَّا هُنَا؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: ـَ: it is taken out of a full positive sentence.

questions.q: Translate. What does ـهَا point to?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ. إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ ـهَا؟
questions.a: “So it is not one of them.” ـهَا = the pillars of the ʿumra.

questions.q: Line 2: which word works like إِلَّا, and what follows it?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ بِمَعْنَى إِلَّا؟ وَمَاذَا بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: سِوَى: “other than”. It is followed by النَّعَمِ السَّائِمَةِ.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: So there is no zakāt on anything other than grazing livestock.

questions.q: In line 1, the word هِيَ stands between “the pillars of the ʿumra” and “the pillars of the pilgrimage”. What does it do?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ كَلِمَةُ هِيَ؟
questions.a: It points back to “the pillars of the ʿumra”: “they are the pillars of the pilgrimage”.

questions.q: In line 2 زَكَاةَ ends in ـَ after لَا. What does this لَا do? (Lesson 59)
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ لَا قَبْلَ زَكَاةَ؟
questions.a: It denies the whole kind: “no zakāt at all”.

questions.q: Which word takes out, and which words come after it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُخْرِجُ؟ وَمَاذَا يَأْتِي بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: إِلَّا, then الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ … (“those who believed …”).

questions.q: Who is taken out of “mankind … in loss” (103:2)?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الَّذِي يَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ فِي الْآيَةِ ٢؟
questions.a: Those who believe, do good, and urge one another: they are not in loss.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: they believed and did righteous deeds

questions.q: How many things do those who are taken out do? Count the verbs.
questions.q_ar: كَمْ شَيْئًا يَفْعَلُ الَّذِينَ يَخْرُجُونَ؟ عُدَّ الْأَفْعَالَ.
questions.a: Four: believed, did righteous deeds, urged one another to the truth, urged one another to patience.

questions.q: Which small word is attached to الْحَقِّ, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْحَرْفُ الَّذِي فِي أَوَّلِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهُ؟
questions.a: بِـ: “with / to” (urge one another to the truth).

questions.q: After إِلَّا comes a group (الَّذِينَ), not one name like سَالِمًا. Can you see its ending change? Why not?
questions.q_ar: بَعْدَ إِلَّا جَاءَتْ جَمَاعَةٌ (الَّذِينَ). هَلْ تَرَى تَغَيُّرَ آخِرِهَا؟ لِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: No: الَّذِينَ keeps one form whatever its job, so its case cannot be seen.

questions.q: What does the plural ending of this verb show?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تُبَيِّنُ النِّهَايَةُ ـُواْ؟
questions.a: The doers are “they” (more than two people).

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: he comes to God with a sound heart

questions.q: Which word means “heart”, and which means “sound”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ بِمَعْنَى «heart»؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ بِمَعْنَى «sound»؟
questions.a: قَلْبٍ = heart; سَلِيمٍ = sound.

questions.q: What does this verse take out of “neither wealth nor children will help”?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُخْرِجُ هَذَا الْقَوْلُ مِنَ الْآيَةِ السَّابِقَةِ؟
questions.a: The one who comes to God with a sound heart.

questions.q: What does مَنْ mean here, and what comes after it?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى مَنْ هُنَا؟ وَمَاذَا يَأْتِي بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: “The one who”; a verb clause: أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ.

questions.q: Which verb means “he came”? What is its present form?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ بِمَعْنَى «he came»؟ وَمَا مُضَارِعُهُ؟
questions.a: أَتَى; يَأْتِي

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water. Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.

questions.q: In the first new line, what does مَا … إِلَّا mean?
questions.a: Only: he drank nothing except pure water.

questions.q: Which two words in the second new line name what could change?
questions.a: لَوْنُهُ (its colour) and طَعْمُهُ (its taste)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy drank only pure water.
questions.a: مَا شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.

translate.en: The students attended the majlis except Yusuf.

translate.ar: مَا ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى السُّوقِ إِلَّا مَعَ أَبِي.
translate.en: I went to the market only with my father.

translate.ar: لَا يَسْمَعُ الدَّرْسَ إِلَّا الَّذِي يَجْلِسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
translate.en: Only the one who sits in the circle hears the lesson.

translate.ar: سَكَنَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ سِوَى طَالِبٍ وَاحِدٍ.
translate.en: The students lived in the ribāṭ except one student.

translate.ar: كَانَ الْمَاءُ غَيْرَ نَظِيفٍ، فَلَمْ يَشْرَبْهُ الْوَلَدُ.
translate.en: The water was not clean, so the boy did not drink it.

translate.ar: مَا رَأَيْتُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ إِلَّا رِجَالًا طَيِّبِينَ.
translate.en: I saw only good men in the majlis.

translate.ar: لَا تَجْلِسْ إِلَّا إِذَا جَلَسَ الْمُعَلِّمُ.
translate.en: Do not sit unless the teacher sits.

translate.ar: مَا فِي الْحَلْقَةِ إِلَّا طُلَّابُ عِلْمٍ.
translate.en: There are only students of knowledge in the circle.

translate.ar: شَكَرَ الْمُعَلِّمُ الطُّلَّابَ غَيْرَ الْوَلَدِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَحْضُرْ.
translate.en: The teacher thanked the students except the boy who did not attend.

translate.ar: لَيْسَ فِي الْبَيْتِ سِوَى الْأُمِّ وَالْبِنْتِ.
translate.en: There is nobody in the house except the mother and the girl.

translate.ar: هَذَا الْمَاءُ غَيْرُ طَاهِرٍ، فَلَا تَشْرَبْهُ.
translate.en: This water is not pure, so do not drink it.

translate.ar: كَانَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ مَاءٌ كَثِيرٌ. شَرِبَ الطُّلَّابُ مِنْهُ إِلَّا طَالِبًا وَاحِدًا. قَالَ: مَا فِيهِ طَعْمٌ وَلَا رِيحٌ، لَكِنَّ لَوْنَهُ غَيْرُ جَيِّدٍ.
translate.en: There was plentiful water in the ribāṭ. The students drank from it except one student. He said: It has no taste and no smell, but its colour is not good.
The students attended, except Salim.
Only Ahmad attended.
Plentiful water does not become impure unless its colour is changed by an impurity.
translate.ar: لَا يَتَنَجَّسُ الْمَاءُ الْكَثِيرُ إِلَّا إِذَا تَغَيَّرَ لَوْنُهُ بِنَجْسٍ.

translate.en: There is nothing in the house except water.
No one reads the book except the one who understands.
translate.ar: لَا يَقْرَأُ الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مَنْ يَفْهَمُ.
alt: لَا يَقْرَأُ الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا الَّذِي يَفْهَمُ.

translate.en: The guests ate the food except the bread.
His house is not far.
The boy went only to the mosque.
translate.ar: مَا ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَّا إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
alt: لَمْ يَذْهَبِ الْوَلَدُ إِلَّا إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.

readings.title_en: Names in a chain: son of, titles, kunya
readings.question_en: How do I read a long name: who is whose son, which words are titles, and what are the endings?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ اسْمًا طَوِيلًا؟ مَنِ ابْنُ مَنْ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ أَلْقَابٌ؟ وَبِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي؟

lines.ar: الْإِمَامُ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ قُطْبُ الدَّعْوَةِ وَالْإِرْشَادِ عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ عَلَوِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْحَدَّادُ الْحُسَيْنِيُّ الْحَضْرَمِيُّ الشَّافِعِيُّ
lines.en: The imām, shaykh of Islam, pole of the call and guidance, ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAlawī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Ḥaddād, the Ḥusaynī, the Ḥaḍramī, the Shāfiʿī.

lines.ar: الْإِمَامُ الْعَلَّامَةُ الْعَالِمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ زَيْنِ بْنِ عَلَوِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْحَبَشِيُّ الْعَلَوِيُّ
lines.en: The imām, the great scholar, the godly knower, Aḥmad ibn Zayn ibn ʿAlawī ibn Aḥmad al-Ḥabashī al-ʿAlawī.

passages.ar: الْإِمَامُ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ قُطْبُ الدَّعْوَةِ وَالْإِرْشَادِ عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ عَلَوِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْحَدَّادُ الْحُسَيْنِيُّ الْحَضْرَمِيُّ الشَّافِعِيُّ الْإِمَامُ الْعَلَّامَةُ الْعَالِمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ زَيْنِ بْنِ عَلَوِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْحَبَشِيُّ الْعَلَوِيُّ
passages.en: The imām, shaykh of Islam, pole of the call and guidance, ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAlawī ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Ḥaddād, the Ḥusaynī, the Ḥaḍramī, the Shāfiʿī. The imām, the great scholar, the godly knower, Aḥmad ibn Zayn ibn ʿAlawī ibn Aḥmad al-Ḥabashī al-ʿAlawī.

lines.ar: لِلشَّيْخِ الْعَالِمِ الْفَاضِلِ سَالِمِ بْنِ سُمَيْرٍ الْحَضْرَمِيِّ
lines.en: By the shaykh, the learned and excellent Sālim ibn Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī.

lines.ar: لِلشَّيْخِ الْفَقِيهِ النَّابِهِ الْعَلَّامَةِ الشَّيْخِ أَحْمَدَ أَبِي الْفَوْزِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ رَمَضَانَ الْحَسَنِيِّ الْمَشْهُورِ بِاسْمِ أَحْمَدَ الْمَرْزُوقِيِّ
lines.en: By the shaykh, the jurist, the perceptive scholar, Aḥmad Abū al-Fawz, Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ramaḍān al-Ḥasanī, known as Aḥmad al-Marzūqī.

passages.ar: لِلشَّيْخِ الْعَالِمِ الْفَاضِلِ سَالِمِ بْنِ سُمَيْرٍ الْحَضْرَمِيِّ لِلشَّيْخِ الْفَقِيهِ النَّابِهِ الْعَلَّامَةِ الشَّيْخِ أَحْمَدَ أَبِي الْفَوْزِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ رَمَضَانَ الْحَسَنِيِّ الْمَشْهُورِ بِاسْمِ أَحْمَدَ الْمَرْزُوقِيِّ
passages.en: By the shaykh, the learned and excellent Sālim ibn Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī. By the shaykh, the jurist, the perceptive scholar, Aḥmad Abū al-Fawz, Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ramaḍān al-Ḥasanī, known as Aḥmad al-Marzūqī.

passages.intro_en: Text 3: his brothers. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Bushrā al-Fuʾād bi-Tarjamat al-Imām al-Ḥaddād of al-Ḥabīb ʿAlawī b. Ḥasan al-Ḥaddād (modern; one line)
passages.cite: ʿAlawī b.
