lines.ar: الْإِخْوَةُ لِلْحَبِيبِ عَبْدِاللهِ بْنِ عَلَوِيٍّ الْحَدَّادِ ثَلَاثَةُ إِخْوَانٍ : عُمَرُ وَعَلِيٌّ وَحَامِدٌ
lines.en: Al-Ḥabīb ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād had three brothers: ʿUmar, ʿAlī and Ḥāmid.

passages.ar: الْإِخْوَةُ لِلْحَبِيبِ عَبْدِاللهِ بْنِ عَلَوِيٍّ الْحَدَّادِ ثَلَاثَةُ إِخْوَانٍ : عُمَرُ وَعَلِيٌّ وَحَامِدٌ
passages.en: Al-Ḥabīb ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād had three brothers: ʿUmar, ʿAlī and Ḥāmid.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 113-114 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
lines.en: The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.

lines.ar: وَكُنْيَتُهُ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ.
lines.en: And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ. وَكُنْيَتُهُ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ.
passages.en: The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf. And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Two name chains from title pages: the Muʿāwana of Imām ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād and the Risāla Jāmiʿa of Imām Aḥmad ibn Zayn al-Ḥabashī.

questions.q: Line 1: write the author’s name, from عَبْدُ to الْحَدَّادُ.
questions.q_ar: اُكْتُبِ اسْمَ الْمُؤَلِّفِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ.
questions.a: عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ عَلَوِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْحَدَّادُ

questions.q: Line 1: how many people does the chain name, counting the author? Who are they?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ شَخْصًا فِي سِلْسِلَةِ السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟ مَنْ هُمْ؟
questions.a: Four: ʿAbdallāh, his father ʿAlawī, his grandfather Muḥammad and his great-grandfather Aḥmad.

questions.q: Which word means “son of”? How many times does it come in line 1?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْكَلِمَةُ الَّتِي بِمَعْنَى «ابْنُ»؟ كَمْ مَرَّةً جَاءَتْ؟
questions.a: بْنُ / بْنِ: three times.

questions.q: Line 1: which words before the name are titles? Write them.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ قَبْلَ الِاسْمِ أَلْقَابٌ؟ اُكْتُبْهَا.
questions.a: الْإِمَامُ، شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ، قُطْبُ الدَّعْوَةِ وَالْإِرْشَادِ

questions.q: The line ends with three words of belonging. What do they tell you about him?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتُ الثَّلَاثُ عَنْهُ؟
questions.a: He is a descendant of al-Ḥusayn, he is from Ḥaḍramawt, and he follows the Shāfiʿī school.

questions.q: Which word is his family name (laqab)? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ لَقَبُهُ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: الْحَدَّادُ: “the smith”.

questions.q: Line 2: translate the name.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الِاسْمَ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي.
questions.a: Aḥmad ibn Zayn ibn ʿAlawī ibn Aḥmad al-Ḥabashī al-ʿAlawī.
questions.ref_ar: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ زَيْنِ بْنِ عَلَوِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ الْحَبَشِيُّ الْعَلَوِيُّ

questions.q: In line 1 the title words (الْإِمَامُ، شَيْخُ، قُطْبُ) and the words of belonging all end in ـُ. Why?
questions.q_ar: كُلُّ كَلِمَاتِ اللَّقَبِ الْأُولَى وَالنِّسْبَةِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ تَنْتَهِي بِضَمَّةٍ. لِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: They stand in apposition (badal) to the name and share its ending: the name is nominative, so they are too.

questions.q: In line 1 the word “son of” ends in ـُ the first time (بْنُ عَلَوِيِّ) but in ـِ later (بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ). Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي «بْنُ» بِضَمَّةٍ أَوَّلًا ثُمَّ بِكَسْرَةٍ؟
questions.a: بْن copies the name before it: after عَبْدُ اللهِ it is ـُ, after the genitive name عَلَوِيِّ it is ـِ.

questions.q: What kind of text is this?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟
questions.a: The line that names the author at the start of a short book (a matn): the Safīna and the ʿAqīdat al-ʿAwāmm.

questions.q: Line 1: write the author’s name (after the titles).
questions.q_ar: اُكْتُبِ اسْمَ الْمُؤَلِّفِ بَعْدَ الْأَلْقَابِ.
questions.a: سَالِمِ بْنِ سُمَيْرٍ الْحَضْرَمِيِّ: Sālim ibn Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī.

questions.q: Both lines start with لِـ (“by”). What ending do all the words after it have?
questions.q_ar: الْكَلِمَةُ الْأُولَى فِيهَا لِـ: بِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي الْكَلِمَاتُ بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: ـِ: the titles, the name, بْنِ and the belonging word all follow the لِـ (أَحْمَدَ and رَمَضَانَ show ـَ only because they refuse tanwīn and kasra).

questions.q: Line 1: write the three titles before the name.
questions.q_ar: اُكْتُبِ الْأَلْقَابَ الثَّلَاثَةَ قَبْلَ الِاسْمِ.
questions.a: الشَّيْخِ الْعَالِمِ الْفَاضِلِ: the shaykh, the scholar, the excellent.

questions.q: Line 2: what is this? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي: مَا هَذِهِ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: His kunya: Abū al-Fawz, “father of al-Fawz”.

questions.q: Line 2: write the chain after the kunya, from أَحْمَدَ to الْحَسَنِيِّ.
questions.q_ar: اُكْتُبِ السِّلْسِلَةَ بَعْدَ الْكُنْيَةِ.
questions.a: أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ رَمَضَانَ الْحَسَنِيِّ: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ramaḍān al-Ḥasanī.

questions.q: Translate. What does this last part add?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ. مَاذَا تُضِيفُ هَذِهِ الْعِبَارَةُ؟
questions.a: “Known by the name of Aḥmad al-Marzūqī”: the name by which people know him.

questions.q: Why does the kunya read أَبِي here, and not أَبُو or أَبَا? (Lesson 40)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «أَبِي» وَلَيْسَتْ «أَبُو» أَوْ «أَبَا»؟
questions.a: The whole line depends on لِـ, so every word is genitive: the five nouns take ـِ.

questions.q: Line 2 gives this author many kinds of name. List them.
questions.q_ar: اُذْكُرْ أَنْوَاعَ الْأَسْمَاءِ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي.
questions.a: Titles; own name (أَحْمَدَ); kunya (أَبِي الْفَوْزِ); chain (بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ رَمَضَانَ); belonging (الْحَسَنِيِّ); the name he is known by (الْمَرْزُوقِيِّ).

questions.q: What kind of text is this?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟
questions.a: One line of a modern biography: it names the brothers of Imām al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: Translate the first part, up to ثَلَاثَةُ.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْجُزْءَ الْأَوَّلَ إِلَى كَلِمَةِ ثَلَاثَةُ.
questions.a: The brothers of al-Ḥabīb ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād are …
questions.ref_ar: الْإِخْوَةُ لِلْحَبِيبِ عَبْدِاللهِ بْنِ عَلَوِيٍّ الْحَدَّادِ

questions.q: How many brothers? Write their names.
questions.q_ar: كَمْ أَخًا؟ اُكْتُبْ أَسْمَاءَهُمْ.
questions.a: Three: عُمَرُ وَعَلِيٌّ وَحَامِدٌ.

questions.q: Which word is the family name (laqab)? Which two words come before it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ اللَّقَبُ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ قَبْلَهَا؟
questions.a: الْحَدَّادِ; before it عَلَوِيٍّ (his father’s name) and بْنِ.

questions.q: The three names come after a colon. What do they do for the words ثَلَاثَةُ إِخْوَانٍ?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الثَّلَاثَةُ بَعْدَ النُّقْطَتَيْنِ؟
questions.a: They name the three brothers: they explain the words before them (badal).

questions.q: The three names end in ـُ or ـٌ. Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي الْأَسْمَاءُ الثَّلَاثَةُ بِضَمَّةٍ؟
questions.a: They are a badal of ثَلَاثَةُ إِخْوَانٍ, which is nominative (the “is” part of the sentence), so they are too.

questions.q: عُمَرُ has no tanwīn but عَلِيٌّ has tanwīn. Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَا تَنْوِينَ فِي عُمَرُ وَفِي عَلِيٌّ تَنْوِينٌ؟
questions.a: عُمَر is one of the names that refuse tanwīn (Lesson 40); عَلِيّ is an ordinary declinable name.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf. And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.

questions.q: Which word links the two names سَالِمُ and يُوسُفَ?
questions.a: بْنُ (son of)

questions.q: What is أَبُو أَحْمَدَ?
questions.a: A kunya: a name with “father of”.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The name of the shaykh is Salim son of Yusuf.
questions.a: اِسْمُ الشَّيْخِ سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ كِتَابَ الشَّيْخِ سَالِمِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ.
translate.en: The boy read the book of Shaykh Salim ibn ʿAli.

translate.ar: رَأَيْتُ أَحْمَدَ بْنَ يُوسُفَ التَّرِيمِيَّ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: I saw Ahmad ibn Yusuf, the Tarimi, in the mosque.

translate.ar: ذَهَبَتْ فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ أَحْمَدَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
translate.en: Fatima, the daughter of Ahmad, went to the school.

translate.ar: سَأَلَ الطَّالِبُ الشَّيْخَ عُمَرَ بْنَ أَحْمَدَ.
translate.en: The student asked Shaykh ʿUmar ibn Ahmad.
The father of Ahmad is a teacher in the school.

translate.ar: كَتَبَ سَالِمُ بْنُ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ رِسَالَةً إِلَى أَبِيهِ.
translate.en: Salim ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAli wrote a letter to his father.
The mother of Maryam lives in Tarim.

translate.ar: الْفَقِيهُ الشَّيْخُ يُوسُفُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
translate.en: The jurist, Shaykh Yusuf ibn ʿAli, is from Tarim.

translate.ar: شَكَرَ الْمُعَلِّمُ الطَّالِبَ سَالِمَ بْنَ أَحْمَدَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
translate.en: The teacher thanked the student Salim ibn Ahmad because he served the guests.

translate.ar: سَمِعْتُ الدَّرْسَ مِنَ الشَّيْخِ عَلِيٍّ الْعَلَوِيِّ.
translate.en: I heard the lesson from Shaykh ʿAli, the ʿAlawī.

translate.ar: قَالَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ لِابْنِهِ: اِقْرَأِ الْكِتَابَ.
translate.en: The father of Ahmad said to his son: Read the book.

translate.ar: هَذَا كِتَابُ الْأَدَبِ. لِلشَّيْخِ سَالِمِ بْنِ عُمَرَ التَّرِيمِيِّ الْعَلَوِيِّ. قَرَأَهُ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
translate.en: This is the book of manners. By Shaykh Salim ibn ʿUmar, the Tarimi, the ʿAlawī. The students read it in the ribāṭ.
This is the book of Shaykh Salim ibn ʿUmar.
translate.ar: هَذَا كِتَابُ الشَّيْخِ سَالِمِ بْنِ عُمَرَ.
alt: هَذَا كِتَابٌ لِلشَّيْخِ سَالِمِ بْنِ عُمَرَ.

translate.en: Fatima, the daughter of Ahmad, went to the school.
translate.ar: ذَهَبَتْ فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ أَحْمَدَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ.

translate.en: The teacher thanked Yusuf ibn Salim.
I went to Shaykh ʿAli, the ʿAlawī.
The father of Ahmad read the book.
Salim ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAli, the Tarimi, wrote a letter.
translate.ar: كَتَبَ سَالِمُ بْنُ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ التَّرِيمِيُّ رِسَالَةً.

translate.en: I saw Ahmad ibn Salim in the mosque.
translate.ar: رَأَيْتُ أَحْمَدَ بْنَ سَالِمٍ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.

translate.en: The students read the book of the jurist, Shaykh Yusuf.
translate.ar: قَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ كِتَابَ الْفَقِيهِ الشَّيْخِ يُوسُفَ.

readings.title_en: A verb and its little word: one unit
readings.question_en: Which little word does this verb take, and does it change the meaning?
readings.question_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَأْتِي مَعَ هَذَا الْفِعْلِ؟ وَهَلْ يُغَيِّرُ الْمَعْنَى؟

passages.intro_en: Counsel from Imam al-Ḥaddād. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: al-Ḥaddād, Risālat al-Muʿāwana wa-l-Muẓāhara wa-l-Muʾāzara (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, no. 3), Dār al-Ḥāwī li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr wa-l-Tawzīʿ, 2nd ed., 1414 AH (title page of the Shamela text); Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, 241.mdb), pp. 14–147 of the digital text (the copy opens the text at p. 13, which suggests it follows the print; not checked against a print). Three sentences (nos. 1, 3 and 4 of the four in the research file); vowels added by the course (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: وَهَذَا التَّفَكُّرُ يُثْمِرُ لَكَ الزُّهْدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالرَّغْبَةَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ
lines.en: And this reflection bears for you detachment from this world and desire for the next.

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِتَرْكِ الْمُزَاحِ رَأْسًا
lines.en: And you should give up joking altogether.

lines.ar: حَمَلَنِي عَلَى وَضْعِهَا الِامْتِثَالُ لِأَمْرِ اللهِ تَعَالَى وَأَمْرِ رَسُولِهِ ، وَالرَّغْبَةُ فِي الْوَعْدِ الصَّادِقِ
lines.en: What moved me to write it was obedience to the command of God Most High and of His messenger, and desire for the true promise.

glossary.en: altogether (an idiom; the word also means “head”)

passages.ar: وَهَذَا التَّفَكُّرُ يُثْمِرُ لَكَ الزُّهْدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالرَّغْبَةَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ وَعَلَيْكَ بِتَرْكِ الْمُزَاحِ رَأْسًا حَمَلَنِي عَلَى وَضْعِهَا الِامْتِثَالُ لِأَمْرِ اللهِ تَعَالَى وَأَمْرِ رَسُولِهِ ، وَالرَّغْبَةُ فِي الْوَعْدِ الصَّادِقِ
passages.en: And this reflection bears for you detachment from this world and desire for the next. And you should give up joking altogether. What moved me to write it was obedience to the command of God Most High and of His messenger, and desire for the true promise.

passages.intro_en: A short text: the saying of the Habib. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: In the evening Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s circle.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: رَغِبَ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ فِي الْمَالِ، وَرَغِبَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَالِ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Some people desired wealth, and some of them turned away from wealth.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: لِمَاذَا رَغِبَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَالِ؟
lines.en: Then Ahmad asked: Why did some of them turn away from wealth?

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِأَنَّهُمْ نَظَرُوا إِلَى الْآخِرَةِ وَرَغِبُوا فِيهَا.
lines.en: The Habib said: Because they looked to the Hereafter and desired it.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: أَنَا أَرْغَبُ فِي الْعِلْمِ.
lines.en: And Umar said: I desire knowledge.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ، وَلَا تَرْغَبْ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Seek knowledge, and do not turn away from the majlis.

lines.ar: رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: أَنَا أَرْغَبُ فِي الْعِلْمِ.
lines.en: Ahmad returned to the house and said to his mother: I desire knowledge.

lines.ar: وَدَعَا الْحَبِيبُ لَهُ: دَعَوْتُ لَكَ يَا أَحْمَدُ.
lines.en: And the Habib prayed for him: I have prayed for you, Ahmad.

passages.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: رَغِبَ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ فِي الْمَالِ، وَرَغِبَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَالِ. ثُمَّ سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: لِمَاذَا رَغِبَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَالِ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِأَنَّهُمْ نَظَرُوا إِلَى الْآخِرَةِ وَرَغِبُوا فِيهَا. وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: أَنَا أَرْغَبُ فِي الْعِلْمِ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ، وَلَا تَرْغَبْ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ. رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: أَنَا أَرْغَبُ فِي الْعِلْمِ. وَدَعَا الْحَبِيبُ لَهُ: دَعَوْتُ لَكَ يَا أَحْمَدُ.
passages.en: In the evening Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s circle. The Habib said: Some people desired wealth, and some of them turned away from wealth. Then Ahmad asked: Why did some of them turn away from wealth? The Habib said: Because they looked to the Hereafter and desired it. And Umar said: I desire knowledge. The Habib said: Seek knowledge, and do not turn away from the majlis. Ahmad returned to the house and said to his mother: I desire knowledge. And the Habib prayed for him: I have prayed for you, Ahmad.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 115-116 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
lines.en: The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
lines.en: So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.

passages.ar: رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ. فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
passages.en: The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin. So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.

glossary.en: altogether (an idiom; the word also means “head”)

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: And this reflection bears for you detachment from this world and desire for the next.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And you should give up joking altogether.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: What moved me to write it was obedience to the command of God Most High and of His messenger, and desire for the true promise.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A piece of counsel (advice) from the Risālat al-Muʿāwana of Imam al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: Line 1: what does the reflection bring? Name the two things.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَاذَا يُثْمِرُ التَّفَكُّرُ؟ اُذْكُرْ شَيْئَيْنِ.
questions.a: Detachment from this world (الزُّهْدُ) and desire for the next (الرَّغْبَةُ).

questions.q: Which little word follows الزُّهْدَ, and which follows الرَّغْبَةَ?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ بَعْدَ الزُّهْدِ؟ وَأَيُّ حَرْفٍ بَعْدَ الرَّغْبَةِ؟
questions.a: Both take فِي.
questions.ref_ar: الزُّهْدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالرَّغْبَةَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ

questions.q: True or false: line 2 tells you to keep joking.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَأْمُرُكَ السَّطْرُ الثَّانِي بِالْمُزَاحِ.
questions.a: False. عَلَيْكَ بِـ means “you should …”: give up joking.

questions.q: Line 3: what two things moved the writer to write? Find the two nouns.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَا الشَّيْئَانِ اللَّذَانِ حَمَلَاهُ عَلَى الْكِتَابَةِ؟
questions.a: Obedience (الِامْتِثَالُ) to the command of God and His messenger, and desire (الرَّغْبَةُ) for the promise.

questions.q: Find the word that means “desire”. What does it have in common with the verb رَغِبَ?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «الْمَيْلَ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ». مَا الَّذِي تَشْتَرِكُ فِيهِ مَعَ رَغِبَ؟
questions.a: الرَّغْبَةُ. Both come from the root ر غ ب, and both take فِي for “desire for”.

questions.q: Who is the writer speaking to in lines 1 and 2? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ الْكَاتِبُ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: To “you”: the endings ـكَ in لَكَ and عَلَيْكَ.

questions.q: Here الرَّغْبَةُ is “desire for”. What would رَغْبَةٌ عَنْ mean, and why would it not fit?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَعْنِي «رَغْبَةٌ عَنْ»؟ وَلِمَاذَا لَا تُنَاسِبُ هُنَا؟
questions.a: “Turning away from”. It would say the writer turns away from the true promise, the opposite of what he means.

questions.q: The writer gives his reasons for writing (line 3). Why would a teacher begin a book of advice with his reasons?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَبْدَأُ الْمُعَلِّمُ كِتَابَ النَّصِيحَةِ بِذِكْرِ أَسْبَابِهِ؟
questions.a: He shows that he writes to obey God and to win the promise, not to show off. The reader then reads the advice in the right spirit.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the Habib’s circle, with Umar.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: The Habib said: Some people desired wealth, and some of them turned away from wealth.

questions.q: Which little word turns رَغِبَ into “turned away from”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَجْعَلُ «رَغِبَ» بِمَعْنَى «ابْتَعَدَ عَنْ»؟
questions.a: عَنْ (here عَنِ الْمَالِ).

questions.q: Which little word gives “desired”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يُعْطِي مَعْنَى «أَرَادَ»؟
questions.a: فِي.

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask in line 3?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ؟
questions.a: Why some of them turned away from wealth.

questions.q: Why did they turn away from wealth? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا رَغِبُوا عَنِ الْمَالِ؟
questions.a: Because they looked to the Hereafter and desired it.

questions.q: What does the ending ـهَا point to?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ ـهَا؟
questions.a: The Hereafter (الْآخِرَةِ).

questions.q: What does Umar desire?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَرْغَبُ عُمَرُ؟
questions.a: Knowledge.

questions.q: True or false: the Habib tells Ahmad to turn away from the majlis.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ: اِبْتَعِدْ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ.
questions.a: False. لَا تَرْغَبْ عَنْ = “do not turn away from”.

questions.q: Who prayed for whom at the end?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ دَعَا لِمَنْ فِي آخِرِ النَّصِّ؟
questions.a: The Habib prayed for Ahmad.

questions.q: Which little word shows that the Habib prayed “for” Ahmad? What would دَعَوْتُ عَلَيْكَ mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّهُ دَعَا «لِأَحْمَدَ»؟ وَمَاذَا تَعْنِي «دَعَوْتُ عَلَيْكَ»؟
questions.a: لَكَ (لِـ = for). دَعَوْتُ عَلَيْكَ would mean “I prayed against you”.

questions.q: The Habib speaks about wealth, then about knowledge, then about the majlis. What one thing joins the three pieces?
questions.q_ar: مَا الَّذِي يَجْمَعُ الْأَجْزَاءَ الثَّلَاثَةَ؟
questions.a: Each says what to turn towards and what to turn away from: the same verb رَغِبَ with فِي and عَنْ.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin. So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.

questions.q: Which preposition goes with رَغِبَ for “to desire” and which for “to turn away from”?
questions.a: فِي for desire; عَنْ for turning away.

questions.q: Which word is the opposite of الْأَجْرِ (reward)?
questions.a: الْإِثْمِ (sin)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy desired knowledge.
questions.a: رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ.

translate.ar: رَغِبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ السُّوقِ.
translate.en: Ahmad desired knowledge and turned away from the market.
The student asked the teacher about the meaning.

translate.ar: نَظَرَ عُمَرُ فِي الْكِتَابِ ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
translate.en: Umar looked into the book, then looked at the Habib.
The Habib prayed for the guests and for his companions.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ عَلَى الْحَبِيبِ وَأَخَذُوا الْعِلْمَ عَنْهُ.
translate.en: The students read to the Habib and took knowledge from him.

translate.ar: كَانَ لِلرَّجُلِ أَجْرٌ لِأَنَّهُ دَعَا النَّاسَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: The man had a reward because he called the people to the mosque.

translate.ar: لَا تَرْغَبْ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ، فَإِنَّ فِيهِ ذِكْرًا طَيِّبًا.
translate.en: Do not turn away from the majlis, for there is good remembrance in it.

translate.ar: سَافَرَ أَبِي إِلَى تَرِيمَ وَرَغِبَ فِي زِيَارَةِ الْحَبِيبِ.
translate.en: My father travelled to Tarim and desired to visit the Habib.

translate.ar: نَظَرَ الطَّالِبُ فِي الْكِتَابِ وَسَأَلَ الْحَبِيبَ عَنِ الْمَعْنَى.
translate.en: The student looked into the book and asked the Habib about the meaning.

lines.ar: وَمَنْ دَعَا إِلَى ضَلَالَةٍ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْإِثْمِ مِثْلُ آثَامِ مَنْ تَبِعَهُ
lines.en: And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him,

lines.ar: لَا يَنْقُصُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ آثَامِهِمْ شَيْئًا
lines.en: without that diminishing their sins in the least."

translate.ar: وَمَنْ دَعَا إِلَى ضَلَالَةٍ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْإِثْمِ مِثْلُ آثَامِ مَنْ تَبِعَهُ لَا يَنْقُصُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ آثَامِهِمْ شَيْئًا
translate.en: And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing their sins in the least."

lines.ar: الَّذِي جَعَلَ الدَّعْوَةَ إِلَى الْهُدَى ، وَالدَّلَالَةَ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ ، وَالنَّصِيحَةَ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ ، مِنْ أَفْضَلِ الْقُرُبَاتِ
lines.en: He who made calling to guidance, pointing to good, and sincere counsel for the Muslims among the best of the acts that bring one near.

translate.ar: الَّذِي جَعَلَ الدَّعْوَةَ إِلَى الْهُدَى ، وَالدَّلَالَةَ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ ، وَالنَّصِيحَةَ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ ، مِنْ أَفْضَلِ الْقُرُبَاتِ
translate.en: He who made calling to guidance, pointing to good, and sincere counsel for the Muslims among the best of the acts that bring one near.
The boy desired knowledge.
Ahmad turned away from the market.
The teacher called the students to the lesson.
He prayed for his mother and his father.
You should hold to patience.
Whoever calls the people to the mosque will have a reward.
translate.ar: مَنْ دَعَا النَّاسَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ كَانَ لَهُ أَجْرٌ.

translate.en: His desire for knowledge was great.
Do not turn away from the majlis.
He asked about the book and looked into it.
I believed in Allah, and I desire the Hereafter.
The students read to the Habib in the ribāṭ.
translate.ar: قَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ عَلَى الْحَبِيبِ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.

translate.en: He did not turn away from the lesson, so he has a reward.
translate.ar: لَمْ يَرْغَبْ عَنِ الدَّرْسِ فَكَانَ لَهُ أَجْرٌ.

readings.title_en: Reading day 5: advice (do, do not, if … then)
readings.question_en: How do I read a text that tells me what to do?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ نَصًّا يَقُولُ لِي: اِفْعَلْ وَلَا تَفْعَلْ؟

passages.intro_en: Counsel from Imam al-Ḥaddād. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād
passages.cite: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, no. 7); Shamela Master Library copy (Ba Zuhayr Library, 233.mdb); publisher and year not stated; pp. 4–5 of the digital text (printed pagination not given); TLNOOR 1256 is a separate scan. Both sentences; the source copy is only partly vowelled, so the course completed the vowels (vowelled for learners; letters unchanged; a misprint وَأوَّلُ corrected to وَأَوَّلُ).

lines.ar: وَأَوَّلُ شَيْءٍ يَبْدَأُ بِهِ الْمُرِيدُ فِي طَرِيقِ اللهِ تَصْحِيحُ التَّوْبَةِ إِلَى اللهِ تَعَالَى مِنْ جَمِيعِ الذُّنُوبِ
lines.en: The first thing the seeker begins with on the path to God is putting right his repentance to God Most High, from all sins.

lines.ar: وَلْيَكُنْ نَاصِحًا لَهُمْ رَحِيمًا بِهِمْ مُشْفِقًا عَلَيْهِمْ، مُعْتَقِدًا الْخَيْرَ فِيهِمْ، يُحِبُّ لَهُمْ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ
lines.en: Let him be sincere towards them, merciful to them, caring for them, thinking well of them, loving for them what he loves for himself of good.

passages.ar: وَأَوَّلُ شَيْءٍ يَبْدَأُ بِهِ الْمُرِيدُ فِي طَرِيقِ اللهِ تَصْحِيحُ التَّوْبَةِ إِلَى اللهِ تَعَالَى مِنْ جَمِيعِ الذُّنُوبِ وَلْيَكُنْ نَاصِحًا لَهُمْ رَحِيمًا بِهِمْ مُشْفِقًا عَلَيْهِمْ، مُعْتَقِدًا الْخَيْرَ فِيهِمْ، يُحِبُّ لَهُمْ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ
passages.en: The first thing the seeker begins with on the path to God is putting right his repentance to God Most High, from all sins. Let him be sincere towards them, merciful to them, caring for them, thinking well of them, loving for them what he loves for himself of good.

passages.intro_en: A short text: the night before. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ فِي اللَّيْلِ: اِجْتَهِدْ، وَاسْتَيْقِظْ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ.
lines.en: The Habib said to Ahmad at night: Strive, and wake before dawn.

lines.ar: وَإِذَا اسْتَيْقَظْتَ فَاذْكُرِ اللَّهَ.
lines.en: And when you wake, remember Allah.

lines.ar: وَلَا تَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ، وَلَا تَذْهَبْ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ بِلَا وُضُوءٍ.
lines.en: And do not sit in the street, and do not go to the mosque without ablution.

lines.ar: سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ ثُمَّ نَامَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
lines.en: Ahmad listened to the Habib, then slept in the ribāṭ.

lines.ar: وَقَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ اسْتَيْقَظَ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ.
lines.en: And before dawn he woke up and remembered Allah.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ مَعَ عُمَرَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: Then he went with Umar to the mosque.

lines.ar: وَجَلَسَ الْحَبِيبُ مَعَهُمْ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ وَقَالَ: إِذَا اجْتَهَدَ الطَّالِبُ فَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ.
lines.en: And the Habib sat with them after the prayer and said: If the student strives, he is happy.

lines.ar: رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: اسْتَيْقَظْتُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ، وَلَمْ أَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ.
lines.en: Ahmad returned to the house and said to his mother: I woke before dawn, and I did not sit in the street.

lines.ar: فَشَكَرَتْهُ أُمُّهُ لِأَنَّهُ اجْتَهَدَ.
lines.en: And his mother thanked him because he had strived.

passages.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ فِي اللَّيْلِ: اِجْتَهِدْ، وَاسْتَيْقِظْ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ. وَإِذَا اسْتَيْقَظْتَ فَاذْكُرِ اللَّهَ. وَلَا تَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ، وَلَا تَذْهَبْ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ بِلَا وُضُوءٍ. سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ ثُمَّ نَامَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ. وَقَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ اسْتَيْقَظَ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ. ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ مَعَ عُمَرَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ. وَجَلَسَ الْحَبِيبُ مَعَهُمْ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ وَقَالَ: إِذَا اجْتَهَدَ الطَّالِبُ فَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ. رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: اسْتَيْقَظْتُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ، وَلَمْ أَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ. فَشَكَرَتْهُ أُمُّهُ لِأَنَّهُ اجْتَهَدَ.
passages.en: The Habib said to Ahmad at night: Strive, and wake before dawn. And when you wake, remember Allah. And do not sit in the street, and do not go to the mosque without ablution. Ahmad listened to the Habib, then slept in the ribāṭ. And before dawn he woke up and remembered Allah. Then he went with Umar to the mosque. And the Habib sat with them after the prayer and said: If the student strives, he is happy. Ahmad returned to the house and said to his mother: I woke before dawn, and I did not sit in the street. And his mother thanked him because he had strived.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 117-118 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
lines.en: The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ جَلَسَ وَاجْتَهَدَ فِي وِرْدِهِ.
lines.en: Then he sat and strove in his wird.

passages.ar: اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ. ثُمَّ جَلَسَ وَاجْتَهَدَ فِي وِرْدِهِ.
passages.en: The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk. Then he sat and strove in his wird.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: The first thing the seeker begins with on the path to God is putting right his repentance to God Most High, from all sins.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: Let him be sincere towards them, merciful to them, caring for them, thinking well of them, loving for them what he loves for himself of good.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Advice (adab) for the seeker, from the Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd of Imam ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: Line 1: what is the first thing the seeker begins with?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: بِمَاذَا يَبْدَأُ الْمُرِيدُ أَوَّلًا؟
questions.a: Putting repentance (التَّوْبَةُ) right.

questions.q: From which sins must he repent?
questions.q_ar: مِنْ أَيِّ الذُّنُوبِ يَتُوبُ؟
questions.a: From all sins (جَمِيعِ الذُّنُوبِ).

questions.q: Find the word for “the seeker”. What is its root?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةَ «الطَّالِبِ». مَا جَذْرُهَا؟
questions.a: الْمُرِيدُ; root ر و د (wanting, seeking).

questions.q: What does طَرِيق mean here?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى طَرِيق هُنَا؟
questions.a: “way, path”: the path to God.

questions.q: Each describing word has its own little word after it. Which three?
questions.q_ar: لِكُلِّ صِفَةٍ حَرْفٌ بَعْدَهَا. مَا الْحُرُوفُ الثَّلَاثَةُ؟
questions.a: لَهُمْ، بِهِمْ، عَلَيْهِمْ.
questions.ref_ar: نَاصِحًا لَهُمْ رَحِيمًا بِهِمْ مُشْفِقًا عَلَيْهِمْ

questions.q: Name two things the seeker should be towards them.
questions.q_ar: اُذْكُرْ شَيْئَيْنِ يَجِبُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْمُرِيدُ عَلَيْهِمَا.
questions.a: Any two of: sincere, merciful, caring, thinking well of them.

questions.q: What does he love for them?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُحِبُّ لَهُمْ؟
questions.a: What he loves for himself of good.

questions.q: This word begins with a “let him” (لِـ). Who is it about: “you” or “him”?
questions.q_ar: هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ تَبْدَأُ بِلَامِ الْأَمْرِ. عَنْ مَنْ تَتَكَلَّمُ: «أَنْتَ» أَمْ «هُوَ»؟
questions.a: About “him”: the seeker. The advice is general, not spoken to one person.

questions.q: Why does the writer begin the seeker’s path with repentance and not with a long list of practices?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَبْدَأُ الْكَاتِبُ طَرِيقَ الْمُرِيدِ بِالتَّوْبَةِ؟
questions.a: Repentance cleans the ground first: it is the start of the way (أَوَّلُ الطَّرِيقِ), and everything after it stands on it.

questions.q: What did the Habib tell Ahmad at night? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَحْمَدَ فِي اللَّيْلِ؟
questions.a: To strive, and to wake before dawn.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And when you wake, remember Allah.

questions.q: Find the two commands in line 1.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْأَمْرَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ.
questions.a: اِجْتَهِدْ and اِسْتَيْقِظْ.

questions.q: Which word tells you when? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الْوَقْتِ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: قَبْلَ: before.

questions.q: Which word makes this a prohibition? What is forbidden?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَجْعَلُهَا نَهْيًا؟ وَمَا الْمَمْنُوعُ؟
questions.a: لَا. Sitting in the street.

questions.q: What is the second thing Ahmad must not do? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَا الشَّيْءُ الثَّانِي الَّذِي لَا يَفْعَلُهُ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: Go to the mosque without ablution.

questions.q: Did Ahmad obey? What shows it? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: هَلْ أَطَاعَ أَحْمَدُ؟ مَا الدَّلِيلُ؟
questions.a: Yes: he woke before dawn and remembered Allah.

questions.q: Who went with Ahmad to the mosque?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ ذَهَبَ مَعَ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: Umar.

questions.q: Translate line 7.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ السَّابِعَ.
questions.a: And the Habib sat with them after the prayer and said: If the student strives, he is happy.

questions.q: Find the word that begins the “if” part and the word that begins the answer.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَبْدَأُ الشَّرْطَ وَالَّتِي تَبْدَأُ الْجَوَابَ.
questions.a: إِذَا begins the condition; فَهُوَ begins the answer.

questions.q: Which of the Habib’s pieces of advice does Ahmad say he obeyed in line 8?
questions.q_ar: أَيَّ نَصِيحَةٍ مِنْ نَصَائِحِ الْحَبِيبِ يَقُولُ أَحْمَدُ إِنَّهُ أَطَاعَهَا فِي السَّطْرِ ٨؟
questions.a: The prohibition of line 3: do not sit in the street.

questions.q: In line 2 the answer to “when you wake” is a command. Why does فَـ join them?
questions.q_ar: جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ أَمْرٌ. لِمَاذَا تَرْبِطُهُ فَـ؟
questions.a: The answer is a command, which cannot stand alone after “if”; فَـ ties it to the condition.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk. Then he sat and strove in his wird.

questions.q: Which verb means “he woke up”? Give its present.
questions.a: اِسْتَيْقَظَ; its present is يَسْتَيْقِظُ

questions.q: Which verb means “he strove”? Give its root.
questions.a: اِجْتَهَدَ (root ج ه د)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy woke up before dawn.
questions.a: اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ.

translate.en: Wake before dawn and remember Allah.

translate.ar: لَا تَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ وَلَا تَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا.
translate.en: Do not sit in the street, and do not talk much.

translate.ar: إِذَا دَخَلْتَ الْمَسْجِدَ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى النَّاسِ.
translate.en: If you enter the mosque, greet the people.
You should hold to patience in seeking knowledge.

translate.ar: إِذَا اجْتَهَدَ الْمُرِيدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ فَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ.
translate.en: If the seeker strives in knowledge, he is happy.
Begin with remembrance, then read the lesson.

translate.ar: اِذْهَبْ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ وَلَا تَرْجِعْ إِلَى النَّوْمِ.
translate.en: Go to the mosque after dawn, and do not go back to sleep.
The way is long, so strive.
The seeker’s repentance is the beginning of the way.

lines.ar: إِذَا اسْتَيْقَظْتَ مِنَ النَّوْمِ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ فَاذْكُرِ اللَّهَ.
lines.en: If you wake from sleep before dawn, remember Allah.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ اجْلِسْ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَاقْرَأْ مِنَ الْمُصْحَفِ.
lines.en: Then sit in the mosque and read from the muṣḥaf.

lines.ar: وَاجْتَهِدْ فِي الذِّكْرِ، وَلَا تَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: And strive in remembrance, and do not talk much.

translate.ar: إِذَا اسْتَيْقَظْتَ مِنَ النَّوْمِ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ فَاذْكُرِ اللَّهَ. ثُمَّ اجْلِسْ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَاقْرَأْ مِنَ الْمُصْحَفِ. وَاجْتَهِدْ فِي الذِّكْرِ، وَلَا تَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا.
translate.en: If you wake from sleep before dawn, remember Allah. Then sit in the mosque and read from the muṣḥaf. And strive in remembrance, and do not talk much.

lines.ar: فَلَا تَتْرُكِ السِّوَاكَ ؛ فَإِنَّهُ مَطْهَرَةٌ لِلْفَمِ وَمَرْضَاةٌ لِلرَّبِّ
lines.en: So do not leave the siwāk, for it cleanses the mouth and pleases the Lord.

translate.ar: فَلَا تَتْرُكِ السِّوَاكَ ؛ فَإِنَّهُ مَطْهَرَةٌ لِلْفَمِ وَمَرْضَاةٌ لِلرَّبِّ
translate.en: So do not leave the siwāk, for it cleanses the mouth and pleases the Lord.
Strive in knowledge.
Wake before dawn, then remember Allah.
translate.ar: اِسْتَيْقِظْ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ ثُمَّ اذْكُرِ اللَّهَ.

translate.en: Do not sit in the street.
If you hear the Habib, sit with him.
You should hold to repentance.
The seeker strove, and he woke before dawn.
Do not go back to sleep.
If you enter the mosque, greet the people.
translate.ar: إِذَا دَخَلْتَ الْمَسْجِدَ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى النَّاسِ.

translate.en: Begin with remembrance of Allah, then read the lesson.
translate.ar: اِبْدَأْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ اقْرَأِ الدَّرْسَ.

translate.en: Do not talk much, and strive in the lesson.
translate.ar: لَا تَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا وَاجْتَهِدْ فِي الدَّرْسِ.

translate.en: When the Habib comes, listen.
The way is long, so be patient.

readings.title_en: Little words of time, place and degree
readings.question_en: What do the little words always, mostly, never, very, also and only add to a sentence?
readings.question_ar: مَاذَا تَزِيدُ كَلِمَاتُ «دَائِمًا» وَ«أَبَدًا» وَ«جِدًّا» عَلَى الْجُمْلَةِ؟

passages.intro_en: Read the story, then answer. (★ rows are for adults and older students.)
passages.cite: Course text (the rawḥa), written for this lesson. Words of Lessons 1–66 and the extra words of Lesson 66 only.

lines.ar: يَذْهَبُ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ دَائِمًا.
lines.en: Ahmad always goes to the rawḥa.

lines.ar: وَغَالِبًا يَجْلِسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ قُرْبَ الْمِحْرَابِ.
lines.en: And mostly he sits in the circle near the miḥrāb.

lines.ar: أَمْسِ سَأَلَهُ عُمَرُ: هَلْ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟
lines.en: Yesterday ʿUmar asked him: Do you go to the rawḥa every day?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، وَلَمْ أَتْرُكِ الرَّوْحَةَ قَطُّ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: Yes, and I have never left the rawḥa.

lines.ar: وَالْحَبِيبُ يَقُولُ لِلطُّلَّابِ: لَا تَتْرُكُوا الرَّوْحَةَ أَبَدًا.
lines.en: And the Habib says to the students: Never leave the rawḥa.

lines.ar: وَالرَّوْحَةُ مُبَارَكَةٌ جِدًّا، وَيَحْضُرُهَا أَخُوهُ أَيْضًا.
lines.en: The rawḥa is very blessed, and his brother attends it too.

lines.ar: يَحْمِلُ أَحْمَدُ مُصْحَفًا فَقَطْ، وَيَسْمَعُ الْحَبِيبَ وَيَكْتُبُ كَلِمَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً.
lines.en: Ahmad carries only a muṣḥaf, and he listens to the Habib and writes new words.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدَ الرَّوْحَةِ يَرْجِعُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا.
lines.en: And after the rawḥa he returns to the house, happy.

passages.ar: يَذْهَبُ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ دَائِمًا. وَغَالِبًا يَجْلِسُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ قُرْبَ الْمِحْرَابِ. أَمْسِ سَأَلَهُ عُمَرُ: هَلْ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، وَلَمْ أَتْرُكِ الرَّوْحَةَ قَطُّ. وَالْحَبِيبُ يَقُولُ لِلطُّلَّابِ: لَا تَتْرُكُوا الرَّوْحَةَ أَبَدًا. وَالرَّوْحَةُ مُبَارَكَةٌ جِدًّا، وَيَحْضُرُهَا أَخُوهُ أَيْضًا. يَحْمِلُ أَحْمَدُ مُصْحَفًا فَقَطْ، وَيَسْمَعُ الْحَبِيبَ وَيَكْتُبُ كَلِمَاتٍ جَدِيدَةً. وَبَعْدَ الرَّوْحَةِ يَرْجِعُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا.
passages.en: Ahmad always goes to the rawḥa. And mostly he sits in the circle near the miḥrāb. Yesterday ʿUmar asked him: Do you go to the rawḥa every day? Ahmad said: Yes, and I have never left the rawḥa. And the Habib says to the students: Never leave the rawḥa. The rawḥa is very blessed, and his brother attends it too. Ahmad carries only a muṣḥaf, and he listens to the Habib and writes new words. And after the rawḥa he returns to the house, happy.

lines.ar: خَوْفُ الِانْدِرَاسِ الَّذِي يَسْتَوْلِي غَالِبًا عَلَى مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ مُدَوَّنًا وَمَجْمُوعًا
lines.en: The fear of loss, which usually overtakes what has not been written down and gathered.

lines.ar: فِي سَيْرِهِ إِلَى اللهِ قَدَمًا بَعْدَ قَدَمٍ
lines.en: On his journey to God, step after step.

passages.ar: خَوْفُ الِانْدِرَاسِ الَّذِي يَسْتَوْلِي غَالِبًا عَلَى مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ مُدَوَّنًا وَمَجْمُوعًا فِي سَيْرِهِ إِلَى اللهِ قَدَمًا بَعْدَ قَدَمٍ
passages.en: The fear of loss, which usually overtakes what has not been written down and gathered. On his journey to God, step after step.

passages.ar: وَمَعَاصِي اللِّسَانِ كَثِيرَةٌ أَيْضًا
passages.en: The sins of the tongue are also many.

lines.ar: لَمْ يَتْرُكِ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ قَطُّ.
lines.en: The boy never missed the rawḥa.

lines.ar: يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
lines.en: The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.

passages.ar: لَمْ يَتْرُكِ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ قَطُّ. يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
passages.en: The boy never missed the rawḥa. The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.

questions.q: Who goes to the rawḥa always?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَذْهَبُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ دَائِمًا؟
questions.a: Ahmad (يَذْهَبُ أَحْمَدُ … دَائِمًا).

questions.q: Where does he mostly sit?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ يَجْلِسُ غَالِبًا؟
questions.a: In the circle, near the miḥrāb.

questions.q: Who asked, and when?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَأَلَ؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: ʿUmar, yesterday (أَمْسِ).

questions.q: What did ʿUmar ask?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ عُمَرُ؟
questions.a: Whether he goes to the rawḥa every day.

questions.q: In line 4, which little word says “ever”, and which word before it makes the sentence “not”?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٤: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «فِي أَيِّ وَقْتٍ»؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ قَبْلَهَا تَنْفِي؟
questions.a: قَطُّ; and لَمْ. Together: “I have never left the rawḥa”.

questions.q: What does the Habib tell the students?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ لِلطُّلَّابِ؟
questions.a: Never leave the rawḥa (لَا تَتْرُكُوا الرَّوْحَةَ أَبَدًا).

questions.q: True or false? The Habib says: “You may leave the rawḥa sometimes.”
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. لَا … أَبَدًا means “never”.

questions.q: How is the rawḥa described, and which little word makes that stronger?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ الرَّوْحَةُ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَزِيدُ الْمَعْنَى قُوَّةً؟
questions.a: Blessed (مُبَارَكَةٌ); جِدًّا (very).

questions.q: Who else attends, and which little word says “too”?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَحْضُرُ أَيْضًا؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي الزِّيَادَةَ؟
questions.a: His brother; أَيْضًا.

questions.q: What does Ahmad carry, and which little word says “only”?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَحْمِلُ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي الْحَصْرَ؟
questions.a: A muṣḥaf only; فَقَطْ.

questions.q: Put in order: (a) he sits in the circle (b) he returns home (c) he goes to the rawḥa.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ.
questions.a: c, a, b.

questions.q: Line 8: what does بَعْدَ say? What would the sentence mean with قَبْلَ?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَعْنِي «بَعْدَ»؟ وَمَاذَا لَوْ كَانَتْ «قَبْلَ»؟
questions.a: بَعْدَ = after the rawḥa. With قَبْلَ: “before the rawḥa he returns to the house”.

questions.q: Lines 4 and 5 both mean “never”, with different words. Which of the two looks back at the past?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَ «قَطُّ» وَ«أَبَدًا»؟
questions.a: لَمْ … قَطُّ looks back (“never up to now”). لَا … أَبَدًا looks at all time (“never at any time”).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A writing of Imam ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād: his Mukātabāt (letters and counsels), vol. 1.

questions.q: Which little word in line 1 says how often?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ١ تَقُولُ كَمْ مَرَّةً؟
questions.a: غَالِبًا (usually).

questions.q: What is feared in line 1?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُخَافُ فِي السَّطْرِ ١؟
questions.a: That what has not been written down and gathered will be lost.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: step after step

questions.q: The phrase قَدَمًا بَعْدَ قَدَمٍ repeats a word with بَعْدَ between. Make the same kind of phrase for “day after day”.
questions.q_ar: كَوِّنْ عِبَارَةً مِثْلَهَا لِمَعْنَى «day after day».
questions.a: يَوْمًا بَعْدَ يَوْمٍ

questions.q: Why might the writer say “step after step” about a journey to God?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَقُولُ «قَدَمًا بَعْدَ قَدَمٍ» عَنِ السَّيْرِ إِلَى اللهِ؟
questions.a: The traveller advances a little at a time: nobody arrives all at once.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A short guide to practice: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa of Imam Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī.

questions.q: What is said about the sins of the tongue?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُقَالُ عَنْ مَعَاصِي اللِّسَانِ؟
questions.a: That they are many (كَثِيرَةٌ).

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: The sins of the tongue are also many.

questions.q: What does this word mean?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟
questions.a: the tongue

questions.q: Which word adds this line to something said before? What might have been said before?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَرْبِطُ هَذَا السَّطْرَ بِمَا قَبْلَهُ؟ وَمَاذَا قِيلَ قَبْلَهُ؟
questions.a: أَيْضًا (“also”). Something else was said to be many: here, the sunnas.

questions.q: Some books write the tanwīn sign before the alif (أيضاً) and some on the alif (أَيْضًا). Are they the same word?
questions.q_ar: بَعْضُ الْكُتُبِ تَكْتُبُ «أيضاً» وَبَعْضُهَا «أَيْضًا». هَلْ هُمَا كَلِمَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ؟
questions.a: Yes. Only the place of the tanwīn sign differs (ـاً and ـًا).

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy never missed the rawḥa. The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.

questions.q: Which word means “never” after لَمْ?
questions.a: قَطُّ

questions.q: Which words mean “always” and “very”?
questions.a: دَائِمًا (always) and جِدًّا (very)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy always attends the rawḥa.
questions.a: يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا.

translate.en: The Habib always reads in the mosque.
The students mostly sit near the miḥrāb.
Ahmad never left the circle.
We never forget this day.

translate.ar: الْكِتَابُ صَغِيرٌ جِدًّا، وَلَكِنَّ دَرْسَهُ كَبِيرٌ.
translate.en: The book is very small, but its lesson is big.

translate.ar: حَضَرَتْ فَاطِمَةُ الرَّوْحَةَ، وَحَضَرَتْ مَرْيَمُ أَيْضًا.
translate.en: Fatima attended the rawḥa, and Maryam attended too.

translate.ar: قَرَأْتُ مُصْحَفًا فَقَطْ، وَلَمْ أَقْرَأْ كِتَابًا.
translate.en: I read only a muṣḥaf, and I did not read a book.
We have never heard this word.

translate.ar: الْيَوْمَ الْمَجْلِسُ كَبِيرٌ جِدًّا، وَأَمْسِ كَانَ صَغِيرًا.
translate.en: Today the majlis is very big, and yesterday it was small.

translate.ar: مَرْيَمُ طَالِبَةٌ جَيِّدَةٌ جِدًّا، وَتَقْرَأُ دَائِمًا.
translate.en: Maryam is a very good student, and she always reads.

translate.ar: لَا تَتْرُكِ الْوِرْدَ أَبَدًا يَا أَحْمَدُ.
translate.en: Never leave the wird, Ahmad.

translate.ar: الْحَبِيبُ كَرِيمٌ جِدًّا، وَيَجْلِسُ مَعَ النَّاسِ دَائِمًا.
translate.en: The Habib is very generous, and he always sits with the people.
Never sit in the street.

translate.ar: أَمْسِ حَضَرَ الْمُعَلِّمُ فَقَطْ، وَالْيَوْمَ حَضَرَ الطُّلَّابُ أَيْضًا.
translate.en: Yesterday only the teacher attended, and today the students attended too.

translate.ar: كَانَ أَحْمَدُ يَجْلِسُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ غَالِبًا. وَلَمْ يَذْهَبْ إِلَى السُّوقِ قَطُّ. وَيَقْرَأُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، وَيَحْفَظُ أَيْضًا.
translate.en: Ahmad mostly used to sit in the library. And he never went to the market. And he reads every day, and he memorises too.
Ahmad always goes to the rawḥa.
The Habib is very kind.
ʿUmar mostly sits near the door.
My son, never leave the lesson.
translate.ar: يَا بُنَيَّ، لَا تَتْرُكِ الدَّرْسَ أَبَدًا.

translate.en: Maryam never went to the market.
translate.ar: لَمْ تَذْهَبْ مَرْيَمُ إِلَى السُّوقِ قَطُّ.

translate.en: The students read the book, and the teacher read it too.
translate.ar: قَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ الْكِتَابَ، وَقَرَأَهُ الْمُعَلِّمُ أَيْضًا.

translate.en: Only Salim attended the lesson.
We never forget the evening of the mawlid.
The lesson was very long yesterday.
He is always happy, and his brother is happy too.
translate.ar: هُوَ سَعِيدٌ دَائِمًا، وَأَخُوهُ سَعِيدٌ أَيْضًا.

translate.en: Never sit in the street, my son.
translate.ar: يَا بُنَيَّ، لَا تَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ أَبَدًا.

translate.en: Fatima is very happy today.

readings.title_en: Joining sentences in depth
readings.question_en: How do “as for … then”, “either … or”, “when”, “while”, “whenever” and “until” tie sentences together?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ تَرْبِطُ «أَمَّا» وَ«إِمَّا» وَ«لَمَّا» وَ«كُلَّمَا» الْجُمَلَ؟

passages.intro_en: Read the letter, then answer. (★ rows are for adults and older students.)
passages.cite: Course text (a letter from the uncle), written for this lesson. Words of Lessons 1–67 and the extra words of Lessons 66–67 only.

lines.ar: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَإِنَّا انْتَظَرْنَا رِسَالَتَكَ يَوْمًا بَعْدَ يَوْمٍ حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ.
lines.en: To proceed: we waited for your letter day after day until it arrived.

lines.ar: وَأَنَا سَعِيدٌ بِهَا جِدًّا.
lines.en: And I am very happy with it.

lines.ar: أَمَّا الدَّرْسُ فَاقْرَأْهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، وَأَمَّا الْوِرْدُ فَلَا تَتْرُكْهُ أَبَدًا.
lines.en: As for the lesson, read it every day, and as for the wird, never leave it.

lines.ar: وَكُلَّمَا قَرَأْتَ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا فَاكْتُبْهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ.
lines.en: And whenever you read something new, write it in your book.

lines.ar: اِجْلِسْ إِمَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَإِمَّا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، وَلَا تَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ.
lines.en: Sit either in the mosque or in the library, and do not sit in the street.

lines.ar: وَبَيْنَمَا كُنْتُ أَقْرَأُ رِسَالَتَكَ جَاءَ الضُّيُوفُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
lines.en: And while I was reading your letter, the guests came to the house.

lines.ar: وَلَمَّا جَاءَ الْإِخْوَانُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ سَلَّمُوا عَلَيْكَ.
lines.en: And when the brothers came to the ribāṭ, they greeted you.

lines.ar: اللَّهُ يَحْفَظُكَ يَا أَحْمَدُ.
lines.en: May Allah protect you, Ahmad.

lines.ar: عَمُّكَ سَالِمٌ
lines.en: Your uncle Salim

passages.ar: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَإِنَّا انْتَظَرْنَا رِسَالَتَكَ يَوْمًا بَعْدَ يَوْمٍ حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ. وَأَنَا سَعِيدٌ بِهَا جِدًّا. أَمَّا الدَّرْسُ فَاقْرَأْهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، وَأَمَّا الْوِرْدُ فَلَا تَتْرُكْهُ أَبَدًا. وَكُلَّمَا قَرَأْتَ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا فَاكْتُبْهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ. اِجْلِسْ إِمَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَإِمَّا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، وَلَا تَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ. وَبَيْنَمَا كُنْتُ أَقْرَأُ رِسَالَتَكَ جَاءَ الضُّيُوفُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ. وَلَمَّا جَاءَ الْإِخْوَانُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ سَلَّمُوا عَلَيْكَ. اللَّهُ يَحْفَظُكَ يَا أَحْمَدُ. عَمُّكَ سَالِمٌ
passages.en: To proceed: we waited for your letter day after day until it arrived. And I am very happy with it. As for the lesson, read it every day, and as for the wird, never leave it. And whenever you read something new, write it in your book. Sit either in the mosque or in the library, and do not sit in the street. And while I was reading your letter, the guests came to the house. And when the brothers came to the ribāṭ, they greeted you. May Allah protect you, Ahmad. Your uncle Salim

Lines 1 and 2 of the passage (line 1 in the exercise); vowelled for learners (vowels added by the course).

lines.ar: أَمَّا بَعْدُ : فَاعْلَمُوا مَعَاشِرَ الْإِخْوَانِ فِي الدِّينِ ، وَالْأَعْوَانِ عَلَى طَاعَةِ اللهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
lines.en: To proceed: know, brothers in religion and helpers in obeying God, Lord of the worlds,

passages.ar: أَمَّا بَعْدُ : فَاعْلَمُوا مَعَاشِرَ الْإِخْوَانِ فِي الدِّينِ ، وَالْأَعْوَانِ عَلَى طَاعَةِ اللهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
passages.en: To proceed: know, brothers in religion and helpers in obeying God, Lord of the worlds,
