lines.ar: وَأَمَّا الصَّوْمُ: وَهُوَ الثَّالِثُ مِنْ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ، فَهُوَ إِمْسَاكٌ مَعْرُوفٌ
lines.en: As for fasting, the third pillar of Islam, it is a well-known abstention.

lines.ar: وَأَمَّا الْحَجُّ: فَهُوَ خَامِسُ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ
lines.en: As for the pilgrimage, it is the fifth pillar of Islam.

passages.ar: وَأَمَّا الصَّوْمُ: وَهُوَ الثَّالِثُ مِنْ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ، فَهُوَ إِمْسَاكٌ مَعْرُوفٌ وَأَمَّا الْحَجُّ: فَهُوَ خَامِسُ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ
passages.en: As for fasting, the third pillar of Islam, it is a well-known abstention. As for the pilgrimage, it is the fifth pillar of Islam.

passages.intro_en: Three verses. (Words: تَقْهَرْ = oppress, تَنْهَرْ = scold.) Read aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Qur’an 93:9–11 (Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā), text produced by program from the verified Madinah text.

lines.ar: فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ
lines.en: As for the orphan, do not oppress him.

lines.ar: وَأَمَّا السَّآئِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ
lines.en: And as for the one who asks, do not scold him.

lines.ar: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ
lines.en: And as for the blessing of your Lord, tell of it.

passages.ar: فَأَمَّا الْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ وَأَمَّا السَّآئِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ
passages.en: As for the orphan, do not oppress him. And as for the one who asks, do not scold him. And as for the blessing of your Lord, tell of it.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 121-122 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: وَصَلَتْ رِسَالَةٌ مِنْ عَمِّ الْوَلَدِ.
lines.en: A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.

lines.ar: بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
lines.en: The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.

passages.ar: وَصَلَتْ رِسَالَةٌ مِنْ عَمِّ الْوَلَدِ. بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
passages.en: A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle. The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.

questions.q: Who is writing to whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَكْتُبُ إِلَى مَنْ؟
questions.a: An uncle (عَمُّكَ سَالِمٌ) to Ahmad.

questions.q: With which words does the letter begin, and what do they mean?
questions.q_ar: بِأَيِّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَبْدَأُ الرِّسَالَةُ؟ وَمَاذَا تَعْنِي؟
questions.a: أَمَّا بَعْدُ: “to proceed”. It is how a letter moves from the greeting to its subject.

questions.q: How long did they wait for Ahmad’s letter, and until when?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ انْتَظَرُوا الرِّسَالَةَ؟ وَإِلَى مَتَى؟
questions.a: Day after day, until it arrived (حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ).

questions.q: What does the uncle say about the lesson? And about the wird?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ عَنِ الدَّرْسِ؟ وَعَنِ الْوِرْدِ؟
questions.a: Read the lesson every day; never leave the wird.

questions.q: In line 3 the uncle speaks about two topics. How many أَمَّا are there, and what follows each one?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٣ مَوْضُوعَانِ. كَمْ «أَمَّا» فِيهِ؟ وَمَاذَا بَعْدَ كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا؟
questions.a: Two. Each topic (الدَّرْسُ، الْوِرْدُ) is followed by فَـ and the advice.

questions.q: What must Ahmad do whenever he reads something new?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ أَحْمَدُ كُلَّمَا قَرَأَ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا؟
questions.a: Write it in his book (كُلَّمَا … فَاكْتُبْهُ).

questions.q: Where may Ahmad sit, and where not?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ يَجْلِسُ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَأَيْنَ لَا يَجْلِسُ؟
questions.a: In the mosque or in the library; not in the street.

questions.q: What happened while the uncle was reading? Which word says “while”?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَقُولُ إِنَّ الْحَدَثَيْنِ فِي وَقْتٍ وَاحِدٍ؟
questions.a: Guests came to the house; بَيْنَمَا.

questions.q: Who greeted Ahmad, and when? Which word says “when”?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَلَّمَ عَلَى أَحْمَدَ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الْوَقْتِ؟
questions.a: The brothers, when they came to the ribāṭ; لَمَّا.

questions.q: True or false? The uncle says: “Sit only in the mosque.”
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False. إِمَّا … وَإِمَّا = either … or: the mosque or the library.

questions.q: How does the uncle end the letter?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يَخْتِمُ الْعَمُّ الرِّسَالَةَ؟
questions.a: With a prayer, اللَّهُ يَحْفَظُكَ (“May Allah protect you”), and his name.

questions.q: In line 1, بَعْدُ ends with ـُ and has no tanwīn. What is different from بَعْدَ in “after the lesson”?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا بَعْدُ بِالضَّمَّةِ فِي «أَمَّا بَعْدُ»؟
questions.a: In this fixed phrase the word after it is left out in the mind, so بَعْدُ keeps a plain ـُ.

questions.q: In line 6, كُنْتُ comes before أَقْرَأُ. What does this give to the meaning?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَزِيدُ «كُنْتُ» عَلَى «أَقْرَأُ»؟
questions.a: “I was reading”: the action was going on when the guests came. This is the usual shape after بَيْنَمَا.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The beginning of a letter of Imam ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥaddād, from his Mukātabāt, vol. 1.

questions.q: Which words open the line, and what do they tell you?
questions.q_ar: بِأَيِّ كَلِمَاتٍ يَبْدَأُ السَّطْرُ؟ وَمَاذَا تَدُلُّ؟
questions.a: أَمَّا بَعْدُ: “to proceed”. The writer now comes to the subject.

questions.q: Which word begins the second half of this frame?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَأْتِي بَعْدَ «أَمَّا بَعْدُ» وَفِيهَا «فَـ»؟
questions.a: فَاعْلَمُوا: فَـ + the command “know!”.

questions.q: Whom does the writer address? Name the two groups.
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يُخَاطِبُ الْكَاتِبُ؟
questions.a: Brothers in religion, and helpers in obeying God.

questions.q: Root hunt: write the root of الْإِخْوَانِ and of طَاعَةِ.
questions.q_ar: اُكْتُبْ جَذْرَ «الْإِخْوَانِ» وَ«طَاعَةِ».
questions.a: أ خ و; ط و ع

questions.q: Which word means “brothers”? What is the one brother?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الْإِخْوَةِ؟ وَمَا الْمُفْرَدُ؟
questions.a: إِخْوَان; أَخ

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A short guide to practice: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa of Imam Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī.

questions.q: What are the two topics, one in each line?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْمَوْضُوعَانِ؟
questions.a: Fasting (الصَّوْم) and the pilgrimage (الْحَجّ).

questions.q: Which place in the order of the pillars does each one have?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَرْتَبَةُ كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا؟
questions.a: Fasting is the third (الثَّالِثُ); the pilgrimage is the fifth (خَامِسُ).

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ ٢.
questions.a: As for the pilgrimage, it is the fifth pillar of Islam.

questions.q: Each line begins with وَأَمَّا and later has فَـ (فَهُوَ). What does the فَـ do?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «فَـ» فِي «فَهُوَ»؟
questions.a: It begins what is said about the topic: “as for fasting, … then it is …”.

questions.q: Each line begins with وَأَمَّا, “and as for”. Why “and”?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا تَبْدَأُ الْجُمْلَتَانِ بِـ «وَأَمَّا»؟ لِمَاذَا «وَ»؟
questions.a: The lines belong to a list of the pillars: each topic follows the one before and is joined to it by وَ.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an: Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā, 93:9–11.

questions.q: How many times does أَمَّا appear? What comes after each topic?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً تَأْتِي «أَمَّا»؟ وَمَاذَا بَعْدَ كُلِّ مَوْضُوعٍ؟
questions.a: Three times, once in each verse. After each topic comes فَـ and the instruction.

questions.q: Who are the two people named, and what is the instruction for each?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الشَّخْصَانِ؟ وَمَاذَا يُقَالُ لِكُلٍّ؟
questions.a: The orphan (الْيَتِيم): do not oppress him. The one who asks (السَّائِل): do not scold him.

questions.q: Verse 11: what is the topic, and what is the instruction? (حَدِّثْ = tell.)
questions.q_ar: الْآيَةُ ١١: مَا الْمَوْضُوعُ؟ وَمَا الْأَمْرُ؟
questions.a: The blessing of your Lord (بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ): tell of it.

questions.q: In verses 9 and 10 the topic is named before the verb. Why does the verse not begin with “Do not oppress”?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَا تَبْدَأُ الْآيَةُ بِالْفِعْلِ؟
questions.a: After أَمَّا the topic comes first, and then فَـ opens what is said about it.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle. The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.

questions.q: How does the uncle begin his letter?
questions.a: With أَمَّا بَعْدُ (“now then”).

questions.q: What does فَـ do after أَمَّا … ?
questions.a: It opens the answer part: أَمَّا … فَـ …

questions.q: Write in Arabic: A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
questions.a: وَصَلَتْ رِسَالَةٌ مِنْ عَمِّ الْوَلَدِ.

translate.en: As for the wird, read it every morning.
When the letter arrived, Ahmad read it.

translate.ar: كُلَّمَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ سَمِعَ كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً.
translate.en: Whenever the boy sat with the Habib, he heard a good word.

translate.ar: بَيْنَمَا كُنَّا نَجْلِسُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ دَخَلَ ضَيْفٌ.
translate.en: While we were sitting in the ribāṭ, a guest came in.

translate.ar: تَذْهَبُ مَرْيَمُ إِمَّا مَعَ أُمِّهَا وَإِمَّا مَعَ أُخْتِهَا.
translate.en: Maryam goes either with her mother or with her sister.
We waited for the Habib until he came.

translate.ar: أَمَّا الْإِخْوَانُ فَجَلَسُوا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ، وَأَمَّا الضُّيُوفُ فَجَلَسُوا فِي الْبَيْتِ.
translate.en: As for the brothers, they sat in the mosque, and as for the guests, they sat in the house.
The one who asked asked the Habib, and the Habib honoured him.

translate.ar: جَاءَ يَتِيمٌ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ، وَسَاعَدَهُ الْإِخْوَانُ.
translate.en: An orphan came to the ribāṭ, and the brothers helped him.

translate.ar: مَا زَالَ أَحْمَدُ يَحْضُرُ الرَّوْحَةَ حَتَّى الْيَوْمِ.
translate.en: Ahmad still attends the rawḥa to this day.
As for sleep, it is after the prayer.

translate.ar: لَمَّا جَاءَ الضُّيُوفُ سَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ عَلَيْهِمْ.
translate.en: When the guests came, the Habib greeted them.
To proceed: read the lesson and write it.

translate.ar: كَانَ لِأَحْمَدَ صَدِيقٌ يَتِيمٌ. كُلَّمَا ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ ذَهَبَ مَعَهُ صَدِيقُهُ. وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ الصَّدِيقُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ أَكَلَ طَعَامًا.
translate.en: Ahmad had an orphan friend. Whenever Ahmad went to the rawḥa, his friend went with him. And when the friend returned to the house, he ate food.
As for the lesson, it is easy.
As for the wird, never leave it.
When the Habib entered, the students stood.
While I was reading, a guest came.
Whenever I sit with my brothers, I learn something.
translate.ar: كُلَّمَا جَلَسْتُ مَعَ إِخْوَانِي تَعَلَّمْتُ شَيْئًا.

translate.en: He is either in the mosque or in the ribāṭ.
translate.ar: هُوَ إِمَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَإِمَّا فِي الرِّبَاطِ.

translate.en: We sat until the Habib came.
Honour the orphan and the one who asks.
As for the brothers, they travelled.
Whenever he reads the muṣḥaf, he is happy.
The orphan sat between the brothers.
To proceed: your letter reached me.
Read either the book or the muṣḥaf.
As for him, he is very happy.

readings.title_en: Who and which in depth
readings.question_en: In “the book that I read”, which word points back to the book, and what do we do when there is no “that”?
readings.question_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعُودُ إِلَى الْكِتَابِ؟ وَمَاذَا نَفْعَلُ إِذَا لَمْ نَقُلْ «الَّذِي»؟

passages.intro_en: Read the text from Bidāyat al-Hidāya, then answer.
passages.cite: Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī, Bidāyat al-Hidāya; Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, 53.mdb), the same text as Shamela 3.28 id 5285 (whose card says it is auto-numbered and does not match the print): so the page is the digital page of this copy, pp. 25–30, NOT a printed page; edition not identified. Skeleton (all letters) exact against the copy; vowelled for learners by the course.

lines.ar: أَنَّ الْهِدَايَةَ الَّتِي هِيَ ثَمَرَةُ الْعِلْمِ لَهَا بِدَايَةٌ وَنِهَايَةٌ ، وَظَاهِرٌ وَبَاطِنٌ
lines.en: That guidance, which is the fruit of knowledge, has a beginning and an end, an outward and an inward.

lines.ar: وَلَا تَسْتَصْحِبْ شَيْئًا عَلَيْهِ اسْمُ اللهِ تَعَالَى وَرَسُولِهِ
lines.en: And do not take with you anything on which the name of God Most High and of His messenger is written.

passages.ar: أَنَّ الْهِدَايَةَ الَّتِي هِيَ ثَمَرَةُ الْعِلْمِ لَهَا بِدَايَةٌ وَنِهَايَةٌ ، وَظَاهِرٌ وَبَاطِنٌ وَلَا تَسْتَصْحِبْ شَيْئًا عَلَيْهِ اسْمُ اللهِ تَعَالَى وَرَسُولِهِ
passages.en: That guidance, which is the fruit of knowledge, has a beginning and an end, an outward and an inward. And do not take with you anything on which the name of God Most High and of His messenger is written.

passages.intro_en: Read the story, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text.

lines.ar: ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ الَّتِي فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
lines.en: Ahmad went to the library that is in the ribāṭ.

lines.ar: أَخَذَ كِتَابًا قَرَأَهُ أَبُوهُ قَبْلَ سَنَةٍ.
lines.en: He took a book that his father had read a year before.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ جَلَسَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ الَّذِي حَضَرَ فِيهِ الْحَبِيبُ أَمْسِ.
lines.en: Then he sat in the majlis in which the Habib had been present yesterday.

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الدَّرْسَ الَّذِي كَتَبَهُ الْإِمَامُ عَنِ الْأَدَبِ.
lines.en: He read the lesson that the imam wrote about good manners.

lines.ar: فَهِمَ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ فِيهِ ، لَكِنَّهُ سَأَلَ عَنْ كَلِمَةٍ لَمْ يَفْهَمْهَا.
lines.en: He understood every word in it, but he asked about a word that he did not understand.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْكَلِمَةُ الَّتِي سَأَلْتَ عَنْهَا كَلِمَةٌ فِيهَا نُورٌ.
lines.en: The Habib said: The word you asked about is a word with light in it.

lines.ar: شَكَرَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا.
lines.en: Ahmad thanked the Habib and went back home, happy.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا كِتَابٌ أَخَذْتُهُ مِنَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ ، وَقَرَأْتُ فِيهِ دَرْسًا جَمِيلًا.
lines.en: And he said to his mother: This is a book that I took from the library, and I read a beautiful lesson in it.

passages.ar: ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ الَّتِي فِي الرِّبَاطِ. أَخَذَ كِتَابًا قَرَأَهُ أَبُوهُ قَبْلَ سَنَةٍ. ثُمَّ جَلَسَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ الَّذِي حَضَرَ فِيهِ الْحَبِيبُ أَمْسِ. قَرَأَ الدَّرْسَ الَّذِي كَتَبَهُ الْإِمَامُ عَنِ الْأَدَبِ. فَهِمَ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ فِيهِ ، لَكِنَّهُ سَأَلَ عَنْ كَلِمَةٍ لَمْ يَفْهَمْهَا. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْكَلِمَةُ الَّتِي سَأَلْتَ عَنْهَا كَلِمَةٌ فِيهَا نُورٌ. شَكَرَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا. وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا كِتَابٌ أَخَذْتُهُ مِنَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ ، وَقَرَأْتُ فِيهِ دَرْسًا جَمِيلًا.
passages.en: Ahmad went to the library that is in the ribāṭ. He took a book that his father had read a year before. Then he sat in the majlis in which the Habib had been present yesterday. He read the lesson that the imam wrote about good manners. He understood every word in it, but he asked about a word that he did not understand. The Habib said: The word you asked about is a word with light in it. Ahmad thanked the Habib and went back home, happy. And he said to his mother: This is a book that I took from the library, and I read a beautiful lesson in it.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 123-124 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib.

lines.ar: هُوَ كِتَابٌ صَغِيرٌ قَرَأْتُهُ ثَلَاثًا.
lines.en: It is a small book that I read three times.

passages.ar: قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ. هُوَ كِتَابٌ صَغِيرٌ قَرَأْتُهُ ثَلَاثًا.
passages.en: The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib. It is a small book that I read three times.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A counsel (advice) from Bidāyat al-Hidāya by Imam al-Ghazālī.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: That guidance, which is the fruit of knowledge, has a beginning and an end, an outward and an inward.

questions.q: Which word is the “which” of line 1? Which noun does it point back to?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ اسْمٍ تَعُودُ إِلَيْهِ «الَّتِي»؟
questions.a: الَّتِي points back to الْهِدَايَةُ (guidance).

questions.q: In the clause after الَّتِي, which word is the returning pronoun?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي الصِّلَةِ هِيَ الضَّمِيرُ الْعَائِدُ؟
questions.a: هِيَ (“she / it”), standing for الْهِدَايَةُ.

questions.q: According to line 1, what is the fruit of knowledge?
questions.q_ar: مَا ثَمَرَةُ الْعِلْمِ؟
questions.a: Guidance (الْهِدَايَةُ).

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And do not take with you anything on which the name of God Most High and of His messenger is written.

questions.q: In line 2, which word points back to شَيْئًا?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي تَعُودُ إِلَى «شَيْئًا»؟
questions.a: عَلَيْهِ (the ending ـهِ).

questions.q: Why is there no الَّذِي after شَيْئًا?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَمْ يَأْتِ «الَّذِي» بَعْدَ «شَيْئًا»؟
questions.a: شَيْئًا has no ال (it means “anything”), so the clause follows it directly.

questions.q: True or false?
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False: it has an outward and an inward (ظَاهِرٌ وَبَاطِنٌ).

questions.q: Why الَّتِي and not الَّذِي?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «الَّتِي» وَلَيْسَ «الَّذِي»؟
questions.a: الْهِدَايَةُ is feminine.

questions.q: The clause after الَّتِي has no verb. What is it made of?
questions.q_ar: مِمَّ تَتَكَوَّنُ جُمْلَةُ الصِّلَةِ هُنَا؟
questions.a: A pronoun (هِيَ) and a noun phrase (ثَمَرَةُ الْعِلْمِ): “she is the fruit of knowledge”.

questions.q: What do the last two words of line 1 (ظَاهِرٌ وَبَاطِنٌ) set side by side?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَجْمَعُ الْكَلِمَتَانِ الْأَخِيرَتَانِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟
questions.a: The two sides of guidance: the outward and the inward.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad go first?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ أَوَّلًا؟
questions.a: To the library in the ribāṭ.

questions.q: Who had read the book before Ahmad?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ قَرَأَ الْكِتَابَ قَبْلَ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: His father.

questions.q: Why is there no الَّذِي after كِتَابًا (line 2)?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَمْ يَأْتِ «الَّذِي» بَعْدَ «كِتَابًا»؟
questions.a: كِتَابًا has no ال, so the clause قَرَأَهُ أَبُوهُ follows it directly.

questions.q: In line 3, which word points back to الْمَجْلِسِ?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعُودُ إِلَى «الْمَجْلِسِ»؟
questions.a: فِيهِ.

questions.q: Who wrote the lesson that Ahmad read?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ كَتَبَ الدَّرْسَ؟
questions.a: The imam.

questions.q: What does the ending ـهُ in كَتَبَهُ (line 4) point back to?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَاذَا تَعُودُ النِّهَايَةُ ـهُ؟
questions.a: الدَّرْسَ (the lesson).

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask about?
questions.q_ar: عَنْ مَاذَا سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: A word that he did not understand.

questions.q: Which ending in this word points back to كَلِمَةٍ?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نِهَايَةٍ فِي هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ تَعُودُ إِلَى «كَلِمَةٍ»؟
questions.a: ـهَا.

questions.q: What did the Habib say about the word?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟
questions.a: That it is a word with light in it.

questions.q: True or false?
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False: he went back home (إِلَى الْبَيْتِ).

questions.q: In line 6, who is “you” (سَأَلْتَ)? What does عَنْهَا point back to?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْمُخَاطَبُ فِي «سَأَلْتَ»؟ وَإِلَى مَاذَا تَعُودُ «عَنْهَا»؟
questions.a: “You” is Ahmad; عَنْهَا points back to الْكَلِمَةُ.

questions.q: Find two clauses in the story that have no الَّذِي. What nouns do they follow?
questions.q_ar: اُذْكُرْ جُمْلَتَيْنِ بِلَا «الَّذِي» وَالِاسْمَ الَّذِي قَبْلَهُمَا.
questions.a: قَرَأَهُ أَبُوهُ (after كِتَابًا); فِيهَا نُورٌ (after كَلِمَةٌ); لَمْ يَفْهَمْهَا (after كَلِمَةٍ); أَخَذْتُهُ (after كِتَابٌ).

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib. It is a small book that I read three times.

questions.q: In the first new line, which ending returns to الْكِتَابُ inside the clause?
questions.a: ـهُ in قَرَأْتُهُ (the returning pronoun)

questions.q: In the second new line, is there an الَّذِي? What does the clause قَرَأْتُهُ ثَلَاثًا describe?
questions.a: No. After an indefinite noun (كِتَابٌ صَغِيرٌ) the clause describes it without الَّذِي.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: This is the book that I read.
questions.a: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ.

translate.en: The book that I read is an old book.
The letter that my mother wrote is long.

translate.ar: شَكَرَ الْحَبِيبُ الطُّلَّابَ الَّذِينَ حَضَرُوا الْحَلْقَةَ.
translate.en: The Habib thanked the students who attended the circle.
This is a mosque in which I prayed yesterday.

translate.ar: الْوَلَدُ الَّذِي أَبُوهُ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ سَعِيدٌ.
translate.en: The boy whose father is in the city is happy.

translate.ar: فَهِمْتُ كُلَّ مَا قَرَأْتُهُ فِي الدَّرْسِ.
translate.en: I understood all that I read in the lesson.

translate.ar: الْعِلْمُ نِعْمَةٌ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ بِهَا عَلَى الطَّالِبِ.
translate.en: Knowledge is a blessing with which God favoured the student.
The road on which I walked is long.

translate.ar: وَكُلُّ مَا أَتَى بِهِ الرَّسُولُ * فَحَقُّهُ التَّسْلِيمُ وَالْقَبُولُ
translate.en: And all that the Messenger brought: its due is submission and acceptance. (بِهِ points back to مَا.)
The book that I read is a good book.
The lesson that the Habib read is easy.
The students whom I thanked are in the mosque.
Knowledge is a tree, and its fruit is guidance.
This is a book that has light in it.
I heard a word that I did not understand.
The Habib heard the question that the boy asked.
translate.ar: سَمِعَ الْحَبِيبُ السُّؤَالَ الَّذِي سَأَلَهُ الْوَلَدُ.

translate.en: The mosque in which he prayed is old.
A teacher whose book is new came in.
The letter that my father wrote is on the desk.
translate.ar: الرِّسَالَةُ الَّتِي كَتَبَهَا أَبِي عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ.

readings.title_en: The verb’s three shapes
readings.question_en: Why does the last vowel of a present verb change after some little words?
readings.question_ar: لِمَاذَا تَتَغَيَّرُ نِهَايَةُ الْفِعْلِ بَعْدَ أَنْ وَلَنْ وَلَمْ وَاللَّامِ؟

passages.intro_en: Read the line from Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd, then answer.
passages.source: Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād
passages.cite: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, no. 7); Shamela Master Library copy (Ba Zuhayr Library, 233.mdb); publisher and year not stated; pp. 3–4 of the digital text (printed pagination not given); TLNOOR 1256 is a separate scan. Letters exact; the source is only partly vowelled, so the full vowelling is added by the course (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: وَلَا تَنْتَظِرُوا الصِّحَّةَ فَإِنَّ انْتِظَارَ الصِّحَّةِ بَطَالَةٌ
lines.en: And do not wait for health, for waiting for health is idleness.

passages.ar: وَلَا تَنْتَظِرُوا الصِّحَّةَ فَإِنَّ انْتِظَارَ الصِّحَّةِ بَطَالَةٌ
passages.en: And do not wait for health, for waiting for health is idleness.

passages.intro_en: Read the story, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text.

lines.ar: اِنْتَظَرَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ حَتَّى يَحْضُرَ الْحَبِيبُ.
lines.en: Ahmad waited in the majlis until the Habib came.

lines.ar: لَمْ يَفْهَمْ دَرْسَ أَمْسِ ، فَسَأَلَ الْحَبِيبَ.
lines.en: He had not understood yesterday’s lesson, so he asked the Habib.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ لِيَعْمَلَ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Let every student learn so that he may act.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ لِلطُّلَّابِ: لَا تَتَكَلَّمُوا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَسْمَعُوا.
lines.en: And he said to the students: Do not speak before you listen.

lines.ar: فَجَلَسَ الطُّلَّابُ كَيْ يَسْمَعُوا ، وَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمُوا.
lines.en: So the students sat so that they might listen, and they did not speak.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ لِيَقْرَأَ الدَّرْسَ ثَلَاثًا.
lines.en: Then Ahmad went to the library to read the lesson three times.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ: لَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ حَتَّى أَفْهَمَ.
lines.en: And he said: I will not go home until I understand.

lines.ar: وَلَمَّا فَهِمَ رَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا.
lines.en: And when he understood, he went back home, happy.

passages.ar: اِنْتَظَرَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ حَتَّى يَحْضُرَ الْحَبِيبُ. لَمْ يَفْهَمْ دَرْسَ أَمْسِ ، فَسَأَلَ الْحَبِيبَ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ لِيَعْمَلَ. وَقَالَ لِلطُّلَّابِ: لَا تَتَكَلَّمُوا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَسْمَعُوا. فَجَلَسَ الطُّلَّابُ كَيْ يَسْمَعُوا ، وَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمُوا. ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ لِيَقْرَأَ الدَّرْسَ ثَلَاثًا. وَقَالَ: لَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ حَتَّى أَفْهَمَ. وَلَمَّا فَهِمَ رَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا.
passages.en: Ahmad waited in the majlis until the Habib came. He had not understood yesterday’s lesson, so he asked the Habib. The Habib said: Let every student learn so that he may act. And he said to the students: Do not speak before you listen. So the students sat so that they might listen, and they did not speak. Then Ahmad went to the library to read the lesson three times. And he said: I will not go home until I understand. And when he understood, he went back home, happy.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 125-126 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.
lines.en: The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.

passages.ar: ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
passages.en: The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson. The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A counsel (advice) from a short book of manners for the seeker, by Imam al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: Translate the line.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ.
questions.a: And do not wait for health, for waiting for health is idleness.

questions.q: Who is being told: one person, or several? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: هَلِ الْمُخَاطَبُ وَاحِدٌ أَمْ جَمَاعَةٌ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: Several: the ending -ū.

questions.q: Is this a statement or a command? Which word shows it?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ هَذَا خَبَرٌ أَمْ نَهْيٌ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: A command not to wait: لَا (“do not”).

questions.q: The plain form is تَنْتَظِرُونَ. What happened to its ن after لَا?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا حَدَثَ لِلنُّونِ بَعْدَ «لَا»؟
questions.a: It fell: لَا تَنْتَظِرُوا.

questions.q: What is waiting for health called, according to the line?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُسَمِّي النَّصُّ انْتِظَارَ الصِّحَّةِ؟
questions.a: Idleness (بَطَالَةٌ).

questions.q: Which word gives the reason?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُبَيِّنُ السَّبَبَ؟
questions.a: فَإِنَّ (“for, because”).

questions.q: True or false? The line tells us to wait for health.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟
questions.a: False: it says do not wait.

questions.q: The word الصِّحَّةِ comes twice. What does the writer want us to do instead of waiting?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُرِيدُ الْكَاتِبُ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ بَدَلَ الِانْتِظَارِ؟
questions.a: To act now, while we are well, and not to put it off.

questions.q: Which root do تَنْتَظِرُوا and انْتِظَار share? What word of Lesson 47 has the same root?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ جَذْرٍ تَشْتَرِكُ فِيهِ الْكَلِمَتَانِ؟
questions.a: ن ظ ر; اِنْتَظَرَ (“he waited”).

questions.q: Who did Ahmad wait for, and until when?
questions.q_ar: لِمَنِ انْتَظَرَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَإِلَى مَتَى؟
questions.a: For the Habib, until he attended.

questions.q: Which shape is يَحْضُرَ, and which word asks for it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ شَكْلٍ هَذَا؟ وَأَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَطْلُبُهُ؟
questions.a: -a; حَتَّى.

questions.q: Did Ahmad understand yesterday’s lesson? Which word tells you?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ فَهِمَ أَحْمَدُ دَرْسَ أَمْسِ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ؟
questions.a: No. لَمْ.

questions.q: Translate. Is لِ “so that” or “let him”? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ. هَلْ لِ «كَيْ» أَمْ «لِيَفْعَلْ»؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: “Let every student learn.” Let him: the verb ends in no vowel.

questions.q: Is this لِ “so that” or “let him”? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ هَذِهِ اللَّامُ لِلْغَايَةِ أَمْ لِلْأَمْرِ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: “So that”: the verb ends in -a.

questions.q: What did the Habib forbid? Who is told?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا مَنَعَ الْحَبِيبُ؟ وَمَنِ الْمُخَاطَبُونَ؟
questions.a: Speaking before listening; the students (the ending -ū).

questions.q: Why did the students sit? Which word gives the aim?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا جَلَسَ الطُّلَّابُ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُبَيِّنُ الْغَايَةَ؟
questions.a: So that they might listen: كَيْ.

questions.q: Did the students speak? What happened to the ن of يَتَكَلَّمُونَ?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ تَكَلَّمَ الطُّلَّابُ؟ مَاذَا حَدَثَ لِنُونِ «يَتَكَلَّمُونَ»؟
questions.a: No. The ن fell after لَمْ.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad go, and why?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: To the library, to read the lesson three times.

questions.q: Translate line 7. Will Ahmad go home soon? Why not?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ السَّابِعَ. لِمَاذَا لَنْ يَذْهَبَ الْآنَ؟
questions.a: “I will not go home until I understand.” Not yet: he wants to understand first.

questions.q: Find two verbs in the story that end in -a. Which little word asks for each?
questions.q_ar: اُذْكُرْ فِعْلَيْنِ مَنْصُوبَيْنِ وَالْحَرْفَ الَّذِي نَصَبَهُمَا.
questions.a: يَحْضُرَ (حَتَّى), لِيَعْمَلَ (لِ), لِيَقْرَأَ (لِ), أَذْهَبَ (لَنْ), أَفْهَمَ (حَتَّى).

questions.q: In line 4, why does the Habib say تَسْمَعُوا and not تَسْمَعُونَ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «تَسْمَعُوا» وَلَيْسَ «تَسْمَعُونَ»؟
questions.a: Because it follows أَنْ: after أَنْ the verb takes the -a shape, and the final ن falls.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson. The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.

questions.q: In لِيَحْضُرَ, what does لِ mean, and what ending does the verb take?
questions.a: “So that / in order to”; the verb ends in ـَ (يَحْضُرَ).

questions.q: In لِيَتَعَلَّمْ, what does لِ do, and what ending does the verb take?
questions.a: It gives a command (“let him learn”); the verb ends with sukūn.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.
questions.a: ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.

translate.en: I will not go to the market today.
The Habib did not attend yesterday.

translate.ar: جَلَسْتُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ أَبِي.
translate.en: I sat in the mosque until my father came back.

translate.ar: طَلَبَ الْمُعَلِّمُ مِنَ الطُّلَّابِ أَنْ يَجْلِسُوا.
translate.en: The teacher asked the students to sit.
Do not drink the water in the mosque.

translate.ar: رَغِبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي أَنْ يَحْفَظَ الْكِتَابَ.
translate.en: Ahmad desired to memorise the book.

translate.ar: لَيْسَ فِي وُسْعِي أَنْ أَحْفَظَ الْكِتَابَ فِي يَوْمٍ.
translate.en: It is not within my capacity to memorise the book in a day.
So let every student strive so that he understands the lesson.

translate.ar: أَخَذْتُ الْمِفْتَاحَ كَيْ لَا أَجْلِسَ فِي الشَّارِعِ.
translate.en: I took the key so that I would not sit in the street.

translate.ar: وَلَنْ تَصِلَ أَيُّهَا الطَّالِبُ إِلَى الْقِيَامِ بِأَوَامِرِ اللهِ تَعَالَى إِلَّا بِمُرَاقَبَةِ قَلْبِكَ وَجَوَارِحِكَ // وَلَنْ تَقْدِرَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ إِلَّا بِأَنْ تُوَزِّعَ أَوْقَاتَكَ ، وَتُرَتِّبَ أَوْرَادَكَ
translate.en: And you, O student, will never attain to carrying out God’s commands except by watching your heart and your limbs. And you will not be able to do that except by dividing up your times and arranging your daily litanies.
Let every student learn so that he may act.
Do not wait for the dawn. (to several people)
He did not go to the mosque.
He strove so that he might understand the lesson.
We will not sit until the Habib attends.
It is not within my capacity to read the whole book today.
translate.ar: لَيْسَ فِي وُسْعِي أَنْ أَقْرَأَ الْكِتَابَ كُلَّهُ الْيَوْمَ.

translate.en: Do not write here!
The teacher asked the students to study the lesson.
translate.ar: طَلَبَ الْمُعَلِّمُ مِنَ الطُّلَّابِ أَنْ يَدْرُسُوا الدَّرْسَ.

translate.en: They did not attend the circle.
He sat in the mosque so as not to sit in the street.
translate.ar: جَلَسَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ كَيْ لَا يَجْلِسَ فِي الشَّارِعِ.

lines.ar: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ
lines.en: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings upon him, saying:

lines.ar: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ
lines.en: "When God wants good for someone, He gives him understanding of the religion."

lines.ar: وَمَنْ تَرَكَ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْوَاجِبَاتِ صَحَّ حَجُّهُ وَلَزِمَهُ دَمٌ
lines.en: And whoever leaves some obligation, his pilgrimage is valid but a sacrifice is due from him.

lines.ar: وَإِنْ كَانَتْ نِيَّتُكَ وَقَصْدُكَ ، بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ اللهِ تَعَالَى ، مِنْ طَلَبِ الْعِلْمِ : الْهِدَايَةَ دُونَ مُجَرَّدِ الرِّوَايَةِ ؛ فَأَبْشِرْ
lines.en: And if your intention and aim, between you and God Most High, in seeking knowledge is guidance and not mere transmission, then rejoice.

lines.ar: إِذَا عَلِمْتُمْ ذَلِكَ : فَاعْلَمُوا وَفَّقَنِي اللهُ وَإِيَّاكُمْ : أَنِّي قَصَدْتُ أَنْ أَجْمَعَ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَوْرَاقِ أَطْرَافًا مِمَّا فَتَحَهُ اللهُ عَلَيَّ
lines.en: If you know that, then know — may God grant me and you success — that I set out to gather in these pages some portions of what God has opened to me.

passages.ar: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ وَمَنْ تَرَكَ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْوَاجِبَاتِ صَحَّ حَجُّهُ وَلَزِمَهُ دَمٌ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ نِيَّتُكَ وَقَصْدُكَ ، بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ اللهِ تَعَالَى ، مِنْ طَلَبِ الْعِلْمِ : الْهِدَايَةَ دُونَ مُجَرَّدِ الرِّوَايَةِ ؛ فَأَبْشِرْ إِذَا عَلِمْتُمْ ذَلِكَ : فَاعْلَمُوا وَفَّقَنِي اللهُ وَإِيَّاكُمْ : أَنِّي قَصَدْتُ أَنْ أَجْمَعَ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَوْرَاقِ أَطْرَافًا مِمَّا فَتَحَهُ اللهُ عَلَيَّ
passages.en: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings upon him, saying: "When God wants good for someone, He gives him understanding of the religion." And whoever leaves some obligation, his pilgrimage is valid but a sacrifice is due from him. And if your intention and aim, between you and God Most High, in seeking knowledge is guidance and not mere transmission, then rejoice. If you know that, then know — may God grant me and you success — that I set out to gather in these pages some portions of what God has opened to me.

passages.intro_en: A short story: the Habib’s word. Read it, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
passages.cite: Course text written for this lesson

lines.ar: فِي صَبَاحِ الْجُمُعَةِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: On Friday morning the boy sat in the circle with the Habib.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَنْ يَعْمَلْ خَيْرًا يَجِدْهُ، وَمَنْ يَصْبِرْ يَصِلْ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Whoever does good will find it, and whoever is patient will arrive.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ: إِذَا جَاءَكَ سَائِلٌ فَاسْمَعْ سُؤَالَهُ.
lines.en: And he said: If someone who asks comes to you, listen to his request.

lines.ar: فِي الطَّرِيقِ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى رَجُلٍ فَقِيرٍ جَالِسٍ عَلَى الْبَابِ.
lines.en: On the way to the house the boy looked at a poor man sitting at the door.

lines.ar: وَلَيْسَ مَعَ الْوَلَدِ إِلَّا خُبْزٌ وَاحِدٌ.
lines.en: And the boy had nothing with him but one loaf of bread.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِلرَّجُلِ: خُذْ هَذَا الْخُبْزَ.
lines.en: So the boy said to the man: Take this bread.

lines.ar: شَكَرَ الرَّجُلُ الْوَلَدَ وَدَعَا لَهُ.
lines.en: The man thanked the boy and prayed for him.

lines.ar: فِي الْبَيْتِ سَأَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ: مَاذَا عَمِلْتَ الْيَوْمَ؟
lines.en: At home his mother asked him: What did you do today?

lines.ar: قَالَ: عَمِلْتُ بِكَلِمَةِ الْحَبِيبِ، وَلَوْلَا الْحَبِيبُ مَا فَهِمْتُهَا.
lines.en: He said: I acted on the Habib’s word, and were it not for the Habib I would not have understood it.

lines.ar: فَقَالَتْ أُمُّهُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ!
lines.en: His mother said: Praise be to God!

lines.ar: إِنْ تَعْمَلْ خَيْرًا فَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ بِهِ.
lines.en: If you do good, God knows of it.

passages.ar: فِي صَبَاحِ الْجُمُعَةِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَنْ يَعْمَلْ خَيْرًا يَجِدْهُ، وَمَنْ يَصْبِرْ يَصِلْ. وَقَالَ: إِذَا جَاءَكَ سَائِلٌ فَاسْمَعْ سُؤَالَهُ. فِي الطَّرِيقِ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى رَجُلٍ فَقِيرٍ جَالِسٍ عَلَى الْبَابِ. وَلَيْسَ مَعَ الْوَلَدِ إِلَّا خُبْزٌ وَاحِدٌ. فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِلرَّجُلِ: خُذْ هَذَا الْخُبْزَ. شَكَرَ الرَّجُلُ الْوَلَدَ وَدَعَا لَهُ. فِي الْبَيْتِ سَأَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ: مَاذَا عَمِلْتَ الْيَوْمَ؟ قَالَ: عَمِلْتُ بِكَلِمَةِ الْحَبِيبِ، وَلَوْلَا الْحَبِيبُ مَا فَهِمْتُهَا. فَقَالَتْ أُمُّهُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ! إِنْ تَعْمَلْ خَيْرًا فَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ بِهِ.
passages.en: On Friday morning the boy sat in the circle with the Habib. The Habib said: Whoever does good will find it, and whoever is patient will arrive. And he said: If someone who asks comes to you, listen to his request. On the way to the house the boy looked at a poor man sitting at the door. And the boy had nothing with him but one loaf of bread. So the boy said to the man: Take this bread. The man thanked the boy and prayed for him. At home his mother asked him: What did you do today? He said: I acted on the Habib’s word, and were it not for the Habib I would not have understood it. His mother said: Praise be to God! If you do good, God knows of it.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 127-128 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَنْ يَخْدُمْ يَتَعَلَّمْ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns.

lines.ar: وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
lines.en: And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.

passages.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَنْ يَخْدُمْ يَتَعَلَّمْ. وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
passages.en: The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns. And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.

questions.q: Lines 1–2: what kind of text is this, and which book is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيِّ كِتَابٍ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth, a saying of the Prophet ﷺ: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, no. 1037.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: When God wants good for someone, He gives him understanding of the religion.

questions.q: In line 2, which word opens the condition? What does it mean here?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى «مَنْ» هُنَا؟
questions.a: مَنْ = “whoever, when someone”.

questions.q: Why does يُرِدِ end in a kasra and not in a sukūn?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَنْتَهِي «يُرِدِ» بِكَسْرَةٍ لَا بِسُكُونٍ؟
questions.a: It is jussive after مَنْ; but the next word begins with ال, so the sukūn becomes a kasra to avoid two silent letters in a row.

questions.q: What is the answer to the condition in line 2? Translate it.
questions.q_ar: مَا جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟ تَرْجِمْهُ.
questions.a: يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ = He gives him understanding of the religion.

questions.q: Line 3 is a rule about the pilgrimage. What follows if someone leaves one of the obligations?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَلْزَمُ مَنْ تَرَكَ وَاجِبًا مِنْ وَاجِبَاتِ الْحَجِّ؟
questions.a: His pilgrimage is still valid, but a sacrifice (دَمٌ) is due from him.

questions.q: In line 3 the answer is two past verbs joined by وَ. Which two verbs are they, and why is there no فَـ?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلَيْنِ مَاضِيَيْنِ فِي الْجَوَابِ؟ وَلِمَاذَا لَا فَاءَ؟
questions.a: صَحَّ (it was valid) and لَزِمَهُ (it was due from him). A past verb needs no فَـ.

questions.q: True or false? Line 3 says the pilgrimage is not valid if an obligation is left.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ السَّطْرُ الثَّالِثُ يَقُولُ: لَا يَصِحُّ الْحَجُّ إِذَا تُرِكَ وَاجِبٌ.
questions.a: False: صَحَّ حَجُّهُ means it is valid, but a sacrifice is due.

questions.q: Line 4 begins with وَإِنْ. What does it tell you?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَقُولُ لَكَ «وَإِنْ»؟
questions.a: “And if”: a new condition begins.

questions.q: In line 4, where does the condition end and where does the answer begin? (Look at the punctuation.)
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ يَنْتَهِي الشَّرْطُ وَأَيْنَ يَبْدَأُ الْجَوَابُ فِي السَّطْرِ الرَّابِعِ؟
questions.a: The condition runs up to the semicolon (؛); the answer is فَأَبْشِرْ.

questions.q: What does the answer in line 4 tell the student to do, and why does it begin with فَـ?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الْجَوَابُ فِي السَّطْرِ الرَّابِعِ؟ وَلِمَاذَا بَدَأَ بِالْفَاءِ؟
questions.a: “Rejoice!” It is a command, so it needs فَـ.

questions.q: Line 4: what kind of text is it, and which book is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا السَّطْرُ؟ وَمِنْ أَيِّ كِتَابٍ؟
questions.a: Counsel to a student of knowledge: Bidāyat al-Hidāya of Imām al-Ghazālī (vowelled for learners).

questions.q: Line 5 begins with إِذَا. Which past verb follows it, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ مَاضٍ بَعْدَ «إِذَا»؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهُ؟
questions.a: عَلِمْتُمْ = you know, you have known.

questions.q: Line 5: which word opens the answer, and what kind of word comes after it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَفْتَحُ الْجَوَابَ فِي السَّطْرِ الْخَامِسِ؟ وَمَا نَوْعُ مَا بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: فَاعْلَمُوا: فَـ plus a command (“then know!”).

questions.q: Line 5 comes from a letter. Whose letter?
questions.q_ar: مِنْ رِسَالَةِ مَنْ هَذَا السَّطْرُ؟
questions.a: A letter of Imām al-Ḥaddād (al-Mukātabāt).

questions.q: Who sat with the Habib, and when?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَلَسَ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: The boy, on Friday morning.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: The Habib said: Whoever does good will find it, and whoever is patient will arrive.

questions.q: In line 2, what does the ending ـهُ in يَجِدْهُ stand for?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَاذَا يَرْجِعُ الضَّمِيرُ فِي «يَجِدْهُ»؟
questions.a: The good (خَيْرًا).

questions.q: What should you do if someone who asks comes to you (line 3)?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ إِذَا جَاءَكَ سَائِلٌ؟
questions.a: Listen to his request.

questions.q: Where was the boy when he looked at the poor man?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ كَانَ الْوَلَدُ حِينَ نَظَرَ إِلَى الرَّجُلِ الْفَقِيرِ؟
questions.a: On the way to the house.

questions.q: What does إِلَّا do in line 5? What did the boy have?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «إِلَّا» فِي السَّطْرِ الْخَامِسِ؟ مَاذَا كَانَ مَعَ الْوَلَدِ؟
questions.a: “Nothing but”: he had only one loaf of bread.

questions.q: What did the boy do with the bread?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ الْوَلَدُ بِالْخُبْزِ؟
questions.a: He told the man to take it.

questions.q: What did the man do?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ الرَّجُلُ؟
questions.a: He thanked the boy and prayed for him.

questions.q: Who asked the boy what he had done, and where?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَأَلَ الْوَلَدَ؟ وَأَيْنَ؟
questions.a: His mother, at home.

questions.q: True or false? The boy says he understood the Habib’s word by himself.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ يَقُولُ الْوَلَدُ إِنَّهُ فَهِمَ كَلِمَةَ الْحَبِيبِ وَحْدَهُ.
questions.a: False: he says that without the Habib he would not have understood it (لَوْلَا).

questions.q: Put in order: (a) the man thanks him (b) the boy sits with the Habib (c) his mother asks (d) the boy gives the bread.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) يَشْكُرُهُ الرَّجُلُ (ب) يَجْلِسُ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ (ج) تَسْأَلُهُ أُمُّهُ (د) يُعْطِي الْخُبْزَ.

questions.q: Why do يَجِدْهُ and يَصِلْ in line 2 have no فَـ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَا فَاءَ فِي جَوَابَيْ السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: Each answer is a plain verb in the jussive.

questions.q: In line 10 the answer starts with فَـ. Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا بَدَأَ الْجَوَابُ بِالْفَاءِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْعَاشِرِ؟
questions.a: The answer is a noun sentence (اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ بِهِ), not a plain jussive or past verb.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns. And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.

questions.q: In مَنْ يَخْدُمْ يَتَعَلَّمْ, which verb is the condition and which is the answer? What ending do both take?
questions.a: يَخْدُمْ is the condition and يَتَعَلَّمْ the answer; both end with sukūn.

questions.q: Which tense follows إِذَا in the second new line?
questions.a: The past: جَلَسَ … فَهِمَ

questions.q: Write in Arabic: Whoever serves, learns.
questions.a: مَنْ يَخْدُمْ يَتَعَلَّمْ.

translate.en: If you seek knowledge, you will find light.
Whoever asks, understands.

translate.ar: إِذَا خَرَجَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: When the boy leaves school, he goes to the mosque.
If the imam is present, listen to his word.

translate.ar: لَوْ كَانَ الْمَاءُ قَرِيبًا لَشَرِبَ الْأَوْلَادُ.
translate.en: If the water had been near, the boys would have drunk.

translate.ar: لَوْلَا الْمَدْرَسَةُ مَا قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ كِتَابًا.
translate.en: Were it not for the school, the boy would not have read a book.

translate.ar: مَهْمَا تَقْرَأْ مِنَ الْمُصْحَفِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ.
translate.en: Whatever you read of the muṣḥaf is good.
Whoever aims at knowledge finds his way.
If you keep to the circle, you will understand the lesson.

translate.ar: وَمَنْ تَرَكَ رُكْنًا مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ لَمْ تَصِحَّ صَلَاتُهُ.
translate.en: And whoever leaves a pillar of the prayer, his prayer is not valid.
The student’s duty is to listen and to understand.

translate.ar: إِذَا جَاءَ الصَّبَاحُ ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ. وَإِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ مَكَانًا فَلَنْ يَجْلِسَ فِي الشَّارِعِ. لَكِنَّهُ يَقْرَأُ فِي الْمُصْحَفِ حَتَّى يَجِدَ مَجْلِسًا.
translate.en: When morning comes, the boy goes to the mosque. If he does not find a place, he will not sit in the street. But he reads in the muṣḥaf until he finds a place to sit.
If you write the lesson, you will memorise it.
Whoever strives will arrive.
Whatever good you do, you will find it.
When the guests came, the boy served them.
If you do not read, you will not understand the lesson.
translate.ar: إِنْ لَمْ تَقْرَأْ فَلَنْ تَفْهَمَ الدَّرْسَ.

translate.en: If the Habib comes, sit down and listen.
Were it not for the teacher, I would not have understood the lesson.
If the boy had known, he would have come to the mosque.
translate.ar: لَوْ عَلِمَ الْوَلَدُ لَجَاءَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.

translate.en: Whoever asks the teacher understands the lesson.
Whatever you read from the book, write it.
The student’s duty is to keep to the circle.
Whoever aims at knowledge will find his way.

readings.title_en: Numbers, dates and times
readings.question_en: How do I read a number, a date or a time in an old book?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ الْعَدَدَ وَالتَّارِيخَ وَالسَّاعَةَ فِي الْكُتُبِ؟

passages.intro_en: Five lines with dates and numbers. Read them, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)

lines.ar: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ الْحَدَّادُ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ ٥ صَفَرٍ ١٠٤٤هـ بِالسَّبِيرِ أَحَدِ ضَوَاحِي مَدِينَةِ تَرِيمَ
lines.en: Imām al-Ḥaddād was born on Monday the 5th of Ṣafar 1044 AH in al-Subayr, one of the suburbs of the city of Tarīm.

lines.ar: وَكَانَ الْفَرَاغُ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهَا لَيْلَةَ الْإِثْنَيْنِ لِسَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ شَهْرِ صَفَرٍ الْخَيْرِ سَنَةَ (١٢٥٧هـ)
lines.en: The writing of it was finished on the night of Monday, the 27th of the month of Ṣafar al-Khayr, in the year 1257 AH.

lines.ar: مَوْلِدُهُ بِمَدِينَةِ الْغُرْفَةِ فِي أَوَائِلِ عَامِ ١٠٦٩ مِنَ الْهِجْرَةِ
lines.en: He was born in the town of al-Ghurfa at the beginning of the year 1069 of the Hijra.

lines.ar: أَرْكَانُ الصَّلَاةِ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ
lines.en: The pillars of the prayer are seventeen.

lines.ar: تَشْدِيدَاتُ الْفَاتِحَةِ أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ
lines.en: The doubled letters of the Fātiḥa are fourteen.

passages.ar: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ الْحَدَّادُ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ ٥ صَفَرٍ ١٠٤٤هـ بِالسَّبِيرِ أَحَدِ ضَوَاحِي مَدِينَةِ تَرِيمَ وَكَانَ الْفَرَاغُ مِنْ كِتَابَتِهَا لَيْلَةَ الْإِثْنَيْنِ لِسَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ شَهْرِ صَفَرٍ الْخَيْرِ سَنَةَ (١٢٥٧هـ) مَوْلِدُهُ بِمَدِينَةِ الْغُرْفَةِ فِي أَوَائِلِ عَامِ ١٠٦٩ مِنَ الْهِجْرَةِ أَرْكَانُ الصَّلَاةِ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ تَشْدِيدَاتُ الْفَاتِحَةِ أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ
passages.en: Imām al-Ḥaddād was born on Monday the 5th of Ṣafar 1044 AH in al-Subayr, one of the suburbs of the city of Tarīm. The writing of it was finished on the night of Monday, the 27th of the month of Ṣafar al-Khayr, in the year 1257 AH. He was born in the town of al-Ghurfa at the beginning of the year 1069 of the Hijra. The pillars of the prayer are seventeen. The doubled letters of the Fātiḥa are fourteen.

passages.intro_en: A short passage: a day in the ribāṭ. Read it, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
passages.cite: Course text written for this lesson (the birth and death years 1044 and 1132 AH are those of Imām al-Ḥaddād)

lines.ar: فِي الرِّبَاطِ اثْنَا عَشَرَ طَالِبًا، وَفِي الْحَلْقَةِ أَرْبَعُونَ رَجُلًا.
lines.en: In the ribāṭ there are twelve students, and in the circle forty men.

lines.ar: يَجْلِسُ الْحَبِيبُ مَعَهُمْ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ.
lines.en: The Habib sits with them after dawn at half past five.

lines.ar: وَدَرْسُ الْيَوْمِ سَاعَةٌ وَنِصْفٌ، ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ الطُّلَّابُ ثُلُثَ الْكِتَابِ.
lines.en: Today’s lesson is an hour and a half, then the students read a third of the book.

lines.ar: فِي الْكِتَابِ ثَلَاثُونَ بَابًا، وَقَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْبَابَ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ.
lines.en: The book has thirty chapters, and the boy read the twelfth chapter.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُكْتُبْ تَارِيخَ الْيَوْمِ: يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ، الْخَامِسَ عَشَرَ مِنْ رَمَضَانَ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Write today’s date: Friday, the fifteenth of Ramaḍān.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ الْحَدَّادُ سَنَةَ ١٠٤٤هـ وَمَاتَ سَنَةَ ١١٣٢هـ.
lines.en: Then he said: Imam al-Ḥaddād was born in 1044 AH and died in 1132 AH.

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ: كَمْ سَنَةً بَيْنَ ١٠٤٤ وَ١١٣٢؟
lines.en: The boy asked: How many years are there between 1044 and 1132?

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: ثَمَانٍ وَثَمَانُونَ سَنَةً، يَا بُنَيَّ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Eighty-eight years, my son.

passages.ar: فِي الرِّبَاطِ اثْنَا عَشَرَ طَالِبًا، وَفِي الْحَلْقَةِ أَرْبَعُونَ رَجُلًا. يَجْلِسُ الْحَبِيبُ مَعَهُمْ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ. وَدَرْسُ الْيَوْمِ سَاعَةٌ وَنِصْفٌ، ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ الطُّلَّابُ ثُلُثَ الْكِتَابِ. فِي الْكِتَابِ ثَلَاثُونَ بَابًا، وَقَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْبَابَ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُكْتُبْ تَارِيخَ الْيَوْمِ: يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ، الْخَامِسَ عَشَرَ مِنْ رَمَضَانَ. ثُمَّ قَالَ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ الْحَدَّادُ سَنَةَ ١٠٤٤هـ وَمَاتَ سَنَةَ ١١٣٢هـ. فَسَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ: كَمْ سَنَةً بَيْنَ ١٠٤٤ وَ١١٣٢؟ فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: ثَمَانٍ وَثَمَانُونَ سَنَةً، يَا بُنَيَّ.
passages.en: In the ribāṭ there are twelve students, and in the circle forty men. The Habib sits with them after dawn at half past five. Today’s lesson is an hour and a half, then the students read a third of the book. The book has thirty chapters, and the boy read the twelfth chapter. The Habib said: Write today’s date: Friday, the fifteenth of Ramaḍān. Then he said: Imam al-Ḥaddād was born in 1044 AH and died in 1132 AH. The boy asked: How many years are there between 1044 and 1132? The Habib said: Eighty-eight years, my son.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 129-129 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
lines.en: The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.

passages.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
passages.en: The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.

questions.q: Line 1: on which day, in which month and in which year was the Imam born?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ يَوْمٍ وَشَهْرٍ وَسَنَةٍ وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ؟
questions.a: On Monday, the 5th of Ṣafar, 1044 AH.

questions.q: Where was he born?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ وُلِدَ؟
questions.a: In al-Subayr, a suburb of the city of Tarīm.

questions.q: Which day of the week is this? (Hint: the root ث ن ي, “two”.)
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ يَوْمٍ هَذَا؟ (تَلْمِيحٌ: الْجَذْرُ ث ن ي)
questions.a: Monday: the second day.

questions.q: Line 2 comes from the end of a manuscript. What was finished, and when?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا انْتَهَى؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: The writing of it was finished on the night of Monday, the 27th of Ṣafar, 1257 AH.

questions.q: In line 2, what number is لِسَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ عَدَدٍ هَذَا؟
questions.a: 27 (“seven and twenty”).

questions.q: In “seven and twenty” which number comes first? Where else in this lesson did you see the same order?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الْعَدَدَيْنِ يَأْتِي أَوَّلًا؟ وَأَيْنَ رَأَيْتَ هَذَا الْأُسْلُوبَ أَيْضًا؟
questions.a: The unit comes first, then the ten: the same order as in “eight and eighty” (88).

questions.q: Line 3: in which year (AH) was the author born?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ سَنَةٍ وُلِدَ صَاحِبُ الْكِتَابِ؟
questions.a: 1069 AH (at the beginning of the year).

questions.q: What do the words مِنَ الْهِجْرَةِ tell you about the year?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَقُولُ «مِنَ الْهِجْرَةِ» عَنِ السَّنَةِ؟
questions.a: It is counted from the Hijra: a Hijri year.

questions.q: True or false? Line 3 says that al-Ghurfa is a room.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ يَقُولُ السَّطْرُ الثَّالِثُ إِنَّ «الْغُرْفَةَ» حُجْرَةٌ.
questions.a: False: it is the name of a town (see the glossed word).

questions.q: Line 4: what number is سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ, and what are there seventeen of?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ عَدَدٍ هَذَا؟ وَمَا الشَّيْءُ الَّذِي عَدَدُهُ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ؟
questions.a: 17: the pillars of the prayer.

questions.q: Line 5: how many doubled letters does the Fātiḥa have? How is the number written?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ تَشْدِيدَةً فِي الْفَاتِحَةِ؟ وَكَيْفَ كُتِبَ الْعَدَدُ؟
questions.a: Fourteen: أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ.

questions.q: Lines 4–5: what kind of text is this, and which book is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيِّ كِتَابٍ؟
questions.a: A short text of fiqh (a matn): Safīnat al-Najā of Sālim b. Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī (vowelled for learners).

questions.q: Line 1: what kind of text is it, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا السَّطْرُ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A short biography of the Imam: Bushrā al-Fuʾād bi-Tarjamat al-Imām al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: Lines 1 and 2 both give a date. Which line writes the day in digits and which in words?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ كَتَبَ الْيَوْمَ بِالْأَرْقَامِ وَأَيُّهُمَا بِالْحُرُوفِ؟
questions.a: Line 1 uses digits (٥ صَفَرٍ ١٠٤٤); line 2 writes the day in words (لِسَبْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ) and the year in digits (١٢٥٧).

questions.q: How many years are there between the birth in line 1 and the birth in line 3?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ سَنَةً بَيْنَ الْوِلَادَةِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ وَالْوِلَادَةِ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ؟

questions.q: How many students are in the ribāṭ, and how many men in the circle?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الرِّبَاطِ؟ وَكَمْ رَجُلًا فِي الْحَلْقَةِ؟
questions.a: Twelve students and forty men.

questions.q: At what time does the Habib sit with them?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ يَجْلِسُ الْحَبِيبُ مَعَهُمْ؟
questions.a: At half past five, after dawn.

questions.q: How long is today’s lesson, and what part of the book do they read?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مُدَّةُ دَرْسِ الْيَوْمِ؟ وَأَيَّ جُزْءٍ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يَقْرَؤُونَ؟
questions.a: An hour and a half; a third of the book.

questions.q: How many chapters has the book, and which chapter did the boy read?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ بَابًا فِي الْكِتَابِ؟ وَأَيَّ بَابٍ قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ؟
questions.a: Thirty chapters; the twelfth.

questions.q: What does الْخَامِسَ عَشَرَ mean?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى «الْخَامِسَ عَشَرَ»؟
questions.a: The fifteenth (of Ramaḍān).

questions.q: Which day of the week does the Habib name in line 5?
questions.q_ar: أَيَّ يَوْمٍ يَذْكُرُ الْحَبِيبُ فِي السَّطْرِ الْخَامِسِ؟
questions.a: Friday.

questions.q: In which year was the Imam born, and in which did he die (line 6)?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ سَنَتَيْنِ وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ وَمَاتَ؟
questions.a: Born in 1044 AH, died in 1132 AH.

questions.q: What does the boy ask in line 7, and what does the Habib answer?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَسْأَلُ الْوَلَدُ؟ وَبِمَاذَا يُجِيبُ الْحَبِيبُ؟
questions.a: How many years between 1044 and 1132: eighty-eight.

questions.q: True or false? The students read half of the book.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ يَقْرَأُ الطُّلَّابُ نِصْفَ الْكِتَابِ.
questions.a: False: they read a third (ثُلُثَ).

questions.q: Put in order: (a) the boy asks a question (b) the Habib gives the date (c) the students read a third (d) the Habib sits with them.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) يَسْأَلُ الْوَلَدُ (ب) يَذْكُرُ الْحَبِيبُ التَّارِيخَ (ج) يَقْرَأُ الطُّلَّابُ الثُّلُثَ (د) يَجْلِسُ الْحَبِيبُ مَعَهُمْ.

questions.q: Check the answer of line 8: 1132 − 1044 = ?
Why is the thing counted in ثَلَاثُونَ بَابًا singular, ending in ـًا?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا جَاءَ «بَابًا» مُفْرَدًا مَنْصُوبًا بَعْدَ «ثَلَاثُونَ»؟
questions.a: After 11 to 99 the thing counted is one singular word with ـًا (the tamyīz).

questions.q: In line 4 الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ ends in a fatḥa on both words. Why does it not change?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَا يَتَغَيَّرُ آخِرُ «الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ»؟
questions.a: Compound numbers from eleven to nineteen keep a fixed fatḥa ending.

questions.q: Translate the new line into English.
questions.a: The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.

questions.q: Which words make the year? Write it in digits.
Which month is named?
questions.a: صَفَرَ (Ṣafar, the second month)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: in the year one thousand and forty-four.
questions.a: فِي سَنَةِ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.

translate.en: There are a hundred books in the library.
Eleven men attended the circle.
The boy wrote thirty words.
The father travelled for fifteen days.

translate.ar: جَلَسَ الْمُعَلِّمُ نِصْفَ سَاعَةٍ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ رُبْعَ الْكِتَابِ.
translate.en: The teacher sat for half an hour, then read a quarter of the book.

translate.ar: السَّاعَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا وَالْحَبِيبُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
translate.en: It is a quarter to eight and the Habib is in the ribāṭ.

translate.ar: فِي السَّنَةِ اثْنَا عَشَرَ شَهْرًا، وَفِي الشَّهْرِ ثَلَاثُونَ يَوْمًا أَوْ تِسْعَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ.
translate.en: In the year there are twelve months, and in the month thirty days or twenty-nine.

translate.ar: مَاتَ الْإِمَامُ الْحَدَّادُ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ مِنَ الْهِجْرَةِ.
translate.en: Imam al-Ḥaddād died in the twelfth century of the Hijra.

translate.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ تَارِيخَ الْيَوْمِ: يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ ٢٧ صَفَرٍ.
translate.en: The boy wrote today’s date: Monday, the 27th of Ṣafar.

translate.ar: فِي الْكِتَابِ ثَلَاثُونَ بَابًا. قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ ثُلُثَهُ: عَشَرَةَ أَبْوَابٍ. وَغَدًا يَقْرَأُ الثُّلُثَ الثَّانِيَ.
translate.en: The book has thirty chapters. The boy read a third of it: ten chapters. And tomorrow he will read the second third.
The water became cold in the morning. Skill: the sisters of كَانَ.
Perhaps the Habib is in the mosque. Skill: the sisters of إِنَّ.
The boy came hurrying. Skill: the ḥāl (the state).
The Habib entered the mosque, happy. Skill: the ḥāl as a clause.
The boy remembered God a great deal. Skill: the absolute object (the same word again).
There is no man in the mosque. Skill: لَا that denies the whole kind.
My son, sit with the righteous. Skill: the call (يَا).
Only three students attended. Skill: exception (مَا … إِلَّا = only).

translate.ar: هَذَا كِتَابُ الشَّيْخِ سَالِمِ بْنِ عُمَرَ الْعَلَوِيِّ.
translate.en: This is the book of Shaykh Sālim ibn ʿUmar al-ʿAlawī. Skill: a name in a chain.

translate.ar: رَغِبَ الطَّالِبُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَلَمْ يَرْغَبْ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ.
translate.en: The student desired knowledge and did not turn away from the gathering. Skill: a verb with its preposition.
Let the student attend the circle so that he understands. Skill: the three shapes of the verb.
As for today, we read the third chapter. Skill: joining (أَمَّا … فَـ).
The book that I read is good. Skill: the returning pronoun.
If you strive, you will arrive. Skill: the if-sentence.
There are twelve students in the ribāṭ.
The boy wrote thirty words.
In the library there are a hundred books.
The father travelled for fifteen days.
The book has thirty chapters.
The boy read the third chapter.
It is half past six.
It is a quarter to eight.
The Imam was born in the year 1044.
He died in the twelfth century of the Hijra.
translate.ar: مَاتَ فِي الْقَرْنِ الثَّانِيَ عَشَرَ مِنَ الْهِجْرَةِ.

translate.en: The students read a third of the book.
Today is Monday, the twenty-seventh of Ṣafar.
translate.ar: الْيَوْمُ يَوْمُ الِاثْنَيْنِ، السَّابِعُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ مِنْ صَفَرٍ.

readings.title_en: The Qur’an with its commentary (tafsīr)
readings.title_ar: الْقُرْآنُ مَعَ التَّفْسِيرِ: أَيْ وَيَعْنِي وَالْمُرَادُ
readings.question_en: Which words are the verse, and which words explain it?
readings.question_ar: أَيُّ الْكَلِمَاتِ هِيَ الْآيَةُ؟ وَأَيُّ الْكَلِمَاتِ هِيَ الشَّرْحُ؟

passages.intro_en: A page of tafsīr: the Qur’an words are in « », the commentary follows them. The text is fully vowelled. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Tafsīr al-Jalālayn (the commentary; the Qur’an words are in « »)
passages.cite: Jalālayn, Tafsīr al-Jalālayn (al-Maḥallī and al-Suyūṭī); Shamela 3.28 id 1301 (digital vowelled text; the card says auto-numbered, NOT matching the print), pp. 7/492–495 and 4/107–109 of that digital text. Commentary lines 3, 5 and 6 of the ten glosses of the research file (slides) and lines 2, 4, 7 and 9 (Exercise A), in the order of the verses; the Qur’an words in « » are set from the Qur’an program (Madinah mushaf), not typed from the commentary; the commentary words are fully vowelled for learners (the source gives them no case endings); before the ال of الْمَرْجِع the course reads أَيِ; the source’s “أَنْ” lemma of research line 2 is the program’s أَنِ; letters unchanged.

lines.ar: «أَنِ» أَيْ وَقُلْنَا لَهُ أَنْ «اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ» عَلَى مَا أَعْطَاكَ مِنَ الْحِكْمَةِ
lines.en: “that”: that is, We said to him that: “Give thanks to Allah” for the wisdom He gave you.

lines.ar: «وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ» أَمَرْنَاهُ أَنْ يَبَرَّهُمَا
lines.en: “We enjoined man regarding his parents”: We commanded him to be dutiful to them.

lines.ar: «وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ» طَرِيقَ «مَنْ أَنَابَ» رَجَعَ «إِلَيَّ» بِالطَّاعَةِ
lines.en: “and follow the path” (the way) “of him who turned” (returned) “to Me”, in obedience.

lines.ar: «إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ» فِي الْمَنَامِ «أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ» تَأْكِيدٌ
lines.en: “Indeed, I saw” in a dream “eleven stars, the sun and the moon; I saw them”: a repetition for emphasis.

passages.ar: «أَنِ» أَيْ وَقُلْنَا لَهُ أَنْ «اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ» عَلَى مَا أَعْطَاكَ مِنَ الْحِكْمَةِ «وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ» أَمَرْنَاهُ أَنْ يَبَرَّهُمَا «وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ» طَرِيقَ «مَنْ أَنَابَ» رَجَعَ «إِلَيَّ» بِالطَّاعَةِ «إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ» فِي الْمَنَامِ «أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ» تَأْكِيدٌ
passages.en: “that”: that is, We said to him that: “Give thanks to Allah” for the wisdom He gave you. “We enjoined man regarding his parents”: We commanded him to be dutiful to them. “and follow the path” (the way) “of him who turned” (returned) “to Me”, in obedience. “Indeed, I saw” in a dream “eleven stars, the sun and the moon; I saw them”: a repetition for emphasis.

passages.intro_en: A short text: the circle after the prayer. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text. The « » words in line 6 are set from the Qur’an program (31:13, words 11–14).

lines.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: After the prayer Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s circle.

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً مِنْ سُورَةِ لُقْمَانَ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
lines.en: The Habib read a verse from Sūrat Luqmān, then he read its commentary.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: وَعَظَ لُقْمَانُ ابْنَهُ، يَعْنِي قَالَ لَهُ نَصِيحَةً.
lines.en: The Habib said: Luqmān counselled his son, that is, he gave him a piece of advice.

lines.ar: قَالَ لَهُ: يَا بُنَيَّ، لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ.
lines.en: He said to him: My little son, do not associate anything with Allah.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْمُرَادُ بِالشِّرْكِ أَنْ تَعْبُدَ مَعَ اللَّهِ غَيْرَهُ.
lines.en: And the Habib said: What is meant by associating is that you worship someone other than Allah along with Him.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَرَأَ: «إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ».
lines.en: Then he read: “indeed, associating others with Him is a great wrong.”

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: مَا مَعْنَى «عَظِيمٌ» يَا حَبِيبُ؟
lines.en: Then Ahmad asked: What is the meaning of “great”, Habib?

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: عَظِيمٌ، أَيْ كَبِيرٌ جِدًّا.
lines.en: And the Habib said: Great, that is, very big.

lines.ar: وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: الْآيَةُ، ثُمَّ التَّفْسِيرُ.
lines.en: And Ahmad wrote in his book: the verse, then the commentary.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ لِأُمِّهِ مَا كَتَبَ.
lines.en: And he returned to the house and read to his mother what he had written.

passages.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ. قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً مِنْ سُورَةِ لُقْمَانَ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: وَعَظَ لُقْمَانُ ابْنَهُ، يَعْنِي قَالَ لَهُ نَصِيحَةً. قَالَ لَهُ: يَا بُنَيَّ، لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ. وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْمُرَادُ بِالشِّرْكِ أَنْ تَعْبُدَ مَعَ اللَّهِ غَيْرَهُ. ثُمَّ قَرَأَ: «إِنَّ الشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ». فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: مَا مَعْنَى «عَظِيمٌ» يَا حَبِيبُ؟ فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: عَظِيمٌ، أَيْ كَبِيرٌ جِدًّا. وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: الْآيَةُ، ثُمَّ التَّفْسِيرُ. وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ لِأُمِّهِ مَا كَتَبَ.
passages.en: After the prayer Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s circle. The Habib read a verse from Sūrat Luqmān, then he read its commentary. The Habib said: Luqmān counselled his son, that is, he gave him a piece of advice. He said to him: My little son, do not associate anything with Allah. And the Habib said: What is meant by associating is that you worship someone other than Allah along with Him. Then he read: “indeed, associating others with Him is a great wrong.” Then Ahmad asked: What is the meaning of “great”, Habib? And the Habib said: Great, that is, very big. And Ahmad wrote in his book: the verse, then the commentary. And he returned to the house and read to his mother what he had written.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 130-131 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
lines.en: The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
lines.en: Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا. ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
passages.en: The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary. Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an with its commentary (tafsīr): the words in « » are the Qur’an; what follows each is the commentary, and أَيْ marks an explanation.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: “That”: that is, We said to him that: “Give thanks to Allah” for the wisdom He gave you.

questions.q: Line 1: which frame-word begins the explanation?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ١: أَيُّ كَلِمَةِ شَرْحٍ تَبْدَأُ الشَّرْحَ؟
questions.a: أَيْ (“that is”).

questions.q: Line 1: for what is Luqmān told to give thanks?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: عَلَى مَاذَا يُؤْمَرُ لُقْمَانُ بِالشُّكْرِ؟
questions.a: For the wisdom (الْحِكْمَة) that Allah gave him.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: “We enjoined man regarding his parents”: We commanded him to be dutiful to them.

questions.q: Line 2: with which word does the commentary explain وَوَصَّيْنَا? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: بِأَيِّ كَلِمَةٍ يَشْرَحُ التَّفْسِيرُ «وَوَصَّيْنَا»؟ مَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: أَمَرْنَاهُ: We commanded him.

questions.q: Line 2: what must man be towards his parents, according to the commentary?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَاذَا يَجِبُ عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ نَحْوَ وَالِدَيْهِ؟
questions.a: Dutiful to them (يَبَرَّهُمَا).

questions.q: Line 2 has no frame-word. How do you know where the verse ends and the commentary begins?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢ بِلَا كَلِمَةِ شَرْحٍ. أَيْنَ تَنْتَهِي الْآيَةُ وَيَبْدَأُ الشَّرْحُ؟
questions.a: The verse is inside « »; the commentary begins after the closing ».

questions.q: Line 3: which word of the verse does طَرِيقَ explain?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ مِنَ الْآيَةِ تُشْرَحُ بِـ«طَرِيقَ»؟
questions.a: سَبِيلَ (“path”).

questions.q: Line 3: which word of the verse does رَجَعَ explain?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ مِنَ الْآيَةِ تُشْرَحُ بِـ«رَجَعَ»؟
questions.a: أَنَابَ (“he turned”).

questions.q: Line 3: what does the commentary add after «إِلَيَّ»?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَاذَا يَزِيدُ الشَّرْحُ بَعْدَ «إِلَيَّ»؟
questions.a: بِالطَّاعَةِ: “in obedience”.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: “Indeed, I saw” in a dream “eleven stars, the sun and the moon; I saw them”: a repetition for emphasis.

questions.q: Line 4: which words of the commentary tell you that this was in a dream?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَقُولُ إِنَّ هَذَا كَانَ فِي مَنَامٍ؟
questions.a: فِي الْمَنَامِ (“in the dream”).

questions.q: Line 4: the commentary says تَأْكِيدٌ. What is repeated, and why?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: يَقُولُ الشَّرْحُ «تَأْكِيدٌ». مَاذَا تَكَرَّرَ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: The word “I saw” is said twice (رَأَيْتُ … رَأَيْتُهُمْ); the repetition stresses it.

questions.q: The commentator does not explain every word of the verse. What does he explain?
questions.q_ar: لَا يَشْرَحُ الْمُفَسِّرُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ. مَاذَا يَشْرَحُ؟
questions.a: Only what needs it: a rare word, a missing phrase, or the reason.

questions.q: Who sat in the Habib’s circle after the prayer? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ؟
questions.a: Ahmad and Umar.

questions.q: What did the Habib read, and what did he read after it? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ؟ وَمَاذَا قَرَأَ بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: A verse from Sūrat Luqmān, then its commentary.

questions.q: Line 3: which frame-word is used? What does it explain?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَةِ شَرْحٍ تُسْتَعْمَلُ؟ مَاذَا تَشْرَحُ؟
questions.a: يَعْنِي: it explains وَعَظَ (“counselled”): he gave him advice.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: He said to him: My little son, do not associate anything with Allah.

questions.q: Line 5: which frame-word is used? What is explained?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٥: أَيُّ كَلِمَةِ شَرْحٍ تُسْتَعْمَلُ؟ مَاذَا يُشْرَحُ؟
questions.a: الْمُرَادُ: “what is meant”; the sense of الشِّرْك.

questions.q: According to the Habib, what is meant by الشِّرْك? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: عِنْدَ الْحَبِيبِ مَا الْمُرَادُ بِالشِّرْكِ؟
questions.a: That you worship someone other than Allah along with Him.

questions.q: Line 6: which words are the Qur’an? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٦: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ هِيَ الْقُرْآنُ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: “indeed, associating others with Him is a great wrong”: they are inside « ».

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask? (line 7)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: What the word عَظِيمٌ (“great”) means.

questions.q: What did the Habib answer? Which frame-word did he use? (line 8)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا أَجَابَ الْحَبِيبُ؟ أَيَّ كَلِمَةِ شَرْحٍ اسْتَعْمَلَ؟
questions.a: Great, that is, very big; he used أَيْ.

questions.q: What did Ahmad write in his book? (line 9)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ؟
questions.a: The verse, then the commentary.

questions.q: Translate line 10.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْعَاشِرَ.
questions.a: And he returned to the house and read to his mother what he had written.

questions.q: Lines 3–6: what is the order of what Ahmad hears? Put it in steps.
questions.q_ar: السُّطُورُ ٣–٦: مَا تَرْتِيبُ مَا يَسْمَعُ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: 1) the Habib says Luqmān counselled his son; 2) the counsel itself; 3) what “associating” means; 4) the verse that gives the reason.

questions.q: Why does the Habib explain a word (عَظِيمٌ) before going on?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَشْرَحُ الْحَبِيبُ كَلِمَةً قَبْلَ أَنْ يَمْضِيَ؟
questions.a: So that the student understands the verse before he writes it down.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary. Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.

questions.q: What does أَيْ do in the second new line?
questions.a: It explains: “that is”. The Habib explains الْحِكْمَةُ as knowledge and action.

questions.q: What is a تَفْسِير?
questions.a: A commentary that explains the verse.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The Habib read a verse.
questions.a: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً.

translate.ar: الْمُصْحَفُ أَيْ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ، وَالْمَسْجِدُ أَيْ بَيْتُ اللَّهِ.
translate.en: The muṣḥaf, that is, the book of Allah, and the mosque, that is, the house of Allah.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ الْمُعَلِّمُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
translate.en: The teacher read a verse, then he read its commentary.
The meaning of the verse is in the commentary.
What is meant by wisdom is knowledge and action.
The sura is big, and in it is a beautiful story.

translate.ar: رَأَى أَحْمَدُ رُؤْيَا جَمِيلَةً فِي اللَّيْلِ.
translate.en: Ahmad saw a beautiful dream in the night.
Luqmān’s wisdom is great, and he counselled his son.
The teacher says: the verse, then the commentary.

translate.ar: الْمَصِيرُ أَيِ الْمَرْجِعُ، وَالْمَرْجِعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ.
translate.en: “The final return”, that is, the place of return, and the return is to Allah.

lines.ar: إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰأَبَتِ
lines.en: When Yūsuf said to his father: “O my father,

lines.ar: إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ
lines.en: I saw eleven

lines.ar: كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ
lines.en: stars, and the sun and the moon; I saw them

lines.ar: لِي سَٰجِدِينَ
lines.en: prostrating to me.”

translate.ar: إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰأَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَٰجِدِينَ
translate.en: When Yūsuf said to his father: “O my father, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.”
The muṣḥaf, that is, the book of Allah.
The Habib read a verse, then he read its commentary.
translate.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.

translate.en: What is meant by light is knowledge.
The majlis, that is, the circle of knowledge.
Luqmān counselled his son.
The sura is long, and in it is a beautiful story.
He means: to Allah is the final return.
Ahmad wrote the commentary of the verse in his book.
translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ تَفْسِيرَ الْآيَةِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.

translate.en: The Habib said: wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.
translate.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْحِكْمَةُ أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
alt: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْحِكْمَةُ، يَعْنِي الْعِلْمَ وَالْعَمَلَ.

translate.en: Ahmad saw a beautiful dream in the night.
translate.ar: رَأَى أَحْمَدُ رُؤْيَا جَمِيلَةً فِي اللَّيْلِ.

translate.en: If you read the verse, read its commentary.
What is meant by the road is the road of knowledge.

readings.title_en: A ḥadīth with its chain and its commentary
readings.question_en: Where does the chain end, where do the words begin, and where does the commentary start?
readings.question_ar: أَيْنَ يَنْتَهِي الْإِسْنَادُ؟ وَأَيْنَ يَبْدَأُ الْمَتْنُ؟ وَأَيْنَ يَبْدَأُ الشَّرْحُ؟

passages.intro_en: A ḥadīth page: the chain, the words, and the commentary. The text is fully vowelled. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (the ḥadīth of Tamīm al-Dārī) with al-Nawawī's commentary (abridged)
passages.cite: Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Dār al-Jīl / Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut (Shamela 3.28 id 1786, vowelled and "matching the print"), 1/53; same ḥadīth no. 55 in the ʿAbd al-Bāqī numbering (Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Shamela 1785, 1/74). Commentary: al-Nawawī, al-Minhāj sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī, Beirut, 2nd ed. 1392 AH, 2/37 (Shamela 2570, print pagination; the vowels are copied from the vowelled copy 2569, whose own numbering is digital: 1/144). ABRIDGED: the printed isnād has a short exchange between Sufyān and Suhayl between lines 1 and 2, omitted here, so the chain reads “Sufyān told us” twice. Lines 1–4 are the ḥadīth as in the vowelled print (the printed formula after النَّبِىَّ is shown as ﷺ; the spaces inside the guillemets are closed up; the print’s spellings النَّبِىَّ، الدَّارِىِّ، وَلأَئِمَّةِ are kept). Lines 5–8 are al-Nawawī’s commentary; the source vowels them only in part, and the course adds the case endings (vowelled for learners; letters unchanged).

lines.ar: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادٍ الْمَكِّىُّ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ
lines.en: Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād al-Makkī told us; Sufyān told us.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ عَنْ سُهَيْلٍ عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ تَمِيمٍ الدَّارِىِّ
lines.en: Then Sufyān told us, from Suhayl, from ʿAṭāʾ b. Yazīd, from Tamīm al-Dārī:

lines.ar: أَنَّ النَّبِىَّ ﷺ قَالَ «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ»
lines.en: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Religion is sincere counsel."

lines.ar: قُلْنَا لِمَنْ قَالَ «لِلَّهِ وَلِكِتَابِهِ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَعَامَّتِهِمْ»
lines.en: We said, "For whom?" He said: "For Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common people."

lines.ar: هَذَا حَدِيثٌ عَظِيمُ الشَّأْنِ وَعَلَيْهِ مَدَارُ الْإِسْلَامِ
lines.en: (Nawawī:) This is a ḥadīth of great weight, and Islam turns upon it.
