lines.ar: وَأَمَّا شَرْحُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ فَقَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَبُو سُلَيْمَانَ الْخَطَّابِيُّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: النَّصِيحَةُ كَلِمَةٌ جَامِعَةٌ مَعْنَاهَا حِيَازَةُ الْحَظِّ لِلْمَنْصُوحِ لَهُ
lines.en: As for explaining this ḥadīth, Imām Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī said: naṣīḥa is a comprehensive word; its meaning is securing what is good for the one counselled.

lines.ar: وَمَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ وَقِوَامُهُ النَّصِيحَةُ
lines.en: And the meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion and what keeps it standing is sincere counsel,

lines.ar: كَقَوْلِهِ: الْحَجُّ عَرَفَةُ أَيْ عِمَادُهُ وَمُعْظَمُهُ عَرَفَةُ
lines.en: like his saying, "Ḥajj is ʿArafa", that is, its pillar and greatest part is ʿArafa.

glossary.en: may He have mercy on him

passages.ar: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادٍ الْمَكِّىُّ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ ثُمَّ حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ عَنْ سُهَيْلٍ عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ تَمِيمٍ الدَّارِىِّ أَنَّ النَّبِىَّ ﷺ قَالَ «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ» قُلْنَا لِمَنْ قَالَ «لِلَّهِ وَلِكِتَابِهِ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَعَامَّتِهِمْ» هَذَا حَدِيثٌ عَظِيمُ الشَّأْنِ وَعَلَيْهِ مَدَارُ الْإِسْلَامِ وَأَمَّا شَرْحُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ فَقَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَبُو سُلَيْمَانَ الْخَطَّابِيُّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: النَّصِيحَةُ كَلِمَةٌ جَامِعَةٌ مَعْنَاهَا حِيَازَةُ الْحَظِّ لِلْمَنْصُوحِ لَهُ وَمَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ وَقِوَامُهُ النَّصِيحَةُ كَقَوْلِهِ: الْحَجُّ عَرَفَةُ أَيْ عِمَادُهُ وَمُعْظَمُهُ عَرَفَةُ
passages.en: Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād al-Makkī told us; Sufyān told us. Then Sufyān told us, from Suhayl, from ʿAṭāʾ b. Yazīd, from Tamīm al-Dārī: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Religion is sincere counsel." We said, "For whom?" He said: "For Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common people." (Nawawī:) This is a ḥadīth of great weight, and Islam turns upon it. As for explaining this ḥadīth, Imām Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī said: naṣīḥa is a comprehensive word; its meaning is securing what is good for the one counselled. And the meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion and what keeps it standing is sincere counsel, like his saying, "Ḥajj is ʿArafa", that is, its pillar and greatest part is ʿArafa.

passages.intro_en: A short text: the circle after dawn. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text. The ḥadīth words in line 9 are copied from the verified text of Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim above; the four names in line 10 are from its chain.

lines.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ.
lines.en: Ahmad sat in the Habib’s circle after dawn.

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ حَدِيثًا مِنْ صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ، وَقَبْلَ الْمَتْنِ قَرَأَ الْإِسْنَادَ.
lines.en: The Habib read a ḥadīth from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, and before the text he read the chain.

lines.ar: سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: مَا الْإِسْنَادُ يَا حَبِيبُ؟
lines.en: Ahmad asked: What is the chain, Habib?

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْإِسْنَادُ طَرِيقُ الْحَدِيثِ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
lines.en: The Habib said: The chain is the way of the ḥadīth to the Prophet ﷺ.

lines.ar: وَالرَّاوِي يَقُولُ: حَدَّثَنِي مُعَلِّمِي، عَنْ مُعَلِّمِهِ.
lines.en: And the narrator says: My teacher told me, from his teacher.

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: وَمَا الْمَتْنُ؟
lines.en: Then Ahmad asked: And what is the text?

lines.ar: قَالَ: الْمَتْنُ هُوَ الْحَدِيثُ نَفْسُهُ، أَيْ مَا قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ.
lines.en: He said: The text is the ḥadīth itself, that is, what the Prophet ﷺ said.

lines.ar: وَالشَّرْحُ هُوَ مَا يَقُولُهُ الْعَالِمُ بَعْدَ الْحَدِيثِ.
lines.en: And the commentary is what the scholar says after the ḥadīth.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ حَدِيثَ تَمِيمٍ: «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ».
lines.en: Then the Habib read the ḥadīth of Tamīm: “Religion is sincere counsel.”

lines.ar: فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: سُفْيَانُ، ثُمَّ سُهَيْلٌ، ثُمَّ عَطَاءٌ، ثُمَّ تَمِيمٌ.
lines.en: And Ahmad wrote in his book: Sufyān, then Suhayl, then ʿAṭāʾ, then Tamīm.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ لِعُمَرَ: الْإِسْنَادُ طَرِيقٌ طَوِيلٌ، وَالْمَتْنُ كَلِمَةٌ قَصِيرَةٌ.
lines.en: And he said to Umar: The chain is a long road, and the text is a short word.

passages.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ. قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ حَدِيثًا مِنْ صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ، وَقَبْلَ الْمَتْنِ قَرَأَ الْإِسْنَادَ. سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: مَا الْإِسْنَادُ يَا حَبِيبُ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْإِسْنَادُ طَرِيقُ الْحَدِيثِ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. وَالرَّاوِي يَقُولُ: حَدَّثَنِي مُعَلِّمِي، عَنْ مُعَلِّمِهِ. فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: وَمَا الْمَتْنُ؟ قَالَ: الْمَتْنُ هُوَ الْحَدِيثُ نَفْسُهُ، أَيْ مَا قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ. وَالشَّرْحُ هُوَ مَا يَقُولُهُ الْعَالِمُ بَعْدَ الْحَدِيثِ. ثُمَّ قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ حَدِيثَ تَمِيمٍ: «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ». فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: سُفْيَانُ، ثُمَّ سُهَيْلٌ، ثُمَّ عَطَاءٌ، ثُمَّ تَمِيمٌ. وَقَالَ لِعُمَرَ: الْإِسْنَادُ طَرِيقٌ طَوِيلٌ، وَالْمَتْنُ كَلِمَةٌ قَصِيرَةٌ.
passages.en: Ahmad sat in the Habib’s circle after dawn. The Habib read a ḥadīth from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, and before the text he read the chain. Ahmad asked: What is the chain, Habib? The Habib said: The chain is the way of the ḥadīth to the Prophet ﷺ. And the narrator says: My teacher told me, from his teacher. Then Ahmad asked: And what is the text? He said: The text is the ḥadīth itself, that is, what the Prophet ﷺ said. And the commentary is what the scholar says after the ḥadīth. Then the Habib read the ḥadīth of Tamīm: “Religion is sincere counsel.” And Ahmad wrote in his book: Sufyān, then Suhayl, then ʿAṭāʾ, then Tamīm. And he said to Umar: The chain is a long road, and the text is a short word.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 132-133 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.
lines.en: The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
lines.en: And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ. وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
passages.en: The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel. And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.

glossary.en: may He have mercy on him

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth with its chain (isnād), its text (matn) and a commentary (sharḥ): lines 1–2 are the chain (حَدَّثَنَا … عَنْ …), lines 3–4 the words after قَالَ, lines 5–8 the scholar’s commentary.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād al-Makkī told us; Sufyān told us.

questions.q: Which two words are repeated in the chain (lines 1–2)?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَتَكَرَّرَانِ فِي الْإِسْنَادِ (السَّطْرَانِ ١–٢)؟
questions.a: حَدَّثَنَا (“told us”) and عَنْ (“from”).

questions.q: Line 2: write the names in order, from the first to the last.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: اُكْتُبِ الْأَسْمَاءَ بِالتَّرْتِيبِ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْأَخِيرِ.
questions.a: Sufyān → Suhayl → ʿAṭāʾ b. Yazīd → Tamīm al-Dārī.

questions.q: Who is the last name in the chain, and about whom does he report?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الِاسْمُ الْأَخِيرُ فِي الْإِسْنَادِ؟ وَعَنْ مَنْ يَرْوِي؟
questions.a: Tamīm al-Dārī, the Companion; he reports that the Prophet ﷺ said these words.

questions.q: Line 3: which words show that the chain has ended and the matn begins?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الْإِسْنَادَ انْتَهَى وَالْمَتْنَ بَدَأَ؟
questions.a: أَنَّ … قَالَ (“that … said”).

questions.q: What is the matn in line 3? Translate it.
questions.q_ar: مَا الْمَتْنُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣؟ تَرْجِمْهُ.
questions.a: «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ»: “Religion is sincere counsel.”

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: We said, “For whom?” He said: “For Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders of the Muslims and their common people.”

questions.q: Line 4: how many things does the answer name? Name the first three.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: كَمْ شَيْئًا يَذْكُرُ الْجَوَابُ؟ اُذْكُرِ الْأَوَّلَ وَالثَّانِيَ وَالثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: Five. The first three: Allah, His Book, His Messenger.
questions.ref_ar: لِلَّهِ وَلِكِتَابِهِ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَعَامَّتِهِمْ

questions.q: Line 5: what does the commentator say about this ḥadīth?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٥: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الشَّارِحُ عَنْ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ؟
questions.a: That it is a ḥadīth of great weight, and Islam turns upon it.

questions.q: Line 6: which word tells you that an explanation begins?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٦: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الشَّرْحَ يَبْدَأُ؟
questions.a: شَرْحُ (“commentary”): “and as for the explanation of this ḥadīth”.

questions.q: Line 6: what does al-Khaṭṭābī say the word “naṣīḥa” is?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٦: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الْخَطَّابِيُّ عَنْ كَلِمَةِ «النَّصِيحَةِ»؟
questions.a: A comprehensive word; its meaning is securing what is good for the one counselled.

questions.q: Line 7: what is “the pillar of religion” in this ḥadīth?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٧: مَا عِمَادُ الدِّينِ فِي هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ؟
questions.a: النَّصِيحَةُ: sincere counsel.

questions.q: Line 8: the commentary gives a second example with قَوْلُهُ … أَيْ. What does “Ḥajj is ʿArafa” mean there?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٨: بِمَاذَا يَشْرَحُ «الْحَجُّ عَرَفَةُ»؟
questions.a: Its pillar and its greatest part is ʿArafa.
questions.ref_ar: الْحَجُّ عَرَفَةُ أَيْ عِمَادُهُ وَمُعْظَمُهُ عَرَفَةُ

questions.q: Why is the chain printed before the words of the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَأْتِي الْإِسْنَادُ قَبْلَ كَلَامِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ؟
questions.a: So that the reader sees how the words came to him, from one narrator to the next, before reading the words themselves.

questions.q: The page has two voices. Who speaks in lines 3–4 and who in lines 5–8?
questions.q_ar: فِي الصَّفْحَةِ صَوْتَانِ. مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ٣–٤؟ وَمَنْ فِي ٥–٨؟
questions.a: Lines 3–4: the Prophet ﷺ (and the Companions asking). Lines 5–8: the commentator (al-Nawawī, quoting al-Khaṭṭābī).

questions.q: When did Ahmad sit in the Habib’s circle? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَتَى جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ؟
questions.a: After dawn.

questions.q: What did the Habib read first: the chain or the text? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ أَوَّلًا: الْإِسْنَادَ أَمِ الْمَتْنَ؟
questions.a: The chain (before the text).

questions.q: From which book was the ḥadīth? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مِنْ أَيِّ كِتَابٍ كَانَ الْحَدِيثُ؟
questions.a: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask first? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ أَوَّلًا؟
questions.a: What the chain is.

questions.q: According to the Habib, what is the chain? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: عِنْدَ الْحَبِيبِ مَا الْإِسْنَادُ؟
questions.a: The way of the ḥadīth to the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: What does the narrator say? Translate. (line 5)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الرَّاوِي؟ تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: “My teacher told me, from his teacher.”

questions.q: Translate line 7.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ السَّابِعَ.
questions.a: He said: The text is the ḥadīth itself, that is, what the Prophet ﷺ said.

questions.q: Line 7: which frame-word is used, and what does it explain?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٧: أَيُّ كَلِمَةِ شَرْحٍ اسْتُعْمِلَتْ؟ وَمَاذَا شَرَحَتْ؟
questions.a: أَيْ explains “the ḥadīth itself”: what the Prophet ﷺ said.

questions.q: What is the commentary (sharḥ), according to line 8?
questions.q_ar: مَا الشَّرْحُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٨؟
questions.a: What the scholar says after the ḥadīth.

questions.q: Which ḥadīth did the Habib read at the end? (line 9)
questions.q_ar: أَيَّ حَدِيثٍ قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ؟
questions.a: The ḥadīth of Tamīm: religion is sincere counsel.

questions.q: Which four names did Ahmad write in his book, in what order? (line 10)
questions.q_ar: أَيَّ أَسْمَاءٍ كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَبِأَيِّ تَرْتِيبٍ؟
questions.a: Sufyān, then Suhayl, then ʿAṭāʾ, then Tamīm.

questions.q: Translate the Habib’s last words. (line 11)
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ الْأَخِيرَ.
questions.a: The chain is a long road, and the text is a short word.
questions.ref_ar: الْإِسْنَادُ طَرِيقٌ طَوِيلٌ، وَالْمَتْنُ كَلِمَةٌ قَصِيرَةٌ

questions.q: Why does the Habib call the chain “a road”? What travels on it?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يُسَمِّي الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ «طَرِيقًا»؟ مَاذَا يَسِيرُ فِيهِ؟
questions.a: The ḥadīth travels on it: from the first narrators to the Prophet ﷺ, step by step.

questions.q: In line 5 the narrator says “from his teacher” (عَنْ مُعَلِّمِهِ). What is the next step up the chain?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٥ يَقُولُ الرَّاوِي «عَنْ مُعَلِّمِهِ». مَا الْخُطْوَةُ التَّالِيَةُ فِي الْإِسْنَادِ؟
questions.a: The teacher’s teacher: each narrator takes from the one above him.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel. And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.

questions.q: What is the إِسْنَاد and what is the مَتْن?
questions.a: The isnād is the chain of narrators; the matn is the words of the ḥadīth itself.

questions.q: Which word in the commentary means “pillar”?
questions.a: عِمَادُ

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The Habib read the chain, then the matn.
questions.a: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ.

translate.ar: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيٌّ عَنْ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ.
translate.en: Ali told us, from Salim, from his father.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ ثُمَّ الشَّرْحَ.
translate.en: The Habib read the chain, then the text, then the commentary.

translate.ar: الْإِسْنَادُ طَرِيقٌ طَوِيلٌ، وَالرَّاوِي يَقُولُ: حَدَّثَنِي مُعَلِّمِي.
translate.en: The chain is a long road, and the narrator says: My teacher told me.

translate.ar: سَمِعْتُ الْحَدِيثَ مِنْ مُعَلِّمِي فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
translate.en: I heard the ḥadīth from my teacher in the ribāṭ.
This is a sound ḥadīth, and its narration is long.

translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ شَرْحَ الْحَدِيثِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
translate.en: Ahmad wrote the commentary of the ḥadīth in his book.

translate.ar: قَالَ الْمُعَلِّمُ: إِذَا سَمِعْتَ حَدِيثًا فَاسْأَلْ عَنْ إِسْنَادِهِ.
translate.en: The teacher said: If you hear a ḥadīth, ask about its chain.
The text is short and the commentary is long.

translate.ar: قَوْلُهُ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ هِدَايَةٌ.
translate.en: His words: “Knowledge is light”, that is, knowledge is guidance.

lines.ar: حَدَّثَنَا سَالِمٌ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، أَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ قَالَ:
lines.en: Salim told us, from his father, from Ali, that the teacher said:

lines.ar: اُدْخُلِ الْمَسْجِدَ بِالْأَدَبِ، وَلَا تَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: “Enter the mosque with good manners, and do not talk much.”

translate.ar: حَدَّثَنَا سَالِمٌ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، أَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ قَالَ: اُدْخُلِ الْمَسْجِدَ بِالْأَدَبِ، وَلَا تَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا.
translate.en: Salim told us, from his father, from Ali, that the teacher said: “Enter the mosque with good manners, and do not talk much.”
Umar told us, from Ahmad.
Salim told me, from Ali.
Umar told us, from Ahmad, that the teacher said: Knowledge is light.
translate.ar: حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ أَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ قَالَ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ.

translate.en: The Habib read the chain, then the text.
The text is the ḥadīth itself.
The commentary is after the ḥadīth.
This is a sound ḥadīth.
Ahmad informed us, from his father.
The chain is a long road.
I heard the ḥadīth from my teacher.
His words: knowledge is light, that is, knowledge is guidance.
translate.ar: قَوْلُهُ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ أَيِ الْعِلْمُ هِدَايَةٌ.

translate.en: Ahmad wrote the commentary of the ḥadīth in his book.
translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ شَرْحَ الْحَدِيثِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.

readings.title_en: A short ḥadīth: condition and reward
readings.question_en: What must a person do, and what does he get for it?
readings.question_ar: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ الْإِنْسَانُ؟ وَمَاذَا يَنَالُ؟

passages.intro_en: Two sayings of the Prophet ﷺ in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. Read them aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Muslim b. al-Ḥajjāj, al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Dār al-Jīl / Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda, Beirut (Shamela 3.28 id 1786, vowelled, matches the print), 1/49: line 1 = ʿAbd al-Bāqī no. 45, line 2 = no. 47 (cut at a clause boundary: the quotation is left open, shown with "..."). The printed salutation formula is shown as the sign ﷺ; the source spelling (لاَ، لأَخِيهِ، النَّبِىِّ) is kept.

lines.ar: عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ عَنِ النَّبِىِّ ﷺ قَالَ « لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ - أَوْ قَالَ لِجَارِهِ - مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ »
lines.en: From Anas b. Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ: "None of you believes until he loves for his brother (or: his neighbour) what he loves for himself."

lines.ar: عَنْ أَبِى هُرَيْرَةَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ « مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ ...
lines.en: From Abū Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent."

passages.ar: عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ عَنِ النَّبِىِّ ﷺ قَالَ « لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ - أَوْ قَالَ لِجَارِهِ - مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ » عَنْ أَبِى هُرَيْرَةَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ « مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ ...
passages.en: From Anas b. Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ: "None of you believes until he loves for his brother (or: his neighbour) what he loves for himself." From Abū Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent."

passages.intro_en: A short text: after ʿIshāʾ in the ribāṭ. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
lines.en: After ʿIshāʾ Ahmad sat with Umar in the ribāṭ.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: دَلَّ أَحْمَدُ ضَيْفًا عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: And Umar said: Ahmad guided a guest to the way to the mosque.

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ: هَلْ لِي أَجْرٌ؟
lines.en: So Ahmad asked the Habib: Do I have a reward?

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: نَعَمْ يَا أَحْمَدُ، مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Yes, Ahmad. Whoever guides to good has a reward.

lines.ar: وَمَنْ سَاعَدَ أَخَاهُ سَاعَدَهُ اللَّهُ.
lines.en: And whoever helps his brother, Allah helps him.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ: لَا يَتَكَلَّمُ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ.
lines.en: Then he said: None of you speaks in the majlis until he has listened.

lines.ar: فَسَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ دَرْسَ الْحَبِيبِ وَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ.
lines.en: So Ahmad listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.

lines.ar: وَفِي الصَّبَاحِ دَلَّ أَحْمَدُ أُمَّهُ عَلَى كِتَابٍ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، فَقَالَتْ: لَكَ ثَوَابٌ يَا أَحْمَدُ.
lines.en: And in the morning Ahmad guided his mother to a book in the library, and she said: You have a reward, Ahmad.

passages.ar: بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ. وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: دَلَّ أَحْمَدُ ضَيْفًا عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ. فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ: هَلْ لِي أَجْرٌ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: نَعَمْ يَا أَحْمَدُ، مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ. وَمَنْ سَاعَدَ أَخَاهُ سَاعَدَهُ اللَّهُ. ثُمَّ قَالَ: لَا يَتَكَلَّمُ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ. فَسَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ دَرْسَ الْحَبِيبِ وَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ. وَفِي الصَّبَاحِ دَلَّ أَحْمَدُ أُمَّهُ عَلَى كِتَابٍ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، فَقَالَتْ: لَكَ ثَوَابٌ يَا أَحْمَدُ.
passages.en: After ʿIshāʾ Ahmad sat with Umar in the ribāṭ. And Umar said: Ahmad guided a guest to the way to the mosque. So Ahmad asked the Habib: Do I have a reward? The Habib said: Yes, Ahmad. Whoever guides to good has a reward. And whoever helps his brother, Allah helps him. Then he said: None of you speaks in the majlis until he has listened. So Ahmad listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak. And in the morning Ahmad guided his mother to a book in the library, and she said: You have a reward, Ahmad.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 134-135 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
lines.en: The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
lines.en: Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.

passages.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ. ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
passages.en: The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it. Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A short ḥadīth of conduct. Each saying opens with the Companion who reported it (عَنْ … عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ … قَالَ), then comes the saying itself, short and without commentary. The second one uses the frame مَنْ … فَـ.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: From Anas b. Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ: “None of you believes until he loves for his brother (or: his neighbour) what he loves for himself.”

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: From Abū Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent ...”

questions.q: Line 1: who is being addressed, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: لِمَنِ الْخِطَابُ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: All of “you” (many): the ending ـكُمْ in أَحَدُكُمْ.

questions.q: True or false: line 1 says that one particular person does not believe.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ السَّطْرُ ١ إِنَّ شَخْصًا مُعَيَّنًا لَا يُؤْمِنُ.
questions.a: False. أَحَد after لَا means “no one”: none of you believes until …

questions.q: Line 1: find the word that means “his neighbour”. What does the ـهِ mean?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «جَارَهُ». مَاذَا تَعْنِي ـهِ؟
questions.a: لِجَارِهِ. ـهِ = “his”.

questions.q: Line 2: what two choices does the speaker have?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَا الْخِيَارَانِ؟
questions.a: To speak good, or to keep silent.

questions.q: Read the ending of each word from its vowels and say why it has it.
questions.q_ar: اِقْرَأْ نِهَايَةَ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ مِنْ حَرَكَاتِهَا، وَقُلْ لِمَاذَا.
questions.a: خَيْرًا: ـًا, what is said (it is the thing said, after فَلْيَقُلْ). الْيَوْمِ: ـِ, joined with وَ to اللَّهِ after بِـ. أَخِيهِ: ـِ, after the little word لِـ (the five nouns: أَخُو → أَخِي).

questions.q: Which words in line 2 name the two things a believer holds to? Find the little word that joins them.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ تُسَمِّيَانِ مَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ الْمُؤْمِنُ؟ وَمَا الْحَرْفُ الَّذِي يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَهُمَا؟
questions.a: بِاللَّهِ and الْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ, joined by وَ.

questions.q: The reporter says أَوْ قَالَ (“or he said”). What does this show about how the reporters worked?
questions.q_ar: يَقُولُ الرَّاوِي «أَوْ قَالَ». عَلَى مَاذَا يَدُلُّ ذَلِكَ فِي طَرِيقَةِ الرُّوَاةِ؟
questions.a: He was not sure whether the Prophet ﷺ said “his brother” or “his neighbour”, so he gives both and tells us. This is honesty and care in passing on the words.

questions.q: Line 2 ends with “...”. Why does a copyist stop in the middle of a ḥadīth, and how does the reader know?
questions.q_ar: يَنْتَهِي السَّطْرُ ٢ بِنُقَطٍ. لِمَاذَا يَقِفُ النَّاسِخُ فِي وَسَطِ الْحَدِيثِ؟ وَكَيْفَ يَعْرِفُ الْقَارِئُ؟
questions.a: The ḥadīth is longer: the copyist keeps only the part he needs. The open quotation mark and the dots tell the reader that more follows.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom, and when?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: In the ribāṭ, with Umar, after ʿIshāʾ.

questions.q: Who said that Ahmad guided someone? What had Ahmad done?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ قَالَ إِنَّ أَحْمَدَ دَلَّ أَحَدًا؟ مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: Umar said it. Ahmad had guided a guest to the way to the mosque.

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask in line 3?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣؟
questions.a: Whether he has a reward.

questions.q: Line 4: which part is the deed and which part is the reward?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: أَيُّ جُزْءٍ هُوَ الْعَمَلُ؟ وَأَيُّ جُزْءٍ هُوَ الثَّوَابُ؟
questions.a: The deed: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ (guided to good). The reward: فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.
questions.ref_ar: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ

questions.q: Which little word opens the reward, and what does لَهُ mean?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَفْتَحُ الثَّوَابَ؟ وَمَاذَا تَعْنِي «لَهُ»؟
questions.a: فَـ opens it. لَهُ = “he has” (for him).

questions.q: Line 5: compare the two verbs. What is the same, and who is the doer of the second?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٥: قَارِنْ بَيْنَ الْفِعْلَيْنِ. مَا الْمُشْتَرَكُ؟ وَمَنْ فَاعِلُ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: The same verb. The doer of the second is Allah (اللَّهُ); the ending ـهُ is the man.

questions.q: Translate line 6.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ ٦.
questions.a: Then he said: None of you speaks in the majlis until he has listened.

questions.q: True or false: the Habib tells them to speak first and listen later.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ: تَكَلَّمُوا أَوَّلًا ثُمَّ اسْمَعُوا.
questions.a: False. حَتَّى means “until”: first listen, then speak.

questions.q: What did Ahmad do in line 7?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٧؟
questions.a: He listened to the Habib’s lesson and did not speak.

questions.q: What did his mother say in line 8, and why?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَتْ أُمُّهُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٨؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: “You have a reward, Ahmad”: because he guided her to a book in the library.

questions.q: Ahmad listened and did not speak. Which sentence of the Habib did he act on? Say it in your own words.
questions.q_ar: بِأَيِّ جُمْلَةٍ لِلْحَبِيبِ عَمِلَ أَحْمَدُ؟ قُلْهَا بِكَلَامِكَ.
questions.a: Line 6: no one speaks until he has listened. He listened first, so he kept silence.

questions.q: Ahmad’s mother says “you have a reward”. Which saying of the Habib is she using? Find the frame.
questions.q_ar: أَيَّ قَوْلٍ لِلْحَبِيبِ اسْتَعْمَلَتْ أُمُّهُ؟ جِدِ الْقَالَبَ.
questions.a: The frame مَنْ … فَلَهُ …: Ahmad guided (دَلَّ) her to a book, so he has a reward. It is the same frame as line 4.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it. Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.

questions.q: Which word begins the condition in the ḥadīth?
questions.a: مَنْ (whoever)

questions.q: What does the ḥadīth promise to the one who guides to good?
questions.a: A reward like the reward of the one who does it.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy guided his friend to the majlis.
questions.a: دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.

translate.ar: مَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ فِي الْفَجْرِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ.
translate.en: Whoever comes to the mosque at dawn has a great reward.

translate.ar: مَنْ سَأَلَ عَنْ أَخِيهِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.
translate.en: Whoever asks after his brother has a reward.

translate.ar: مَنْ عَلَّمَ ابْنَ أَخِيهِ الْقُرْآنَ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِهِ.
translate.en: Whoever teaches his brother’s son the Qur’an has the like of his reward.

translate.ar: لَا يَتَكَلَّمُ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الطُّلَّابِ حَتَّى يَدْخُلَ الْحَبِيبُ.
translate.en: None of the students speaks until the Habib comes in.

translate.ar: مَنْ سَاعَدَ جَارَهُ فِي الْبَيْتِ سَاعَدَهُ اللَّهُ.
translate.en: Whoever helps his neighbour in the house, Allah helps him.

translate.ar: لَا يَذْهَبُ أَحَدُكُمْ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ حَتَّى يَسْأَلَ الْمُعَلِّمَ عَنِ الدَّرْسِ.
translate.en: None of you goes home until he asks the teacher about the lesson.

translate.ar: مَنْ سَتَرَ أَخَاهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا سَتَرَهُ اللَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ.
translate.en: Whoever covers his brother’s fault in this world, Allah covers him in the next.

translate.ar: مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ سَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
translate.en: Whoever sits in the circle hears the lesson.

translate.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَكَ ثَوَابٌ يَا عُمَرُ، لِأَنَّكَ سَاعَدْتَ أَخَاكَ.
translate.en: The Habib said: You have a reward, Umar, because you helped your brother.

translate.ar: مَنْ قَرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ فَلَهُ ثَوَابٌ كَبِيرٌ.
translate.en: Whoever reads the Qur’an has a great reward.

translate.ar: لَا يَخْرُجُ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْحَلْقَةِ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ الدَّرْسَ.
translate.en: No one leaves the circle until he has heard the lesson.

lines.ar: وَاللَّهُ فِى عَوْنِ الْعَبْدِ مَا كَانَ الْعَبْدُ فِى عَوْنِ أَخِيهِ
lines.en: Allah is helping the servant as long as the servant is helping his brother.

lines.ar: وَمَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
lines.en: And whoever takes a road seeking knowledge on it, Allah makes easy for him by it a road to Paradise."

translate.ar: وَاللَّهُ فِى عَوْنِ الْعَبْدِ مَا كَانَ الْعَبْدُ فِى عَوْنِ أَخِيهِ وَمَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
translate.en: Allah is helping the servant as long as the servant is helping his brother. And whoever takes a road seeking knowledge on it, Allah makes easy for him by it a road to Paradise."
Whoever comes to the lesson has a reward.
translate.ar: مَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.

translate.en: Whoever visits his teacher has a great reward.
translate.ar: مَنْ زَارَ مُعَلِّمَهُ فَلَهُ ثَوَابٌ كَبِيرٌ.
alt: مَنْ زَارَ مُعَلِّمَهُ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ.

translate.en: Whoever helps his neighbour, Allah helps him.
None of you speaks until he has listened.
Whoever guides his brother to the mosque has the like of his reward.
translate.ar: مَنْ دَلَّ أَخَاهُ عَلَى الْمَسْجِدِ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِهِ.

translate.en: Whoever honours his guest, Allah honours him.
None of the students goes back to the house until he reads the lesson.
translate.ar: لَا يَرْجِعُ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الطُّلَّابِ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ حَتَّى يَقْرَأَ الدَّرْسَ.

translate.en: Whoever teaches the people has a reward.
Whoever serves the guests has a reward, and whoever honours them, Allah honours him.
translate.ar: مَنْ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ، وَمَنْ أَكْرَمَهُمْ أَكْرَمَهُ اللَّهُ.

translate.en: No one reads in the book until he sits down.
translate.ar: لَا يَقْرَأُ أَحَدٌ فِي الْكِتَابِ حَتَّى يَجْلِسَ.

translate.en: Whoever serves his teacher has a reward.
None of you leaves the circle until he has heard the lesson.
translate.ar: لَا يَخْرُجُ أَحَدُكُمْ مِنَ الْحَلْقَةِ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ الدَّرْسَ.

readings.title_en: Fiqh: matn, sharḥ and the ruling
readings.question_en: What is the ruling, and what is it about?
readings.question_ar: مَا الْحُكْمُ؟ وَفِي أَيِّ شَيْءٍ؟

passages.intro_en: The fourth place, and the limit. Matn in brackets, then the sharḥ. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Safīnat al-Najā (matn, in brackets) with Kāshifat al-Sajā of Nawawī al-Jāwī (sharḥ)
passages.cite: Muḥammad Nawawī b. ʿUmar al-Jāwī, Kāshifat al-Sajā fī sharḥ Safīnat al-Najā (commentary on the matn of Sālim b. Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī); Shamela 3.28 id 4055 (the card gives no publisher or year and does not say the numbering matches a print), digital pages 153 (lines 1–7) and 164 (lines 8–10); printed edition not identified. The vowels are the course's; the same matn text is in 3.28 id 4059 (Matn Safīnat al-Najā, digital p. 3–6). Nayl al-Rajā (the sharḥ the plan names) exists on the SSD only as a scanned PDF (nayl al-rajāʾ sharḥ Safīnat al-Najā, 164 pp): not used. ABRIDGED: lines 1-7 of the ten are used (lines 8-10 are left out). The vowels are the course's (vowelled for learners); the letters are those of the source; before the ال of الرَّفْعِ (line 5) the course reads أَيِ.

lines.ar: (وَ) رَابِعُهَا: (عِنْدَ الْقِيَامِ مِنَ التَّشَهُّدِ الْأَوَّلِ) لِلِاتِّبَاعِ رَوَاهُ الشَّيْخَانِ
lines.en: And the fourth: at rising from the first tashahhud, following the Prophet's example, as the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim) report.

lines.ar: وَلَا يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي غَيْرِ هَذِهِ الْمَوَاضِعِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ
lines.en: And raising the hands is not recommended anywhere but these four places.

passages.ar: (وَ) رَابِعُهَا: (عِنْدَ الْقِيَامِ مِنَ التَّشَهُّدِ الْأَوَّلِ) لِلِاتِّبَاعِ رَوَاهُ الشَّيْخَانِ وَلَا يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي غَيْرِ هَذِهِ الْمَوَاضِعِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ
passages.en: And the fourth: at rising from the first tashahhud, following the Prophet's example, as the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim) report. And raising the hands is not recommended anywhere but these four places.

passages.intro_en: A short text: the lesson in the rawḥa. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: فِي الرَّوْحَةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ وَمَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: In the rawḥa Ahmad sat with Umar and with the Habib.

lines.ar: وَفَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ كِتَابَ «سَفِينَةِ النَّجَا» وَقَالَ: يَجِبُ الْوُضُوءُ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ.
lines.en: And the Habib opened the book “Safīnat al-Najā” and said: Ablution is obligatory before the prayer.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ: يُسَنُّ الذِّكْرُ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ، وَيُكْرَهُ النَّوْمُ قَبْلَ الْعِشَاءِ.
lines.en: Then he said: Dhikr after the prayer is recommended, and sleeping before ʿishāʾ is disliked.

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: هَلِ الْوُضُوءُ سُنَّةٌ؟
lines.en: So Ahmad asked: Is ablution a sunna?

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا يَا أَحْمَدُ، الْوُضُوءُ وَاجِبٌ، وَيُشْتَرَطُ لِلصَّلَاةِ.
lines.en: The Habib said: No, Ahmad. Ablution is obligatory, and it is a condition of the prayer.

lines.ar: وَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ: هَلْ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَاجِبٌ؟
lines.en: And Umar asked: Is raising the hands in the prayer obligatory?

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا، هُوَ سُنَّةٌ، وَلَيْسَ وَاجِبًا.
lines.en: The Habib said: No, it is a sunna, and not obligatory.

lines.ar: وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كُرَّاسَتِهِ: وَاجِبٌ، سُنَّةٌ، مَكْرُوهٌ، حَرَامٌ.
lines.en: And Ahmad wrote in his notebook: obligatory, sunna, disliked, forbidden.

glossary.en: a ship; here the title word

passages.ar: فِي الرَّوْحَةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ وَمَعَ الْحَبِيبِ. وَفَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ كِتَابَ «سَفِينَةِ النَّجَا» وَقَالَ: يَجِبُ الْوُضُوءُ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ. ثُمَّ قَالَ: يُسَنُّ الذِّكْرُ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ، وَيُكْرَهُ النَّوْمُ قَبْلَ الْعِشَاءِ. فَسَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: هَلِ الْوُضُوءُ سُنَّةٌ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا يَا أَحْمَدُ، الْوُضُوءُ وَاجِبٌ، وَيُشْتَرَطُ لِلصَّلَاةِ. وَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ: هَلْ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَاجِبٌ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا، هُوَ سُنَّةٌ، وَلَيْسَ وَاجِبًا. وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كُرَّاسَتِهِ: وَاجِبٌ، سُنَّةٌ، مَكْرُوهٌ، حَرَامٌ.
passages.en: In the rawḥa Ahmad sat with Umar and with the Habib. And the Habib opened the book “Safīnat al-Najā” and said: Ablution is obligatory before the prayer. Then he said: Dhikr after the prayer is recommended, and sleeping before ʿishāʾ is disliked. So Ahmad asked: Is ablution a sunna? The Habib said: No, Ahmad. Ablution is obligatory, and it is a condition of the prayer. And Umar asked: Is raising the hands in the prayer obligatory? The Habib said: No, it is a sunna, and not obligatory. And Ahmad wrote in his notebook: obligatory, sunna, disliked, forbidden.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 136-137 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ مِنَ الْمَتْنِ: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
lines.en: In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟
lines.en: Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands?

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
lines.en: The boy said: A sunna.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ مِنَ الْمَتْنِ: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ. ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
passages.en: In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places. Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.

glossary.en: a ship; here the title word

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A page of fiqh: a matn with its sharḥ. A ruling verb (يُسَنُّ) opens the sentence; the brackets hold the matn and the words outside them are the commentary.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: And fourth: at rising from the first tashahhud, following the Prophet’s example, as the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim) report.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And raising the hands is not recommended anywhere but these four places.

questions.q: Which place is this? What does the ending ـهَا point to?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ مَوْضِعٍ هَذَا؟ إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ ـهَا؟
questions.a: The fourth place. ـهَا points back to الْمَوَاضِع (the places).

questions.q: Which words are the matn here? How can you tell?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ هِيَ الْمَتْنُ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: The words in brackets: عِنْدَ الْقِيَامِ مِنَ التَّشَهُّدِ الْأَوَّلِ.

questions.q: Is this part of the matn or the sharḥ? What does it tell you?
questions.q_ar: أَهَذَا مِنَ الْمَتْنِ أَمْ مِنَ الشَّرْحِ؟ مَاذَا يُخْبِرُكَ؟
questions.a: The sharḥ (it is outside the bracket). It gives the reason: the Prophet ﷺ did this, and the two Shaykhs report it.

questions.q: Line 2: what is the ruling verb? Does it mean “forbidden”?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَا فِعْلُ الْحُكْمِ؟ هَلْ يَعْنِي «حَرَامٌ»؟
questions.a: لَا يُسَنُّ: it is not recommended. It does not say “forbidden”; it only says the act is not a sunna there.

questions.q: Read the endings of رَفْعُ، الْيَدَيْنِ، الْمَوَاضِعِ in line 2 from the vowels and say why.
questions.q_ar: اِقْرَأْ نِهَايَاتِ الْكَلِمَاتِ الثَّلَاثِ مِنْ حَرَكَاتِهَا وَقُلْ لِمَاذَا.
questions.a: رَفْعُ ـُ: what the ruling is about, after لَا يُسَنُّ. الْيَدَيْنِ: the dual in the genitive (the second word of “raising of the hands”). الْمَوَاضِعِ ـِ: like هَذِهِ before it, it comes after فِي غَيْرِ (“in other than”), so kasra.

questions.q: True or false: the book gives five places for raising the hands.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَذْكُرُ الْكِتَابُ خَمْسَةَ مَوَاضِعَ لِرَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ.
questions.a: False. Four places: أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ. The book gives them one by one.

questions.q: The sharḥ adds “the two Shaykhs report it”. Why does a book of fiqh give this?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَذْكُرُ كِتَابُ الْفِقْهِ «رَوَاهُ الشَّيْخَانِ»؟
questions.a: To show that the ruling rests on an authentic report. The reader can trust it, and a student can go and find the ḥadīth.

questions.q: Why would a short matn be written, and then a long sharḥ on it? What does each give the student?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يُكْتَبُ مَتْنٌ قَصِيرٌ ثُمَّ شَرْحٌ طَوِيلٌ؟
questions.a: The matn is short enough to learn by heart. The sharḥ explains each phrase, gives the reason, and opens the meaning. Memory comes from the one, understanding from the other.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the rawḥa, with Umar and the Habib.

questions.q: What did the Habib open, and what did he say?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ؟ وَمَاذَا قَالَ؟
questions.a: He opened a book of fiqh (Safīnat al-Najā). He said: ablution is obligatory before the prayer.

questions.q: Line 3: which verb gives the ruling on dhikr? Is it a duty?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ يُبَيِّنُ حُكْمَ الذِّكْرِ؟ هَلْ هُوَ وَاجِبٌ؟
questions.a: يُسَنُّ: recommended. It is not a duty.

questions.q: Line 3: what is the ruling on sleeping before ʿishāʾ?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَا حُكْمُ النَّوْمِ قَبْلَ الْعِشَاءِ؟
questions.a: Disliked (يُكْرَهُ): it is better to leave it.

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask in line 4? What did the Habib answer?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٤؟ وَمَاذَا أَجَابَ الْحَبِيبُ؟
questions.a: He asked whether ablution is a sunna. The Habib said no: it is obligatory.

questions.q: Line 5: what else does the Habib say about ablution?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٥: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ أَيْضًا عَنِ الْوُضُوءِ؟
questions.a: It is a condition of the prayer (يُشْتَرَطُ).

questions.q: What did Umar ask? What was the answer?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ عُمَرُ؟ وَمَا الْجَوَابُ؟
questions.a: Whether raising the hands in the prayer is obligatory. The answer: no, it is a sunna.

questions.q: True or false: the Habib says raising the hands is obligatory.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ إِنَّ رَفْعَ الْيَدَيْنِ وَاجِبٌ.
questions.a: False. هُوَ سُنَّةٌ وَلَيْسَ وَاجِبًا: it is a sunna, not obligatory.

questions.q: What four words did Ahmad write in his notebook?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْكَلِمَاتُ الْأَرْبَعُ الَّتِي كَتَبَهَا أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: Obligatory, sunna, disliked, forbidden.

questions.q: Find the word in line 5 or line 7 that means “obligatory”. Which verb in line 2 comes from the same root?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «لَا بُدَّ مِنْهُ». أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ مِنْ جَذْرِهَا؟
questions.a: وَاجِبٌ. The verb يَجِبُ in line 2.

questions.q: Ahmad’s four words go from what must be done to what is forbidden. Say in your own words what each one asks of a person.
questions.q_ar: قُلْ بِكَلَامِكَ: مَاذَا تَطْلُبُ كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ مِنَ الْكَلِمَاتِ الْأَرْبَعِ مِنَ الْإِنْسَانِ؟
questions.a: Obligatory (وَاجِبٌ): do it. Sunna (سُنَّةٌ): good to do, and rewarded. Disliked (مَكْرُوهٌ): better to leave. Forbidden (حَرَامٌ): do not do it; it is a sin.

questions.q: Why does a student of fiqh first learn the ruling words before the long chapters?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَتَعَلَّمُ طَالِبُ الْفِقْهِ أَلْفَاظَ الْحُكْمِ أَوَّلًا؟
questions.a: Every chapter is built of them: each sentence of a matn gives the ruling on an act. If you know the ruling words, you can read any page.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places. Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.

questions.q: Which word in the matn gives the ruling? What does it mean?
questions.a: يُسَنُّ: it is recommended (a sunna).

questions.q: How many places does the matn name?
questions.a: Four (أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ).

questions.q: Write in Arabic: Raising the hands is recommended.
questions.a: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ.

translate.en: Fasting in Ramadan is obligatory.

translate.ar: يُسَنُّ الذِّكْرُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَفِي الْمَسَاءِ.
translate.en: Dhikr is recommended in the morning and in the evening.
Much talk after ʿishāʾ is disliked.
Wronging people is forbidden.
Fasting without an intention is not valid.
Ablution and the qibla are conditions of the prayer.

translate.ar: الْأَكْلُ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ مُبَاحٌ فِي غَيْرِ رَمَضَانَ.
translate.en: Eating after dawn is permitted outside Ramadan.

translate.ar: سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْحَبِيبَ: مَا حُكْمُ الذِّكْرِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ؟ فَقَالَ: هُوَ سُنَّةٌ.
translate.en: Ahmad asked the Habib: What is the ruling on dhikr after the prayer? He said: It is a sunna.
A prayer without ablution is invalid.
Talking in the prayer is forbidden.

translate.ar: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ عِنْدَ الرُّكُوعِ وَعِنْدَ الِاعْتِدَالِ.
translate.en: Raising the hands is recommended at bowing and at standing upright.

lines.ar: (يَجِبُ الْوُضُوءُ) أَيْ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ.
lines.en: (Matn:) Ablution is obligatory. (Sharḥ:) that is, before the prayer.

lines.ar: (وَيُكْرَهُ النَّوْمُ قَبْلَ الْعِشَاءِ) أَيْ تَرْكُهُ أَحْسَنُ.
lines.en: (Matn:) And sleeping before ʿishāʾ is disliked. (Sharḥ:) that is, leaving it is better.

lines.ar: (وَلَا يَصِحُّ الْوُضُوءُ بِلَا مَاءٍ) أَيْ يَكُونُ بَاطِلًا.
lines.en: (Matn:) And ablution without water is not valid. (Sharḥ:) that is, it is invalid.

translate.ar: (يَجِبُ الْوُضُوءُ) أَيْ قَبْلَ الصَّلَاةِ. (وَيُكْرَهُ النَّوْمُ قَبْلَ الْعِشَاءِ) أَيْ تَرْكُهُ أَحْسَنُ. (وَلَا يَصِحُّ الْوُضُوءُ بِلَا مَاءٍ) أَيْ يَكُونُ بَاطِلًا.
translate.en: (Matn:) Ablution is obligatory. (Sharḥ:) that is, before the prayer. (Matn:) And sleeping before ʿishāʾ is disliked. (Sharḥ:) that is, leaving it is better. (Matn:) And ablution without water is not valid. (Sharḥ:) that is, it is invalid.
Ablution is obligatory before the prayer.
Dhikr after the prayer is recommended.
Sleeping before ʿishāʾ is disliked.
Wronging people is forbidden.
Ablution without water is not valid.
Ablution is a condition of the prayer.
Raising the hands at bowing is recommended.
Raising the hands is not recommended anywhere but these places.
translate.ar: لَا يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي غَيْرِ هَذِهِ الْمَوَاضِعِ.

translate.en: Fasting in Ramadan is obligatory.
Dhikr in the morning is recommended.
Much talk after ʿishāʾ is disliked.
Write a matn and its sharḥ: the matn says ablution is obligatory; the sharḥ says “that is, before the prayer”.

readings.title_en: Creed in verse and prose
readings.question_en: What is a creed made of, and how do I read a line of verse?
readings.question_ar: مِمَّ تَتَأَلَّفُ الْعَقِيدَةُ؟ وَكَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ بَيْتًا مِنَ الشِّعْرِ؟

passages.intro_en: A creed in verse: the first six lines of ʿAqīdat al-ʿAwāmm. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Marzūqī, ʿAqīdat al-ʿAwāmm, "Matn ʿAqīdat al-ʿAwāmm", Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih Sufi library, id 98910, 5 pp, digital, unvowelled; no publisher or year), p. 2 of the copy; consonants checked letter by letter (verse 3 of the source, which the copy misprints, is left out); vowelled for learners; the pause spellings ـْ (وَحَيّْ، شَيّْ، بَصَرْ، اسْتَمَرّْ) are as in the recitation; in line 4 حَيَاةٌ keeps its tanwīn before الْعِلْمُ, recited ḥayātuni-l-ʿilmu (the tanwīn takes a kasra to meet the hamzat al-waṣl). Lines 1-6.

lines.ar: أَبْدَأُ بِسْمِ اللهِ وَالرَّحْمَنِ * وَبِالرَّحِيمِ دَائِمِ الْإِحْسَانِ
lines.en: I begin with the name of God, the Merciful, and with the Compassionate, constant in kindness.

lines.ar: فَاللهُ مَوْجُودٌ قَدِيمٌ بَاقِي * مُخَالِفٌ لِلْخَلْقِ بِالْإِطْلَاقِ
lines.en: God exists, is without beginning, remains, and differs from creation in every way.

lines.ar: وَقَائِمٌ غَنِيٌّ وَوَاحِدٌ وَحَيّْ * قَادِرٌ مُرِيدٌ عَالِمٌ بِكُلِّ شَيّْ
lines.en: He stands by Himself, is self-sufficient, One and Living, Able, Willing, Knowing everything.

lines.ar: فَقُدْرَةٌ إِرَادَةٌ سَمْعٌ بَصَرْ * حَيَاةٌ الْعِلْمُ كَلَامٌ اسْتَمَرّْ
lines.en: Power, will, hearing, sight, life, knowledge, speech: they continue.

lines.ar: وَجَائِزٌ بِفَضْلِهِ وَعَدْلِهِ * تَرْكٌ لِكُلِّ مُمْكِنٍ كَفِعْلِهِ
lines.en: And it is permissible for Him, by His favour and justice, to leave any possible thing as to do it.

lines.ar: وَالْمُسْتَحِيلُ ضِدُّ كُلِّ وَاجِبِ * فَاحْفَظْ لِخَمْسِينَ بِحُكْمٍ وَاجِبِ
lines.en: And the impossible is the opposite of each obligatory attribute: so memorise fifty by an obligatory ruling.

passages.ar: أَبْدَأُ بِسْمِ اللهِ وَالرَّحْمَنِ * وَبِالرَّحِيمِ دَائِمِ الْإِحْسَانِ فَاللهُ مَوْجُودٌ قَدِيمٌ بَاقِي * مُخَالِفٌ لِلْخَلْقِ بِالْإِطْلَاقِ وَقَائِمٌ غَنِيٌّ وَوَاحِدٌ وَحَيّْ * قَادِرٌ مُرِيدٌ عَالِمٌ بِكُلِّ شَيّْ فَقُدْرَةٌ إِرَادَةٌ سَمْعٌ بَصَرْ * حَيَاةٌ الْعِلْمُ كَلَامٌ اسْتَمَرّْ وَجَائِزٌ بِفَضْلِهِ وَعَدْلِهِ * تَرْكٌ لِكُلِّ مُمْكِنٍ كَفِعْلِهِ وَالْمُسْتَحِيلُ ضِدُّ كُلِّ وَاجِبِ * فَاحْفَظْ لِخَمْسِينَ بِحُكْمٍ وَاجِبِ
passages.en: I begin with the name of God, the Merciful, and with the Compassionate, constant in kindness. God exists, is without beginning, remains, and differs from creation in every way. He stands by Himself, is self-sufficient, One and Living, Able, Willing, Knowing everything. Power, will, hearing, sight, life, knowledge, speech: they continue. And it is permissible for Him, by His favour and justice, to leave any possible thing as to do it. And the impossible is the opposite of each obligatory attribute: so memorise fifty by an obligatory ruling.

passages.intro_en: A creed in prose: the opening of a short book on tawḥīd. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Durūs al-Tawḥīd of al-Ḥabīb Muḥammad b. Sālim b. Ḥafīẓ
passages.cite: Muḥammad b. Sālim b. Ḥafīẓ, Matn Durūs al-Tawḥīd (small typeset booklet; publisher and year not stated on the copy; TLNOOR PDF id 1055, 30 pp), printed p. 8, read against the page image; the printed page is partly vowelled and the rest is vowelled for learners. Lines 7-10 only (four lines).

lines.ar: عِلْمُ التَّوْحِيدِ: هُوَ عِلْمٌ يُعْرَفُ بِهِ إِثْبَاتُ الْعَقَائِدِ الدِّينِيَّةِ بِالْأَدِلَّةِ الْيَقِينِيَّةِ
lines.en: The science of tawḥīd: a science by which religious beliefs are established with certain proofs.

lines.ar: «الْوَاجِبُ» وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ عَدَمُهُ،
lines.en: "The obligatory": that whose non-existence cannot be conceived by the mind;

lines.ar: «الْمُسْتَحِيلُ» وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ،
lines.en: "the impossible": that whose existence cannot be conceived by the mind;

lines.ar: «الْجَائِزُ» هُوَ الَّذِي يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ وَعَدَمُهُ.
lines.en: "the possible": that whose existence and non-existence can both be conceived by the mind.

passages.ar: عِلْمُ التَّوْحِيدِ: هُوَ عِلْمٌ يُعْرَفُ بِهِ إِثْبَاتُ الْعَقَائِدِ الدِّينِيَّةِ بِالْأَدِلَّةِ الْيَقِينِيَّةِ «الْوَاجِبُ» وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ عَدَمُهُ، «الْمُسْتَحِيلُ» وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ، «الْجَائِزُ» هُوَ الَّذِي يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ وَعَدَمُهُ.
passages.en: The science of tawḥīd: a science by which religious beliefs are established with certain proofs. "The obligatory": that whose non-existence cannot be conceived by the mind; "the impossible": that whose existence cannot be conceived by the mind; "the possible": that whose existence and non-existence can both be conceived by the mind.

passages.intro_en: A short text: the evening in the majlis. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَتْ أُخْتِي مَرْيَمُ مَعَ أُمِّنَا فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
lines.en: In the evening my sister Maryam sat with our mother in the majlis.

lines.ar: وَجَلَسْتُ أَنَا مَعَ عُمَرَ قُرْبَ الْبَابِ.
lines.en: And I sat with Umar near the door.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِمَرْيَمَ: هَلْ حَفِظْتِ الْعَقِيدَةَ؟
lines.en: The Habib said to Maryam: Have you memorised the creed?

lines.ar: قَالَتْ مَرْيَمُ: نَعَمْ، حَفِظْتُهَا.
lines.en: Maryam said: Yes, I have memorised it.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ فَتَحَتْ كِتَابَهَا وَقَرَأَتْ بَيْتًا بَعْدَ بَيْتٍ، وَالنَّاسُ جَالِسُونَ يَسْمَعُونَ.
lines.en: Then she opened her book and read verse after verse, while the people sat listening.

lines.ar: وَكَانَ فِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ نِصْفَانِ، وَفِي آخِرِ النِّصْفَيْنِ قَافِيَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ.
lines.en: And every verse had two halves, and at the end of the two halves one rhyme.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: فِي هَذِهِ الْعَقِيدَةِ صِفَاتُ اللَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ.
lines.en: The Habib said: In this creed are the attributes of God, and God is all-hearing, all-seeing.

lines.ar: وَسَأَلَ: مَا الْوَاجِبُ؟
lines.en: And he asked: What is the obligatory?

lines.ar: وَمَا الْمُسْتَحِيلُ؟
lines.en: What is the impossible?

lines.ar: وَمَا الْجَائِزُ؟
lines.en: What is the possible?

lines.ar: قَالَتْ مَرْيَمُ: اثْنَانِ وَاثْنَانِ أَرْبَعَةٌ، وَهَذَا وَاجِبٌ.
lines.en: Maryam said: Two and two are four, and this is obligatory.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ دَعَا الْحَبِيبُ لِمَرْيَمَ وَلِأُمِّهَا، وَرَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.
lines.en: Then the Habib prayed for Maryam and her mother, and we returned to the house, and praise be to God.

passages.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَتْ أُخْتِي مَرْيَمُ مَعَ أُمِّنَا فِي الْمَجْلِسِ. وَجَلَسْتُ أَنَا مَعَ عُمَرَ قُرْبَ الْبَابِ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِمَرْيَمَ: هَلْ حَفِظْتِ الْعَقِيدَةَ؟ قَالَتْ مَرْيَمُ: نَعَمْ، حَفِظْتُهَا. ثُمَّ فَتَحَتْ كِتَابَهَا وَقَرَأَتْ بَيْتًا بَعْدَ بَيْتٍ، وَالنَّاسُ جَالِسُونَ يَسْمَعُونَ. وَكَانَ فِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ نِصْفَانِ، وَفِي آخِرِ النِّصْفَيْنِ قَافِيَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: فِي هَذِهِ الْعَقِيدَةِ صِفَاتُ اللَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ. وَسَأَلَ: مَا الْوَاجِبُ؟ وَمَا الْمُسْتَحِيلُ؟ وَمَا الْجَائِزُ؟ قَالَتْ مَرْيَمُ: اثْنَانِ وَاثْنَانِ أَرْبَعَةٌ، وَهَذَا وَاجِبٌ. ثُمَّ دَعَا الْحَبِيبُ لِمَرْيَمَ وَلِأُمِّهَا، وَرَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.
passages.en: In the evening my sister Maryam sat with our mother in the majlis. And I sat with Umar near the door. The Habib said to Maryam: Have you memorised the creed? Maryam said: Yes, I have memorised it. Then she opened her book and read verse after verse, while the people sat listening. And every verse had two halves, and at the end of the two halves one rhyme. The Habib said: In this creed are the attributes of God, and God is all-hearing, all-seeing. And he asked: What is the obligatory? What is the impossible? What is the possible? Maryam said: Two and two are four, and this is obligatory. Then the Habib prayed for Maryam and her mother, and we returned to the house, and praise be to God.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 138-139 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ.
lines.en: Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her.

lines.ar: قَالَتْ: اللَّهُ مَوْجُودٌ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ.
lines.en: She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

passages.ar: قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ. قَالَتْ: اللَّهُ مَوْجُودٌ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ.
passages.en: Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her. She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

questions.q: Which text type is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A creed in verse (عَقِيدَةٌ): every line is a bayt in two halves with a * between them, the ends of the halves rhyme, and the lines list what is due to God.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: I begin with the name of God, the Merciful, and with the Compassionate, constant in kindness.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: God exists, is without beginning, remains, and differs from creation in every way.

questions.q: Translate line 6.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ السَّادِسَ.
questions.a: And the impossible is the opposite of each obligatory attribute: so memorise fifty by an obligatory ruling.

questions.q: Line 1: do the two halves rhyme? Which sound do the ends share?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: هَلْ يَتَّفِقُ آخِرُ النِّصْفَيْنِ؟ أَيُّ صَوْتٍ يَشْتَرِكَانِ فِيهِ؟
questions.a: Yes: both end in ـانِ.

questions.q: Line 1: which two names of God are in the line, and in which half is each?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: أَيُّ اسْمَيْنِ لِلَّهِ فِي الْبَيْتِ؟ وَفِي أَيِّ نِصْفٍ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا؟
questions.a: The Merciful (الرَّحْمَنِ), in the first half; and the Compassionate (الرَّحِيمِ), which begins the second half.

questions.q: Line 2: name three of the attributes that are listed.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: اُذْكُرْ ثَلَاثَ صِفَاتٍ.
questions.a: Any three of: مَوْجُودٌ (exists), قَدِيمٌ (without beginning), بَاقِي (remains), مُخَالِفٌ لِلْخَلْقِ (differs from creation).

questions.q: Line 3: this word has a pause form. What is its full form, and what dropped?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: لِهَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ صُورَةُ وَقْفٍ. مَا صُورَتُهَا الْكَامِلَةُ؟ وَمَاذَا سَقَطَ؟
questions.a: حَيٌّ: the tanwīn dropped and the shadda stayed.

questions.q: Line 3: which two words end the two halves? Do they rhyme?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تُنْهِيَانِ النِّصْفَيْنِ؟ هَلْ تَتَّفِقَانِ؟
questions.a: وَحَيّْ and شَيّْ: yes, both end in ـيّْ.

questions.q: Line 4: how many attributes are listed? Name them in English.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: كَمْ صِفَةً؟ اُذْكُرْهَا بِالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةِ.
questions.a: Seven: power, will, hearing, sight, life, knowledge and speech.

questions.q: Line 4: the two ends of this line are pause forms. Write their full forms.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: نِهَايَتَا هَذَا الْبَيْتِ صُورَتَا وَقْفٍ. اُكْتُبْ صُورَتَيْهِمَا الْكَامِلَتَيْنِ.
questions.a: بَصَرٌ and اسْتَمَرَّ.

questions.q: Line 5: true or false: the line says it is obligatory for God to leave every possible thing.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٥: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ الْبَيْتُ إِنَّ تَرْكَ كُلِّ مُمْكِنٍ وَاجِبٌ.
questions.a: False. It says it is جَائِزٌ (permissible) for Him to leave any possible thing, as it is to do it.

questions.q: Line 6: what is the مُسْتَحِيلٌ?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٦: مَا الْمُسْتَحِيلُ؟
questions.a: The opposite of every obligatory attribute.

questions.q: Read the vowels: what case ending does each word have (ـُ، ـَ، ـِ، ـٌ)? Say which.
questions.q_ar: اِقْرَأِ الْحَرَكَاتِ: مَا حَرَكَةُ آخِرِ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ؟
questions.a: مَوْجُودٌ: ـٌ (nominative, indefinite). لِلْخَلْقِ: ـِ (after لِـ). ضِدُّ: ـُ (nominative).

questions.q: The poem puts the attributes in verse. Why would a teacher want beginners to memorise a creed in verse?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يُرِيدُ الْمُعَلِّمُ أَنْ يَحْفَظَ الْمُبْتَدِئُونَ الْعَقِيدَةَ بِالشِّعْرِ؟
questions.a: Verse is easy to memorise and to recite together, so the whole class learns it by heart and carries it with them.

questions.q: Line 6 ends with the number fifty. Why might a teacher give the number after the list?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَذْكُرُ الْمُعَلِّمُ الْعَدَدَ بَعْدَ الْقَائِمَةِ؟
questions.a: So the student can check that he knows them all: a counted list is easier to hold and to test.

questions.q: Which text type is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A creed in prose: it defines terms one by one, each in quotation marks followed by وَهُوَ الَّذِي, and it has no rhyme.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: The science of tawḥīd: a science by which religious beliefs are established with certain proofs.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: “The obligatory”: that whose non-existence cannot be conceived by the mind.

questions.q: Line 1: what is being defined?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَا الَّذِي يُعَرَّفُ؟
questions.a: The science of tawḥīd (عِلْمُ التَّوْحِيدِ).

questions.q: Why is الْوَاجِبُ written between « » in line 2?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا كُتِبَ «الْوَاجِبُ» بَيْنَ « »؟
questions.a: The marks show that it is the word being defined.

questions.q: In line 2, which word goes back to «الْوَاجِبُ»? Which ending shows it?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَرْجِعُ إِلَى «الْوَاجِبِ»؟ وَأَيُّ نِهَايَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: The ending ـهُ in عَدَمُهُ: it means “its non-existence”.
questions.ref_ar: الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ عَدَمُهُ

questions.q: Line 3: what is the مُسْتَحِيلٌ? Say it in your own words.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَا الْمُسْتَحِيلُ؟ قُلْهُ بِكَلِمَاتِكَ.
questions.a: Something whose existence the mind cannot conceive.

questions.q: Line 4: what is the جَائِزٌ?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: مَا الْجَائِزُ؟
questions.a: Something whose existence and non-existence the mind can both conceive.

questions.q: Which of these two words is “its existence”, and which is “its non-existence”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الْكَلِمَتَيْنِ «وُجُودُهُ»؟ وَأَيُّهُمَا «عَدَمُهُ»؟
questions.a: وُجُودُهُ is its existence; عَدَمُهُ is its non-existence.

questions.q: Which of the three terms (lines 2–4) cannot be conceived as existing?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الْمُصْطَلَحَاتِ الثَّلَاثَةِ لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ وُجُودُهُ؟
questions.a: الْمُسْتَحِيلُ (line 3).

questions.q: True or false: the jāʾiz is the same as the wājib.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: الْجَائِزُ هُوَ الْوَاجِبُ.
questions.a: False. The wājib cannot be conceived as non-existent; the jāʾiz can be conceived both ways.

questions.q: What does هُوَ الَّذِي do in lines 2–4?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «هُوَ الَّذِي» فِي السُّطُورِ ٢–٤؟
questions.a: It begins the definition: “it is that which …”.

questions.q: Each definition says “in the mind” (فِي الْعَقْلِ). What kind of knowledge is a definition like this: seen, heard or reasoned?
questions.q_ar: هَذِهِ التَّعْرِيفَاتُ تَقُولُ «فِي الْعَقْلِ». مَا نَوْعُ هَذِهِ الْمَعْرِفَةِ؟
questions.a: Reasoned: the mind decides it without going to look.

questions.q: Why does a book on tawḥīd begin by defining three terms, before it says anything about God?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَبْدَأُ كِتَابُ التَّوْحِيدِ بِتَعْرِيفِ ثَلَاثِ كَلِمَاتٍ؟
questions.a: The three terms are the tools of the whole science: everything later is sorted with them.

questions.q: Where did Maryam sit, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَتْ مَرْيَمُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the majlis, with her mother.

questions.q: Where did the writer sit?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ الْكَاتِبُ؟
questions.a: Near the door, with Umar.

questions.q: What did the Habib ask Maryam?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ مَرْيَمَ؟
questions.a: Whether she had memorised the creed.

questions.q: What does the ending ـهَا stand for?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ ـهَا؟
questions.a: The creed (الْعَقِيدَةَ).

questions.q: Translate line 5.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْخَامِسَ.
questions.a: Then she opened her book and read verse after verse, while the people sat listening.

questions.q: What did every verse have? (line 6)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَانَ فِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ؟
questions.a: Two halves, and one rhyme at the end of the two halves.

questions.q: What does the Habib say is in this creed?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْعَقِيدَةِ؟
questions.a: The attributes of God (صِفَاتُ اللَّهِ).

questions.q: What three questions did he ask? (line 8)
questions.q_ar: مَا الْأَسْئِلَةُ الثَّلَاثَةُ؟
questions.a: What is the obligatory, the impossible and the possible.

questions.q: True or false: Maryam’s example is an example of the impossible.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: مِثَالُ مَرْيَمَ عَلَى الْمُسْتَحِيلِ.
questions.a: False. She gave it as an example of the obligatory (وَاجِبٌ).

questions.q: Who prayed for whom at the end?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ دَعَا لِمَنْ فِي آخِرِ النَّصِّ؟
questions.a: The Habib prayed for Maryam and her mother.

questions.q: Who is “I” in line 2? Which ending shows it?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ «أَنَا» فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟ أَيُّ نِهَايَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: The writer (Ahmad): the ending ـتُ means “I”. He sat with Umar near the door.

questions.q: The text never says that Maryam was told to recite. What does it show about the girls and women in the majlis?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُظْهِرُ النَّصُّ عَنِ الْبَنَاتِ وَالنِّسَاءِ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ؟
questions.a: They memorise and recite before the Habib, and he asks them questions like any student.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her. She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

questions.q: Which three words in the second new line are attributes (صِفَات) of Allah?
questions.a: مَوْجُودٌ (existing), سَمِيعٌ (all-hearing), بَصِيرٌ (all-seeing)

questions.q: Why is the verb قَرَأَتْ feminine?
questions.a: Its doer, مَرْيَمُ, is feminine.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: Maryam read a small creed.
questions.a: قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً.

translate.en: The creed has the attributes of God in it.

translate.ar: اللَّهُ مَوْجُودٌ وَاحِدٌ، وَهُوَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ.
translate.en: God exists, is One, and is all-hearing and all-seeing.
The obligatory is never impossible.
Maryam memorised the first verse and the second.

translate.ar: فِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ نِصْفَانِ، وَآخِرُ النِّصْفَيْنِ قَافِيَةٌ.
translate.en: In every verse there are two halves, and the end of the two halves is a rhyme.

translate.ar: يَجِبُ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَعْلَمَ مَا يَجِبُ لِلَّهِ.
translate.en: Every Muslim must know what is due to God.

translate.ar: جَلَسْنَا فِي الْمَجْلِسِ وَسَمِعْنَا مَرْيَمَ تَقْرَأُ الْعَقِيدَةَ.
translate.en: We sat in the majlis and heard Maryam reading the creed.

translate.ar: أَنْ يَذْهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى السُّوقِ جَائِزٌ، وَأَنْ يَكُونَ فِي بَيْتَيْنِ فِي وَقْتٍ وَاحِدٍ مُسْتَحِيلٌ.
translate.en: That Ahmad goes to the market is possible, and that he is in two houses at one time is impossible.

translate.ar: سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ الطُّلَّابَ عَنِ الْوَاجِبِ وَالْمُسْتَحِيلِ وَالْجَائِزِ.
translate.en: The Habib asked the students about the obligatory, the impossible and the possible.

translate.source: Durūs al-Tawḥīd of al-Ḥabīb Muḥammad b. Sālim b. Ḥafīẓ

lines.ar: «الْمُسْتَحِيلُ» وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ،
lines.en: "the impossible": that whose existence cannot be conceived by the mind;

lines.ar: «الْجَائِزُ» هُوَ الَّذِي يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ وَعَدَمُهُ.
lines.en: "the possible": that whose existence and non-existence can both be conceived by the mind.

translate.ar: «الْمُسْتَحِيلُ» وَهُوَ الَّذِي لَا يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ، «الْجَائِزُ» هُوَ الَّذِي يُتَصَوَّرُ فِي الْعَقْلِ وُجُودُهُ وَعَدَمُهُ.
translate.en: "the impossible": that whose existence cannot be conceived by the mind; "the possible": that whose existence and non-existence can both be conceived by the mind.
God is all-hearing and all-seeing.
Two and two are four: this is obligatory.
It is impossible that two and two are five.
translate.ar: مِنَ الْمُسْتَحِيلِ أَنْ يَكُونَ اثْنَانِ وَاثْنَانِ خَمْسَةً.

translate.en: Maryam memorised the creed in the majlis.
It is possible that Ahmad goes to the market.
translate.ar: أَنْ يَذْهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى السُّوقِ جَائِزٌ.
alt: جَائِزٌ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى السُّوقِ.

translate.en: The attributes of God are in the creed.
Every verse has two halves, and the two halves have one rhyme.
translate.ar: لِكُلِّ بَيْتٍ نِصْفَانِ، وَلِلنِّصْفَيْنِ قَافِيَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ.
alt: فِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ نِصْفَانِ وَقَافِيَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ.

translate.en: Every Muslim must know what is due to God.
translate.ar: يَجِبُ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَعْلَمَ مَا يَجِبُ لِلَّهِ.

translate.en: The Habib asked: What is the obligatory?

readings.title_en: Counsel: the four frames
readings.question_en: How does a teacher’s counsel speak, and what do its four little frames say?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ يَتَكَلَّمُ الْمُعَلِّمُ فِي النَّصِيحَةِ؟ وَمَاذَا تَقُولُ عِبَارَاتُهَا الْأَرْبَعُ؟

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا
lines.en: Hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَبِالْوَفَاءِ بِمَا عَاهَدْتَ عَلَيْهِ وَوَعَدْتَ بِهِ
lines.en: Hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping what you have promised and pledged,

lines.ar: فَإِنَّ نَقْضَ الْعُهُودِ وَالْخُلْفَ فِي الْوُعُودِ مِنْ أَمَارَاتِ النِّفَاقِ
lines.en: for breaking pledges and failing promises are among the signs of hypocrisy.

passages.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا وَعَلَيْكَ بِصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَبِالْوَفَاءِ بِمَا عَاهَدْتَ عَلَيْهِ وَوَعَدْتَ بِهِ فَإِنَّ نَقْضَ الْعُهُودِ وَالْخُلْفَ فِي الْوُعُودِ مِنْ أَمَارَاتِ النِّفَاقِ
passages.en: Hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it. Hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping what you have promised and pledged, for breaking pledges and failing promises are among the signs of hypocrisy.

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِتَرْكِ الْمُزَاحِ رَأْسًا فَإِنْ مَزَحْتَ نَادِرًا عَلَى نِيَّةِ تَطْيِيبِ قَلْبِ مُسْلِمٍ فَلَا تَقُلْ إِلَّا حَقًّا
lines.en: Hold fast to giving up joking altogether; and if you do joke, rarely, intending to cheer a Muslim's heart, say nothing but the truth.

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِإِجْلَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَتَوْقِيرِهِمْ لَا سِيَّمَا أَهْلَ الْفَضْلِ مِنْهُمْ كَالْعُلَمَاءِ وَالصُّلَحَاءِ
lines.en: Hold fast to honouring and respecting the Muslims, above all the people of merit among them, such as the scholars and the righteous.

lines.ar: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّكَ لَوْ جِئْتَ عَلَى رَأْسِكَ مِنْ أَقْصَى بِلَادِ الْإِسْلَامِ لِزِيَارَتِهِ ﷺ لَمْ تَقُمْ بِشُكْرِ نِعْمَةِ الْهِدَايَةِ الَّتِي أَوْصَلَهَا اللهُ إِلَيْكَ عَلَى يَدِهِ
lines.en: And know that if you came on your head from the farthest land of Islam to visit him ﷺ, you would not have fulfilled thanks for the blessing of guidance that God brought you through his hand.

passages.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِتَرْكِ الْمُزَاحِ رَأْسًا فَإِنْ مَزَحْتَ نَادِرًا عَلَى نِيَّةِ تَطْيِيبِ قَلْبِ مُسْلِمٍ فَلَا تَقُلْ إِلَّا حَقًّا وَعَلَيْكَ بِإِجْلَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَتَوْقِيرِهِمْ لَا سِيَّمَا أَهْلَ الْفَضْلِ مِنْهُمْ كَالْعُلَمَاءِ وَالصُّلَحَاءِ وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّكَ لَوْ جِئْتَ عَلَى رَأْسِكَ مِنْ أَقْصَى بِلَادِ الْإِسْلَامِ لِزِيَارَتِهِ ﷺ لَمْ تَقُمْ بِشُكْرِ نِعْمَةِ الْهِدَايَةِ الَّتِي أَوْصَلَهَا اللهُ إِلَيْكَ عَلَى يَدِهِ
passages.en: Hold fast to giving up joking altogether; and if you do joke, rarely, intending to cheer a Muslim's heart, say nothing but the truth. Hold fast to honouring and respecting the Muslims, above all the people of merit among them, such as the scholars and the righteous. And know that if you came on your head from the farthest land of Islam to visit him ﷺ, you would not have fulfilled thanks for the blessing of guidance that God brought you through his hand.

passages.intro_en: A short text: his father’s counsel before the journey. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: قَالَ الْأَبُ لِأَحْمَدَ قَبْلَ السَّفَرِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِالْأَمَانَةِ.
lines.en: The father said to Ahmad before the journey: My son, hold fast to trust.

lines.ar: وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْعَمَلِ.
lines.en: And beware of betrayal in money and in work.

lines.ar: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَكَ فِي كُلِّ مَكَانٍ.
lines.en: And know that God is with you in every place.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ أَعْطَاهُ كِتَابًا وَقَالَ: خُذْ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ إِلَى صَدِيقِي فِي تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: Then he gave him a book and said: Take this book to my friend in Tarim.

lines.ar: الْكِتَابُ أَمَانَةٌ عِنْدَكَ، فَلَا تَفْتَحْهُ.
lines.en: The book is a trust with you, so do not open it.

lines.ar: سَافَرَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فَوَصَلَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: Ahmad travelled with Umar, and he arrived in Tarim.

lines.ar: فَدَخَلَ بَيْتَ صَدِيقِ أَبِيهِ وَأَعْطَاهُ الْكِتَابَ.
lines.en: He entered the house of his father’s friend and gave him the book.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَصَلَتِ الْأَمَانَةُ.
lines.en: The man said: Praise be to God, the trust has arrived.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ فِي قَلْبِهِ: نِعْمَ الْأَبُ أَبِي.
lines.en: And Ahmad said in his heart: What an excellent father is mine.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَبِيهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ: وَصَلَتِ الْأَمَانَةُ يَا أَبِي.
lines.en: Then he returned to his father and said to him: The trust has arrived, Father.

passages.ar: قَالَ الْأَبُ لِأَحْمَدَ قَبْلَ السَّفَرِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِالْأَمَانَةِ. وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْعَمَلِ. وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَكَ فِي كُلِّ مَكَانٍ. ثُمَّ أَعْطَاهُ كِتَابًا وَقَالَ: خُذْ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ إِلَى صَدِيقِي فِي تَرِيمَ. الْكِتَابُ أَمَانَةٌ عِنْدَكَ، فَلَا تَفْتَحْهُ. سَافَرَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فَوَصَلَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ. فَدَخَلَ بَيْتَ صَدِيقِ أَبِيهِ وَأَعْطَاهُ الْكِتَابَ. فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَصَلَتِ الْأَمَانَةُ. وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ فِي قَلْبِهِ: نِعْمَ الْأَبُ أَبِي. ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَبِيهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ: وَصَلَتِ الْأَمَانَةُ يَا أَبِي.
passages.en: The father said to Ahmad before the journey: My son, hold fast to trust. And beware of betrayal in money and in work. And know that God is with you in every place. Then he gave him a book and said: Take this book to my friend in Tarim. The book is a trust with you, so do not open it. Ahmad travelled with Umar, and he arrived in Tarim. He entered the house of his father’s friend and gave him the book. The man said: Praise be to God, the trust has arrived. And Ahmad said in his heart: What an excellent father is mine. Then he returned to his father and said to him: The trust has arrived, Father.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 140-141 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا.
lines.en: The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَبِالْوَفَاءِ بِالْوَعْدِ.
lines.en: And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.

passages.ar: قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا. وَعَلَيْكَ بِصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ وَبِالْوَفَاءِ بِالْوَعْدِ.
passages.en: The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it. And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.

questions.q: Which text type is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: Counsel: the writer speaks to “you”, tells you what to hold fast to (عَلَيْكَ بِـ) and what to beware of (إِيَّاكَ وَ), and gives a reason with فَإِنَّ.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: Hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping what you have promised and pledged,

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: for breaking pledges and failing promises are among the signs of hypocrisy.

questions.q: Which word means “trust” and which means “betrayal”?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى «الْأَمَانَةِ»؟ وَمَا مَعْنَى «الْخِيَانَةَ»؟
questions.a: الْأَمَانَةِ is trust; الْخِيَانَةَ is betrayal.

questions.q: Line 1: which two frames begin the two parts? What does each ask?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: أَيُّ عِبَارَتَيْنِ تَبْدَآنِ الْجُزْأَيْنِ؟ مَاذَا تَطْلُبُ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا؟
questions.a: عَلَيْكَ: hold fast to (do it). إِيَّاكَ: beware of (keep away).

questions.q: Line 1: what does the ending ـهَا stand for?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ ـهَا؟
questions.a: The trust (الْأَمَانَةِ).

questions.q: Line 2: which little word follows عَلَيْكَ? Find it twice.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ بَعْدَ «عَلَيْكَ»؟ جِدْهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ.
questions.a: بِـ: in بِصِدْقِ and in وَبِالْوَفَاءِ.

questions.q: Line 2: what two things must you hold fast to?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: بِمَاذَا تَلْزَمُ؟ اُذْكُرْ شَيْئَيْنِ.
questions.a: Truthful speech, and keeping what you have promised and pledged.

questions.q: Line 3: which word begins the reason? What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَبْدَأُ السَّبَبَ؟ مَاذَا تَعْنِي؟
questions.a: فَإِنَّ: “for, because”.

questions.q: True or false: line 3 says that keeping promises is a sign of hypocrisy.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ السَّطْرُ ٣ إِنَّ الْوَفَاءَ بِالْوَعْدِ مِنْ أَمَارَاتِ النِّفَاقِ.
questions.a: False. It says that breaking pledges and failing promises are signs of hypocrisy.

questions.q: Read the vowels: what case ending does each word have, and why?
questions.q_ar: اِقْرَأِ الْحَرَكَاتِ: مَا نِهَايَةُ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: الْأَمَانَةِ: ـِ (second word of a possessive phrase). الْخِيَانَةَ: ـَ (after إِيَّاكَ وَ). نَقْضَ: ـَ (after فَإِنَّ).

questions.q: Line 3 calls broken promises “signs of hypocrisy”. Why would a teacher use so strong a word for a small failing?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَسْتَعْمِلُ الْمُعَلِّمُ كَلِمَةً قَوِيَّةً كَهَذِهِ؟
questions.a: A promise is made with the tongue and kept by the heart. Failing it shows that the words and the heart did not agree: that is what the word means.

questions.q: Each “hold fast to” is followed by a “beware of”, or by a reason. What does that show about how the writer teaches?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَدُلُّ تَرْتِيبُ الْعِبَارَاتِ عَلَى طَرِيقَةِ الْكَاتِبِ فِي التَّعْلِيمِ؟
questions.a: He does not only command: he names the danger beside the good thing and gives the reason, so the reader understands and agrees.

questions.q: Which text type is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: Counsel again: عَلَيْكَ بِـ in lines 1 and 2, and وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ in line 3.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Hold fast to giving up joking altogether; and if you do joke, rarely, intending to cheer a Muslim’s heart, say nothing but the truth.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: Hold fast to honouring and respecting the Muslims, above all the people of merit among them, such as the scholars and the righteous.

questions.q: Line 1: which word means “joking” and which means “rarely”?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «الْمُزَاحَ»؟ وَأَيُّهَا «قَلِيلًا»؟
questions.a: الْمُزَاحِ is joking; نَادِرًا is rarely.

questions.q: Line 1: what does إِلَّا do here?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «إِلَّا» هُنَا؟
questions.a: It makes an exception: say nothing except the truth (حَقًّا). Even in a joke, say only what is true.

questions.q: Line 1: which word opens the “if”, and which word opens the answer?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَفْتَحُ الشَّرْطَ؟ وَأَيُّهَا تَفْتَحُ الْجَوَابَ؟
questions.a: فَإِنْ opens the “if”; فَلَا opens the answer, a prohibition.

questions.q: Line 2: whom must you honour, and above all whom?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَنْ تُجِلُّ؟ وَمَنْ تُجِلُّ خَاصَّةً؟
questions.a: The Muslims; above all the people of merit among them, such as the scholars and the righteous.

questions.q: Line 2: what does the كَـ at the front mean?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَاذَا تَعْنِي الْكَافُ فِي أَوَّلِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟
questions.a: “such as”: it gives examples (the scholars and the righteous).

questions.q: Line 3: what does the word that begins the line tell you?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَاذَا تَقُولُ الْكَلِمَةُ الَّتِي تَبْدَأُ بِهَا السَّطْرُ؟
questions.a: “And know”: an important statement follows.

questions.q: Line 3: what does the writer say you would not have fulfilled, even if you came from the farthest land?
