questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَا الَّذِي لَا تَقُومُ بِهِ وَلَوْ جِئْتَ مِنْ أَقْصَى الْبِلَادِ؟
questions.a: Thanks for the blessing of guidance.

questions.q: Line 3: who is “him” (ـهِ)?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَنْ «هُوَ» فِي «لِزِيَارَتِهِ»؟
questions.a: The Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: Line 3: what does لَمْ do to the verb here?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «لَمْ» بِالْفِعْلِ؟
questions.a: لَمْ makes it a negative of the past: “you would not have fulfilled”; the verb shortens to تَقُمْ.

questions.q: Line 3 says that even a journey on one’s head from the farthest land would not repay the blessing of guidance. What is the writer teaching about gratitude?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُعَلِّمُنَا السَّطْرُ ٣ عَنِ الشُّكْرِ؟
questions.a: That the blessing is greater than any effort a person can make; so gratitude is never finished, and one asks God’s help to be grateful.

questions.q: Line 1 gives up joking but allows it in one case. What does the writer teach about the purpose of speech?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُعَلِّمُنَا السَّطْرُ ١ عَنِ الْغَايَةِ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ؟
questions.a: Speech is for the good of the listener, and it must stay true: even a light word should cheer a heart and say nothing false.

questions.q: What did the father say to Ahmad before the journey?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الْأَبُ لِأَحْمَدَ قَبْلَ السَّفَرِ؟
questions.a: Hold fast to trust, and beware of betrayal in money and work, and know that God is with you.

questions.q: Who is the father speaking to? Which word tells you?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يُخَاطِبُ الْأَبُ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: Ahmad, his son: يَا بُنَيَّ, “my little son”.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: And know that God is with you in every place.

questions.q: What did the father give Ahmad, and where was it to go?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا أَعْطَى الْأَبُ أَحْمَدَ؟ وَإِلَى أَيْنَ؟
questions.a: A book, to his friend in Tarim.

questions.q: True or false: Ahmad may open the book on the way.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَجُوزُ لِأَحْمَدَ أَنْ يَفْتَحَ الْكِتَابَ فِي الطَّرِيقِ.
questions.a: False. “So do not open it”: the book is a trust.

questions.q: Which word shows that the trust is with Ahmad, and who is “you”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الْأَمَانَةَ مَعَ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: عِنْدَكَ (ـكَ): “with you”, Ahmad.

questions.q: Who travelled with Ahmad?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَافَرَ مَعَ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: Umar.

questions.q: What did Ahmad do when he arrived?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ حِينَ وَصَلَ؟
questions.a: He entered the house of his father’s friend and gave him the book.

questions.q: What did the man say?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَ الرَّجُلُ؟
questions.a: Praise be to God, the trust has arrived.

questions.q: Which frame of counsel does the father use in line 2? What does it ask?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ عِبَارَةٍ اسْتَعْمَلَهَا الْأَبُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟ مَاذَا تَطْلُبُ؟
questions.a: إِيَّاكَ وَ: “beware of”: keep away from betrayal.

questions.q: Why does the verb end in ـتِ? Who is the doer?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا انْتَهَى الْفِعْلُ بِـ ـتِ؟ مَنِ الْفَاعِلُ؟
questions.a: The doer الْأَمَانَةُ is feminine, so the verb is feminine (وَصَلَتْ; the final ـتِ is the usual vowel before the الـ of الْأَمَانَةُ).

questions.q: The book was never opened and was handed over. What does the story show about “trust”?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تُظْهِرُ الْقِصَّةُ عَنِ الْأَمَانَةِ؟
questions.a: Trust is kept in small things too: carrying a thing safely and handing it over as it was.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it. And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.

questions.q: What does وَعَلَيْكَ بِـ mean?
questions.a: “Hold fast to …” (a command to keep something).

questions.q: What does وَإِيَّاكَ mean?
questions.a: “Beware of …” (keep away from it).

questions.q: Write in Arabic: Beware of betrayal.
questions.a: إِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ.

translate.en: Hold fast to trust, for it is a blessing.
Beware of betrayal in money.

translate.ar: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الصِّدْقَ خَيْرٌ وَأَنَّ النِّفَاقَ شَرٌّ.
translate.en: And know that truthfulness is good and that hypocrisy is evil.
Hold fast to keeping your promises, students.

translate.ar: قَالَ الْأَبُ لِوَلَدِهِ: إِيَّاكَ وَنَقْضَ الْوَعْدِ.
translate.en: The father said to his son: Beware of breaking a promise.
Know that the book is a trust with you.
And beware of breaking a promise, Maryam.
Keeping a promise is a trust, and breaking it is betrayal.
If you promise, hold fast to fulfilling it.

translate.source: Risālat al-Muʿāwana of Imam ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِإِجْلَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَتَوْقِيرِهِمْ لَا سِيَّمَا أَهْلَ الْفَضْلِ مِنْهُمْ كَالْعُلَمَاءِ وَالصُّلَحَاءِ
lines.en: Hold fast to honouring and respecting the Muslims, above all the people of merit among them, such as the scholars and the righteous.

lines.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا
lines.en: Hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.

translate.ar: وَعَلَيْكَ بِإِجْلَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَتَوْقِيرِهِمْ لَا سِيَّمَا أَهْلَ الْفَضْلِ مِنْهُمْ كَالْعُلَمَاءِ وَالصُّلَحَاءِ وَعَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا
translate.en: Hold fast to honouring and respecting the Muslims, above all the people of merit among them, such as the scholars and the righteous. Hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.
Hold fast to trust.
Beware of betrayal.
Hold fast to truthfulness, and beware of hypocrisy.
And know that God is with you.
Hold fast to keeping a promise, for breaking a promise is betrayal.
translate.ar: عَلَيْكَ بِالْوَفَاءِ بِالْوَعْدِ فَإِنَّ نَقْضَ الْوَعْدِ خِيَانَةٌ.

translate.en: (To a woman) Hold fast to patience.
(To several students) Hold fast to knowledge.
Know that knowledge is light, so hold fast to the lesson.
translate.ar: اِعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْعِلْمَ نُورٌ فَعَلَيْكَ بِالدَّرْسِ.

translate.en: My father said: Hold fast to trust, and beware of betrayal in your work.
translate.ar: قَالَ أَبِي: عَلَيْكَ بِالْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِي عَمَلِكَ.

readings.title_en: A page of advice: the long sentence
readings.question_en: How do I read a long sentence, and follow the thread of the argument from line to line?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ جُمْلَةً طَوِيلَةً، وَكَيْفَ أَتَّبِعُ خَيْطَ الْكَلَامِ مِنْ سَطْرٍ إِلَى سَطْرٍ؟

passages.intro_en: Four lines from the same page of advice. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya wa-l-Waṣāyā al-Īmāniyya of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād (chapter on taqwā)
passages.cite: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya wa-l-Waṣāyā al-Īmāniyya, Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, id 184250, 409 pp; no publisher or year on the digital copy), pages 28–29 of the copy (its own pagination); printed edition not identified. The SSD also has PDFs of 102, 432 and 468 pp (one with takhrīj) which were not read. The page has eight lines: line 1 is on slide 7, lines 3-5 on slide 11, and lines 2, 6, 7 and 8 are Exercise A. The Qurʾān verses that follow each «وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ» in the source are left out (abridged). Vowels added by the course (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: وَمَا مِنْ شَرٍّ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ، ظَاهِرٍ وَلَا بَاطِنٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى حِرْزٌ حَرِيزٌ، وَحِصْنٌ حَصِينٌ لِلسَّلَامَةِ مِنْهُ، وَالنَّجَاةِ مِنْ ضَرَرِهِ
lines.en: And there is no evil, present or future, outward or inward, but taqwā is a sure safeguard and a strong fortress for safety from it and escape from its harm.

lines.ar: وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْفُرْقَانُ عِنْدَ الِاشْتِبَاهِ وَوُقُوعِ الْإِشْكَالِ، وَالْكَفَّارَةُ لِلسَّيِّئَاتِ، وَالْمَغْفِرَةُ لِلذُّنُوبِ
lines.en: And of that: discernment at times of confusion and difficulty, the wiping out of bad deeds and the forgiveness of sins.

lines.ar: وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْوَعْدُ بِالْجَنَّةِ
lines.en: And of that: the promise of Paradise.

lines.ar: وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْكَرَامَةُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
lines.en: And of that: honour in this world and the next.

passages.ar: وَمَا مِنْ شَرٍّ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ، ظَاهِرٍ وَلَا بَاطِنٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى حِرْزٌ حَرِيزٌ، وَحِصْنٌ حَصِينٌ لِلسَّلَامَةِ مِنْهُ، وَالنَّجَاةِ مِنْ ضَرَرِهِ وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْفُرْقَانُ عِنْدَ الِاشْتِبَاهِ وَوُقُوعِ الْإِشْكَالِ، وَالْكَفَّارَةُ لِلسَّيِّئَاتِ، وَالْمَغْفِرَةُ لِلذُّنُوبِ وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْوَعْدُ بِالْجَنَّةِ وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْكَرَامَةُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
passages.en: And there is no evil, present or future, outward or inward, but taqwā is a sure safeguard and a strong fortress for safety from it and escape from its harm. And of that: discernment at times of confusion and difficulty, the wiping out of bad deeds and the forgiveness of sins. And of that: the promise of Paradise. And of that: honour in this world and the next.

passages.intro_en: A short text: how to read a long passage. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحَبِيبِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ.
lines.en: Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s majlis after the prayer.

lines.ar: فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ الْكِتَابَ وَقَرَأَ كَلَامًا طَوِيلًا.
lines.en: The Habib opened the book and read a long passage.

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ: يَا حَبِيبُ، الْكَلَامُ طَوِيلٌ، فَكَيْفَ أَفْهَمُهُ؟
lines.en: Umar asked: Habib, the passage is long, so how do I understand it?

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا مِنْ كَلَامٍ طَوِيلٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ مَعْنًى وَاحِدٌ.
lines.en: The Habib said: There is no long passage but there is one meaning in it.

lines.ar: اِبْدَأْ بِالْكَلِمَاتِ الصَّغِيرَةِ، فَهِيَ مِفْتَاحُ الْكَلَامِ.
lines.en: Begin with the little words, for they are the key of the speech.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ اُنْظُرْ إِلَى «وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ»: بَعْدَ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ يَأْتِي شَيْءٌ جَدِيدٌ.
lines.en: Then look at “and of that”: after these words something new comes.

lines.ar: فَقَرَأَ عُمَرُ الْكَلَامَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى وَقَالَ: الْآنَ فَهِمْتُ، يَا حَبِيبُ!
lines.en: So Umar read the passage once more and said: Now I understand, Habib!

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: وَاجْلِسْ بِأَدَبٍ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا.
lines.en: The Habib said: And sit with good manners, outwardly and inwardly.

lines.ar: وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: الصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَهْمِ، وَالْفَهْمُ سَعَادَةٌ.
lines.en: And Ahmad wrote in his book: Patience is the key of understanding, and understanding is happiness.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ وَعُمَرُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدَيْنِ.
lines.en: And Ahmad and Umar went back to the house, happy.

passages.ar: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحَبِيبِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ. فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ الْكِتَابَ وَقَرَأَ كَلَامًا طَوِيلًا. فَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ: يَا حَبِيبُ، الْكَلَامُ طَوِيلٌ، فَكَيْفَ أَفْهَمُهُ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا مِنْ كَلَامٍ طَوِيلٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ مَعْنًى وَاحِدٌ. اِبْدَأْ بِالْكَلِمَاتِ الصَّغِيرَةِ، فَهِيَ مِفْتَاحُ الْكَلَامِ. ثُمَّ اُنْظُرْ إِلَى «وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ»: بَعْدَ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ يَأْتِي شَيْءٌ جَدِيدٌ. فَقَرَأَ عُمَرُ الْكَلَامَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى وَقَالَ: الْآنَ فَهِمْتُ، يَا حَبِيبُ! قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: وَاجْلِسْ بِأَدَبٍ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا. وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: الصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَهْمِ، وَالْفَهْمُ سَعَادَةٌ. وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ وَعُمَرُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدَيْنِ.
passages.en: Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s majlis after the prayer. The Habib opened the book and read a long passage. Umar asked: Habib, the passage is long, so how do I understand it? The Habib said: There is no long passage but there is one meaning in it. Begin with the little words, for they are the key of the speech. Then look at “and of that”: after these words something new comes. So Umar read the passage once more and said: Now I understand, Habib! The Habib said: And sit with good manners, outwardly and inwardly. And Ahmad wrote in his book: Patience is the key of understanding, and understanding is happiness. And Ahmad and Umar went back to the house, happy.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 142-143 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً عَنِ التَّقْوَى.
lines.en: The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness).

lines.ar: وَمَعْنَاهَا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
lines.en: And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً عَنِ التَّقْوَى. وَمَعْنَاهَا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
passages.en: The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness). And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.

questions.q: Translate line 1 (the long sentence).
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ (الْجُمْلَةَ الطَّوِيلَةَ).
questions.a: And there is no evil, present or future, outward or inward, but taqwā is a sure safeguard and a strong fortress for safety from it and escape from its harm.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And of that: discernment at times of confusion and difficulty, the wiping out of bad deeds and the forgiveness of sins.

questions.q: Translate lines 3 and 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَيْنِ الثَّالِثَ وَالرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: And of that: the promise of Paradise. And of that: honour in this world and the next.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A page of counsel (advice) with long sentences, from al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya of Imam ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, the chapter on taqwā.

questions.q: Which two words make the frame of line 1?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَصْنَعَانِ إِطَارَ السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟
questions.a: مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا: “there is no … but …”.

questions.q: Line 1 has two pairs of opposites. What do they mean?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ زَوْجَانِ مِنَ الْأَضْدَادِ. مَا مَعْنَاهُمَا؟
questions.a: Present or future (this life or the next); outward or inward.
questions.ref_ar: عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ، ظَاهِرٍ وَلَا بَاطِنٍ

questions.q: Line 1 gives two pictures of what taqwā is for the evil. Name them.
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ صُورَتَانِ لِلتَّقْوَى. اُذْكُرْهُمَا.
questions.a: A sure safeguard, and a strong fortress.

questions.q: What two things does the fortress give? Find the two nouns.
questions.q_ar: مَا الشَّيْئَانِ اللَّذَانِ يُعْطِيهِمَا الْحِصْنُ؟ جِدِ الِاسْمَيْنِ.
questions.a: Safety (السَّلَامَةُ) from it, and escape (النَّجَاةُ) from its harm.

questions.q: Line 2 lists three things. Which word joins the last two?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْيَاءَ. أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَجْمَعُ الْأَخِيرَيْنِ؟
questions.a: وَ. The three things are discernment, the wiping out of bad deeds, and the forgiveness of sins; وَ comes before the second (وَالْكَفَّارَةُ) and before the third (وَالْمَغْفِرَةُ).

questions.q: Lines 2, 3 and 4 each begin with the same words. Which, and what do they tell the reader?
questions.q_ar: تَبْدَأُ السُّطُورُ ٢ وَ٣ وَ٤ بِالْكَلِمَاتِ نَفْسِهَا. مَا هِيَ؟ وَمَاذَا تَقُولُ لِلْقَارِئِ؟
questions.a: وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ: “and of that”. Each line is one more item of the list of what taqwā brings.

questions.q: Find the word that means “Paradise”.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «Paradise».
questions.a: الْجَنَّةِ.

questions.q: True or false: line 4 speaks only about the Hereafter.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَتَكَلَّمُ السَّطْرُ الرَّابِعُ عَنِ الْآخِرَةِ فَقَطْ.
questions.a: False. “In this world and the next”: honour in both.

questions.q: Read the vowels of line 1. What ending does each of these three words have, and why?
questions.q_ar: اِقْرَأِ الْحَرَكَاتِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ. مَا حَرَكَةُ آخِرِ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ مِنْ هَذِهِ الثَّلَاثِ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: شَرٍّ: ـٍ (after مِنْ). حِرْزٌ: ـٌ (what taqwā is: the statement). السَّلَامَةِ: ـِ (after لِـ).

questions.q: Line 1 says taqwā protects from every evil, and lines 2–4 say what good it brings. Why would the writer put both on one page?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ التَّقْوَى حِفْظٌ مِنَ الشَّرِّ، وَفِي الْبَاقِي هِيَ طَرِيقُ الْخَيْرِ. لِمَاذَا جَمَعَ الْكَاتِبُ بَيْنَهُمَا؟
questions.a: Taqwā works in two directions: it keeps harm away and it brings good. Putting them together shows that one thing does both.

questions.q: Line 1 says “present or future”, and line 4 says “in this world and the next”. What is the same, and what does it do for the page?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ «عَاجِلٌ وَآجِلٌ» وَفِي الرَّابِعِ «الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةُ». مَا الَّذِي يَتَشَابَهُ؟ وَمَاذَا يَفْعَلُ بِالصَّفْحَةِ؟
questions.a: The same pair of worlds, said in two ways. The page ends where it began: with both worlds.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the Habib’s majlis, with Umar.

questions.q: What did the Habib read? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ؟
questions.a: A long passage from the book.

questions.q: Who asks this question, and what is his problem?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَسْأَلُ هَذَا السُّؤَالَ؟ وَمَا مُشْكِلَتُهُ؟
questions.a: Umar. The passage is long, and he does not know how to understand it.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: The Habib said: There is no long passage but there is one meaning in it.

questions.q: Find the two words that make the frame of this sentence.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَتَيْنِ اللَّتَيْنِ تَصْنَعَانِ إِطَارَ الْجُمْلَةِ.
questions.a: مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا.
questions.ref_ar: مَا مِنْ كَلَامٍ طَوِيلٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ مَعْنًى وَاحِدٌ

questions.q: With what does the Habib tell Umar to begin? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: بِمَاذَا يَأْمُرُ الْحَبِيبُ عُمَرَ أَنْ يَبْدَأَ؟
questions.a: With the little words, for they are the key of the speech.

questions.q: Is اِبْدَأْ a command or a statement? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: هَلِ «اِبْدَأْ» أَمْرٌ أَمْ خَبَرٌ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A command: it has no ending and begins with an alif; the Habib speaks to Umar.

questions.q: What does “and of that” tell the reader? (line 6)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَقُولُ «وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ» لِلْقَارِئِ؟
questions.a: That something new is coming: the next item of the list.

questions.q: What did Umar do, and what did he say? (line 7)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ عُمَرُ؟ وَمَاذَا قَالَ؟
questions.a: He read the passage once more and said: Now I understand.

questions.q: What does the pair mean? What do both words end in?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى الزَّوْجِ؟ بِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي الْكَلِمَتَانِ؟
questions.a: Outwardly and inwardly. Both end in ـًا, because they say how Umar should sit.

questions.q: True or false: Ahmad wrote that understanding is the key of patience.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ أَنَّ الْفَهْمَ مِفْتَاحُ الصَّبْرِ.
questions.a: False. Patience is the key of understanding.

questions.q: Find the word that means “happiness”. Which other word in line 10 means “happy”?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «happiness». أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَخِيرِ تَعْنِي «happy»؟
questions.a: سَعَادَةٌ. And سَعِيدَيْنِ (the two, happy). Both come from the root س ع د.

questions.q: Who went back to the house at the end?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ رَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ فِي الْآخِرِ؟
questions.a: Ahmad and Umar (the verb رَجَعَ stays singular before its two doers).

questions.q: Umar first says the passage is long, then says “Now I understand”. What did the Habib change: the passage, or the way of reading it?
questions.q_ar: قَالَ عُمَرُ أَوَّلًا إِنَّ الْكَلَامَ طَوِيلٌ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: فَهِمْتُ. مَاذَا غَيَّرَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْكَلَامَ أَمْ طَرِيقَةَ الْقِرَاءَةِ؟
questions.a: The way of reading it: he showed him where to look first (the little words, the frame, the thread). The passage stayed as long as before.

questions.q: The Habib says “sit with good manners, outwardly and inwardly”. How is this advice about reading, and not only about sitting?
questions.q_ar: يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ: «اِجْلِسْ بِأَدَبٍ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا». كَيْفَ هُوَ نَصِيحَةٌ فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ وَلَيْسَ فِي الْجُلُوسِ فَقَطْ؟
questions.a: A reader sits to learn: patience, attention and respect (outward and inward) are what let the meaning open. The advice joins manners to understanding.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness). And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.

questions.q: Which two words mean “in this life” and “later”?
questions.a: عَاجِلٍ (soon, in this life) and آجِلٍ (later)

questions.q: What does the long sentence say taqwā is?
questions.a: A road (سَبِيلٌ) to every good, whether now or later.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The Habib read a long counsel.
questions.a: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً.

translate.ar: مَا مِنْ طَالِبٍ فِي تَرِيمَ إِلَّا وَلَهُ مُعَلِّمٌ.
translate.en: There is no student in Tarim who has not a teacher.

translate.ar: وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ السَّعَادَةُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ.
translate.en: And of that: happiness in this world and the next.
Hold to taqwā, outwardly and inwardly.

translate.ar: مَا مِنْ خَوْفٍ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى أَمَانٌ مِنْهُ.
translate.en: There is no fear, in this world or the next, but taqwā is safety from it.

translate.ar: وَكَمْ سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ مِنْ دَرْسٍ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحَبِيبِ!
translate.en: How many lessons Ahmad has heard in the Habib’s majlis!

translate.ar: السَّعَادَةُ الْعَاجِلَةُ فِي الدُّنْيَا، وَالسَّعَادَةُ الْآجِلَةُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ.
translate.en: The near happiness is in this world, and the later happiness in the Hereafter.

translate.ar: مَا مِنْ كَلَامٍ طَوِيلٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ مَعْنًى وَاحِدٌ، فَاقْرَأْهُ بِصَبْرٍ.
translate.en: There is no long passage but it has one meaning: so read it with patience.

translate.ar: مَا مِنْ طَرِيقٍ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ صَبْرٌ، وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الصَّبْرُ عَلَى الدَّرْسِ.
translate.en: There is no road to good without patience in it; and of that: patience with the lesson.

translate.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: التَّقْوَى بَابُ كُلِّ خَيْرٍ. وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْعِلْمُ، وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْعَمَلُ. وَمَا مِنْ طَالِبٍ يَخَافُ اللَّهَ إِلَّا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ.
translate.en: The Habib said: Taqwā is the door of every good. And of that: knowledge, and of that: action. And there is no student who fears God but he is happy.
There is no student who has not a book.
translate.ar: مَا مِنْ طَالِبٍ إِلَّا وَلَهُ كِتَابٌ.

translate.en: There is no good, in this world or the next, but taqwā is a way to it.
translate.ar: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى طَرِيقٌ إِلَيْهِ.
alt: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.

translate.en: And of that: happiness in this world and in the Hereafter.
translate.ar: وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ السَّعَادَةُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ.

translate.en: Hold to taqwā, outwardly and inwardly.
How many books the student has read!
There is no evil but taqwā is a protection from it.
translate.ar: مَا مِنْ شَرٍّ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى حِفْظٌ مِنْهُ.

translate.en: And of that: knowledge and understanding.
There is no house in Tarim without a majlis.
translate.ar: مَا مِنْ بَيْتٍ فِي تَرِيمَ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ مَجْلِسٌ.

translate.en: Taqwā is a fortress and a way to happiness.

readings.title_en: The litany whole: Wird and Rātib
readings.question_en: How do I read the whole litany at speed: what is said, how many times, and which part is the Qur’an?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ الْوِرْدَ كُلَّهُ بِسُرْعَةٍ: مَاذَا يُقَالُ؟ وَكَمْ مَرَّةً؟ وَأَيُّ جُزْءٍ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ؟

passages.intro_en: The end of the Wird and the Rātib: six lines, each with its count. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: al-Wird al-Laṭīf (lines 1–8) and Rātib al-Ḥaddād (lines 9–13) of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād
passages.cite: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, "Awrād wa-Aḥzāb" (al-Wird al-Laṭīf and Rātib al-Ḥaddād); Shamela Master Library copy (id 184180, 10 pp; originally an 01-BOOKS .bok file, "sameelh haddad"; no publisher or year; the copy is partly vowelled), pages 1–3 of part 1 (the Wird: lines 1–8) and pages 2–3 of part 2 (the Rātib: lines 9–13). The scanned books Dhakhīrat al-Maʿād sharḥ al-Rātib (SSD PDF, 220 pp; TLNOOR 190, OCR) and al-Maqṣad al-Munīf (51 pp) were not used for the wording: the first is a scan with poor OCR and was not read. Thirteen lines in all: lines 1-3 on slide 5, lines 4-7 on slide 10, lines 8-13 are Exercise A. The counts written with digits and unvowelled words in the copy (3 مرات, 7 مرات, 50 مرة) are vowelled by the course (vowelled for learners); no letter is changed.

lines.ar: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ، وَرِضَى نَفْسِهِ، وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ، وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ (ثَلَاثًا)
lines.en: Glory and praise to God, as many as His creatures, as much as pleases Him, the weight of His Throne and the ink of His words (three times).

lines.ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (3 مَرَّاتٍ)
lines.en: There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His the praise; He gives life and death and has power over all things (3 times).

lines.ar: رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (3 مَرَّاتٍ)
lines.en: Our Lord, forgive us and accept our repentance; You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful (3 times).

lines.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمْ (3 مَرَّاتٍ)
lines.en: O God, bless Muḥammad; O God, bless him and give him peace (3 times).

lines.ar: يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ، أَمِتْنَا عَلَى دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ (7 مَرَّاتٍ)
lines.en: O Possessor of majesty and honour, let us die in the religion of Islam (7 times).

lines.ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ (50 مَرَّةً)
lines.en: There is no god but God (50 times).

passages.ar: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ، وَرِضَى نَفْسِهِ، وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ، وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ (ثَلَاثًا) لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (3 مَرَّاتٍ) رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (3 مَرَّاتٍ) اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمْ (3 مَرَّاتٍ) يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ، أَمِتْنَا عَلَى دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ (7 مَرَّاتٍ) لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ (50 مَرَّةً)
passages.en: Glory and praise to God, as many as His creatures, as much as pleases Him, the weight of His Throne and the ink of His words (three times). There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His the praise; He gives life and death and has power over all things (3 times). Our Lord, forgive us and accept our repentance; You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful (3 times). O God, bless Muḥammad; O God, bless him and give him peace (3 times). O Possessor of majesty and honour, let us die in the religion of Islam (7 times). There is no god but God (50 times).

passages.intro_en: From the Qur’an, inside the wird: the first part of Āyat al-Kursī. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Qur’an 2:255, words 1–19 (the first part of Āyat al-Kursī), by program from the Madinah muṣḥaf data (quran_util). Said in al-Wird al-Laṭīf (wird_ratib_whole entry of texts/level8.py).

lines.ar: اللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ
lines.en: God: there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

passages.ar: اللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ
passages.en: God: there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

passages.intro_en: A short text: the whole Rātib. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: After the prayer the people of Tarim sat in the mosque.

lines.ar: وَجَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ وَعُمَرَ وَالضُّيُوفِ.
lines.en: And Ahmad sat with his father, Umar and the guests.

lines.ar: وَبَدَأَ الْإِمَامُ بِالرَّاتِبِ، وَقَالَ الْجَمِيعُ: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ.
lines.en: The imam began the Rātib, and everyone said: I seek refuge in God from evil.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ سُورَةً قَصِيرَةً ثَلَاثًا، وَسَبَّحُوا اللَّهَ عَشْرًا.
lines.en: Then they read a short sura three times, and glorified God ten times.

lines.ar: وَقَالُوا: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً.
lines.en: And they said: There is no god but God, fifty times.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ عُمَرُ لِأَحْمَدَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ الرَّاتِبَ كُلَّهُ!
lines.en: And Umar said to Ahmad: How beautiful the whole Rātib is!

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: كَمْ مَرَّةً قُلْنَا لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ؟
lines.en: Ahmad said: How many times did we say “There is no god but God”?

lines.ar: فَقَالَ أَبُوهُ: خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً، وَأَحْسَنُ الذِّكْرِ مَا كَانَ بِالْقَلْبِ وَاللِّسَانِ.
lines.en: His father said: Fifty times; and the best dhikr is the one with both the heart and the tongue.

lines.ar: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا.
lines.en: O God, forgive us and accept our repentance.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ إِلَى بُيُوتِهِمْ، وَفِي قُلُوبِهِمْ سَعَادَةٌ.
lines.en: And the people of Tarim went back to their houses, with happiness in their hearts.

passages.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. وَجَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ وَعُمَرَ وَالضُّيُوفِ. وَبَدَأَ الْإِمَامُ بِالرَّاتِبِ، وَقَالَ الْجَمِيعُ: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ. ثُمَّ قَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ سُورَةً قَصِيرَةً ثَلَاثًا، وَسَبَّحُوا اللَّهَ عَشْرًا. وَقَالُوا: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً. وَقَالَ عُمَرُ لِأَحْمَدَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ الرَّاتِبَ كُلَّهُ! قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: كَمْ مَرَّةً قُلْنَا لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ؟ فَقَالَ أَبُوهُ: خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً، وَأَحْسَنُ الذِّكْرِ مَا كَانَ بِالْقَلْبِ وَاللِّسَانِ. اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا. وَرَجَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ إِلَى بُيُوتِهِمْ، وَفِي قُلُوبِهِمْ سَعَادَةٌ.
passages.en: After the prayer the people of Tarim sat in the mosque. And Ahmad sat with his father, Umar and the guests. The imam began the Rātib, and everyone said: I seek refuge in God from evil. Then they read a short sura three times, and glorified God ten times. And they said: There is no god but God, fifty times. And Umar said to Ahmad: How beautiful the whole Rātib is! Ahmad said: How many times did we say “There is no god but God”? His father said: Fifty times; and the best dhikr is the one with both the heart and the tongue. O God, forgive us and accept our repentance. And the people of Tarim went back to their houses, with happiness in their hearts.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 144-145 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ الرَّاتِبَ بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ وَحَضَرَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَهُمْ.
lines.en: The people of Tarim read the Rātib after ʿIshāʾ, and the boy attended with them.

lines.ar: وَقَالُوا: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ثَلَاثًا.
lines.en: And they said: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created (three times).

passages.ar: قَرَأَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ الرَّاتِبَ بَعْدَ الْعِشَاءِ وَحَضَرَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَهُمْ. وَقَالُوا: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ثَلَاثًا.
passages.en: The people of Tarim read the Rātib after ʿIshāʾ, and the boy attended with them. And they said: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created (three times).

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Glory and praise to God, as many as His creatures, as much as pleases Him, the weight of His Throne and the ink of His words (three times).

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His the praise; He gives life and death and has power over all things (3 times).

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: Our Lord, forgive us and accept our repentance; You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful (3 times).

questions.q: Translate lines 4 and 5.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَيْنِ الرَّابِعَ وَالْخَامِسَ.
questions.a: O God, bless Muḥammad; O God, bless him and give him peace (3 times). O Possessor of majesty and honour, let us die in the religion of Islam (7 times).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A litany (wird): short lines of dhikr and prayer, each with its count. From the end of al-Wird al-Laṭīf and the Rātib of Imam ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: How many times is line 1 said? How is the count written?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً يُقَالُ السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ؟ كَيْفَ كُتِبَ الْعَدَدُ؟
questions.a: Three times; the number word alone, in brackets at the end of the line.

questions.q: How many times is line 6 said? Why is it مَرَّةً and not مَرَّاتٍ?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً يُقَالُ السَّطْرُ السَّادِسُ؟ لِمَاذَا «مَرَّةً» لَا «مَرَّاتٍ»؟
questions.a: Fifty times. After 11 and up the counted word is singular.

questions.q: Line 2: what do the two verbs mean? What do they have in common?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي: مَا مَعْنَى الْفِعْلَيْنِ؟ مَا الَّذِي يَجْمَعُهُمَا؟
questions.a: He gives life and He gives death: a pair of opposites, like عَاجِلٌ وَآجِلٌ, that covers everything.

questions.q: Line 3: the command تُبْ and the name التَّوَّابُ come from the same root as the word تَوْبَة (Lesson 65). What does the plea ask for?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ: «تُبْ» وَ«التَّوَّابُ» مِنْ جَذْرِ «تَوْبَة». مَاذَا يَطْلُبُ الدُّعَاءُ؟
questions.a: They share ت و ب. The plea asks God to accept our repentance, for He is the one who accepts it.

questions.q: Line 4: which two words are the commands? What are we asking?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الرَّابِعِ: مَا الْفِعْلَانِ الْأَمْرَانِ؟ مَاذَا نَطْلُبُ؟
questions.a: صَلِّ and سَلِّمْ: that God bless him and give him peace.

questions.q: How many of the six lines ask God for something with a command? Which lines?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ سَطْرًا مِنَ السِّتَّةِ فِيهِ طَلَبٌ بِفِعْلِ أَمْرٍ؟ أَيُّهَا؟
questions.a: Three: lines 3 (اغْفِرْ، تُبْ), 4 (صَلِّ، سَلِّمْ) and 5 (أَمِتْنَا).

questions.q: Read the vowels of line 1. What ending do these three words have, and why?
questions.q_ar: اِقْرَأِ الْحَرَكَاتِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ. مَا حَرَكَةُ آخِرِ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ مِنَ الثَّلَاثِ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: عَدَدَ: ـَ (“as many as”). خَلْقِهِ: ـِ (of what? after the noun عَدَدَ). عَرْشِهِ: ـِ (after زِنَةَ).

questions.q: Why is the count written after the words and in brackets, and not as part of the sentence?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يُكْتَبُ الْعَدَدُ بَعْدَ الْكَلَامِ بَيْنَ قَوْسَيْنِ؟
questions.a: The count belongs to the practice, not to the meaning: the reciter knows how many times to say the words without breaking them.

questions.q: Line 1 is long and rich; line 6 is four words, said fifty times. What does a litany gain by having both?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ طَوِيلٌ وَغَنِيٌّ، وَالسَّادِسُ أَرْبَعُ كَلِمَاتٍ تُقَالُ خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً. مَاذَا يَكْسَبُ الْوِرْدُ مِنَ الِاثْنَيْنِ؟
questions.a: The long line spreads praise over everything created; the short one is the simplest word, repeated until it settles. Together they give a range from the full to the plain.

questions.q: Translate the verse (the first part).
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْآيَةَ.
questions.a: God: there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it said in the wird?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَأَيْنَ يُقَالُ فِي الْوِرْدِ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an: the beginning of Āyat al-Kursī (2:255), which the wird names and the reciter reads from the muṣḥaf.

questions.q: Which two words make the frame, as in “there is no … but …” (Lessons 62 and 78)?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَصْنَعَانِ الْإِطَارَ كَمَا فِي «مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا»؟
questions.a: لَا … إِلَّا: “no god but He”.

questions.q: These two words follow هُوَ. What are they?
questions.q_ar: هَاتَانِ الْكَلِمَتَانِ بَعْدَ «هُوَ». مَا هُمَا؟
questions.a: Two descriptions of God: the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting.

questions.q: Which word denies? What two things are denied?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَنْفِي؟ مَا الشَّيْئَانِ الْمَنْفِيَّانِ؟
questions.a: لَا; drowsiness and sleep (a pair, like عَاجِلٌ وَآجِلٌ).

questions.q: Which pair covers everything? What does مَا mean here?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ زَوْجٍ يَشْمَلُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ؟ مَا مَعْنَى «مَا» هُنَا؟
questions.a: The heavens and the earth. مَا = “whatever”.
questions.ref_ar: مَا فِي السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ

questions.q: True or false: the verse says God is overtaken by sleep.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: تَقُولُ الْآيَةُ إِنَّ النَّوْمَ يَأْخُذُ اللَّهَ.
questions.a: False. It says neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.

questions.q: Who does ـهُ stand for? What does the verse say belongs to Him?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَنْ تَعُودُ ـهُ؟ مَاذَا يَقُولُ إِنَّهُ لَهُ؟
questions.a: God. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

questions.q: In the wird the verse is read, not explained. What is the reader asked to do with it?
questions.q_ar: فِي الْوِرْدِ تُقْرَأُ الْآيَةُ وَلَا تُشْرَحُ. مَاذَا يُطْلَبُ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟
questions.a: To read it exactly as it stands, from the muṣḥaf, and let its meaning settle by repetition.

questions.q: Compare this verse with the “no … but …” of Lesson 78. What is the same, and what is different?
questions.q_ar: قَارِنْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ بِإِطَارِ «مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا» فِي الدَّرْسِ ٧٨. مَا الَّذِي يَتَّفِقُ؟ وَمَا الَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُ؟
questions.a: The same frame: a denial of the whole kind, then the one exception. Different: Lesson 78’s frame is human advice about taqwā; here it is God’s own statement about Himself.

questions.q: Where did the people of Tarim sit, and when? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: In the mosque, after the prayer.

questions.q: With whom did Ahmad sit? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَعَ مَنْ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: With his father, Umar and the guests.

questions.q: Which little word comes before the One they run to? And which before what they run from?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ قَبْلَ مَنْ يَلْجَؤُونَ إِلَيْهِ؟ وَأَيُّ حَرْفٍ قَبْلَ مَا يَهْرُبُونَ مِنْهُ؟
questions.a: بِـ (بِاللَّهِ) and مِنْ (مِنَ الشَّرِّ).
questions.ref_ar: وَقَالَ الْجَمِيعُ: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: Then they read a short sura three times, and glorified God ten times.

questions.q: Find the two counts of line 4. What are the numbers?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْعَدَدَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ الرَّابِعِ. مَا الرَّقْمَانِ؟
questions.a: ثَلَاثًا = 3 times; عَشْرًا = 10 times.

questions.q: How many times did they say لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً قَالُوا «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ»؟
questions.a: Fifty times.

questions.q: Why is it مَرَّةً and not مَرَّاتٍ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «مَرَّةً» وَلَيْسَ «مَرَّاتٍ»؟
questions.a: After 11 and up the counted word is singular.

questions.q: Translate. What kind of sentence is it?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ. مَا نَوْعُ الْجُمْلَةِ؟
questions.a: How beautiful the whole Rātib is! An exclamation of wonder (Lesson 52).

questions.q: What did Ahmad ask his father? (line 7)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ أَبَاهُ؟
questions.a: How many times they said لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ.

questions.q: What did his father answer, and what did he add? (line 8)
questions.q_ar: بِمَاذَا أَجَابَ أَبُوهُ؟ وَمَاذَا زَادَ؟
questions.a: Fifty times; and the best dhikr is the one with both the heart and the tongue.

questions.q: Find the two commands in line 9. What do they ask for?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْأَمْرَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ التَّاسِعِ. مَاذَا يَطْلُبَانِ؟
questions.a: اغْفِرْ and تُبْ: forgiveness, and that God accept our repentance.

questions.q: Where did the people of Tarim go at the end, and what was in their hearts? (line 10)
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْآخِرِ؟ وَمَاذَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ؟
questions.a: To their houses; happiness.

questions.q: Find the word of Lesson 78 that means “happiness”.
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةَ الدَّرْسِ ٧٨ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «happiness».
questions.a: سَعَادَةٌ.

questions.q: The father says the best dhikr is with the heart and the tongue. Why does he say this right after the count?
questions.q_ar: يَقُولُ الْأَبُ إِنَّ أَحْسَنَ الذِّكْرِ بِالْقَلْبِ وَاللِّسَانِ. لِمَاذَا يَقُولُهُ بَعْدَ الْعَدَدِ؟
questions.a: A count can become only a number. He reminds Ahmad that the count serves the heart: the number holds the tongue, and the heart must be present.

questions.q: The story ends with “happiness in their hearts”. Which earlier lines prepare for it?
questions.q_ar: تَنْتَهِي الْقِصَّةُ بِـ«سَعَادَةٌ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ». أَيُّ سُطُورٍ سَبَقَتْ تُمَهِّدُ لَهَا؟
questions.a: The refuge in line 3, the dhikr of lines 4–5, and the prayer of line 9: the evening moves from refuge to remembrance to prayer.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The people of Tarim read the Rātib after ʿIshāʾ, and the boy attended with them. And they said: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created (three times).

questions.q: What does أَعُوذُ mean, and in what do they seek refuge?
questions.a: “I seek refuge”: in the perfect words of Allah.

questions.q: Which word gives the count?
questions.a: ثَلَاثًا (three times)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The people of Tarim read the Rātib.
questions.a: قَرَأَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ الرَّاتِبَ.

translate.ar: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا.
translate.en: I seek refuge in God from evil, outward and inward.

translate.ar: قَالَ الْإِمَامُ: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ ثَلَاثًا، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ثَلَاثًا.
translate.en: The imam said: Glory to God three times, and praise to God three times.

translate.ar: اللَّهُمَّ عَلِّمْنَا الْحِكْمَةَ وَاهْدِنَا إِلَى طَرِيقِ الْخَيْرِ.
translate.en: O God, teach us wisdom and guide us to the road of good.

translate.ar: رَجَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ إِلَى بُيُوتِهِمْ بَعْدَ الرَّاتِبِ.
translate.en: The people of Tarim went back to their houses after the Rātib.

translate.ar: وَكَمْ ذَكَرَ الطُّلَّابُ اللَّهَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ!
translate.en: How often the students have remembered God in the mosque!

translate.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ.
translate.en: O God, I seek refuge in You from weakness and laziness, and I ask You for well-being.

translate.ar: مَا مِنْ وِرْدٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ عَدَدٌ.
translate.en: There is no wird without a count in it.

translate.ar: رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا، فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ.
translate.en: Our Lord, forgive us and accept our repentance, for You are the Accepting of repentance.

translate.ar: قَالَ أَبُوهُ: اِقْرَأْ سُورَةً قَصِيرَةً ثَلَاثًا. ثُمَّ قُلْ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً. وَمَنْ ذَكَرَ اللَّهَ فَلَهُ أَجْرٌ.
translate.en: His father said: Read a short sura three times. Then say: There is no god but God, fifty times. And whoever remembers God has a reward.
O God, guide us.
I seek refuge in God from laziness.
I ask God for forgiveness seven times.
Glory to God, three times.
There is no god but God, fifty times.
translate.ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً.

translate.en: O God, forgive us and accept our repentance.
O God, bless our master Muḥammad and give him peace, ten times.
translate.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَسَلِّمْ عَشْرًا.

translate.en: God is the One who gives life and death.
I seek refuge in You from worry and grief.

readings.title_en: Mawlid prose: rhyme, chains, blessings
readings.question_en: How do I read a page of mawlid prose, where the clauses rhyme, the nouns hang in long chains, and the vowels begin to disappear?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ صَفْحَةً مِنْ نَثْرِ الْمَوْلِدِ، وَجُمَلُهَا مُسَجَّعَةٌ وَأَسْمَاؤُهَا فِي سَلَاسِلَ، وَالْحَرَكَاتُ تَغِيبُ؟

passages.intro_en: From the mawlid sermon. Read it aloud, listening for the rhymes, then answer.
passages.source: Simṭ al-Durar (Khuṭbat al-Mawlid) of Imām ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Ḥabshī
passages.cite: ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. Ḥusayn al-Ḥabshī, Simṭ al-Durar fī akhbār mawlid khayr al-bashar, Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, id 169330, 22 pp, digital; its title page says "first edition of its kind, corrected, vowelled and re-arranged"; no publisher or year), page 7 of the copy. The SSD also has the book as PDFs (432 pp; the translated 74 pp); TLNOOR 711 was not used. Four of the nine sentences (nos. 1, 2, 6 and 9); the source’s vowels are kept as printed, with the source misprints corrected by the course as recorded in the research file; in no. 9 (the blessing) the missing vowels are completed by the course without changing a letter (vowelled for learners). In no. 6 the English ends with a full stop because the sentence is cut here.

lines.ar: الحَمْدُ للهِ القَوِيِّ سُلْطَانُه، الوَاضِحِ بُرْهَانُه، المَبْسُوْطِ فِي الوُجُودِ كَرَمُهُ وَإِحْسَانُه
lines.en: Praise be to God, whose authority is strong and whose proof is clear, whose generosity and kindness are spread through existence.

lines.ar: تَعَالَى مَجْدُهُ وَعَظُمَ شَأنُه، خَلَقَ الخَلْقَ لِحِكْمَه، وَطَوَى عَلَيْهَا عِلْمَه
lines.en: Exalted is His glory and great His standing; He created creation for a wisdom, and enfolded it in His knowledge.

lines.ar: فَمَا أَجَلَّ هَذَا المَنَّ الَّذِي تَكَرَّمَ بِهِ المَنَّان، وَمَا أَعْظَمَ هَذَا الفَضْلَ الَّذِي بَرَزَ مِنْ حَضْرَةِ الإِحْسَان
lines.en: How great is this gift that the Bestower graciously gave, and how mighty this favour that came forth from the presence of kindness.

lines.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ أَفْضَلَ الصَّلَاةِ وَالتَّسْلِيمِ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا وَنَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ الرَّؤُوفِ الرَّحِيمِ
lines.en: O God, bless and give peace, with the best of blessing and peace, to our master and prophet Muḥammad, the Kind, the Merciful.

passages.ar: الحَمْدُ للهِ القَوِيِّ سُلْطَانُه، الوَاضِحِ بُرْهَانُه، المَبْسُوْطِ فِي الوُجُودِ كَرَمُهُ وَإِحْسَانُه تَعَالَى مَجْدُهُ وَعَظُمَ شَأنُه، خَلَقَ الخَلْقَ لِحِكْمَه، وَطَوَى عَلَيْهَا عِلْمَه فَمَا أَجَلَّ هَذَا المَنَّ الَّذِي تَكَرَّمَ بِهِ المَنَّان، وَمَا أَعْظَمَ هَذَا الفَضْلَ الَّذِي بَرَزَ مِنْ حَضْرَةِ الإِحْسَان اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ أَفْضَلَ الصَّلَاةِ وَالتَّسْلِيمِ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا وَنَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ الرَّؤُوفِ الرَّحِيمِ
passages.en: Praise be to God, whose authority is strong and whose proof is clear, whose generosity and kindness are spread through existence. Exalted is His glory and great His standing; He created creation for a wisdom, and enfolded it in His knowledge. How great is this gift that the Bestower graciously gave, and how mighty this favour that came forth from the presence of kindness. O God, bless and give peace, with the best of blessing and peace, to our master and prophet Muḥammad, the Kind, the Merciful.

passages.intro_en: A short paragraph, printed with no vowels. Read it aloud, check your reading by the meaning, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (the key shows it fully vowelled)

lines.ar: مَجْلِسُ الْمَوْلِدِ فِي تَرِيمَ مَجْلِسٌ كَرِيمٌ، وَنُورُهُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ عَظِيمٌ.
lines.en: The mawlid gathering in Tarim is a noble gathering, and its light in the mosque is great.
lines.ar_bare: مجلس المولد في تريم مجلس كريم، ونوره في المسجد عظيم.

lines.ar: يَجْتَمِعُ فِيهِ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ وَالْإِخْوَانُ وَالضُّيُوفُ.
lines.en: The people of Tarim, the brothers and the guests gather in it.
lines.ar_bare: يجتمع فيه أهل تريم والإخوان والضيوف.

lines.ar: وَيَقْرَأُ الْحَبِيبُ قِصَّةَ مَوْلِدِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، وَالنَّاسُ يَسْمَعُونَ بِأَدَبٍ وَمَحَبَّةٍ.
lines.en: And the Habib reads the story of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, and the people listen with courtesy and love.
lines.ar_bare: ويقرأ الحبيب قصة مولد النبي ﷺ، والناس يسمعون بأدب ومحبة.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ يَذْكُرُ الْجَمِيعُ اللَّهَ وَيَشْكُرُونَ نِعْمَتَهُ.
lines.en: Then everyone remembers Allah and thanks Him for His blessing.
lines.ar_bare: ثم يذكر الجميع الله ويشكرون نعمته.

lines.ar: وَالْقَلْبُ سَعِيدٌ وَالْوَجْهُ بَهِيٌّ.
lines.en: And the heart is happy and the face is radiant.
lines.ar_bare: والقلب سعيد والوجه بهي.

lines.ar: وَفِي آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ يَرْجِعُ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ.
lines.en: And at the end of the night each one returns to his home.
lines.ar_bare: وفي آخر الليل يرجع كل واحد إلى بيته.

passages.ar: مَجْلِسُ الْمَوْلِدِ فِي تَرِيمَ مَجْلِسٌ كَرِيمٌ، وَنُورُهُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ عَظِيمٌ. يَجْتَمِعُ فِيهِ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ وَالْإِخْوَانُ وَالضُّيُوفُ. وَيَقْرَأُ الْحَبِيبُ قِصَّةَ مَوْلِدِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، وَالنَّاسُ يَسْمَعُونَ بِأَدَبٍ وَمَحَبَّةٍ. ثُمَّ يَذْكُرُ الْجَمِيعُ اللَّهَ وَيَشْكُرُونَ نِعْمَتَهُ. وَالْقَلْبُ سَعِيدٌ وَالْوَجْهُ بَهِيٌّ. وَفِي آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ يَرْجِعُ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ.
passages.en: The mawlid gathering in Tarim is a noble gathering, and its light in the mosque is great. The people of Tarim, the brothers and the guests gather in it. And the Habib reads the story of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, and the people listen with courtesy and love. Then everyone remembers Allah and thanks Him for His blessing. And the heart is happy and the face is radiant. And at the end of the night each one returns to his home.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 146-147 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ اِجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gathered in the mosque.

lines.ar: وَقَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ الْمَوْلِدَ وَذَكَرُوا جَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ.
lines.en: And everyone read the mawlid and they mentioned the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.

passages.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ اِجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. وَقَرَأَ الْجَمِيعُ الْمَوْلِدَ وَذَكَرُوا جَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ.
passages.en: On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gathered in the mosque. And everyone read the mawlid and they mentioned the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Praise be to God, whose authority is strong and whose proof is clear, whose generosity and kindness are spread through existence.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: O God, bless and give peace, with the best of blessing and peace, to our master and prophet Muḥammad, the Kind, the Merciful.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A mawlid sermon in rhymed prose (sajʿ), from Simṭ al-Durar of Imam ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Ḥabshī: the clauses end in the same sound, the nouns hang in chains, and it closes with the blessing formula.

questions.q: Line 1: what three things are said about God?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَا الْأَشْيَاءُ الثَّلَاثَةُ الَّتِي قِيلَتْ عَنِ اللَّهِ؟
questions.a: His authority is strong, His proof is clear, and His generosity and kindness are spread through existence.

questions.q: Line 1: what do these three words have in common?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْمُشْتَرَكُ بَيْنَ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ الثَّلَاثِ؟
questions.a: They all end in the same sound, -ānuh: the clauses rhyme (sajʿ).

questions.q: Find in line 1 the word for “proof” and the word for “authority”.
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةَ «proof» وَكَلِمَةَ «authority» فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ.
questions.a: بُرْهَانُه = proof; سُلْطَانُه = authority.

questions.q: Line 2: which two words rhyme? What is odd about how they are written?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَتَقَافَيَانِ؟ وَمَا الْغَرِيبُ فِي كِتَابَتِهِمَا؟
questions.a: لِحِكْمَه and عِلْمَه (-mah). In the first the ـة of “wisdom” is written ـه, as it is said when you stop; the second is “his knowledge” with the ـهُ cut short.

questions.q: Line 3: two clauses begin the same way. Which words begin them, and what does each mean?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ جُمْلَتَانِ تَبْدَآنِ بِالْبِنَاءِ نَفْسِهِ. مَا هُمَا؟
questions.a: مَا أَجَلَّ … “how mighty …” and مَا أَعْظَمَ … “how great …”: two parallel clauses.

questions.q: Line 4: find the chain. What does it mean?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الرَّابِعِ: جِدِ الْإِضَافَةَ. مَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: أَفْضَلَ الصَّلَاةِ: “the best of blessing”; التَّسْلِيمِ is joined to الصَّلَاةِ by وَ.

questions.q: Line 4: who is blessed, and which two words describe him?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: مَنِ الَّذِي يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَصِفَانِهِ؟
questions.a: Our master and prophet Muḥammad; الرَّؤُوفِ (the kind) and الرَّحِيمِ (the merciful).

questions.q: Line 1: these three describing words all end in kasra. Which word do they describe, and why kasra?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: هَذِهِ الصِّفَاتُ الثَّلَاثُ مَكْسُورَةٌ. مَا الْمَوْصُوفُ؟ وَلِمَاذَا الْكَسْرَةُ؟
questions.a: They describe اللهِ (الحَمْدُ للهِ): a describing word copies the ending of the noun it describes, here genitive after لِـ.

questions.q: Line 4: why does أَفْضَلَ end in fatḥa? (Think of Lesson 58: “how?”.)
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: لِمَاذَا «أَفْضَلَ» مَفْتُوحَةٌ؟ (اُنْظُرِ الدَّرْسَ ٥٨.)
questions.a: It answers “how?”: bless with the best blessing. It is the absolute object (Lesson 58), so it is accusative.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: The mawlid gathering in Tarim is a noble gathering, and its light in the mosque is great.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: And the Habib reads the story of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, and the people listen with courtesy and love.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A short passage of mawlid prose in rhymed clauses: the ends of line 1 rhyme (كَرِيمٌ / عَظِيمٌ), the nouns hang in chains, and the words are about the mawlid night.

questions.q: Who gathers in the gathering? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَجْتَمِعُ؟ (السَّطْرُ ٢)
questions.a: The people of Tarim, the brothers and the guests.

questions.q: Who reads the story, and what is it about? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقْرَأُ الْقِصَّةَ؟ وَعَمَّ هِيَ؟
questions.a: The Habib reads it; it is the story of the Prophet’s ﷺ birth.

questions.q: How do the people listen? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يَسْمَعُ النَّاسُ؟
questions.a: With courtesy and love (بِأَدَبٍ وَمَحَبَّةٍ).

questions.q: Line 1: which two words end the clauses, and do they rhyme?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تُنْهِيَانِ الْجُمْلَتَيْنِ؟ وَهَلْ تَتَقَافَيَانِ؟
questions.a: كَرِيمٌ and عَظِيمٌ: yes, both end in -īm.

questions.q: Line 3: find the chain of three nouns. Give its meaning.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: جِدْ سِلْسِلَةَ الْإِضَافَةِ مِنْ ثَلَاثَةِ أَسْمَاءٍ. مَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: قِصَّةَ مَوْلِدِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: the story of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: What does everyone do after the story? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ الْجَمِيعُ بَعْدَ الْقِصَّةِ؟
questions.a: They remember Allah and thank Him for His blessing.

questions.q: What are the heart and the face like in line 5?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا عَنِ الْقَلْبِ وَالْوَجْهِ فِي السَّطْرِ ٥؟
questions.a: The heart is happy and the face is radiant.

questions.q: Line 3: قِصَّةَ ends in fatḥa. What is its job, and which word makes the next two words end in kasra?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: «قِصَّةَ» مَفْتُوحَةٌ. مَا وَظِيفَتُهَا؟ وَلِمَاذَا «مَوْلِدِ» وَ«النَّبِيِّ» مَكْسُورَتَانِ؟
questions.a: قِصَّةَ is the object of يَقْرَأُ, so fatḥa. مَوْلِدِ ends in kasra because it is the second link of the chain, and النَّبِيِّ ﷺ in kasra because it is the third.

questions.q: Line 1: why does تَرِيمَ end in fatḥa after فِي, where we expect kasra?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: لِمَاذَا «تَرِيمَ» مَفْتُوحَةٌ بَعْدَ «فِي»؟
questions.a: Names like تَرِيم do not take tanwīn or kasra (Lesson 40): فِي تَرِيمَ.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gathered in the mosque. And everyone read the mawlid and they mentioned the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.

questions.q: Which two words in the second new line name qualities of the Prophet ﷺ? Which sound alike?
questions.a: جَمَالَ (beauty) and كَمَالَهُ (perfection): they sound alike, like the matching ends in mawlid prose.

questions.q: Why is the verb اِجْتَمَعَ singular although أَهْلُ means “people”?
questions.a: A verb before its doer stays singular.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The people of Tarim gathered in the mosque.
questions.a: اِجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.

translate.en: The mawlid gathering is noble and its light is great.
His authority is strong and his proof is clear.

translate.ar: يَقْرَأُ الْحَبِيبُ قِصَّةَ مَوْلِدِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَالنَّاسُ يَسْمَعُونَ.
translate.en: The Habib reads the story of the birth of the Prophet ﷺ and the people listen.

translate.ar: مَا أَعْظَمَ إِحْسَانَ اللَّهِ وَمَا أَكْبَرَ فَضْلَهُ.
translate.en: How great is the kindness of Allah, and how vast is His favour!

translate.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ.
translate.en: O God, bless and grant peace to our master Muhammad and to his family.

translate.ar: جَمَالُ الْمَجْلِسِ ظَاهِرٌ وَكَمَالُ نُورِهِ وَاضِحٌ.
translate.en: The beauty of the gathering is outward and the perfection of its light is clear.

translate.ar: اجْتَمَعَ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ لَيْلَةَ الْمَوْلِدِ.
translate.en: The people of Tarim gathered in the mosque on the night of the mawlid.
The heart is happy and the face is radiant.

translate.ar: مَرْيَمُ تَسْمَعُ قِصَّةَ الْمَوْلِدِ مَعَ أُمِّهَا.
translate.en: Maryam listens to the story of the mawlid with her mother.

lines.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ يَجْتَمِعُ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْكَبِيرِ.
lines.en: On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gather in the great mosque.

lines.ar: وَيَقْرَأُ الْحَبِيبُ قِصَّةَ الْمَوْلِدِ وَالْقُلُوبُ سَعِيدَةٌ.
lines.en: And the Habib reads the story of the mawlid, and the hearts are happy.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ يَقُولُ النَّاسُ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ.
lines.en: Then the people say: O God, bless and grant peace to the Prophet.

translate.ar: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ يَجْتَمِعُ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْكَبِيرِ. وَيَقْرَأُ الْحَبِيبُ قِصَّةَ الْمَوْلِدِ وَالْقُلُوبُ سَعِيدَةٌ. ثُمَّ يَقُولُ النَّاسُ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ.
translate.en: On the night of the mawlid the people of Tarim gather in the great mosque. And the Habib reads the story of the mawlid, and the hearts are happy. Then the people say: O God, bless and grant peace to the Prophet.
The night of the mawlid is a night of light.
His authority is strong and his proof is clear.
The Habib reads the story of the Prophet’s ﷺ birth.
translate.ar: يَقْرَأُ الْحَبِيبُ قِصَّةَ مَوْلِدِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.

translate.en: O God, bless and grant peace to our master Muhammad.
translate.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ.

translate.en: How great is the kindness of Allah!
The beauty of the gathering is clear.
The people of Tarim gather in the mosque, and their hearts are happy.
translate.ar: يَجْتَمِعُ أَهْلُ تَرِيمَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ سَعِيدَةٌ.

translate.en: The gathering is noble, and its light is great.
The perfection of the Prophet’s ﷺ beauty is a clear proof.
translate.ar: كَمَالُ جَمَالِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ بُرْهَانٌ وَاضِحٌ.

translate.en: The people listen with courtesy and love.

readings.title_en: The qaṣīda: bayt, rhyme, beat
readings.question_en: How do I read a poem: where does each bayt break, how does the rhyme work, and why are some words in a strange order?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ قَصِيدَةً؟ أَيْنَ يَنْكَسِرُ الْبَيْتُ؟ وَكَيْفَ تَعْمَلُ الْقَافِيَةُ؟ وَلِمَاذَا تَأْتِي بَعْضُ الْكَلِمَاتِ فِي غَيْرِ مَكَانِهَا؟

passages.intro_en: Two bayts from the poem of Imam al-Ḥaddād. Read them aloud, tapping the beat, then answer.
passages.source: al-Durr al-Manẓūm of Imam ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād (lines 7 and 8)
passages.cite: Haddad: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, al-Durr al-Manẓūm li-Dhawī al-ʿUqūl wa-l-Fuhūm (the dīwān), the first poem (rhyme -ā), Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih Sufi library, id 184200, 174 pp; no publisher or year; its vowels have many errors and were not used), page 1 of the copy; the SSD also has a 768-pp PDF of the dīwān (not read).. Two lines (nos. 7 and 8); the vowels are the course’s (vowelled for learners), the letters are exact.

lines.ar: يَا أَمَلَ الْمُؤَمِّلِينْ * وَيَا مَلَاذاً كُنْ لَنَا
lines.en: O hope of those who hope, O refuge, be for us!

lines.ar: فَمِنْكَ كُلُّ خِيرَةٍ * وَكُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ بِنَا
lines.en: From You is every good and every blessing upon us.

glossary.en: those who hope (ـين with a sukūn at the stop)

passages.ar: يَا أَمَلَ الْمُؤَمِّلِينْ * وَيَا مَلَاذاً كُنْ لَنَا فَمِنْكَ كُلُّ خِيرَةٍ * وَكُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ بِنَا
passages.en: O hope of those who hope, O refuge, be for us! From You is every good and every blessing upon us.

passages.intro_en: The opening bayt of a famous poem of praise. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: the Burda of al-Būṣīrī (the first bayt)
passages.cite: Burda: Muḥammad b. Saʿīd al-Būṣīrī, Qaṣīdat al-Burda, "Qaṣīdat al-Burda al-Mubāraka", Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih Sufi library, id 78421, 10 pp; no publisher), page 1 of the copy; the plan's ids 283 and 178 were not used. The first bayt only (no. 10 of the research file); the misvowelled تَذَكِّرِ of the copy is corrected by the course to تَذَكُّرِ.

lines.ar: أَمِنْ تَذَكُّرِ جِيرَانٍ بِذِي سَلَمِ * مَزَجْتَ دَمْعاً جَرَى مِنْ مُقْلَةٍ بِدَمِ
lines.en: (Burda:) Is it the memory of neighbours at Dhū Salam that made you mix tears running from your eye with blood?

passages.ar: أَمِنْ تَذَكُّرِ جِيرَانٍ بِذِي سَلَمِ * مَزَجْتَ دَمْعاً جَرَى مِنْ مُقْلَةٍ بِدَمِ
passages.en: (Burda:) Is it the memory of neighbours at Dhū Salam that made you mix tears running from your eye with blood?

passages.intro_en: A short paragraph, printed with no vowels. Read it aloud, check your reading by the meaning, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (the key shows it fully vowelled)

lines.ar: فِي الْمَجْلِسِ شَاعِرٌ يَقْرَأُ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
lines.en: In the gathering a poet reads a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
lines.ar_bare: في المجلس شاعر يقرأ قصيدة في مدح النبي ﷺ.

lines.ar: كُلُّ بَيْتٍ فِيهِ شَطْرَانِ، وَالْقَافِيَةُ وَاحِدَةٌ.
lines.en: Every bayt has two halves, and the rhyme is one.
lines.ar_bare: كل بيت فيه شطران، والقافية واحدة.

lines.ar: وَالنَّاسُ يَسْمَعُونَ بِأَدَبٍ وَمَحَبَّةٍ.
lines.en: And the people listen with courtesy and love.
lines.ar_bare: والناس يسمعون بأدب ومحبة.

lines.ar: يَذْكُرُ الشَّاعِرُ جَلَالَ اللَّهِ وَبَهَاءَهُ وَجَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ.
lines.en: The poet mentions the majesty of Allah and His splendour, and the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.
lines.ar_bare: يذكر الشاعر جلال الله وبهاءه وجمال النبي ﷺ وكماله.

lines.ar: وَفِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ كَلِمَاتٌ قَلِيلَةٌ وَمَعْنًى كَبِيرٌ.
lines.en: And in every bayt there are few words and a great meaning.
lines.ar_bare: وفي كل بيت كلمات قليلة ومعنى كبير.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ الشَّاعِرُ، وَيَقُولُ النَّاسُ: آمِينَ.
lines.en: Then the poet sits down, and the people say: Amen.
lines.ar_bare: ثم يجلس الشاعر، ويقول الناس: آمين.

passages.ar: فِي الْمَجْلِسِ شَاعِرٌ يَقْرَأُ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. كُلُّ بَيْتٍ فِيهِ شَطْرَانِ، وَالْقَافِيَةُ وَاحِدَةٌ. وَالنَّاسُ يَسْمَعُونَ بِأَدَبٍ وَمَحَبَّةٍ. يَذْكُرُ الشَّاعِرُ جَلَالَ اللَّهِ وَبَهَاءَهُ وَجَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَكَمَالَهُ. وَفِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ كَلِمَاتٌ قَلِيلَةٌ وَمَعْنًى كَبِيرٌ. ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ الشَّاعِرُ، وَيَقُولُ النَّاسُ: آمِينَ.
passages.en: In the gathering a poet reads a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ. Every bayt has two halves, and the rhyme is one. And the people listen with courtesy and love. The poet mentions the majesty of Allah and His splendour, and the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection. And in every bayt there are few words and a great meaning. Then the poet sits down, and the people say: Amen.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 148-149 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
lines.en: The boy heard in the majlis a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.

lines.ar: وَفِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ صَدْرٌ وَعَجُزٌ.
lines.en: And in every verse there is a first half and a second half.

passages.ar: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. وَفِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ صَدْرٌ وَعَجُزٌ.
passages.en: The boy heard in the majlis a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ. And in every verse there is a first half and a second half.

glossary.en: those who hope (ـين with a sukūn at the stop)

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: O hope of those who hope, O refuge, be for us!

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: From You is every good and every blessing upon us.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A poem (qaṣīda): every line is a bayt of two halves (marked *), and every bayt ends in the same sound, -nā. It is a prayer in verse.

questions.q: Line 1: write the first half and the second half.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: اُكْتُبِ الشَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ وَالشَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: First half: يَا أَمَلَ الْمُؤَمِّلِينْ. Second half: وَيَا مَلَاذاً كُنْ لَنَا.

questions.q: Which words end the second half of line 1 and of line 2? What is the rhyme?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تُنْهِيَانِ الشَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ؟ مَا الْقَافِيَةُ؟
questions.a: لَنَا and بِنَا: the rhyme is -nā.

questions.q: Line 2: which word comes first that we would say last? Say the half in prose order.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ جَاءَتْ أَوَّلًا؟ اُكْتُبِ الشَّطْرَ بِتَرْتِيبِ النَّثْرِ.
questions.a: مِنْكَ comes first. In prose: كُلُّ خِيرَةٍ مِنْكَ.

questions.q: Line 1: what has happened to the ending of this word?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَاذَا حَدَثَ لِآخِرِ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ؟
questions.a: The case vowel has dropped and a sukūn closes the word: pausal rhyme. In prose it is الْمُؤَمِّلِينَ.

questions.q: Who is spoken to in line 1, and what is asked of Him?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْمُخَاطَبُ فِي السَّطْرِ ١؟ وَمَاذَا يُطْلَبُ مِنْهُ؟
questions.a: Allah, called “hope of those who hope” and “refuge”; the poet asks that He be a refuge for us.

questions.q: Line 2: which little word is said twice, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَكَرَّرَتْ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: كُلُّ: “every”.

questions.q: Line 2: is the second half “every blessing is upon us”? Which little word gives “upon us”?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى «upon us»؟
questions.a: Yes; بِنَا (“with us / upon us”): بِ + نَا.

questions.q: Line 1: why does أَمَلَ end in fatḥa after يَا? (Lesson 61.)
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: لِمَاذَا «أَمَلَ» مَفْتُوحَةٌ بَعْدَ «يَا»؟ (الدَّرْسُ ٦١.)
questions.a: The noun called with يَا, when it is the first noun of a chain (أَمَلَ الْمُؤَمِّلِينْ), is accusative: يَا أَمَلَ.

questions.q: Line 1: why does مَلَاذاً have tanwīn and fatḥa, and why is the ا written?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: لِمَاذَا «مَلَاذاً» مُنَوَّنَةٌ مَفْتُوحَةٌ؟ وَلِمَاذَا كُتِبَتِ الْأَلِفُ؟
questions.a: The poet calls “any refuge”, not one named person: such a called noun takes tanwīn with fatḥa. At the stop the tanwīn becomes ā, which also carries the rhyme -nā.

questions.q: Translate the bayt.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الْبَيْتَ.
questions.a: Is it the memory of neighbours at Dhū Salam that made you mix tears running from your eye with blood?

questions.q: What kind of poem is this, and who wrote it?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذِهِ الْقَصِيدَةِ؟ وَمَنْ نَظَمَهَا؟
questions.a: The first bayt of the Burda, a qaṣīda of praise (مَدْح) of the Prophet ﷺ by Imam al-Būṣīrī.

questions.q: Write the first half and the second half.
questions.q_ar: اُكْتُبِ الشَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ وَالشَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: First half: أَمِنْ تَذَكُّرِ جِيرَانٍ بِذِي سَلَمِ. Second half: مَزَجْتَ دَمْعاً جَرَى مِنْ مُقْلَةٍ بِدَمِ.

questions.q: Both halves end in the same sound. Which two words, and what sound?
questions.q_ar: الشَّطْرَانِ يَنْتَهِيَانِ بِصَوْتٍ وَاحِدٍ. أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ؟ وَمَا الصَّوْتُ؟
questions.a: سَلَمِ and بِدَمِ: -mi. In the opening bayt of a qaṣīda both halves rhyme; from then on only the second half does.

questions.q: Find the word for “neighbours” and the word for “tears”.
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةَ «neighbours» وَكَلِمَةَ «tears».
questions.a: جِيرَانٍ = neighbours; دَمْعاً = tears.

questions.q: Find the word for “blood”. Which little word comes before it?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةَ «blood». أَيُّ حَرْفٍ قَبْلَهَا؟
questions.a: دَمِ = blood; بِ = “with”.

questions.q: Where did the tears run from?
questions.q_ar: مِنْ أَيْنَ جَرَى الدَّمْعُ؟
questions.a: From the eye (مِنْ مُقْلَةٍ).

questions.q: Find the chain. What is its meaning, and why does تَذَكُّرِ end in kasra?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْإِضَافَةَ. مَا مَعْنَاهَا؟ وَلِمَاذَا «تَذَكُّرِ» مَكْسُورَةٌ؟
questions.a: تَذَكُّرِ جِيرَانٍ: “the remembering of neighbours”. تَذَكُّرِ is genitive after مِنْ (in أَمِنْ), and جِيرَانٍ is genitive as the second link.

questions.q: Is the kasra on the last letter of each half (سَلَمِ, دَمِ) a pausal change?
questions.q_ar: هَلِ الْكَسْرَةُ فِي آخِرِ الشَّطْرَيْنِ تَغَيُّرٌ لِلْوُقُوفِ؟
questions.a: No: it is an ordinary case ending (after بِ and after ذِي). The rhyme is simply the sound -mi.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: In the gathering a poet reads a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: The poet mentions the majesty of Allah and His splendour, and the beauty of the Prophet ﷺ and his perfection.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A short passage about a poem sung in the majlis: it speaks of the poet, the qaṣīda, the bayt and the rhyme.

questions.q: How many halves does every bayt have? What is one? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: كَمْ شَطْرًا فِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ؟ وَكَمِ الْقَافِيَةُ؟ (السَّطْرُ ٢)
questions.a: Two; the rhyme is one.

questions.q: How do the people listen? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يَسْمَعُ النَّاسُ؟
questions.a: With courtesy and love.

questions.q: What is said in praise of Allah, and what of the Prophet ﷺ? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُذْكَرُ مِنْ صِفَاتِ اللَّهِ؟ وَمَاذَا مِنْ صِفَاتِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ؟
questions.a: Allah’s majesty and splendour; the Prophet’s ﷺ beauty and perfection.

questions.q: What is in every bayt? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فِي كُلِّ بَيْتٍ؟
questions.a: Few words and a great meaning.

questions.q: What do the people say at the end? (line 6)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ فِي النِّهَايَةِ؟
questions.a: Amen (آمِينَ).

questions.q: Line 1 begins with فِي الْمَجْلِسِ and then شَاعِرٌ. Which order is this, and what would the ordinary order be?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١ يَبْدَأُ بِـ«فِي الْمَجْلِسِ» ثُمَّ «شَاعِرٌ». أَيُّ تَرْتِيبٍ هَذَا؟
questions.a: Inverted order: the place comes first. Ordinary: شَاعِرٌ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ, “a poet is in the gathering”.

questions.q: Line 4: find the two chains. Which word is the first noun of each?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: جِدِ السِّلْسِلَتَيْنِ. مَا الْأَوَّلُ فِي كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا؟
questions.a: جَلَالَ اللَّهِ (first noun جَلَالَ) and جَمَالَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ (first noun جَمَالَ); both are objects of يَذْكُرُ, so fatḥa.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy heard in the majlis a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ. And in every verse there is a first half and a second half.

questions.q: What are the two halves of a verse called?
questions.a: صَدْرٌ (the first half) and عَجُزٌ (the second half)

questions.q: What is the qaṣīda about?
questions.a: Praise (مَدْح) of the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy heard a qaṣīda.
questions.a: سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ قَصِيدَةً.

translate.ar: يَقْرَأُ الشَّاعِرُ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.
translate.en: The poet reads a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
Every bayt has two halves, and the rhyme is one.
Poetry is speech that has a metre and a rhyme.

translate.ar: ذَكَرَ الشَّاعِرُ جَلَالَ اللَّهِ وَبَهَاءَ نُورِهِ.
translate.en: The poet mentioned the majesty of Allah and the splendour of His light.
From You is every blessing, and praise is Yours.
In the gathering is a poet who reads a qaṣīda.
Ahmad heard the qaṣīda with his father.

translate.ar: رَبِّي عَظِيمٌ وَكَرِيمٌ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الرَّحِيمِ.
translate.en: My Lord is great and generous, and praise be to Allah, the Merciful.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْمُعَلِّمُ لِأَحْمَدَ: الشِّعْرُ كَلَامٌ لَهُ وَزْنٌ وَقَافِيَةٌ.
lines.en: The teacher said to Ahmad: Poetry is speech that has a metre and a rhyme.

lines.ar: وَالْقَصِيدَةُ أَبْيَاتٌ كَثِيرَةٌ، وَلِكُلِّ بَيْتٍ شَطْرَانِ.
lines.en: And a qaṣīda is many bayts, and every bayt has two halves.

lines.ar: وَيَقُولُ الشَّاعِرُ: مِنْكَ كُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ، وَالْمَعْنَى: كُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ مِنْكَ.
lines.en: And the poet says “from You is every blessing”, and the meaning is: “every blessing is from You”.

translate.ar: قَالَ الْمُعَلِّمُ لِأَحْمَدَ: الشِّعْرُ كَلَامٌ لَهُ وَزْنٌ وَقَافِيَةٌ. وَالْقَصِيدَةُ أَبْيَاتٌ كَثِيرَةٌ، وَلِكُلِّ بَيْتٍ شَطْرَانِ. وَيَقُولُ الشَّاعِرُ: مِنْكَ كُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ، وَالْمَعْنَى: كُلُّ نِعْمَةٍ مِنْكَ.
translate.en: The teacher said to Ahmad: Poetry is speech that has a metre and a rhyme. And a qaṣīda is many bayts, and every bayt has two halves. And the poet says “from You is every blessing”, and the meaning is: “every blessing is from You”.
The poet reads a qaṣīda in praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
translate.ar: يَقْرَأُ الشَّاعِرُ قَصِيدَةً فِي مَدْحِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.

translate.en: Every bayt has two halves.
The rhyme is one in the qaṣīda.
The majesty of Allah and the splendour of His light.
From You is every blessing.
Praise be to Allah, the Merciful.
We listen to the qaṣīda with courtesy.
O my Lord, You are great and generous.
Poetry is speech that has a rhyme.
In the gathering a poet reads a qaṣīda.

readings.title_en: The sīra: born, grew up, travelled
readings.question_en: How do I read the story of a life, section by section: who, when, where, and what came next?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ قِصَّةَ حَيَاةٍ فِي مَقَاطِعَ قَصِيرَةٍ: مَنْ؟ وَمَتَى؟ وَأَيْنَ؟ وَمَاذَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ؟

passages.intro_en: A page from a book of the Prophet’s life (sīra). Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Nūr al-Yaqīn fī sīrat sayyid al-mursalīn of Muḥammad al-Khuḍarī
passages.cite: Muḥammad b. ʿAfīfī al-Khuḍarī, Nūr al-Yaqīn fī sīrat sayyid al-mursalīn, ed. Haytham Hilāl, Dār al-Maʿrifa, Beirut, 1st ed. 1425 AH / 2004 (Shamela 3.28 id 5582, "numbering matches the print"), pp. 8, 9, 10 and 11 (line 1 on p. 8; lines 2–5 on pp. 8–9; lines 6–8 on p. 9; lines 9–10 on p. 10; line 11 on p. 11). Abridged: three consecutive sentences (lines 9–11 of the eleven in the research file); the print is unvowelled and the vowels are added by the course (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: ثُمَّ إِنَّ أُمَّهُ أَخَذَتْهُ مِنْهَا، وَتَوَجَّهَتْ بِهِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لِزِيَارَةِ أَخْوَالِ أَبِيهِ بَنِي عَدِيِّ بْنِ النَّجَّارِ
lines.en: Then his mother took him back from her and set out with him for Medina to visit his father's maternal relatives, the Banū ʿAdī b. al-Najjār,

lines.ar: وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ عَبْدُ الْمُطَّلِبِ
lines.en: and his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib took him into his care.

lines.ar: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَتْ سِنُّهُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً، أَرَادَ عَمُّهُ وَكَفِيلُهُ السَّفَرَ بِتِجَارَةٍ إِلَى الشَّامِ
lines.en: When his age, upon him be blessings and peace, reached twelve years, his uncle and guardian wanted to travel with merchandise to Syria.

passages.ar: ثُمَّ إِنَّ أُمَّهُ أَخَذَتْهُ مِنْهَا، وَتَوَجَّهَتْ بِهِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لِزِيَارَةِ أَخْوَالِ أَبِيهِ بَنِي عَدِيِّ بْنِ النَّجَّارِ وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ عَبْدُ الْمُطَّلِبِ وَلَمَّا بَلَغَتْ سِنُّهُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً، أَرَادَ عَمُّهُ وَكَفِيلُهُ السَّفَرَ بِتِجَارَةٍ إِلَى الشَّامِ
passages.en: Then his mother took him back from her and set out with him for Medina to visit his father's maternal relatives, the Banū ʿAdī b. al-Najjār, and his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib took him into his care. When his age, upon him be blessings and peace, reached twelve years, his uncle and guardian wanted to travel with merchandise to Syria.

passages.intro_en: A short text: a page of Ahmad’s notes from the sīra circle. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: فِي الْحَلْقَةِ قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ مِنْ كِتَابِ السِّيرَةِ، وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَا سَمِعَ.
lines.en: In the circle the Habib read from the book of the sīra, and Ahmad wrote down what he heard.

lines.ar: وُلِدَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فِي مَكَّةَ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ.
lines.en: The Prophet ﷺ was born in Mecca on a Monday.

lines.ar: وَكَانَ اسْمُ أُمِّهِ آمِنَةَ.
lines.en: And his mother’s name was Āmina.

lines.ar: وَلَمَّا وُلِدَ سَمَّاهُ جَدُّهُ مُحَمَّدًا.
lines.en: When he was born his grandfather named him Muḥammad ﷺ.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَتْ بِهِ أُمُّهُ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ.
lines.en: Then his mother went with him to Medina.

lines.ar: وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ، ثُمَّ كَفَلَهُ عَمُّهُ.
lines.en: His grandfather took him into his care, and then his uncle took him in.

lines.ar: وَلَمَّا نَشَأَ سَافَرَ مَعَ عَمِّهِ إِلَى الشَّامِ.
lines.en: When he had grown up he travelled with his uncle to Syria.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ لِعُمَرَ: السِّيرَةُ قِصَّةٌ، وَلَكِنَّ فِيهَا حِكْمَةً كَثِيرَةً.
lines.en: Ahmad said to Umar: The sīra is a story, but there is much wisdom in it.
