passages.ar: فِي الْحَلْقَةِ قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ مِنْ كِتَابِ السِّيرَةِ، وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَا سَمِعَ. وُلِدَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فِي مَكَّةَ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ. وَكَانَ اسْمُ أُمِّهِ آمِنَةَ. وَلَمَّا وُلِدَ سَمَّاهُ جَدُّهُ مُحَمَّدًا. ثُمَّ ذَهَبَتْ بِهِ أُمُّهُ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ. وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ، ثُمَّ كَفَلَهُ عَمُّهُ. وَلَمَّا نَشَأَ سَافَرَ مَعَ عَمِّهِ إِلَى الشَّامِ. قَالَ أَحْمَدُ لِعُمَرَ: السِّيرَةُ قِصَّةٌ، وَلَكِنَّ فِيهَا حِكْمَةً كَثِيرَةً.
passages.en: In the circle the Habib read from the book of the sīra, and Ahmad wrote down what he heard. The Prophet ﷺ was born in Mecca on a Monday. And his mother’s name was Āmina. When he was born his grandfather named him Muḥammad ﷺ. Then his mother went with him to Medina. His grandfather took him into his care, and then his uncle took him in. When he had grown up he travelled with his uncle to Syria. Ahmad said to Umar: The sīra is a story, but there is much wisdom in it.

passages.intro_en: A bare paragraph: no vowels. Read it aloud; the vowels you know will tell you the words. Then answer.
passages.cite: Course text. Printed without vowels for the student; the key has them.

lines.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ قِصَّةَ جَدِّهِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
lines.en: Ahmad wrote the story of his grandfather in his book.
lines.ar_bare: كتب أحمد قصة جده في كتابه.

lines.ar: وُلِدَ جَدُّهُ فِي تَرِيمَ وَنَشَأَ فِي بَيْتِ عِلْمٍ.
lines.en: His grandfather was born in Tarim and grew up in a house of knowledge.
lines.ar_bare: ولد جده في تريم ونشأ في بيت علم.

lines.ar: وَلَمَّا نَشَأَ سَافَرَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
lines.en: When he had grown up he travelled to Mecca with his father.
lines.ar_bare: ولما نشأ سافر إلى مكة مع أبيه.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ رَجَعَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ وَحَضَرَ حَلْقَةَ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: After a while he returned to Tarim and attended the Habib’s circle.
lines.ar_bare: وبعد مدة رجع إلى تريم وحضر حلقة الحبيب.

lines.ar: قَالَتْ أُمُّ أَحْمَدَ: كَانَ جَدُّكَ يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ.
lines.en: Ahmad’s mother said: Your grandfather used to read the Qur’an after dawn.
lines.ar_bare: قالت أم أحمد: كان جدك يقرأ القرآن بعد الفجر.

lines.ar: فَقَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ الْقِصَّةَ لِأُمِّهِ وَلِعُمَرَ.
lines.en: And Ahmad read the story to his mother and to Umar.
lines.ar_bare: فقرأ أحمد القصة لأمه ولعمر.

passages.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ قِصَّةَ جَدِّهِ فِي كِتَابِهِ. وُلِدَ جَدُّهُ فِي تَرِيمَ وَنَشَأَ فِي بَيْتِ عِلْمٍ. وَلَمَّا نَشَأَ سَافَرَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ مَعَ أَبِيهِ. وَبَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ رَجَعَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ وَحَضَرَ حَلْقَةَ الْحَبِيبِ. قَالَتْ أُمُّ أَحْمَدَ: كَانَ جَدُّكَ يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ. فَقَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ الْقِصَّةَ لِأُمِّهِ وَلِعُمَرَ.
passages.en: Ahmad wrote the story of his grandfather in his book. His grandfather was born in Tarim and grew up in a house of knowledge. When he had grown up he travelled to Mecca with his father. After a while he returned to Tarim and attended the Habib’s circle. Ahmad’s mother said: Your grandfather used to read the Qur’an after dawn. And Ahmad read the story to his mother and to Umar.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 150-151 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ سِيرَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: وُلِدَ فِي مَكَّةَ وَنَشَأَ يَتِيمًا وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ.
lines.en: The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ: He was born in Mecca, grew up an orphan, and his grandfather took him in his care.

lines.ar: فَأَحَبَّ الْوَلَدُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ أَكْثَرَ.
lines.en: So the boy loved the Prophet ﷺ even more.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ سِيرَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: وُلِدَ فِي مَكَّةَ وَنَشَأَ يَتِيمًا وَكَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ. فَأَحَبَّ الْوَلَدُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ أَكْثَرَ.
passages.en: The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ: He was born in Mecca, grew up an orphan, and his grandfather took him in his care. So the boy loved the Prophet ﷺ even more.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Then his mother took him back from her and set out with him for Medina to visit his father’s maternal relatives, the Banū ʿAdī b. al-Najjār,

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: and his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib took him into his care.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: When his age, upon him be blessings and peace, reached twelve years, his uncle and guardian wanted to travel with merchandise to Syria.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A sīra (the life of the Prophet ﷺ), from Nūr al-Yaqīn fī sīrat sayyid al-mursalīn of Muḥammad al-Khuḍarī.

questions.q: Where did his mother go with him? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبَتْ بِهِ أُمُّهُ؟
questions.a: To Medina.

questions.q: Who took him into his care? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ كَفَلَهُ؟
questions.a: His grandfather, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.

questions.q: How old was he when his uncle wanted to travel? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: كَمْ كَانَ عُمْرُهُ لَمَّا أَرَادَ عَمُّهُ السَّفَرَ؟
questions.a: Twelve years old.

questions.q: Where did his uncle want to travel, and with what?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ أَرَادَ عَمُّهُ أَنْ يُسَافِرَ؟ وَبِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: To Syria (الشَّام), with merchandise (تِجَارَة).

questions.q: Which word shows this came after earlier events?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ هَذَا جَاءَ بَعْدَ حَدَثٍ قَبْلَهُ؟
questions.a: ثُمَّ: “then”.

questions.q: Which word means “when”? What verb follows it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ بِمَعْنَى «عِنْدَمَا»؟ وَأَيُّ فِعْلٍ بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: لَمَّا, then the past verb بَلَغَتْ (“reached”).

questions.q: Whose maternal relatives (أَخْوَالُ) does the line say they are? Who are they by name?
questions.q_ar: أَخْوَالُ مَنْ هُمْ؟ وَمَا اسْمُهُمْ؟
questions.a: Those of his father (أَخْوَالُ أَبِيهِ): the visit was to his father’s side of the family. The line names them: the Banū ʿAdī b. al-Najjār.

questions.q: The uncle is called two things. What are they, and what does the second one say about his place in the boy’s life?
questions.q_ar: بِأَيِّ وَصْفَيْنِ سُمِّيَ الْعَمُّ؟ وَمَاذَا يَقُولُ الثَّانِي عَنْ مَكَانِهِ فِي حَيَاةِ الْوَلَدِ؟
questions.a: عَمُّهُ (his uncle) and كَفِيلُهُ (his guardian). The second says that the uncle was the one who now looked after the boy.

questions.q: What did the Habib read, and what did Ahmad do? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ؟ وَمَاذَا فَعَلَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: The Habib read from the book of the sīra; Ahmad wrote down what he heard.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: The Prophet ﷺ was born in Mecca on a Monday.

questions.q: Where and on which day was he born?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ وُلِدَ؟ وَفِي أَيِّ يَوْمٍ؟
questions.a: In Mecca, on Monday.

questions.q: What was his mother’s name? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَا اسْمُ أُمِّهِ؟
questions.a: Āmina.

questions.q: Who named him, and what name did he give? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَمَّاهُ؟ وَمَاذَا سَمَّاهُ؟
questions.a: His grandfather named him Muḥammad ﷺ.

questions.q: Put the events in order: (a) he travelled to Syria (b) he was born (c) his mother went with him to Medina (d) his grandfather took him in.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) سَافَرَ إِلَى الشَّامِ (ب) وُلِدَ (ج) ذَهَبَتْ بِهِ أُمُّهُ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ (د) كَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ.
questions.a: b, c, d, a.

questions.q: True or false: Ahmad wrote the notes before the Habib read.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَقْرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ.
questions.a: False: he wrote what he heard (مَا سَمِعَ), so after hearing it.

questions.q: Which word gives the order, and who came first?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُعْطِي التَّرْتِيبَ؟ وَمَنْ جَاءَ أَوَّلًا؟
questions.a: ثُمَّ; the grandfather first, then the uncle.

questions.q: Find the word for “when”. What does نَشَأَ mean?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةَ «عِنْدَمَا». مَا مَعْنَى نَشَأَ؟
questions.a: لَمَّا; نَشَأَ: he grew up.

questions.q: Who did Ahmad say the last sentence to? (line 8)
questions.q_ar: لِمَنْ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ الْجُمْلَةَ الْأَخِيرَةَ؟
questions.a: To Umar.

questions.q: What does Ahmad say the sīra is more than? Why read it?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ أَحْمَدُ عَنِ السِّيرَةِ؟ لِمَاذَا نَقْرَؤُهَا؟
questions.a: More than a story: it holds much wisdom (حِكْمَة), so we read it to learn from it.
questions.ref_ar: السِّيرَةُ قِصَّةٌ، وَلَكِنَّ فِيهَا حِكْمَةً كَثِيرَةً

questions.q: Which verbs in the notes are about a person’s life (events), and which about the circle?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الْأَفْعَالِ تَخُصُّ حَيَاةَ الشَّخْصِ، وَأَيُّهَا تَخُصُّ الْحَلْقَةَ؟
questions.a: Life: وُلِدَ، سَمَّاهُ، ذَهَبَتْ، كَفَلَهُ، نَشَأَ، سَافَرَ. Circle: قَرَأَ، كَتَبَ، سَمِعَ، قَالَ.

questions.q: Translate lines 1 and 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَ وَالثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: Ahmad wrote the story of his grandfather in his book. His grandfather was born in Tarim and grew up in a house of knowledge.

questions.q: The word ولد in line 2 can be “a boy” or “was born”. Which is it here, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: كَلِمَةُ «ولد» فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ قَدْ تَكُونُ «وَلَد» أَوْ «وُلِدَ». أَيُّهُمَا هُنَا؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: “Was born” (وُلِدَ): a place follows it (فِي تَرِيمَ) and the next verb is نَشَأَ.

questions.q: Where did the grandfather travel, and with whom? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ سَافَرَ الْجَدُّ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: To Mecca, with his father.

questions.q: What did he do after a while? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ بَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ؟
questions.a: He returned to Tarim and attended the Habib’s circle.

questions.q: What did Ahmad’s mother say about the grandfather? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَالَتْ أُمُّ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ الْجَدِّ؟
questions.a: He used to read the Qur’an after dawn.

questions.q: To whom did Ahmad read the story? (line 6)
questions.q_ar: لِمَنْ قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ الْقِصَّةَ؟
questions.a: To his mother and to Umar.

questions.q: What kind of text is the story that Ahmad wrote, and what shows it?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ قِصَّةِ أَحْمَدَ؟ وَمَا الدَّلِيلُ؟
questions.a: A life story in the sīra frame: past verbs one after another (وُلِدَ، نَشَأَ، سَافَرَ، رَجَعَ) and words of place and order (فِي، إِلَى، لَمَّا، بَعْدَ).

questions.q: The writer does not say how old the grandfather was. Which word gives only the order, not a number?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُعْطِي التَّرْتِيبَ وَلَا تُعْطِي عَدَدًا؟
questions.a: لَمَّا (“when”): it tells the order of events, and gives no age.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ: He was born in Mecca, grew up an orphan, and his grandfather took him in his care. So the boy loved the Prophet ﷺ even more.

questions.q: Which verb tells that he grew up? Give its meaning.
questions.a: نَشَأَ: he grew up

questions.q: Where was he born?
questions.a: In Mecca (مَكَّةَ).

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy read the life of the Prophet ﷺ.
questions.a: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ سِيرَةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ.

translate.ar: وُلِدَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فِي مَكَّةَ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ.
translate.en: The Prophet ﷺ was born in Mecca on Monday.

translate.ar: نَشَأَ أَحْمَدُ فِي بَيْتِ عِلْمٍ وَحَفِظَ الْقُرْآنَ.
translate.en: Ahmad grew up in a house of knowledge and memorised the Qur’an.
His grandfather took him into his care, and then his uncle did.

translate.ar: سَافَرَ عُمَرُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الشَّامِ بَعْدَ عَامٍ.
translate.en: Umar travelled with his father to Syria after a year.

translate.ar: لَمَّا وُلِدَتْ مَرْيَمُ ذَهَبَ أَبُوهَا إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: When Maryam was born, her father went to the mosque.
The period of his journey was long.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ مِنَ السِّيرَةِ ثُمَّ جَلَسَ مَعَ النَّاسِ.
translate.en: The Habib read from the sīra, then sat with the people.

translate.ar: نَشَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي تَرِيمَ وَسَافَرَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ بَعْدَ سَنَتَيْنِ.
translate.en: The boy grew up in Tarim and travelled to Mecca after two years.

translate.ar: مَاتَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ بَعْدَ عَامٍ وَكَفَلَهُ عَمُّهُ.
translate.en: Ahmad’s father died after a year, and his uncle took him into his care.

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ مِنَ السِّيرَةِ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ.
lines.en: The Habib read from the sīra after dawn.

lines.ar: وُلِدَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فِي مَكَّةَ ثُمَّ كَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ.
lines.en: The Prophet ﷺ was born in Mecca, and then his grandfather took him into his care.

lines.ar: وَلَمَّا نَشَأَ سَافَرَ مَعَ عَمِّهِ إِلَى الشَّامِ.
lines.en: When he had grown up he travelled with his uncle to Syria.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ مِنَ السِّيرَةِ بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ. وُلِدَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ فِي مَكَّةَ ثُمَّ كَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ. وَلَمَّا نَشَأَ سَافَرَ مَعَ عَمِّهِ إِلَى الشَّامِ.
translate.en: The Habib read from the sīra after dawn. The Prophet ﷺ was born in Mecca, and then his grandfather took him into his care. When he had grown up he travelled with his uncle to Syria.
Ahmad was born in Tarim.
He grew up in a house of knowledge.
Maryam grew up with her grandfather.
His uncle took him into his care.
Then he travelled to Mecca.
After a year he returned to the house.
When he had grown up he travelled with his father.
The Habib read from the sīra after the prayer.
translate.ar: قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ مِنَ السِّيرَةِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ.

translate.en: She was born on Friday in Mecca.
The period of the pregnancy was long.
The Prophet ﷺ was born in Mecca.
Umar’s grandfather took him in, and then he travelled to Syria.
translate.ar: كَفَلَهُ جَدُّهُ ثُمَّ سَافَرَ إِلَى الشَّامِ.
alt: كَفَلَ جَدُّ عُمَرَ عُمَرَ ثُمَّ سَافَرَ إِلَى الشَّامِ.

readings.title_en: A scholar’s life-entry and a classical letter
readings.question_en: How do I read a scholar’s biography entry, and the opening and closing of a classical letter?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ تَرْجَمَةَ عَالِمٍ وَبِدَايَةَ الرِّسَالَةِ وَنِهَايَتَهَا؟

passages.intro_en: From the entry of a scholar. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Khulāṣat al-Athar of al-Muḥibbī (the entry of Abū Bakr b. Aḥmad al-Shillī Bāʿalawī)
passages.cite: Tarjama: Muḥammad Amīn al-Muḥibbī, Khulāṣat al-athar fī aʿyān al-qarn al-ḥādī ʿashar (d. 1111 AH), the entry of al-sayyid Abū Bakr b. Aḥmad al-Shillī Bāʿalawī, which quotes his son Muḥammad al-Shillī's al-Mashraʿ al-Rawī; Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, id 48410, 1978 pp; the same work is Shamela 3.28 id 7146), copy pages 71–72 (its own counter; printed edition not identified). Letters: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, part 1 ("Jāmiʿ al-mukātabāt wa-l-waṣāyā wa-l-kalimāt wa-l-qaṣāʾid"), a printed edition (publisher and year not identified from the scan; TLNOOR id 144, OCR PDF), printed p. 43 (lines 7–10: the opening of the first letter) and p. 92 (lines 11–14: the end of a later letter); read against the page images. Abridged: lines 3–5 of the tarjama (the research file has 14 lines); the copy is unvowelled and the vowels are added by the course (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: فَقَامَ بِتَرْبِيَتِهِ شَيْخُهُ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ شِهَابِ الدِّينِ
lines.en: and his teacher, the Shaykh of Islam ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, undertook his upbringing.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ اشْتَغَلَ بِتَحْصِيلِ الْعُلُومِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ فَقَرَأَ الْفِقْهَ عَلَى شَيْخِهِ الْمَذْكُورِ
lines.en: Then he busied himself acquiring the religious sciences, and read jurisprudence with the teacher just mentioned,

lines.ar: وَقَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ فِي الْحَدِيثِ وَالتَّفْسِيرِ وَالتَّصَوُّفِ وَالْعَرَبِيَّةِ
lines.en: and read with him in ḥadīth, Qurʾān commentary, Sufism and Arabic.

passages.ar: فَقَامَ بِتَرْبِيَتِهِ شَيْخُهُ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ شِهَابِ الدِّينِ ثُمَّ اشْتَغَلَ بِتَحْصِيلِ الْعُلُومِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ فَقَرَأَ الْفِقْهَ عَلَى شَيْخِهِ الْمَذْكُورِ وَقَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ فِي الْحَدِيثِ وَالتَّفْسِيرِ وَالتَّصَوُّفِ وَالْعَرَبِيَّةِ
passages.en: and his teacher, the Shaykh of Islam ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, undertook his upbringing. Then he busied himself acquiring the religious sciences, and read jurisprudence with the teacher just mentioned, and read with him in ḥadīth, Qurʾān commentary, Sufism and Arabic.

passages.intro_en: From the letters of Imam al-Ḥaddād. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād (the greeting of a letter, and the end of another)
passages.cite: Tarjama: Muḥammad Amīn al-Muḥibbī, Khulāṣat al-athar fī aʿyān al-qarn al-ḥādī ʿashar (d. 1111 AH), the entry of al-sayyid Abū Bakr b. Aḥmad al-Shillī Bāʿalawī, which quotes his son Muḥammad al-Shillī's al-Mashraʿ al-Rawī; Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, id 48410, 1978 pp; the same work is Shamela 3.28 id 7146), copy pages 71–72 (its own counter; printed edition not identified). Letters: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, part 1 ("Jāmiʿ al-mukātabāt wa-l-waṣāyā wa-l-kalimāt wa-l-qaṣāʾid"), a printed edition (publisher and year not identified from the scan; TLNOOR id 144, OCR PDF), printed p. 43 (lines 7–10: the opening of the first letter) and p. 92 (lines 11–14: the end of a later letter); read against the page images. Abridged: line 10 is the greeting and hinge of the first letter, lines 11, 12 and 14 are the end of a later letter (line 13 left out); the printed page is unvowelled and the vowels are added by the course (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: وَبَعْدُ، فَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، وَمَغْفِرَتُهُ وَرِضْوَانُهُ، وَقَدْ وَصَلَ إِلَيْنَا
lines.en: And then: peace be upon you, and God's mercy, blessings, forgiveness and good pleasure; and there has reached us...

lines.ar: وَقَدْ وَصَلَتْ مِنْكُمْ حَفِظَكُمُ اللهُ إِلَيْنَا كُتُبٌ عَدِيدَةٌ، وَكُلُّهَا حَسَنَةٌ مُفِيدَةٌ
lines.en: (Letter, closing, from a later letter in the same book:) Many letters from you, God keep you, have reached us, all of them good and useful.

lines.ar: وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا أَنْتُمْ مِنْ صَالِحِ دُعَائِكُمْ
lines.en: And do not forget us in your good prayers.

lines.ar: وَالسَّلَامُ
lines.en: And peace.

passages.ar: وَبَعْدُ، فَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، وَمَغْفِرَتُهُ وَرِضْوَانُهُ، وَقَدْ وَصَلَ إِلَيْنَا وَقَدْ وَصَلَتْ مِنْكُمْ حَفِظَكُمُ اللهُ إِلَيْنَا كُتُبٌ عَدِيدَةٌ، وَكُلُّهَا حَسَنَةٌ مُفِيدَةٌ وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا أَنْتُمْ مِنْ صَالِحِ دُعَائِكُمْ وَالسَّلَامُ
passages.en: And then: peace be upon you, and God's mercy, blessings, forgiveness and good pleasure; and there has reached us... (Letter, closing, from a later letter in the same book:) Many letters from you, God keep you, have reached us, all of them good and useful. And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.

passages.intro_en: A short text: a letter from Ahmad to his father. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: مِنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ إِلَى أَبِيهِ الْكَرِيمِ.
lines.en: From Ahmad b. ʿAlī to his noble father.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدُ، فَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ.
lines.en: And now: peace be upon you, and God’s mercy and blessings.

lines.ar: وَقَدْ وَصَلَ إِلَيْنَا كِتَابُكُمْ وَقَرَأْنَاهُ، فَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.
lines.en: Your letter has reached us and we have read it, so praise be to God.

lines.ar: نَحْنُ فِي خَيْرٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ، وَقَدْ حَضَرْتُ دَرْسَ الْحَبِيبِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
lines.en: We are well and in good health, and I have attended the Habib’s lesson every day.

lines.ar: وَقَرَأْتُ مِنَ السِّيرَةِ وَوَجَدْتُ فِيهَا حِكْمَةً كَثِيرَةً.
lines.en: I have read from the sīra and found much wisdom in it.

lines.ar: وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا مِنْ صَالِحِ دُعَائِكُمْ.
lines.en: And do not forget us in your good prayers.

lines.ar: وَالسَّلَامُ.
lines.en: And peace.

passages.ar: مِنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ إِلَى أَبِيهِ الْكَرِيمِ. وَبَعْدُ، فَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ. وَقَدْ وَصَلَ إِلَيْنَا كِتَابُكُمْ وَقَرَأْنَاهُ، فَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. نَحْنُ فِي خَيْرٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ، وَقَدْ حَضَرْتُ دَرْسَ الْحَبِيبِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. وَقَرَأْتُ مِنَ السِّيرَةِ وَوَجَدْتُ فِيهَا حِكْمَةً كَثِيرَةً. وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا مِنْ صَالِحِ دُعَائِكُمْ. وَالسَّلَامُ.
passages.en: From Ahmad b. ʿAlī to his noble father. And now: peace be upon you, and God’s mercy and blessings. Your letter has reached us and we have read it, so praise be to God. We are well and in good health, and I have attended the Habib’s lesson every day. I have read from the sīra and found much wisdom in it. And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.

passages.intro_en: A bare paragraph: no vowels. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (Shaykh Sālim is a course name). Printed without vowels for the student; the key has them.

lines.ar: هَذِهِ تَرْجَمَةُ الشَّيْخِ سَالِمِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، كَتَبَهَا أَحْمَدُ بَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ.
lines.en: This is the biography of Shaykh Sālim b. ʿAlī; Ahmad wrote it after the lesson.
lines.ar_bare: هذه ترجمة الشيخ سالم بن علي، كتبها أحمد بعد الدرس.

lines.ar: وُلِدَ الشَّيْخُ سَالِمٌ فِي تَرِيمَ وَنَشَأَ فِي بَيْتٍ صَالِحٍ.
lines.en: Shaykh Sālim was born in Tarim and grew up in a righteous house.
lines.ar_bare: ولد الشيخ سالم في تريم ونشأ في بيت صالح.

lines.ar: حَفِظَ الْقُرْآنَ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَلَى شَيْخِهِ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
lines.en: He memorised the Qur’an, then read with his shaykh in the mosque.
lines.ar_bare: حفظ القرآن ثم قرأ على شيخه في المسجد.

lines.ar: وَسَافَرَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ وَحَجَّ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ وَعَلَّمَ النَّاسَ.
lines.en: He travelled to Mecca and made the pilgrimage, then returned to Tarim and taught the people.
lines.ar_bare: وسافر إلى مكة وحج، ثم رجع إلى تريم وعلم الناس.

lines.ar: وَتُوُفِّيَ وَعُمْرُهُ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً.
lines.en: He died when his age was seventy years.
lines.ar_bare: وتوفي وعمره سبعون سنة.

lines.ar: وَدُفِنَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: And he was buried in Tarim.
lines.ar_bare: ودفن في تريم.

passages.ar: هَذِهِ تَرْجَمَةُ الشَّيْخِ سَالِمِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، كَتَبَهَا أَحْمَدُ بَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ. وُلِدَ الشَّيْخُ سَالِمٌ فِي تَرِيمَ وَنَشَأَ فِي بَيْتٍ صَالِحٍ. حَفِظَ الْقُرْآنَ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَلَى شَيْخِهِ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ. وَسَافَرَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ وَحَجَّ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ وَعَلَّمَ النَّاسَ. وَتُوُفِّيَ وَعُمْرُهُ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً. وَدُفِنَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
passages.en: This is the biography of Shaykh Sālim b. ʿAlī; Ahmad wrote it after the lesson. Shaykh Sālim was born in Tarim and grew up in a righteous house. He memorised the Qur’an, then read with his shaykh in the mosque. He travelled to Mecca and made the pilgrimage, then returned to Tarim and taught the people. He died when his age was seventy years. And he was buried in Tarim.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 152-153 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً مِنْ رَسَائِلِ الْإِمَامِ.
lines.en: The boy copied out a letter from the letters of the Imam.

lines.ar: وَكَانَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا: وَبَعْدُ، وَفِي آخِرِهَا: وَالسَّلَامُ.
lines.en: At its beginning was: “And now”, and at its end: “And peace”.

passages.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً مِنْ رَسَائِلِ الْإِمَامِ. وَكَانَ فِي أَوَّلِهَا: وَبَعْدُ، وَفِي آخِرِهَا: وَالسَّلَامُ.
passages.en: The boy copied out a letter from the letters of the Imam. At its beginning was: “And now”, and at its end: “And peace”.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: and his teacher, the Shaykh of Islam ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, undertook his upbringing.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: Then he busied himself acquiring the religious sciences, and read jurisprudence with the teacher just mentioned,

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: and read with him in ḥadīth, Qur’ān commentary, Sufism and Arabic.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A biography entry (tarjama) of a scholar, from Khulāṣat al-Athar of al-Muḥibbī.

questions.q: Who undertook his upbringing? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ قَامَ بِتَرْبِيَتِهِ؟
questions.a: His teacher, the Shaykh of Islam ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn.

questions.q: Which sciences did he read with that teacher? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: أَيَّ الْعُلُومِ قَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: Ḥadīth, Qur’ān commentary (tafsīr), Sufism and Arabic. (Jurisprudence, in line 2.)

questions.q: What does ثُمَّ show at the start of line 2?
questions.q_ar: عَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ «ثُمَّ» فِي بِدَايَةِ السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: The next stage of his life: after his upbringing, his studies.

questions.q: Which little word comes after قَرَأَ and means “with (a teacher)”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ بَعْدَ «قَرَأَ» يَعْنِي «عِنْدَ شَيْخٍ»؟
questions.a: عَلَى.

questions.q: Who is “his teacher just mentioned” (الْمَذْكُور)?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ «شَيْخُهُ الْمَذْكُورُ»؟
questions.a: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Shihāb al-Dīn, named in line 1.

questions.q: What does بْنُ mean here? How many names make up the teacher’s name?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى «بْنُ» هُنَا؟ كَمْ شَخْصًا فِي الِاسْمِ؟
questions.a: بْنُ = “son of”. The name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, son of Shihāb al-Dīn: one person, with a title (شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ) before it.

questions.q: Why does line 2 write “his teacher just mentioned” and not the name again?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَمْ يُكَرِّرِ الْكَاتِبُ الِاسْمَ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: The entry has already named him in line 1; a biography avoids repeating a name that is clear.

questions.q: Translate line 1 (it stops where the source goes on).
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: And now: peace be upon you, and God’s mercy, blessings, forgiveness and good pleasure; and there has reached us…

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: Many letters from you, God keep you, have reached us, all of them good and useful.

questions.q: Translate lines 3 and 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَيْنِ الثَّالِثَ وَالرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A classical letter (the greeting and the end), from Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: What does وَبَعْدُ do in a letter?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ «وَبَعْدُ» فِي الرِّسَالَةِ؟
questions.a: It is the hinge: it follows the address (from … to …) and leads into the greeting and the letter’s message.

questions.q: How many blessings are named after “peace” in line 1? Which?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ دُعَاءً بَعْدَ «السَّلَامِ» فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟ مَا هِيَ؟
questions.a: Four: mercy, blessings, forgiveness, good pleasure.

questions.q: What is this little phrase inside line 2, and who is it said to?
questions.q_ar: مَا هَذِهِ الْعِبَارَةُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟ وَلِمَنْ تُقَالُ؟
questions.a: “God keep you”: a short prayer for the receiver, said to him by the writer.

questions.q: What does the writer ask of the receiver in line 3?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَطْلُبُ الْكَاتِبُ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ؟
questions.a: Not to forget him in his good prayers: a request for du‘ā’.
questions.ref_ar: وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا أَنْتُمْ مِنْ صَالِحِ دُعَائِكُمْ

questions.q: Which word ends the letter?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُنْهِي الرِّسَالَةَ؟
questions.a: وَالسَّلَامُ: “and peace”.

questions.q: The letter is to one man, yet it says عَلَيْكُمْ (“you all”). Why?
questions.q_ar: الرِّسَالَةُ إِلَى رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ لَكِنَّهَا تَقُولُ «عَلَيْكُمْ». لِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: The plural of respect: a writer honours the one he writes to by using “you” in the plural.

questions.q: Line 2 says the letters were “good and useful”. What do the writer’s words tell you about how the two men wrote to each other?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تُخْبِرُنَا كَلِمَاتُ السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي عَنْ مُكَاتَبَةِ الرَّجُلَيْنِ؟
questions.a: They wrote often: many letters had arrived, and the writer valued them.

questions.q: Who writes the letter, and to whom? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَكْتُبُ الرِّسَالَةَ؟ وَإِلَى مَنْ؟
questions.a: Ahmad b. ʿAlī writes to his father.

questions.q: Which little word marks the writer, and which the receiver?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ لِلْكَاتِبِ؟ وَأَيُّ حَرْفٍ لِلْمُرْسَلِ إِلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: مِنْ: the writer. إِلَى: the receiver.
questions.ref_ar: مِنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ إِلَى أَبِيهِ

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And now: peace be upon you, and God’s mercy and blessings.

questions.q: What reached Ahmad, and what did he do with it? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا وَصَلَ إِلَى أَحْمَدَ؟ وَمَاذَا فَعَلَ بِهِ؟
questions.a: His father’s letter reached him, and he read it.

questions.q: How are they? What has Ahmad attended? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ حَالُهُمْ؟ وَمَاذَا حَضَرَ أَحْمَدُ؟
questions.a: They are well and in good health; he attended the Habib’s lesson every day.

questions.q: What did Ahmad read and find? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَاذَا وَجَدَ؟
questions.a: He read from the sīra and found much wisdom in it.

questions.q: Find the request for prayer. What does he ask?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ طَلَبَ الدُّعَاءِ. مَاذَا يَطْلُبُ؟
questions.a: Line 6: not to forget him in his father’s good prayers.

questions.q: Which part of the letter is this?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ جُزْءٍ مِنَ الرِّسَالَةِ هَذَا؟
questions.a: The end.

questions.q: Put the parts in order: (a) the request for prayer (b) from … to … (c) and peace (d) the greeting and وَبَعْدُ.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَجْزَاءَ: (أ) طَلَبُ الدُّعَاءِ (ب) مِنْ … إِلَى … (ج) وَالسَّلَامُ (د) التَّحِيَّةُ وَ«وَبَعْدُ».
questions.a: b, d, a, c.

questions.q: Which lines are the “business” of the letter, between the hinge and the request?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ السُّطُورِ هِيَ «الْمَوْضُوعُ» بَيْنَ «وَبَعْدُ» وَطَلَبِ الدُّعَاءِ؟
questions.a: Lines 3–5: the news (the letter reached us, we are well, I have attended and read).

questions.q: Translate lines 1 and 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَ وَالثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: This is the biography of Shaykh Sālim b. ʿAlī; Ahmad wrote it after the lesson. Shaykh Sālim was born in Tarim and grew up in a righteous house.

questions.q: What kind of text is this?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟
questions.a: A biography entry (tarjama) of a scholar.

questions.q: What did he do first, and with whom did he read? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ أَوَّلًا؟ وَعِنْدَ مَنْ قَرَأَ؟
questions.a: He memorised the Qur’an, then read with his shaykh in the mosque.

questions.q: What did he do after Mecca? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ بَعْدَ مَكَّةَ؟
questions.a: He returned to Tarim and taught the people.

questions.q: How old was he when he died? Which word tells you “his age”?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ كَانَ عُمْرُهُ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «سِنَّهُ»؟
questions.a: Seventy years old; عُمْرُهُ is “his age”.

questions.q: The word توفي in line 5 has no vowels. What does it say, and what does it mean?
questions.q_ar: كَلِمَةُ «توفي» بِلَا حَرَكَاتٍ. كَيْفَ تُقْرَأُ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: وَتُوُفِّيَ (passive): “and he died”.

questions.q: Where was he buried? What does دفن say?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ دُفِنَ؟ كَيْفَ تُقْرَأُ «دفن»؟
questions.a: In Tarim. وَدُفِنَ: “and he was buried”.

questions.q: Which verbs of the entry have no doer named, and why does an entry like to use them?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الْأَفْعَالِ بِلَا فَاعِلٍ؟ وَلِمَاذَا تُحِبُّهَا التَّرْجَمَةُ؟
questions.a: وُلِدَ، تُوُفِّيَ، دُفِنَ: these three events are not done by the man himself. A life-entry names the person and the event, not who did it.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy copied out a letter from the letters of the Imam. At its beginning was: “And now”, and at its end: “And peace”.

questions.q: Which word begins the main part of the letter, and which word closes it?
questions.a: وَبَعْدُ begins it (“and now”); وَالسَّلَامُ closes it (“and peace”).

questions.q: What is the singular of رَسَائِلِ?
questions.a: رِسَالَة (a letter)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy wrote a letter.
questions.a: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً.

translate.ar: وُلِدَ الشَّيْخُ سَالِمٌ فِي تَرِيمَ وَنَشَأَ فِي بَيْتِ عِلْمٍ.
translate.en: Shaykh Sālim was born in Tarim and grew up in a house of knowledge.

translate.ar: حَفِظَ الْقُرْآنَ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَلَى شَيْخِهِ فِي الْفِقْهِ.
translate.en: He memorised the Qur’an, then read jurisprudence with his shaykh.

translate.ar: سَافَرَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ وَحَجَّ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
translate.en: He travelled to Mecca and made the pilgrimage, then returned to Tarim.

translate.ar: تُوُفِّيَ وَعُمْرُهُ سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً وَدُفِنَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
translate.en: He died at the age of seventy and was buried in Tarim.
From Umar to his friend Ahmad.
And now: peace be upon you, and God’s mercy.
Your letter has reached us and we have read it.

translate.ar: وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا مِنْ صَالِحِ دُعَائِكُمْ، وَالسَّلَامُ.
translate.en: And do not forget us in your good prayers. And peace.

translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ تَرْجَمَةَ جَدِّهِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
translate.en: Ahmad wrote the biography of his grandfather in his book.

lines.ar: وُلِدَ الشَّيْخُ فِي تَرِيمَ وَقَرَأَ عَلَى شَيْخِهِ فِي الْفِقْهِ.
lines.en: The shaykh was born in Tarim and read jurisprudence with his teacher.

lines.ar: وَتُوُفِّيَ فِي تَرِيمَ وَدُفِنَ فِيهَا.
lines.en: He died in Tarim and was buried in it.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدُ، فَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا مِنْ دُعَائِكُمْ، وَالسَّلَامُ.
lines.en: And now: peace be upon you, and do not forget us in your prayers. And peace.

translate.ar: وُلِدَ الشَّيْخُ فِي تَرِيمَ وَقَرَأَ عَلَى شَيْخِهِ فِي الْفِقْهِ. وَتُوُفِّيَ فِي تَرِيمَ وَدُفِنَ فِيهَا. وَبَعْدُ، فَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، وَلَا تَنْسَوْنَا مِنْ دُعَائِكُمْ، وَالسَّلَامُ.
translate.en: The shaykh was born in Tarim and read jurisprudence with his teacher. He died in Tarim and was buried in it. And now: peace be upon you, and do not forget us in your prayers. And peace.
The shaykh was born in Tarim.
He read jurisprudence with his shaykh.
He travelled to Mecca, then returned to Tarim.
translate.ar: سَافَرَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
alt: وَسَافَرَ إِلَى مَكَّةَ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.

translate.en: He died in Tarim.
And he was buried in Tarim.
His age was seventy years.
From Ahmad to his father.
And now: peace be upon you.
Your letter has reached us.
Do not forget us in your prayers.
And peace.
Maryam wrote her grandfather’s biography.

readings.title_en: The majlis record: who is speaking?
readings.question_en: In a record of a majlis, whose words am I reading: the writer’s or the teacher’s? Which little formulas tell me?
readings.question_ar: مَنِ الَّذِي يَتَكَلَّمُ فِي مَا كُتِبَ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ؟ وَكَيْفَ أَعْرِفُ كَلَامَ الشَّيْخِ مِنْ كَلَامِ الْكَاتِبِ؟

passages.intro_en: A page of a record of a majlis: the second saying. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Tathbīt al-Fuʾād bi-dhikr majālis al-Quṭb ʿAbdallāh al-Ḥaddād, collected by Aḥmad b. ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Ḥasāwī al-Shajjār
passages.cite: Aḥmad b. ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Ḥasāwī, Tathbīt al-Fuʾād bi-dhikr majālis al-Quṭb ʿAbdallāh al-Ḥaddād, Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih Sufi library, id 184280, 734 pp, digital; no publisher or year; also an epub in TLNOOR 697 and a three-volume OCR PDF in TLNOOR 905–907), page 100 of the copy (digital pagination: the page column equals the record id); printed edition not identified. Lines 4-8 of the page (the second saying; lines 1-3 are on the slides). The copy is unvowelled: vowelled for learners by the course, a letter-for-letter match with the copy. In the line beginning مَعَ رِزْقِهِ the verb فَيَتَّسِعُ is read as the start of a new clause (indicative); the other reading is فَيَتَّسِعَ (subjunctive).

lines.ar: وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ: سَمِعْنَا فِيمَا بَلَغَنَا: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً مُوَكَّلِينَ بِخَزَائِنِ أَرْزَاقِ الْعِبَادِ
lines.en: And he, God be pleased with him, said: We have heard, in what has reached us, that God has angels put in charge of the stores of the servants' provisions,

lines.ar: وَإِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا
lines.en: and that the servant has in every moment a known provision.

lines.ar: فَإِذَا أَطَاعَ الْعَبْدُ رَبَّهُ وَأَحْسَنَ لَهُ الْمُعَامَلَةَ أَمَرَ اللهُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ الْمُوَكَّلِينَ بِخَزَائِنِ أَرْزَاقِ الْعِبَادِ أَنْ يُعَجِّلُوا لَهُ مِنْ رِزْقِهِ فِي الْوَقْتِ الْآتِي
lines.en: So when the servant obeys his Lord and deals well with Him, God commands the angels in charge of the stores to hasten for him some of his provision of the coming time,

lines.ar: مَعَ رِزْقِهِ فِي الْوَقْتِ الْحَاضِرِ، فَيَتَّسِعُ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فِيهِ
lines.en: together with his provision of the present time, so his provision widens for him in it.

lines.ar: وَإِذَا عَصَى وَأَسَاءَ الْمُعَامَلَةَ أَمَرَ الْخَزَنَةَ وَقَالَ: ادَّخِرُوا رِزْقَ هَذَا لَهُ فِي الْخَزَائِنِ
lines.en: And when he disobeys and deals badly, He commands the keepers and says: store this one's provision for him in the stores.

passages.ar: وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ: سَمِعْنَا فِيمَا بَلَغَنَا: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَلَائِكَةً مُوَكَّلِينَ بِخَزَائِنِ أَرْزَاقِ الْعِبَادِ وَإِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا فَإِذَا أَطَاعَ الْعَبْدُ رَبَّهُ وَأَحْسَنَ لَهُ الْمُعَامَلَةَ أَمَرَ اللهُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ الْمُوَكَّلِينَ بِخَزَائِنِ أَرْزَاقِ الْعِبَادِ أَنْ يُعَجِّلُوا لَهُ مِنْ رِزْقِهِ فِي الْوَقْتِ الْآتِي مَعَ رِزْقِهِ فِي الْوَقْتِ الْحَاضِرِ، فَيَتَّسِعُ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فِيهِ وَإِذَا عَصَى وَأَسَاءَ الْمُعَامَلَةَ أَمَرَ الْخَزَنَةَ وَقَالَ: ادَّخِرُوا رِزْقَ هَذَا لَهُ فِي الْخَزَائِنِ
passages.en: And he, God be pleased with him, said: We have heard, in what has reached us, that God has angels put in charge of the stores of the servants' provisions, and that the servant has in every moment a known provision. So when the servant obeys his Lord and deals well with Him, God commands the angels in charge of the stores to hasten for him some of his provision of the coming time, together with his provision of the present time, so his provision widens for him in it. And when he disobeys and deals badly, He commands the keepers and says: store this one's provision for him in the stores.

passages.intro_en: A short text: the notebook of Ahmad. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: After the prayer Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s majlis.

lines.ar: فَتَحَ أَحْمَدُ كِتَابَهُ وَكَتَبَ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: Ahmad opened his book and wrote down the Habib’s speech.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الرِّزْقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ، فَاشْكُرِ اللَّهَ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Provision is from Allah, so thank Allah.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ شَكَرَ اللَّهَ أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ رِزْقًا كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: Then he said, as to the sense: Whoever thanks Allah, Allah gives him much provision.

lines.ar: وَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ أَحْمَدَ: لِمَاذَا كَتَبْتَ «مَا مَعْنَاهُ»؟
lines.en: And Umar asked Ahmad: Why did you write “as to the sense”?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: لِأَنِّي سَمِعْتُ الْمَعْنَى وَلَمْ أَحْفَظْ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَاتِ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: Because I heard the meaning and did not memorise every word.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: حَسَنٌ، اُكْتُبْ مَا سَمِعْتَ، وَلَا تَكْتُبْ مَا لَمْ تَسْمَعْ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Good. Write what you heard, and do not write what you did not hear.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ لِعُمَرَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِالْحَبِيبِ وَبِكَلَامِهِ.
lines.en: After the lesson Ahmad said to Umar: May Allah benefit us by the Habib and by his speech.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ لِأُمِّهِ.
lines.en: He returned to the house and read the Habib’s speech to his mother.

lines.ar: وَقَالَتْ أُمُّهُ: نَفَعَكَ اللَّهُ يَا بُنَيَّ.
lines.en: And his mother said: May Allah benefit you, my son.

passages.ar: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحَبِيبِ. فَتَحَ أَحْمَدُ كِتَابَهُ وَكَتَبَ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الرِّزْقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ، فَاشْكُرِ اللَّهَ. ثُمَّ قَالَ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ شَكَرَ اللَّهَ أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ رِزْقًا كَثِيرًا. وَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ أَحْمَدَ: لِمَاذَا كَتَبْتَ «مَا مَعْنَاهُ»؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: لِأَنِّي سَمِعْتُ الْمَعْنَى وَلَمْ أَحْفَظْ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَاتِ. فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: حَسَنٌ، اُكْتُبْ مَا سَمِعْتَ، وَلَا تَكْتُبْ مَا لَمْ تَسْمَعْ. وَبَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ لِعُمَرَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِالْحَبِيبِ وَبِكَلَامِهِ. وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ لِأُمِّهِ. وَقَالَتْ أُمُّهُ: نَفَعَكَ اللَّهُ يَا بُنَيَّ.
passages.en: After the prayer Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s majlis. Ahmad opened his book and wrote down the Habib’s speech. The Habib said: Provision is from Allah, so thank Allah. Then he said, as to the sense: Whoever thanks Allah, Allah gives him much provision. And Umar asked Ahmad: Why did you write “as to the sense”? Ahmad said: Because I heard the meaning and did not memorise every word. The Habib said: Good. Write what you heard, and do not write what you did not hear. After the lesson Ahmad said to Umar: May Allah benefit us by the Habib and by his speech. He returned to the house and read the Habib’s speech to his mother. And his mother said: May Allah benefit you, my son.

passages.intro_en: One paragraph with no vowels: a record of the Habib’s majlis. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (vowelled in the key; the student book shows no vowels).

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: إِنَّ لِلطَّالِبِ أَدَبًا مَعَ مُعَلِّمِهِ.
lines.en: And the Habib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The student has manners to keep with his teacher.
lines.ar_bare: وقال الحبيب رضي الله عنه: إن للطالب أدبا مع معلمه.

lines.ar: فَمَنْ جَلَسَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَلْيَسْمَعْ، وَلَا يَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: So whoever sits in the majlis, let him listen, and let him not talk much.
lines.ar_bare: فمن جلس في المجلس فليسمع، ولا يتكلم كثيرا.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ عَمِلَ بِعِلْمِهِ نَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ بِهِ.
lines.en: And he said, as to the sense: Whoever acts on his knowledge, Allah benefits him by it.
lines.ar_bare: وقال ما معناه: من عمل بعلمه نفعه الله به.

lines.ar: وَسَمِعْنَا مِنْهُ أَنَّ الرِّزْقَ مِنَ اللَّهِ، وَأَنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ رِزْقًا فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ.
lines.en: And we heard from him that provision is from Allah, and that the servant has a provision in every time.
lines.ar_bare: وسمعنا منه أن الرزق من الله، وأن للعبد رزقا في كل وقت.

lines.ar: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ وَبِكَلَامِهِ.
lines.en: May Allah benefit us by him and by his speech.
lines.ar_bare: نفعنا الله به وبكلامه.

passages.ar: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: إِنَّ لِلطَّالِبِ أَدَبًا مَعَ مُعَلِّمِهِ. فَمَنْ جَلَسَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَلْيَسْمَعْ، وَلَا يَتَكَلَّمْ كَثِيرًا. وَقَالَ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ عَمِلَ بِعِلْمِهِ نَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ بِهِ. وَسَمِعْنَا مِنْهُ أَنَّ الرِّزْقَ مِنَ اللَّهِ، وَأَنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ رِزْقًا فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ. نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ وَبِكَلَامِهِ.
passages.en: And the Habib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The student has manners to keep with his teacher. So whoever sits in the majlis, let him listen, and let him not talk much. And he said, as to the sense: Whoever acts on his knowledge, Allah benefits him by it. And we heard from him that provision is from Allah, and that the servant has a provision in every time. May Allah benefit us by him and by his speech.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 154-155 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: إِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا.
lines.en: The Habib said, in meaning: The servant has in every moment a known provision.

lines.ar: وَكَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ.
lines.en: And the boy wrote that down and said: May Allah benefit us through him.

passages.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: إِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا. وَكَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ: نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ.
passages.en: The Habib said, in meaning: The servant has in every moment a known provision. And the boy wrote that down and said: May Allah benefit us through him.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A record of a majlis: sayings of Imam al-Ḥaddād, written down by a student, from Tathbīt al-Fuʾād.

questions.q: Which words open the passage and show that someone else is speaking?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَفْتَحُ النَّصَّ وَتَدُلُّ عَلَى مُتَكَلِّمٍ آخَرَ؟
questions.a: وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: “and he said, may Allah be pleased with him”. The saying follows the colon.

questions.q: What do these words tell you about how the teacher knows what he says next?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتُ عَنْ مَصْدَرِ مَا يَقُولُهُ بَعْدَهَا؟
questions.a: He says it reached him from others (“we heard in what has reached us”): he reports it, he does not claim it as his own discovery.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: And he said, God be pleased with him: We have heard, in what has reached us, that God has angels put in charge of the stores of the servants’ provisions,

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: and that the servant has in every moment a known provision.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: So when the servant obeys his Lord and deals well with Him, God commands the angels in charge of the stores to hasten for him some of his provision of the coming time,

questions.q: True or false: the servant’s provision is not known.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: رِزْقُ الْعَبْدِ غَيْرُ مَعْلُومٍ.
questions.a: False. The provision is مَعْلُومًا, known (to God, who has set it).
questions.ref_ar: وَإِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ رِزْقًا مَعْلُومًا

questions.q: What does God command the angels when the servant obeys?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَأْمُرُ اللَّهُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ إِذَا أَطَاعَ الْعَبْدُ؟
questions.a: To hasten for him some of the provision of the coming time, together with that of the present time.

questions.q: What happens to the servant’s provision then?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَحْدُثُ لِرِزْقِ الْعَبْدِ حِينَئِذٍ؟
questions.a: It widens for him.

questions.q: What happens when the servant disobeys and deals badly? What is commanded?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَحْدُثُ إِذَا عَصَى الْعَبْدُ وَأَسَاءَ الْمُعَامَلَةَ؟
questions.a: God commands the keepers: store this one’s provision for him in the stores.

questions.q: Who says ادَّخِرُوا, and to whom? How can you tell it is a quotation inside the quotation?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقُولُ «ادَّخِرُوا»؟ وَلِمَنْ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ أَنَّهُ كَلَامٌ دَاخِلَ كَلَامٍ؟
questions.a: God says it to the keepers. وَقَالَ and the colon open it, inside the teacher’s own report.

questions.q: Find the word that means “provisions” in line 1. What is its singular, and what lesson taught it?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةَ «أَرْزَاقٍ» فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ. مَا مُفْرَدُهَا؟
questions.a: أَرْزَاقِ is the plural of رِزْق (this lesson).

questions.q: Both halves speak of obeying and disobeying. What does each half teach about provision?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُعَلِّمُ كُلُّ نِصْفٍ عَنِ الرِّزْقِ؟
questions.a: Obedience brings provision sooner and wider; disobedience delays it. In both, the provision is already decreed: the servant’s conduct changes when it reaches him.

questions.q: The writer uses “God be pleased with him” and “we heard in what reached us” in one passage. Why does a careful record keep these formulas?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَحْفَظُ السِّجِلُّ الدَّقِيقُ هَذَيْنِ التَّعْبِيرَيْنِ؟
questions.a: The first marks whose saying it is, with respect; the second tells the reader how far the teacher himself stands behind the report. A reader sees both the speaker and the source.

questions.q: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
questions.a: In the Habib’s majlis, with Umar, after the prayer.

questions.q: What did Ahmad write in his book?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ؟
questions.a: The speech of the Habib.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: The Habib said: Provision is from Allah, so thank Allah.

questions.q: Which two words tell you the writer gives only the sense of line 4?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَدُلَّانِ عَلَى أَنَّ الْكَاتِبَ يَنْقُلُ الْمَعْنَى فَقَطْ؟
questions.a: مَا مَعْنَاهُ: “as to the sense”.

questions.q: What did Umar ask Ahmad? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ عُمَرُ أَحْمَدَ؟
questions.a: Why he wrote “as to the sense”.

questions.q: Why did Ahmad write “as to the sense”? (line 6)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ «مَا مَعْنَاهُ»؟
questions.a: Because he heard the meaning and did not memorise every word.

questions.q: True or false: the Habib tells Ahmad to write what he did not hear.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَأْمُرُ الْحَبِيبُ أَحْمَدَ بِأَنْ يَكْتُبَ مَا لَمْ يَسْمَعْ.
questions.a: False. He says: write what you heard, and do not write what you did not hear.
questions.ref_ar: اُكْتُبْ مَا سَمِعْتَ، وَلَا تَكْتُبْ مَا لَمْ تَسْمَعْ

questions.q: Is this a saying of the Habib, or a prayer of Ahmad? Who is “us”?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ هَذَا كَلَامُ الْحَبِيبِ أَمْ دُعَاءُ أَحْمَدَ؟ مَنْ «نَا»؟
questions.a: A prayer of Ahmad. “Us” is Ahmad and Umar (and those who listen).

questions.q: Who heard the Habib’s speech at home?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَمِعَ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ فِي الْبَيْتِ؟
questions.a: His mother: Ahmad read it to her.

questions.q: Who says this, and to whom? Which ending shows “you”?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقُولُ هَذَا؟ وَلِمَنْ؟ أَيُّ نِهَايَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى «أَنْتَ»؟
questions.a: His mother, to Ahmad. The ending ـكَ in نَفَعَكَ.

questions.q: Ahmad wrote only the meaning of line 4, but the exact words of line 3. How can you tell which is which on the page?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ تُمَيِّزُ بَيْنَ الْعِبَارَةِ الدَّقِيقَةِ وَعِبَارَةِ الْمَعْنَى؟
questions.a: Line 3 has قَالَ and the colon; line 4 has مَا مَعْنَاهُ before the colon.

questions.q: Why does the Habib say “write what you heard”? What would a record be worth if the writer added things?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ: «اُكْتُبْ مَا سَمِعْتَ»؟
questions.a: A record is only as good as its writer is honest: if he adds, the reader can no longer tell the teacher’s words from the writer’s own.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: And the Habib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The student has manners to keep with his teacher.

questions.q: What must the one who sits in the majlis do? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَجِبُ عَلَى مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ؟
questions.a: Listen, and not talk much.

questions.q: Which two words in line 3 tell you the writer gives only the sense?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣ تَدُلَّانِ عَلَى نَقْلِ الْمَعْنَى؟
questions.a: مَا مَعْنَاهُ.

questions.q: What does line 3 say Allah does for the one who acts on his knowledge?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ عَمِلَ بِعِلْمِهِ؟
questions.a: Benefits him by it.

questions.q: Line 4 begins وَسَمِعْنَا. What was heard, and from whom?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤ يَبْدَأُ بِـ «وَسَمِعْنَا». مَاذَا سُمِعَ؟ وَمِمَّنْ؟
questions.a: That provision is from Allah, and that the servant has a provision in every time; from the Habib.

questions.q: Is line 5 a saying of the Habib or a prayer of the writer? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: هَلِ السَّطْرُ ٥ كَلَامُ الْحَبِيبِ أَمْ دُعَاءُ الْكَاتِبِ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A prayer of the writer: it opens with نَفَعَنَا and has no وَقَالَ or colon.

questions.q: Find a word from the root ر ز ق in line 4.
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةً مِنْ جَذْرِ ر ز ق فِي السَّطْرِ ٤.
questions.a: الرِّزْقَ (and رِزْقًا).

questions.q: Without vowels, how can you tell that أَنَّ in line 4 is followed by الرِّزْقَ (accusative) and not الرِّزْقُ?
questions.q_ar: بِلَا حَرَكَاتٍ: كَيْفَ تَعْرِفُ حَرَكَةَ «الرِّزْقَ» بَعْدَ «أَنَّ»؟
questions.a: After أَنَّ the noun is accusative; with no vowels the page does not show it, so you must know the rule. Here the sense (provision is from Allah) agrees.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib said, in meaning: The servant has in every moment a known provision. And the boy wrote that down and said: May Allah benefit us through him.

questions.q: What does مَا مَعْنَاهُ tell the reader?
questions.a: That these are words to this effect: the meaning is given, not word for word.

questions.q: What does نَفَعَنَا اللَّهُ بِهِ mean?
questions.a: May Allah benefit us through him.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy wrote what he heard.
questions.a: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ.

translate.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الرِّزْقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ، فَاشْكُرِ اللَّهَ.
translate.en: The Habib said: Provision is from Allah, so thank Allah.

translate.ar: وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ عَمِلَ بِعِلْمِهِ نَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ.
translate.en: And he said, may Allah be pleased with him, as to the sense: Whoever acts on his knowledge, Allah benefits him.

translate.ar: سَمِعْنَا مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ أَنَّ الصَّبْرَ جَمِيلٌ.
translate.en: We heard from the Habib that patience is beautiful.

translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ ثُمَّ قَرَأَهُ لِأُمِّهِ.
translate.en: Ahmad wrote down the Habib’s speech, then read it to his mother.
May Allah benefit us by the Habib, by his knowledge and his speech.

translate.ar: لِمَاذَا كَتَبْتَ الْمَعْنَى فَقَطْ يَا أَحْمَدُ؟
translate.en: Why did you write only the meaning, Ahmad?

translate.ar: إِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ رِزْقًا فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ، فَاشْكُرِ اللَّهَ.
translate.en: The servant has a provision in every time, so thank Allah.

translate.ar: إِذَا أَطَاعَ الْعَبْدُ رَبَّهُ نَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ.
translate.en: If the servant obeys his Lord, Allah benefits him in this world and the next.

translate.ar: جَلَسَ عُمَرُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ وَسَمِعَ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ وَلَمْ يَتَكَلَّمْ.
translate.en: Umar sat in the majlis and listened to the Habib’s speech and did not talk.

translate.ar: قَالَ أَبِي: اُكْتُبْ مَا سَمِعْتَ، وَلَا تَكْتُبْ مَا لَمْ تَسْمَعْ.
translate.en: My father said: Write what you heard, and do not write what you did not hear.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ ذَكَرَ اللَّهَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ نَفَعَهُ ذَلِكَ.
lines.en: And the Habib said, as to the sense: Whoever remembers Allah in the majlis, that benefits him.

lines.ar: وَإِنَّ لِلْمَجْلِسِ أَدَبًا، فَمَنْ حَضَرَ فَلْيَسْمَعْ.
lines.en: And the majlis has its manners, so whoever attends, let him listen.

translate.ar: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ ذَكَرَ اللَّهَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ نَفَعَهُ ذَلِكَ. وَإِنَّ لِلْمَجْلِسِ أَدَبًا، فَمَنْ حَضَرَ فَلْيَسْمَعْ.
translate.en: And the Habib said, as to the sense: Whoever remembers Allah in the majlis, that benefits him. And the majlis has its manners, so whoever attends, let him listen.
The Habib said: Seek knowledge.
And he said, may Allah be pleased with him, as to the sense: Patience is beautiful.
translate.ar: وَقَالَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: الصَّبْرُ جَمِيلٌ.

translate.en: We heard from the Habib that provision is from Allah.
translate.ar: سَمِعْنَا مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ أَنَّ الرِّزْقَ مِنَ اللَّهِ.

translate.en: May Allah benefit us by him and by his speech.
Ahmad wrote the speech of the Habib in his book.
translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ كَلَامَ الْحَبِيبِ فِي كِتَابِهِ.

translate.en: And the Habib said, as to the sense: Whoever remembers Allah, Allah benefits him.
translate.ar: وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ مَا مَعْنَاهُ: مَنْ ذَكَرَ اللَّهَ نَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ.

translate.en: Write what you heard, and do not write what you did not hear.
translate.ar: اُكْتُبْ مَا سَمِعْتَ، وَلَا تَكْتُبْ مَا لَمْ تَسْمَعْ.

translate.en: The servant has a provision in every time.
translate.ar: إِنَّ لِلْعَبْدِ رِزْقًا فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ.

translate.en: So whoever sits in the majlis, let him listen.
Umar said to Ahmad: Why did you write only the meaning?
translate.ar: قَالَ عُمَرُ لِأَحْمَدَ: لِمَاذَا كَتَبْتَ الْمَعْنَى فَقَطْ؟

translate.en: And his mother said: May Allah benefit you, my son.
translate.ar: وَقَالَتْ أُمُّهُ: نَفَعَكَ اللَّهُ يَا بُنَيَّ.

translate.en: Allah was pleased with him.

readings.title_en: A fatwā, a sermon, a will: three frames
readings.question_en: Who asks and who answers in a fatwā? How does a sermon begin and end? What does a will say, and to whom?
readings.question_ar: مَنْ يَسْأَلُ وَمَنْ يُجِيبُ فِي الْفَتْوَى؟ كَيْفَ تَبْدَأُ الْخُطْبَةُ وَكَيْفَ تَنْتَهِي؟ مَاذَا تَقُولُ الْوَصِيَّةُ، وَلِمَنْ؟

passages.intro_en: From a waṣiyya (a will of counsel) of Imam ʿAlī al-Ḥabshī. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Waṣāyā of Imam ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Ḥabshī (a waṣiyya)
passages.cite: ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. Ḥusayn al-Ḥabshī, "Majmūʿ waṣāyā wa-ijāzāt al-Imām ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Ḥabshī" (TLNOOR id 590, a scan; the title page says: first edition Shaʿbān 1410 / March 1990, Karjai Press, Singapore, corrected and vowelled by Aḥmad b. ʿAlawī b. ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Ḥabshī), the waṣiyya "to his righteous lover Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbdallāh Makārim", printed p. 7 of that waṣiyya (PDF page 12), read against the page image. ABRIDGED: lines 5, 10 and 11 of the waṣiyya as set out in the research file (lines 6-9 are left out). The print is vowelled; the lines are copied from the print.

lines.ar: هَذَا وَاللهَ اللهَ فِي حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ مَعَ جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ
lines.en: (Waṣiyya:) And now — God, God! — in good character with all creatures:

lines.ar: وَاللهَ اللهَ فِي الْوَرَعِ، فَإِنَّهُ أَسَاسُ هَذَا الدِّينِ، وَعُمْدَةُ الْقَاصِدِينَ
lines.en: God, God! — in scrupulousness, for it is the foundation of this religion and the support of those who seek God.

lines.ar: فَأَطِبْ مَطْعَمَكَ، يَصْفُ قَلْبُكَ، وَتَغْشَاهُ الْأَنْوَارُ، وَتَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْأَسْرَارُ
lines.en: So make your food good and your heart will be clear, lights will cover it and secrets will come out of it.

passages.ar: هَذَا وَاللهَ اللهَ فِي حُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ مَعَ جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ وَاللهَ اللهَ فِي الْوَرَعِ، فَإِنَّهُ أَسَاسُ هَذَا الدِّينِ، وَعُمْدَةُ الْقَاصِدِينَ فَأَطِبْ مَطْعَمَكَ، يَصْفُ قَلْبُكَ، وَتَغْشَاهُ الْأَنْوَارُ، وَتَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْأَسْرَارُ
passages.en: (Waṣiyya:) And now — God, God! — in good character with all creatures: God, God! — in scrupulousness, for it is the foundation of this religion and the support of those who seek God. So make your food good and your heart will be clear, lights will cover it and secrets will come out of it.

passages.intro_en: A short text: a question for the Habib. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ ابْنَهَا أَحْمَدَ: هَلْ يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ؟
lines.en: In the evening Fatima asked her son Ahmad: Is fasting obligatory for a small boy?

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: لَا أَعْلَمُ يَا أُمِّي، وَلَكِنِّي أَسْأَلُ الْحَبِيبَ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: I do not know, Mother, but I will ask the Habib.

lines.ar: ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ وَجَلَسَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: He went to the mosque after the prayer and sat in the Habib’s circle.

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ: يَا حَبِيبُ، هَلْ يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ؟
lines.en: And he asked: Habib, is fasting obligatory for a small boy?

lines.ar: فَأَجَابَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ.
lines.en: The Habib answered: Fasting is not obligatory for a small boy until he comes of age.

lines.ar: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
lines.en: And Allah knows best.

lines.ar: فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: سُئِلَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنْ صِيَامِ الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ.
lines.en: Then Ahmad wrote in his book: The Habib was asked about the fasting of a small boy.

lines.ar: وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ الْفَتْوَى لِأُمِّهِ.
lines.en: He returned to the house and read the fatwā to his mother.

lines.ar: فَقَالَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: نَفَعَكَ اللَّهُ يَا بُنَيَّ.
lines.en: And Fatima said: May Allah benefit you, my son.

passages.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ ابْنَهَا أَحْمَدَ: هَلْ يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ؟ قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: لَا أَعْلَمُ يَا أُمِّي، وَلَكِنِّي أَسْأَلُ الْحَبِيبَ. ذَهَبَ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ وَجَلَسَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ. فَسَأَلَ: يَا حَبِيبُ، هَلْ يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ؟ فَأَجَابَ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ. وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ. فَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: سُئِلَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنْ صِيَامِ الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ. وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَرَأَ الْفَتْوَى لِأُمِّهِ. فَقَالَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: نَفَعَكَ اللَّهُ يَا بُنَيَّ.
passages.en: In the evening Fatima asked her son Ahmad: Is fasting obligatory for a small boy? Ahmad said: I do not know, Mother, but I will ask the Habib. He went to the mosque after the prayer and sat in the Habib’s circle. And he asked: Habib, is fasting obligatory for a small boy? The Habib answered: Fasting is not obligatory for a small boy until he comes of age. And Allah knows best. Then Ahmad wrote in his book: The Habib was asked about the fasting of a small boy. He returned to the house and read the fatwā to his mother. And Fatima said: May Allah benefit you, my son.

passages.intro_en: One paragraph with no vowels: a sermon. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (vowelled in the key; the student book shows no vowels).

lines.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ.
lines.en: Praise be to Allah, who has made us Muslims.
lines.ar_bare: الحمد لله الذي جعلنا مسلمين.

lines.ar: وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ.
lines.en: And blessings and peace upon the Prophet ﷺ, and upon his family and his Companions.
lines.ar_bare: والصلاة والسلام على النبي ﷺ وعلى آله وأصحابه.

lines.ar: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَيَا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ، أُوصِيكُمْ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالصِّيَامِ وَالصَّدَقَةِ.
lines.en: And now, servants of Allah, I counsel you to keep the prayer, the fast and charity.
lines.ar_bare: أما بعد، فيا عباد الله، أوصيكم بالصلاة والصيام والصدقة.

lines.ar: وَأُوصِيكُمْ بِالْأَدَبِ مَعَ الْأَبِ وَالْأُمِّ وَالْعُلَمَاءِ.
lines.en: And I counsel you to good manners with the father, the mother and the scholars.
lines.ar_bare: وأوصيكم بالأدب مع الأب والأم والعلماء.

lines.ar: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الْآخِرَةَ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا.
lines.en: And know that the Hereafter is better than this world.
lines.ar_bare: واعلموا أن الآخرة خير من الدنيا.

lines.ar: أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ.
lines.en: I say these words of mine and ask Allah’s forgiveness for me and for you.
lines.ar_bare: أقول قولي هذا وأستغفر الله لي ولكم.

passages.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ. وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ. أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَيَا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ، أُوصِيكُمْ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالصِّيَامِ وَالصَّدَقَةِ. وَأُوصِيكُمْ بِالْأَدَبِ مَعَ الْأَبِ وَالْأُمِّ وَالْعُلَمَاءِ. وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الْآخِرَةَ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا. أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ.
passages.en: Praise be to Allah, who has made us Muslims. And blessings and peace upon the Prophet ﷺ, and upon his family and his Companions. And now, servants of Allah, I counsel you to keep the prayer, the fast and charity. And I counsel you to good manners with the father, the mother and the scholars. And know that the Hereafter is better than this world. I say these words of mine and ask Allah’s forgiveness for me and for you.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 156-157 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَبِيعَ الرَّجُلُ الرُّطَبَ فِي السُّوقِ؟
lines.en: Fatima asked: Is it allowed for a man to sell fresh dates in the market?

lines.ar: سُئِلَ الْحَبِيبُ فَأَجَابَ: نَعَمْ، يَجُوزُ.
lines.en: The Habib was asked, and he answered: Yes, it is allowed.

passages.ar: سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ: هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَبِيعَ الرَّجُلُ الرُّطَبَ فِي السُّوقِ؟ سُئِلَ الْحَبِيبُ فَأَجَابَ: نَعَمْ، يَجُوزُ.
passages.en: Fatima asked: Is it allowed for a man to sell fresh dates in the market? The Habib was asked, and he answered: Yes, it is allowed.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A waṣiyya: counsel from a teacher to a student, from the waṣāyā of Imam ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Ḥabshī.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: And now: God, God! in good character with all creatures.

questions.q: The first word is هَذَا. What does it do at the start of a will? (Think of وَبَعْدُ.)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ كَلِمَةُ «هَذَا» فِي أَوَّلِ الْوَصِيَّةِ؟
questions.a: It turns from the greeting to the point: “and now”.

questions.q: What does وَاللهَ اللهَ فِي … ask of the reader?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَطْلُبُ «وَاللهَ اللهَ فِي …» مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟
questions.a: An urgent command: be mindful of God, take great care, in what follows (here good character, then scrupulousness).

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: God, God! in scrupulousness, for it is the foundation of this religion and the support of those who seek God.

questions.q: Which word introduces the reason? What does ـهُ refer to?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَبْدَأُ السَّبَبَ؟ إِلَى مَاذَا يَرْجِعُ الضَّمِيرُ ـهُ؟
questions.a: فَإِنَّ: “for”. The ending ـهُ refers to الْوَرَع (scrupulousness).

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: So make your food good, and your heart will be clear, lights will cover it, and secrets will come out of it.

questions.q: Which word is the command, and which is its result?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ الْأَمْرُ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ النَّتِيجَةُ؟
questions.a: فَأَطِبْ is the command; يَصْفُ (without ـُ) is the result.

questions.q: Find the word for “food”. Which ending shows “your”?
questions.q_ar: جِدْ كَلِمَةً مَعْنَاهَا «الطَّعَامُ». أَيُّ نِهَايَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى «كَ»؟
questions.a: مَطْعَمَكَ: the ending ـكَ = “your” (one person).

questions.q: Who is the writer speaking to? How many people, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ الْكَاتِبُ؟ كَمْ شَخْصًا؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: To one person (“you”): the endings ـكَ in مَطْعَمَكَ and قَلْبُكَ.

questions.q: Line 3 gives a result for good food. What are the results named?
questions.q_ar: مَا النَّتَائِجُ الَّتِي ذُكِرَتْ لِطِيبِ الْمَطْعَمِ؟
questions.a: The heart becomes clear; lights cover it; secrets come out of it.

questions.q: The will uses commands, not questions and answers. Why is this the natural frame for counsel?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يُنَاسِبُ الْأَمْرُ إِطَارَ الْوَصِيَّةِ؟
questions.a: A will speaks from the teacher to one student he wants to guide: it tells him what to do and what to avoid, with a short reason (فَإِنَّهُ …).

questions.q: What did Fatima ask her son?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ ابْنَهَا؟
questions.a: Whether fasting is obligatory for a small boy.

questions.q: Why did Ahmad go to the Habib?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ؟
questions.a: He did not know the answer, so he went to ask.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: And he asked: Habib, is fasting obligatory for a small boy?

questions.q: Which word shows that an answer follows? Who answers?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الْجَوَابَ يَأْتِي؟ مَنْ يُجِيبُ؟
questions.a: فَأَجَابَ. The Habib.

questions.q: What is the answer? (lines 5 and 6)
questions.q_ar: مَا الْجَوَابُ؟ (السَّطْرُ ٥)
questions.a: Fasting is not obligatory for a small boy until he comes of age.

questions.q: What do these words close, and what do they mean?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَخْتِمُ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتُ؟ وَمَا مَعْنَاهَا؟
questions.a: They close the answer: “and Allah knows best”.

questions.q: In line 7, who is the one who was asked? Who is the one who asked?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٧: مَنْ سُئِلَ؟ وَمَنْ سَأَلَ؟
questions.a: The Habib was asked. The asker (Ahmad) is not named: the passive.

questions.q: What did Ahmad write down in his book? Which two verbs open it?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ؟ أَيُّ فِعْلَيْنِ يَفْتَحَانِهِ؟
questions.a: The question and the answer, as a fatwā: سُئِلَ … فَأَجَابَ.

questions.q: Translate line 5.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْخَامِسَ.
questions.a: The Habib answered: Fasting is not obligatory for a small boy until he comes of age,

questions.q: Until when is fasting not obligatory for the small boy? Which word starts that answer?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَتَى لَا يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَبْدَأُ الْجَوَابَ؟
questions.a: Until he comes of age. حَتَّى (“until”) starts it.
questions.ref_ar: لَا يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ

questions.q: To whom did Ahmad read the fatwā?
questions.q_ar: لِمَنْ قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ الْفَتْوَى؟
questions.a: To his mother.

questions.q: Who says this, and to whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقُولُ هَذَا؟ وَلِمَنْ؟
questions.a: Fatima, to Ahmad (ـكَ = “you”).

questions.q: Ahmad did not give the ruling himself. Why did he go to the Habib?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا لَمْ يُفْتِ أَحْمَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ؟
questions.a: Because a ruling must come from one who knows: he asked, and then wrote exactly what he was told.

questions.q: Which three of the Habib’s words close the answer in a way that shows modesty?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَخْتِمُ الْجَوَابَ بِتَوَاضُعٍ؟
questions.a: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ: even after answering, the scholar says that knowledge belongs to Allah.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A sermon (khuṭba): it opens with praise (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ), has أَمَّا بَعْدُ and أُوصِيكُمْ, and closes with أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَذَا.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Praise be to Allah, who has made us Muslims.

questions.q: What comes in line 2, after the praise?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَأْتِي فِي السَّطْرِ ٢ بَعْدَ الْحَمْدِ؟
questions.a: Blessings and peace upon the Prophet ﷺ, his family and his Companions.

questions.q: Which words in line 3 mark the turn from praise to counsel?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الِانْتِقَالِ مِنَ الْحَمْدِ إِلَى النُّصْحِ؟
questions.a: أَمَّا بَعْدُ: “and now”.

questions.q: What three things does the preacher counsel in line 3?
questions.q_ar: بِمَاذَا يُوصِي الْخَطِيبُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٣؟
questions.a: The prayer, the fast and charity.

questions.q: Whom does line 4 say to treat with good manners?
questions.q_ar: مَعَ مَنْ يَكُونُ الْأَدَبُ فِي السَّطْرِ ٤؟
questions.a: The father, the mother and the scholars.

questions.q: Translate line 5. Which word starts the “that” clause?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْخَامِسَ. أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَبْدَأُ جُمْلَةَ «أَنَّ»؟
questions.a: And know that the Hereafter is better than this world. أَنَّ starts it.

questions.q: Without vowels, what shows that وَاعْلَمُوا in line 5 is a command to many people?
questions.q_ar: بِلَا حَرَكَاتٍ: مَا الَّذِي يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ «وَاعْلَمُوا» أَمْرٌ لِجَمَاعَةٍ؟
questions.a: The plural ending of the verb. The preacher is speaking to the whole congregation, as in أُوصِيكُمْ above; without vowels you read the shape from the ending and the sense.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: Fatima asked: Is it allowed for a man to sell fresh dates in the market? The Habib was asked, and he answered: Yes, it is allowed.

questions.q: Which verb is passive in the second new line? Who was asked?
questions.a: سُئِلَ (was asked): the Habib (الْحَبِيبُ).

questions.q: Which word opens the answer?
questions.a: فَأَجَابَ (and he answered)

questions.q: Write in Arabic: Fatima asked a question.
questions.a: سَأَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ سُؤَالًا.

translate.ar: سُئِلَ الْحَبِيبُ عَنِ الصِّيَامِ فَأَجَابَ: يَجِبُ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ الْكَبِيرِ.
translate.en: The Habib was asked about fasting, and he answered: It is obligatory for the grown Muslim.

translate.ar: هَلْ يَصِحُّ الصِّيَامُ بِلَا نِيَّةٍ؟ لَا، لَا يَصِحُّ.
translate.en: Is fasting valid without intention? No, it is not valid.

translate.ar: قَامَ الْخَطِيبُ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ وَقَالَ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، أَمَّا بَعْدُ.
translate.en: The preacher stood on the pulpit and said: Praise be to Allah. And now.
I counsel you to keep the prayer, remembrance and good manners.

translate.ar: أَوْصَى الْأَبُ ابْنَهُ فَقَالَ: عَلَيْكَ بِالصَّبْرِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ.
translate.en: The father counselled his son and said: Hold to patience, and beware of betrayal.

translate.ar: كَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ الْجَوَابَ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَقَرَأَ الْفَتْوَى لِأُمِّهِ.
translate.en: Ahmad wrote the answer in his book and read the fatwā to his mother.
Remember Allah much and give thanks for His blessing.

translate.ar: جَلَسَ النَّاسُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَسَمِعُوا الْخُطْبَةَ ثُمَّ صَلَّوْا.
translate.en: The people sat in the mosque and listened to the sermon, then prayed.

translate.ar: لَا يَجِبُ الصِّيَامُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ الصَّغِيرِ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ.
translate.en: Fasting is not obligatory for a small boy until he comes of age.

translate.ar: سُئِلَ الْعَالِمُ عَنْ شَيْءٍ لَا يَعْلَمُهُ فَقَالَ: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translate.en: The scholar was asked about something he did not know, so he said: And Allah knows best.

lines.ar: أَوْصَى الشَّيْخُ طُلَّابَهُ فَقَالَ: عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْعِلْمِ وَالْأَدَبِ.
lines.en: The shaykh counselled his students and said: Hold to knowledge and good manners.

lines.ar: وَاللَّهَ اللَّهَ فِي الْأَمَانَةِ، فَإِنَّهَا أَسَاسُ الدِّينِ.
lines.en: And Allah, Allah! (take care) in trust, for it is the foundation of religion.

translate.ar: أَوْصَى الشَّيْخُ طُلَّابَهُ فَقَالَ: عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْعِلْمِ وَالْأَدَبِ. وَاللَّهَ اللَّهَ فِي الْأَمَانَةِ، فَإِنَّهَا أَسَاسُ الدِّينِ.
translate.en: The shaykh counselled his students and said: Hold to knowledge and good manners. And Allah, Allah! (take care) in trust, for it is the foundation of religion.
The Habib was asked: Is ablution obligatory for prayer?
translate.ar: سُئِلَ الْحَبِيبُ: هَلْ يَجِبُ الْوُضُوءُ لِلصَّلَاةِ؟

translate.en: And he answered: Yes, it is obligatory.
And Allah knows best.
Praise be to Allah. And now, servants of Allah, I counsel you to be conscious of Allah.
translate.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَيَا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ، أُوصِيكُمْ بِتَقْوَى اللَّهِ.

translate.en: The shaykh counselled his son to patience.
Hold to knowledge, and beware of betrayal.
The student was asked about the prayer, and he answered.
It is not valid without intention.
I say these words of mine and ask Allah’s forgiveness for me and for you.
translate.ar: أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ.

translate.en: Ahmad read the fatwā to his mother.
I counsel you to good manners with the father and the mother.
The preacher stood on the pulpit.

readings.title_en: The grammar primer: the names of the signs
readings.question_en: What does a text about grammar call the signs I have been reading since Lesson 1?
readings.question_ar: بِمَاذَا يُسَمِّي كِتَابُ النَّحْوِ الْعَلَامَاتِ الَّتِي أَقْرَأُهَا مُنْذُ الدَّرْسِ الْأَوَّلِ؟

passages.intro_en: A short text: the evening in the library. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، وَفَتَحَ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا فِي الْإِعْرَابِ.
lines.en: In the evening Ahmad sat with Umar in the library and opened a small book on iʿrāb.

lines.ar: قَالَ عُمَرُ: مَا الْكَلَامُ؟
lines.en: Umar said: What is speech?

lines.ar: وَمَا أَقْسَامُ الْكَلِمَةِ؟
lines.en: And what are the parts of the word?

lines.ar: فَقَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ: الْكَلَامُ هُوَ اللَّفْظُ الْمُفِيدُ، وَأَقْسَامُ الْكَلِمَةِ ثَلَاثَةٌ: اِسْمٌ وَفِعْلٌ وَحَرْفٌ.
lines.en: So Ahmad read: Speech is the useful utterance, and the parts of the word are three: noun, verb and particle.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ جَاءَ الْحَبِيبُ وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُمَا.
lines.en: Then the Habib came and sat with them.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ: لِلرَّفْعِ عَلَامَةٌ، وَلِلنَّصْبِ عَلَامَةٌ، وَلِلْخَفْضِ عَلَامَةٌ، وَلِلْجَزْمِ عَلَامَةٌ.
lines.en: And he said: Rafʿ has a sign, naṣb has a sign, khafḍ has a sign and jazm has a sign.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: عَلَامَةُ الرَّفْعِ الضَّمَّةُ، وَعَلَامَةُ النَّصْبِ الْفَتْحَةُ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: The sign of rafʿ is the ḍamma, and the sign of naṣb is the fatḥa.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: وَعَلَامَةُ الْخَفْضِ الْكَسْرَةُ، وَعَلَامَةُ الْجَزْمِ السُّكُونُ.
lines.en: And Umar said: The sign of khafḍ is the kasra, and the sign of jazm is the sukūn.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: أَحْسَنْتُمَا.
lines.en: The Habib said: Well done, you two.

lines.ar: اُنْظُرْ يَا أَحْمَدُ إِلَى آخِرِ الْكَلِمَةِ فِي «جَاءَ الْمُعَلِّمُ» وَفِي «رَأَيْتُ الْمُعَلِّمَ».
lines.en: Look, Ahmad, at the end of the word in “The teacher came” and in “I saw the teacher”.

lines.ar: فَنَظَرَ أَحْمَدُ وَقَالَ: الضَّمَّةُ فِي الْأُولَى، وَالْفَتْحَةُ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ.
lines.en: Ahmad looked and said: the ḍamma in the first, and the fatḥa in the second.

passages.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، وَفَتَحَ كِتَابًا صَغِيرًا فِي الْإِعْرَابِ. قَالَ عُمَرُ: مَا الْكَلَامُ؟ وَمَا أَقْسَامُ الْكَلِمَةِ؟ فَقَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ: الْكَلَامُ هُوَ اللَّفْظُ الْمُفِيدُ، وَأَقْسَامُ الْكَلِمَةِ ثَلَاثَةٌ: اِسْمٌ وَفِعْلٌ وَحَرْفٌ. ثُمَّ جَاءَ الْحَبِيبُ وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُمَا. وَقَالَ: لِلرَّفْعِ عَلَامَةٌ، وَلِلنَّصْبِ عَلَامَةٌ، وَلِلْخَفْضِ عَلَامَةٌ، وَلِلْجَزْمِ عَلَامَةٌ. فَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: عَلَامَةُ الرَّفْعِ الضَّمَّةُ، وَعَلَامَةُ النَّصْبِ الْفَتْحَةُ. وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: وَعَلَامَةُ الْخَفْضِ الْكَسْرَةُ، وَعَلَامَةُ الْجَزْمِ السُّكُونُ. فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: أَحْسَنْتُمَا. اُنْظُرْ يَا أَحْمَدُ إِلَى آخِرِ الْكَلِمَةِ فِي «جَاءَ الْمُعَلِّمُ» وَفِي «رَأَيْتُ الْمُعَلِّمَ». فَنَظَرَ أَحْمَدُ وَقَالَ: الضَّمَّةُ فِي الْأُولَى، وَالْفَتْحَةُ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ.
passages.en: In the evening Ahmad sat with Umar in the library and opened a small book on iʿrāb. Umar said: What is speech? And what are the parts of the word? So Ahmad read: Speech is the useful utterance, and the parts of the word are three: noun, verb and particle. Then the Habib came and sat with them. And he said: Rafʿ has a sign, naṣb has a sign, khafḍ has a sign and jazm has a sign. Ahmad said: The sign of rafʿ is the ḍamma, and the sign of naṣb is the fatḥa. And Umar said: The sign of khafḍ is the kasra, and the sign of jazm is the sukūn. The Habib said: Well done, you two. Look, Ahmad, at the end of the word in “The teacher came” and in “I saw the teacher”. Ahmad looked and said: the ḍamma in the first, and the fatḥa in the second.
