readings.title_en: Fable and classical story: how a tale is told
readings.question_en: How does a tale begin, move and end, and who is speaking?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ تَبْدَأُ الْحِكَايَةُ؟ وَكَيْفَ تَسِيرُ؟ وَكَيْفَ تَنْتَهِي؟ وَمَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟

passages.intro_en: A tale of Kalīla wa-Dimna. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Kalīla wa-Dimna (Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ), "The Monkey and the Tortoise"
passages.cite: Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ, Kalīla wa-Dimna, 'Bāb al-Qird wa-l-Ghaylam'; Shamela Master Library [31990] (Maktabah Classic loose .bok; the same text as Shamela 3.28 id 6580, whose card says 'auto-numbered, not matching the print'), digital pages 65 (tale) and 66 (moral); printed edition not identified, so no printed page is claimed. 8 versions of the book exist on the SSD; this one was read. Extract of three lines (nos. 5-7 of the seven in the research file); vowels are the course’s (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: فَخَرَجَ هَارِبًا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى السَّاحِلِ، فَوَجَدَ شَجَرَةً مِنْ شَجَرِ التِّينِ فَارْتَقَى إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَهَا مَقَامَهُ.
lines.en: He went out fleeing headlong until he reached the shore, found a fig tree, climbed it and made it his home.
lines.ar_bare: فخرج هاربا على وجهه حتى انتهى إلى الساحل، فوجد شجرة من شجر التين فارتقى إليها وجعلها مقامه.

lines.ar: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ يَأْكُلُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ التِّينِ إِذَا سَقَطَتْ مِنْ يَدِهِ تِينَةٌ فِي الْمَاءِ، فَسَمِعَ لَهَا صَوْتًا وَإِيقَاعًا، فَجَعَلَ يَأْكُلُ وَيَرْمِي فِي الْمَاءِ، فَأَطْرَبَهُ ذَلِكَ.
lines.en: One day, while he was eating of those figs, a fig fell from his hand into the water; he heard a sound and a splash from it, so he went on eating and throwing into the water, and that delighted him.
lines.ar_bare: فبينما هو ذات يوم يأكل من ذلك التين إذا سقطت من يده تينة في الماء، فسمع لها صوتا وإيقاعا، فجعل يأكل ويرمي في الماء، فأطربه ذلك.

lines.ar: فَهَذَا مَثَلُ الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي يَطْلُبُ الْحَاجَةَ فَإِذَا ظَفِرَ بِهَا أَضَاعَهَا.
lines.en: This is the likeness of the man who seeks a need and, when he gains it, loses it. (The moral, as the tale ends on the next page.)
lines.ar_bare: فهذا مثل الرجل الذي يطلب الحاجة فإذا ظفر بها أضاعها.

passages.ar: فَخَرَجَ هَارِبًا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ حَتَّى انْتَهَى إِلَى السَّاحِلِ، فَوَجَدَ شَجَرَةً مِنْ شَجَرِ التِّينِ فَارْتَقَى إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَهَا مَقَامَهُ. فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ يَأْكُلُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ التِّينِ إِذَا سَقَطَتْ مِنْ يَدِهِ تِينَةٌ فِي الْمَاءِ، فَسَمِعَ لَهَا صَوْتًا وَإِيقَاعًا، فَجَعَلَ يَأْكُلُ وَيَرْمِي فِي الْمَاءِ، فَأَطْرَبَهُ ذَلِكَ. فَهَذَا مَثَلُ الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي يَطْلُبُ الْحَاجَةَ فَإِذَا ظَفِرَ بِهَا أَضَاعَهَا.
passages.en: He went out fleeing headlong until he reached the shore, found a fig tree, climbed it and made it his home. One day, while he was eating of those figs, a fig fell from his hand into the water; he heard a sound and a splash from it, so he went on eating and throwing into the water, and that delighted him. This is the likeness of the man who seeks a need and, when he gains it, loses it. (The moral, as the tale ends on the next page.)

passages.intro_en: A tale told at the rawḥa. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text: a fable written for this lesson in the register of Kalīla wa-Dimna.

lines.ar: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ سُلَحْفَاةً كَانَتْ تَسْكُنُ قُرْبَ الْوَادِي.
lines.en: They claimed that a tortoise used to live near the wadi.
lines.ar_bare: زعموا أن سلحفاة كانت تسكن قرب الوادي.

lines.ar: وَكَانَ قِرْدٌ شَابٌّ قَدْ سَكَنَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ تِينٍ هُنَاكَ.
lines.en: And a young monkey had settled on a fig tree there.
lines.ar_bare: وكان قرد شاب قد سكن على شجرة تين هناك.

lines.ar: وَكَانَ الْقِرْدُ يَأْكُلُ مِنَ التِّينِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَيَرْمِي بَعْضَهُ فِي الْمَاءِ.
lines.en: The monkey used to eat of the figs every day and throw some of them into the water.
lines.ar_bare: وكان القرد يأكل من التين كل يوم ويرمي بعضه في الماء.

lines.ar: وَكَانَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ تَجْمَعُ التِّينَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ وَتَحْمِلُهُ إِلَى بَيْتِهَا.
lines.en: And the tortoise used to gather the figs from the water and carry them to her house.
lines.ar_bare: وكانت السلحفاة تجمع التين من الماء وتحمله إلى بيتها.

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ الْقِرْدُ: لِمَاذَا تَجْمَعِينَ التِّينَ؟
lines.en: So the monkey asked: Why do you gather the figs?
lines.ar_bare: فسأل القرد: لماذا تجمعين التين؟

lines.ar: فَقَالَتْ: لِأَنَّ التِّينَ لَا يَكُونُ كَثِيرًا دَائِمًا.
lines.en: She said: Because figs are not always plentiful.
lines.ar_bare: فقالت: لأن التين لا يكون كثيرا دائما.

lines.ar: فَلَمْ يَسْمَعِ الْقِرْدُ كَلَامَهَا.
lines.en: But the monkey did not listen to her words.
lines.ar_bare: فلم يسمع القرد كلامها.

lines.ar: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الشَّجَرَةِ إِذَا الشَّجَرَةُ لَيْسَ فِيهَا تِينٌ.
lines.en: One day, while he was looking at the tree, suddenly the tree had no figs in it.
lines.ar_bare: فبينما هو ذات يوم ينظر إلى الشجرة إذا الشجرة ليس فيها تين.

lines.ar: فَنَزَلَ حَزِينًا إِلَى الْوَادِي وَطَلَبَ التِّينَ مِنَ السُّلَحْفَاةِ.
lines.en: So he came down sadly to the wadi and asked the tortoise for figs.
lines.ar_bare: فنزل حزينا إلى الوادي وطلب التين من السلحفاة.

lines.ar: فَقَالَتْ: خُذْ هَذَا التِّينَ وَاشْكُرِ اللَّهَ.
lines.en: She said: Take these figs and thank Allah.
lines.ar_bare: فقالت: خذ هذا التين واشكر الله.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْقِرْدُ: فَهِمْتُ الْآنَ.
lines.en: The monkey said: Now I understand.
lines.ar_bare: فقال القرد: فهمت الآن.

lines.ar: فَهَذِهِ عِبْرَةٌ: مَنْ جَمَعَ وَجَدَ، وَمَنْ رَمَى لَمْ يَجِدْ.
lines.en: So this is the lesson: whoever gathers finds, and whoever throws away does not find.
lines.ar_bare: فهذه عبرة: من جمع وجد، ومن رمى لم يجد.

passages.ar: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ سُلَحْفَاةً كَانَتْ تَسْكُنُ قُرْبَ الْوَادِي. وَكَانَ قِرْدٌ شَابٌّ قَدْ سَكَنَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ تِينٍ هُنَاكَ. وَكَانَ الْقِرْدُ يَأْكُلُ مِنَ التِّينِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَيَرْمِي بَعْضَهُ فِي الْمَاءِ. وَكَانَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ تَجْمَعُ التِّينَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ وَتَحْمِلُهُ إِلَى بَيْتِهَا. فَسَأَلَ الْقِرْدُ: لِمَاذَا تَجْمَعِينَ التِّينَ؟ فَقَالَتْ: لِأَنَّ التِّينَ لَا يَكُونُ كَثِيرًا دَائِمًا. فَلَمْ يَسْمَعِ الْقِرْدُ كَلَامَهَا. فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى الشَّجَرَةِ إِذَا الشَّجَرَةُ لَيْسَ فِيهَا تِينٌ. فَنَزَلَ حَزِينًا إِلَى الْوَادِي وَطَلَبَ التِّينَ مِنَ السُّلَحْفَاةِ. فَقَالَتْ: خُذْ هَذَا التِّينَ وَاشْكُرِ اللَّهَ. فَقَالَ الْقِرْدُ: فَهِمْتُ الْآنَ. فَهَذِهِ عِبْرَةٌ: مَنْ جَمَعَ وَجَدَ، وَمَنْ رَمَى لَمْ يَجِدْ.
passages.en: They claimed that a tortoise used to live near the wadi. And a young monkey had settled on a fig tree there. The monkey used to eat of the figs every day and throw some of them into the water. And the tortoise used to gather the figs from the water and carry them to her house. So the monkey asked: Why do you gather the figs? She said: Because figs are not always plentiful. But the monkey did not listen to her words. One day, while he was looking at the tree, suddenly the tree had no figs in it. So he came down sadly to the wadi and asked the tortoise for figs. She said: Take these figs and thank Allah. The monkey said: Now I understand. So this is the lesson: whoever gathers finds, and whoever throws away does not find.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 170-171 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ حِكَايَةً: يُحْكَى أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ صَدِيقَ سُلَحْفَاةٍ.
lines.en: In the rawḥa the boy read a tale: It is told that a monkey was a friend of a tortoise.

lines.ar: وَفِي آخِرِهَا عِبْرَةٌ لِكُلِّ صَدِيقٍ.
lines.en: And at its end is a lesson for every friend.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ حِكَايَةً: يُحْكَى أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ صَدِيقَ سُلَحْفَاةٍ. وَفِي آخِرِهَا عِبْرَةٌ لِكُلِّ صَدِيقٍ.
passages.en: In the rawḥa the boy read a tale: It is told that a monkey was a friend of a tortoise. And at its end is a lesson for every friend.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: He went out fleeing headlong until he reached the shore, found a fig tree, climbed it and made it his home.

questions.q: Who is “he” in line 1? Look back at the slides.
questions.q_ar: مَنْ هُوَ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟ اُنْظُرْ إِلَى الشَّرَائِحِ.
questions.a: Māhir, the old king of the monkeys, who was overcome by a young monkey of the royal house.

questions.q: What did he do after he found the tree?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلَ بَعْدَ أَنْ وَجَدَ الشَّجَرَةَ؟
questions.a: He climbed it and made it his home.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: One day, while he was eating of those figs, a fig fell from his hand into the water; he heard a sound and a splash from it, so he went on eating and throwing into the water, and that delighted him.

questions.q: What is the turn of the tale, and which word brings it?
questions.q_ar: مَا مُفَاجَأَةُ الْحِكَايَةِ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَأْتِي بِهَا؟
questions.a: A fig falls into the water. The word is إِذَا (“suddenly”).

questions.q: True or false: the monkey was angry at the splash.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: غَضِبَ الْقِرْدُ مِنَ الصَّوْتِ.
questions.a: False. The sound delighted him (فَأَطْرَبَهُ ذَلِكَ).

questions.q: Put in order: (a) he reaches the shore (b) a fig falls into the water (c) he climbs the tree.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (أ) يَصِلُ إِلَى السَّاحِلِ (ب) تَسْقُطُ تِينَةٌ فِي الْمَاءِ (ج) يَصْعَدُ الشَّجَرَةَ.
questions.a: a, c, b.

questions.q: Translate line 3: the moral.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ: الْعِبْرَةَ.
questions.a: So this is the likeness of the man who seeks a need and, when he gains it, loses it.

questions.q: Find the word that means “need”. Which word of line 3 shows that the man loses it?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَدُلُّ عَلَى مَا يَطْلُبُهُ الرَّجُلُ. أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الضَّيَاعِ؟
questions.a: الْحَاجَةَ is “the need”. أَضَاعَهَا (“lost it”) shows the loss.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A fable (a tale with animal characters and a moral) from Kalīla wa-Dimna by Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ.

questions.q: Line 2 chains فَسَمِعَ، فَجَعَلَ، فَأَطْرَبَهُ. What does the chain do to the pace of the story?
questions.q_ar: سِلْسِلَةُ «فَـ» فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ بِسُرْعَةِ الْحِكَايَةِ؟
questions.a: It makes the events follow one another at once, like a list: heard, went on, delighted.

questions.q: How does the monkey’s throwing of the figs show the moral of line 3?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يُبَيِّنُ رَمْيُ الْقِرْدِ لِلتِّينِ الْعِبْرَةَ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ؟
questions.a: He has a tree of figs (what he needed) and wastes them for a moment’s pleasure: he gains the need and loses it.

questions.q: Who are the two animals, and where do they live?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْحَيَوَانَانِ؟ وَأَيْنَ يَسْكُنَانِ؟
questions.a: A tortoise, who lives near the wadi, and a young monkey, who lives on a fig tree there.

questions.q: What did the monkey do with the figs every day?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَانَ يَفْعَلُ الْقِرْدُ بِالتِّينِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟
questions.a: He ate of them and threw some of them into the water.

questions.q: What did the tortoise do with the figs?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا كَانَتْ تَفْعَلُ السُّلَحْفَاةُ بِالتِّينِ؟
questions.a: She gathered them from the water and carried them to her house.

questions.q: Translate line 5 (the question and the answer).
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْخَامِسَ.
questions.a: So the monkey asked: Why do you gather the figs? She said: Because figs are not always plentiful.

questions.q: True or false: the monkey listened to the tortoise.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: سَمِعَ الْقِرْدُ كَلَامَ السُّلَحْفَاةِ.
questions.a: False. لَمْ يَسْمَعْ = he did not listen.

questions.q: Find the turn: which two words (بَيْنَمَا … إِذَا) frame it? What was the surprise?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْمُفَاجَأَةَ: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تُحِيطَانِ بِهَا؟ وَمَا هِيَ؟
questions.a: فَبَيْنَمَا … إِذَا. The surprise: the tree had no figs left.

questions.q: How did the tortoise treat the monkey when he came down sadly?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ عَامَلَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ الْقِرْدَ حِينَ نَزَلَ حَزِينًا؟
questions.a: She gave him figs (خُذْ هَذَا التِّينَ) and told him to thank Allah.

questions.q: Who says “Now I understand”, and what has he understood?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَقُولُ «فَهِمْتُ الْآنَ»؟ وَمَاذَا فَهِمَ؟
questions.a: The monkey. He has understood the tortoise’s words: do not waste what you have.

questions.q: Translate the last line: the moral.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَخِيرَ: الْعِبْرَةَ.
questions.a: So this is the lesson: whoever gathers finds, and whoever throws away does not find.

questions.q: Which word tells you that a moral follows? Which word opens the tale?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الْعِبْرَةِ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَفْتَحُ الْحِكَايَةَ؟
questions.a: عِبْرَةٌ (“lesson”) tells you the moral follows. زَعَمُوا أَنَّ opens the tale.

questions.q: Lines 3 and 4 use كَانَ + present (كَانَ يَأْكُلُ … وَكَانَتْ تَجْمَعُ), but the later events use plain past verbs after فَـ. Why?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَسْتَعْمِلُ السَّطْرَانِ ٣ وَ٤ «كَانَ + الْمُضَارِعَ»؟ وَلِمَاذَا تَسْتَعْمِلُ الْأَحْدَاثُ بَعْدَهُمَا الْمَاضِيَ؟
questions.a: The كَانَ + present lines describe what the animals used to do every day (the scene). The plain past verbs tell what happened on one day (the plot).

questions.q: Compare this tale with the monkey of Kalīla wa-Dimna (Exercise A). What do the two monkeys share?
questions.q_ar: قَارِنْ بَيْنَ هَذِهِ الْحِكَايَةِ وَقِرْدِ كَلِيلَةَ وَدِمْنَةَ. مَاذَا يَشْتَرِكُ فِيهِ الْقِرْدَانِ؟
questions.a: Each monkey has plenty of figs and wastes them by throwing them away; each tale ends by telling us not to lose what we have gained.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: In the rawḥa the boy read a tale: It is told that a monkey was a friend of a tortoise. And at its end is a lesson for every friend.

questions.q: Which words open the story (“it is told that”)?
questions.a: يُحْكَى أَنَّ

questions.q: Who are the two characters?
questions.a: A monkey (قِرْد) and a tortoise (سُلَحْفَاة).

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy read a tale.
questions.a: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ حِكَايَةً.

translate.ar: يُحْكَى أَنَّ شَابًّا كَانَ يَسْكُنُ قُرْبَ الْمَسْجِدِ.
translate.en: It is told that a young man used to live near the mosque.
And he had collected many books.

translate.ar: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَقْرَأُ إِذَا سَمِعَ صَوْتًا.
translate.en: While he was reading, suddenly he heard a sound.
So he looked and found the monkey under the tree.
The monkey said to him: I am your neighbour.

translate.ar: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ سُلَحْفَاةً حَمَلَتِ الْقِرْدَ إِلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.
translate.en: They claimed that a tortoise carried the monkey to the tree.

translate.ar: فَهَذِهِ عِبْرَةٌ لِمَنْ يَطْلُبُ الْعِلْمَ: اِصْبِرْ.
translate.en: So this is a lesson for whoever seeks knowledge: be patient.

translate.ar: كَانَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ تَسْكُنُ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ، وَكَانَ الْقِرْدُ فَوْقَهَا.
translate.en: The tortoise used to live under the tree, and the monkey was above her.

translate.source: al-Jāḥiẓ, Kitāb al-Bukhalāʾ (anecdote of the Khurāsānī travellers and the lamp)

lines.ar: فَكَانُوا إِذَا جَاءَ الْمِصْبَاحُ شَدُّوا عَيْنَهُ بِمِنْدِيلٍ، وَلَا يَزَالُ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ كَذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ يَنَامُوا وَيُطْفِئُوا الْمِصْبَاحَ،
lines.en: So whenever the lamp came they would bind his eye with a handkerchief, and he and they stayed like that until they slept and put out the lamp;
lines.ar_bare: فكانوا إذا جاء المصباح شدوا عينه بمنديل، ولا يزال ولا يزالون كذلك إلى أن يناموا ويطفئوا المصباح،

lines.ar: فَإِذَا أَطْفَأُوهُ أَطْلَقُوا عَيْنَيْهِ.
lines.en: and when they had put it out, they freed his eyes.
lines.ar_bare: فإذا أطفأوه أطلقوا عينيه.

translate.ar: فَكَانُوا إِذَا جَاءَ الْمِصْبَاحُ شَدُّوا عَيْنَهُ بِمِنْدِيلٍ، وَلَا يَزَالُ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ كَذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ يَنَامُوا وَيُطْفِئُوا الْمِصْبَاحَ، فَإِذَا أَطْفَأُوهُ أَطْلَقُوا عَيْنَيْهِ.
translate.en: So whenever the lamp came they would bind his eye with a handkerchief, and he and they stayed like that until they slept and put out the lamp; and when they had put it out, they freed his eyes.
They claim that a monkey was king of the animals.
translate.ar: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ مَلِكَ الْحَيَوَانَاتِ.
alt: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ مَلِكَ الْحَيَوَانِ.

translate.en: It is told that a tortoise lived near the wadi.
translate.ar: يُحْكَى أَنَّ سُلَحْفَاةً سَكَنَتْ قُرْبَ الْوَادِي.
alt: يُحْكَى أَنَّ سُلَحْفَاةً كَانَتْ تَسْكُنُ قُرْبَ الْوَادِي.

translate.en: She used to gather figs every day.
The monkey had already climbed the tree.
translate.ar: كَانَ الْقِرْدُ قَدْ صَعِدَ إِلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.
alt: وَكَانَ الْقِرْدُ قَدْ صَعِدَ إِلَى الشَّجَرَةِ.

translate.en: So he went out, found a door and entered.
alt: فَخَرَجَ ثُمَّ وَجَدَ بَابًا ثُمَّ دَخَلَ.

translate.en: While he was sitting, suddenly he heard a sound.
translate.ar: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ جَالِسٌ إِذَا سَمِعَ صَوْتًا.
alt: بَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَجْلِسُ إِذَا سَمِعَ صَوْتًا.

translate.en: The monkey said: I am sad.
The tortoise asked the monkey: Why do you throw the figs?
translate.ar: سَأَلَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ الْقِرْدَ: لِمَاذَا تَرْمِي التِّينَ؟
alt: قَالَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ لِلْقِرْدِ: لِمَاذَا تَرْمِي التِّينَ؟

translate.en: The monkey did not listen to her.
So this is a lesson for the people.
Whoever is patient finds.
The student sat in the ribāṭ, then he stood.
translate.ar: جَلَسَ الطَّالِبُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ ثُمَّ قَامَ.

readings.title_en: Proverbs and a line of poetry
readings.question_en: How do I read a saying with no verb, or a verse whose words are turned around?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ مَثَلًا لَا فِعْلَ فِيهِ، أَوْ بَيْتًا تَقَدَّمَتْ فِيهِ بَعْضُ الْكَلِمَاتِ؟

passages.intro_en: Five proverbs from al-Maydānī’s book. Read them aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Majmaʿ al-Amthāl of al-Maydānī, the section on later-coined sayings
passages.cite: Abū l-Faḍl Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Maydānī al-Naysābūrī (d. 518 H), Majmaʿ al-Amthāl, ed. Muḥammad Muḥyī l-Dīn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, Dār al-Maʿrifa, Beirut (Shamela 3.28 id 6587; the card gives no year; 2 vols), vol. 1 p. 417–418 (the page column differs from the record id, so it is the printed pagination; ./sh read 6587 2251). The proverbs follow the heading «المولدون» (later-coined sayings, not pre-Islamic ones). All five proverbs; vowels as in the source (the misprints of the copy are not used).

lines.ar: صَبْرُ سَاعَةٍ أَطْوَلُ لِلرَّاحَةِ
lines.en: An hour of patience is longer for rest (patience now buys lasting ease).
lines.ar_bare: صبر ساعة أطول للراحة

lines.ar: الصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَرَجِ
lines.en: Patience is the key to relief.
lines.ar_bare: الصبر مفتاح الفرج

lines.ar: صَفْقَةٌ بِنَقْدٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ بَدْرَةٍ بِنَسِيئَةٍ
lines.en: A cash deal is better than a purse (of 10,000 dirhams) on credit.
lines.ar_bare: صفقة بنقد خير من بدرة بنسيئة

lines.ar: الصِّنَاعَةُ فِي الْكَفِّ أَمَانٌ مِنَ الْفَقْرِ
lines.en: A craft in the hand is safety from poverty.
lines.ar_bare: الصناعة في الكف أمان من الفقر

lines.ar: صَدِيقُ الْوَالِدِ عَمُّ الْوَلَدِ
lines.en: The father's friend is the child's uncle.
lines.ar_bare: صديق الوالد عم الولد

passages.ar: صَبْرُ سَاعَةٍ أَطْوَلُ لِلرَّاحَةِ الصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَرَجِ صَفْقَةٌ بِنَقْدٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ بَدْرَةٍ بِنَسِيئَةٍ الصِّنَاعَةُ فِي الْكَفِّ أَمَانٌ مِنَ الْفَقْرِ صَدِيقُ الْوَالِدِ عَمُّ الْوَلَدِ
passages.en: An hour of patience is longer for rest (patience now buys lasting ease). Patience is the key to relief. A cash deal is better than a purse (of 10,000 dirhams) on credit. A craft in the hand is safety from poverty. The father's friend is the child's uncle.

passages.intro_en: The Habib’s circle in the evening. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text: written for this lesson (the proverbs inside it are those of al-Maydānī’s book).

lines.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ.
lines.en: In the evening Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s circle.
lines.ar_bare: في المساء جلس أحمد مع عمر في حلقة الحبيب.

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ وَمَعْنَاهُ كَبِيرٌ.
lines.en: The Habib said: A proverb is a small word, and its meaning is great.
lines.ar_bare: قال الحبيب: المثل كلمة صغيرة ومعناه كبير.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ: الرَّفِيقَ قَبْلَ الطَّرِيقِ.
lines.en: Then he said: The companion before the road.
lines.ar_bare: ثم قال: الرفيق قبل الطريق.

lines.ar: فَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ: مَا مَعْنَى هَذَا الْمَثَلِ؟
lines.en: Umar asked: What is the meaning of this proverb?
lines.ar_bare: فسأل عمر: ما معنى هذا المثل؟

lines.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: خُذِ الرَّفِيقَ الصَّالِحَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ فِي الطَّرِيقِ.
lines.en: The Habib said: Take the good companion before you set out on the road.
lines.ar_bare: قال الحبيب: خذ الرفيق الصالح قبل أن تخرج في الطريق.

lines.ar: فَإِنَّ الطَّرِيقَ طَوِيلٌ، وَالرَّفِيقُ يَسْمَعُ وَيُسَاعِدُ.
lines.en: For the road is long, and the companion listens and helps.
lines.ar_bare: فإن الطريق طويل، والرفيق يسمع ويساعد.

lines.ar: قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: أَبِي رَفِيقِي فِي الطَّرِيقِ.
lines.en: Ahmad said: My father is my companion on the road.
lines.ar_bare: قال أحمد: أبي رفيقي في الطريق.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: وَالْجَارَ ثُمَّ الدَّارَ.
lines.en: The Habib said: And the neighbour, then the house.
lines.ar_bare: فقال الحبيب: والجار ثم الدار.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ قَالَ عُمَرُ: وَالصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَرَجِ.
lines.en: Then Umar said: And patience is the key to relief.
lines.ar_bare: ثم قال عمر: والصبر مفتاح الفرج.

lines.ar: فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: هَذِهِ أَمْثَالٌ، وَفِي الشِّعْرِ بَيْتٌ يَصِيرُ مَثَلًا.
lines.en: The Habib said: These are proverbs, and in poetry there is a verse that becomes a proverb.
lines.ar_bare: فقال الحبيب: هذه أمثال، وفي الشعر بيت يصير مثلا.

passages.ar: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ. قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ وَمَعْنَاهُ كَبِيرٌ. ثُمَّ قَالَ: الرَّفِيقَ قَبْلَ الطَّرِيقِ. فَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ: مَا مَعْنَى هَذَا الْمَثَلِ؟ قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: خُذِ الرَّفِيقَ الصَّالِحَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ فِي الطَّرِيقِ. فَإِنَّ الطَّرِيقَ طَوِيلٌ، وَالرَّفِيقُ يَسْمَعُ وَيُسَاعِدُ. قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: أَبِي رَفِيقِي فِي الطَّرِيقِ. فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: وَالْجَارَ ثُمَّ الدَّارَ. ثُمَّ قَالَ عُمَرُ: وَالصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَرَجِ. فَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: هَذِهِ أَمْثَالٌ، وَفِي الشِّعْرِ بَيْتٌ يَصِيرُ مَثَلًا.
passages.en: In the evening Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s circle. The Habib said: A proverb is a small word, and its meaning is great. Then he said: The companion before the road. Umar asked: What is the meaning of this proverb? The Habib said: Take the good companion before you set out on the road. For the road is long, and the companion listens and helps. Ahmad said: My father is my companion on the road. The Habib said: And the neighbour, then the house. Then Umar said: And patience is the key to relief. The Habib said: These are proverbs, and in poetry there is a verse that becomes a proverb.

passages.intro_en: A bayt of al-Mutanabbī: the two lines are the two halves. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī, Dīwān, Shamela 3.28 id 6707 ('ديوان المتنبي'; the card names neither publisher nor editor, and says nothing on pagination: UNSURE), p. 131 of the copy, the qaṣīda «على قدر أهل العزم». Cross-checked with al-Wāḥidī, Sharḥ Dīwān al-Mutanabbī (Shamela 3.28 id 6553, digital p. 274; card: auto-numbered, not matching the print; lines 1–2 identical). The verse is already in the hub register (Homeschool_Curriculum g11_content.py, flagged) with full vowels, which agree with these. Bayt 2 (lines 3-4 of the entry); the full vowelling is the course’s (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: وَتَعْظُمُ فِي عَيْنِ الصَّغِيرِ صِغَارُهَا
lines.en: Small things grow large in the small man's eye,

lines.ar: وَتَصْغُرُ فِي عَيْنِ الْعَظِيمِ الْعَظَائِمُ
lines.en: and great things grow small in the great man's eye.

passages.ar: وَتَعْظُمُ فِي عَيْنِ الصَّغِيرِ صِغَارُهَا وَتَصْغُرُ فِي عَيْنِ الْعَظِيمِ الْعَظَائِمُ
passages.en: Small things grow large in the small man's eye, and great things grow small in the great man's eye.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 172-173 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: ذَكَرَ الْحَبِيبُ مَثَلًا: الرَّفِيقُ قَبْلَ الطَّرِيقِ.
lines.en: The Habib mentioned a proverb: The companion before the road.

lines.ar: وَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِعُمَرَ: أَنْتَ رَفِيقِي فِي الطَّرِيقِ.
lines.en: And the boy said to Umar: You are my companion on the road.

passages.ar: ذَكَرَ الْحَبِيبُ مَثَلًا: الرَّفِيقُ قَبْلَ الطَّرِيقِ. وَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِعُمَرَ: أَنْتَ رَفِيقِي فِي الطَّرِيقِ.
passages.en: The Habib mentioned a proverb: The companion before the road. And the boy said to Umar: You are my companion on the road.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: An hour of patience is longer for rest (patience now buys lasting ease).

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: A cash deal is better than a purse (of 10,000 dirhams) on credit.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: A craft in the hand is safety from poverty.

questions.q: Translate line 5.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْخَامِسَ.
questions.a: The father’s friend is the child’s uncle.

questions.q: How many of the five lines contain a verb?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ سَطْرًا فِيهِ فِعْلٌ؟
questions.a: None. Every line is made of nouns (a subject and its predicate).

questions.q: Line 2: which noun is the subject, and what is patience called?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَا الْمُبْتَدَأُ؟ وَبِمَاذَا سُمِّيَ الصَّبْرُ؟
questions.a: The subject is الصَّبْرُ. It is called “the key” (مِفْتَاحُ الْفَرَجِ): the key to relief.

questions.q: Line 3: which words mean “better than”? What is compared?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَعْنِيَانِ «أَفْضَلُ مِنْ»؟ مَا الَّذِي يُقَارَنُ؟
questions.a: خَيْرٌ مِنْ. A cash deal (صَفْقَةٌ بِنَقْدٍ) is compared with a purse on credit.

questions.q: Line 4: what is the predicate? What is the craft said to give?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: مَا الْخَبَرُ؟ مَاذَا تُعْطِي الصِّنَاعَةُ؟
questions.a: أَمَانٌ مِنَ الْفَقْرِ: safety from poverty.

questions.q: Line 5: which two nouns form a chain in the first half? In the second half?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٥: أَيُّ اِسْمَيْنِ يَكُونَانِ سِلْسِلَةً فِي النِّصْفِ الْأَوَّلِ؟ وَفِي النِّصْفِ الثَّانِي؟
questions.a: صَدِيقُ الْوَالِدِ (“the father’s friend”) and عَمُّ الْوَلَدِ (“the child’s uncle”).

questions.q: True or false: line 3 says credit is better than cash.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ السَّطْرُ ٣ إِنَّ الدَّيْنَ خَيْرٌ مِنَ النَّقْدِ.
questions.a: False. A cash deal is better than a larger purse on credit.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Proverbs (later-coined sayings) from al-Maydānī’s book Majmaʿ al-Amthāl.

questions.q: Why do proverbs prefer two nouns with no verb?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يُفَضِّلُ الْمَثَلُ جُمْلَةً مِنِ اِسْمَيْنِ بِلَا فِعْلٍ؟
questions.a: A verbless sentence is short, balanced and not tied to a time: it states a truth that holds always.

questions.q: Line 1 puts the same idea as line 2 in another way. What do the two lines teach together?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يَلْتَقِي السَّطْرَانِ ١ وَ٢ فِي مَعْنًى وَاحِدٍ؟
questions.a: Patience for a short time opens relief and brings long rest.

questions.q: Who sat in the Habib’s circle, and when?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ جَلَسَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ؟ وَمَتَى؟
questions.a: Ahmad and Umar, in the evening.

questions.q: What does the Habib say about a proverb (line 2)?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ عَنِ الْمَثَلِ؟
questions.a: It is a small word with a great meaning.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: Then he said: The companion before the road.

questions.q: What did Umar ask?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا سَأَلَ عُمَرُ؟
questions.a: What the meaning of this proverb is.

questions.q: Translate line 5.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْخَامِسَ.
questions.a: The Habib said: Take the good companion before you set out on the road.

questions.q: Why does the companion matter? (line 6)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا الرَّفِيقُ مُهِمٌّ؟
questions.a: Because the road is long, and the companion listens and helps.

questions.q: Who is Ahmad’s companion on the road? Which ending shows “my”?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ رَفِيقُ أَحْمَدَ فِي الطَّرِيقِ؟ أَيُّ نِهَايَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى «أَنَا»؟
questions.a: His father. The ending ـي in رَفِيقِي is “my”.

questions.q: Translate line 8.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّامِنَ.
questions.a: The Habib said: And the neighbour, then the house.

questions.q: True or false: the Habib says a line of poetry can become a proverb.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ إِنَّ بَيْتَ الشِّعْرِ قَدْ يَصِيرُ مَثَلًا.
questions.a: True (line 10).

questions.q: Find the word that means “proverb” and the word that means “a verse of poetry”.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَدُلُّ عَلَى الْقَوْلِ الْمَأْثُورِ وَالْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَدُلُّ عَلَى سَطْرَيْنِ مِنَ الشِّعْرِ.
questions.a: مَثَل (line 2, and أَمْثَال in line 10) and بَيْت (line 10).

questions.q: Lines 3 and 8 are proverbs with no verb, and their first word ends in ـَ (الرَّفِيقَ، الْجَارَ). What does that ending tell you?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرَانِ ٣ وَ٨ لَا فِعْلَ فِيهِمَا وَأَوَّلُهُمَا مَنْصُوبٌ. مَاذَا تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ هَذِهِ النِّهَايَةُ؟
questions.a: That a verb has been left out: “take the companion”, “look for the neighbour”.

questions.q: How does the Habib’s explanation in line 5 supply the missing verb?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يَذْكُرُ الْحَبِيبُ الْفِعْلَ الْمَحْذُوفَ فِي السَّطْرِ ٥؟
questions.a: He begins with the verb خُذِ (“take”) and puts the same noun after it: خُذِ الرَّفِيقَ.

questions.q: Translate the first half.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ النِّصْفَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: And small things grow large in the small man’s eye,

questions.q: Translate the second half.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ النِّصْفَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: and great things grow small in the great man’s eye.

questions.q: Find the verb of the first half and its doer.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْفِعْلَ وَفَاعِلَهُ فِي النِّصْفِ الْأَوَّلِ.
questions.a: The verb تَعْظُمُ (“grows large”). The doer صِغَارُهَا comes last.

questions.q: Find the verb of the second half and its doer.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْفِعْلَ وَفَاعِلَهُ فِي النِّصْفِ الثَّانِي.
questions.a: The verb تَصْغُرُ (“grows small”). The doer الْعَظَائِمُ comes last.

questions.q: Say the first half in plain order (verb first).
questions.q_ar: قُلِ النِّصْفَ الْأَوَّلَ بِالتَّرْتِيبِ الْعَادِيِّ.
questions.a: وَتَعْظُمُ صِغَارُهَا فِي عَيْنِ الصَّغِيرِ.

questions.q: Which two words are opposites, and who are the two kinds of man?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ ضِدَّانِ؟ وَمَنْ هُمَا الرَّجُلَانِ؟
questions.a: الصَّغِيرِ and الْعَظِيمِ: the small-minded man and the great-minded man.

questions.q: Which half ends with the rhyme -ā’imu?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ نِصْفٍ يَنْتَهِي بِالْقَافِيَةِ ـائِمُ؟
questions.a: The second half (الْعَظَائِمُ). Only the second half of a later bayt carries the rhyme.

questions.q: True or false: the great man thinks great things are large.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَرَى الرَّجُلُ الْعَظِيمُ الْعَظَائِمَ كَبِيرَةً.
questions.a: False. Great things grow small in his eye.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A bayt (a line of verse with two halves) by al-Mutanabbī, from the qaṣīda he composed for Sayf al-Dawla.

questions.q: The two halves mirror each other. What is the same, and what is turned around?
questions.q_ar: النِّصْفَانِ يُشْبِهُ أَحَدُهُمَا الْآخَرَ. مَا الَّذِي يَتَشَابَهُ؟ وَمَا الَّذِي يَنْعَكِسُ؟
questions.a: The frame is the same (وَتَعْظُمُ / وَتَصْغُرُ فِي عَيْنِ …); the verbs and the men are opposites, so the meaning is turned around.

questions.q: Bayt 1 (on the slides) says noble deeds come in proportion to the noble. How does bayt 2 continue the thought?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يُتَابِعُ الْبَيْتُ الثَّانِي فِكْرَةَ الْبَيْتِ الْأَوَّلِ؟
questions.a: What we call great or small depends on the man who looks: a great soul sees great matters as small.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The Habib mentioned a proverb: The companion before the road. And the boy said to Umar: You are my companion on the road.

questions.q: The proverb has no verb. What are its two halves?
questions.a: الرَّفِيقُ (the companion) and قَبْلَ الطَّرِيقِ (before the road).

questions.q: What is the proverb’s meaning?
questions.a: Choose your companion before you choose the road.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: You are my companion on the road.
questions.a: أَنْتَ رَفِيقِي فِي الطَّرِيقِ.

translate.ar: الْعِلْمُ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْمَالِ لِأَنَّ الْعِلْمَ نُورٌ.
translate.en: Knowledge is better than wealth, because knowledge is light.

translate.ar: الصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَرَجِ وَالْعَزْمُ مِفْتَاحُ الْخَيْرِ.
translate.en: Patience is the key to relief and resolve is the key to good.

translate.ar: بَيْتُ الْحَبِيبِ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ بَيْتِي وَأَقْرَبُ مِنَ السُّوقِ.
translate.en: The Habib’s house is bigger than my house and nearer than the market.

translate.ar: خُذِ الرَّفِيقَ الصَّالِحَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ.
translate.en: Take the good companion before you set out.

translate.ar: الصِّنَاعَةُ فِي الْيَدِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْمَالِ الْكَثِيرِ.
translate.en: A craft in the hand is better than much wealth.
In the ribāṭ the students sit and read.
Good manners come in proportion to knowledge.

translate.ar: لِلْبَيْتِ نِصْفَانِ، وَفِي آخِرِ الثَّانِي قَافِيَةٌ.
translate.en: A verse has two halves, and at the end of the second there is a rhyme.

translate.ar: الْجَارَ ثُمَّ الدَّارَ، وَالرَّفِيقَ قَبْلَ الطَّرِيقِ.
translate.en: The neighbour, then the house; the companion before the road.

translate.ar: الْعَزْمُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْمَالِ فِي طَلَبِ الْعِلْمِ.
translate.en: In seeking knowledge, resolve is greater than wealth.

translate.ar: مَا كُلُّ مَا يَتَمَنَّى الْمَرْءُ يُدْرِكُهُ * تَجْرِي الرِّيَاحُ بِمَا لَا تَشْتَهِي السُّفُنُ
translate.en: Not everything a man wishes for does he reach: the winds blow in ways the ships do not desire.
Knowledge is light.
Patience is the key to relief.
The companion before the road.
Knowledge is better than wealth.
The neighbour, then the house.
The father’s friend is like a brother.
The Habib’s house is bigger than my house.
A craft in the hand is better than wealth.
translate.ar: الصِّنَاعَةُ فِي الْيَدِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْمَالِ.

translate.en: Relief comes in proportion to patience.
Resolve is the key to good.
A verse has two halves.
A proverb is a small word, and its meaning is great.

readings.title_en: Science and encyclopaedia
readings.question_en: How does a reference book say what a thing is, and how do I find the word it is explaining?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ يَقُولُ كِتَابُ الْمَعْلُومَاتِ مَا هُوَ الشَّيْءُ؟ وَكَيْفَ أَجِدُ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي يَشْرَحُهَا؟

passages.source: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿUbayd Allāh al-Saqqāf, Idām al-Qūt fī Dhikr Buldān Ḥaḍramawt, the entry on ʿAyn Bāmaʿbad
passages.cite: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. Muḥsin al-Saqqāf (d. 1375 H), Idām al-Qūt fī Dhikr Buldān Ḥaḍramawt (the TLNOOR epub 702; edition: ed. Ibrāhīm Aḥmad al-Maqḥafī and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Ḥasan al-Saqqāf, Maktabat al-Irshād, Ṣanʿāʾ, as named in Minḥat al-Karīm's notes); text read in the Shamela copy of the Master Library [173760] 'إدام القوت معجم بلدان حضرموت' (Bafaqih 22222 install; with al-Maqḥafī's introduction), page 20 of that copy ('القسم الأول: مرافئ حضرموت'). A second copy [174190] exists. The copy's page numbers differ from the Maktabat al-Irshād print (the Tarīm entry is p. 573 in the copy, p. 490 in the print), so no printed page is claimed. 4 lines only (the author died 1375 H / 1955). All four lines of the entry as recorded; vowels added by the course (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: عَيْنُ بَامَعْبَدٍ: هِيَ كَقَرْيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ وَاقِعَةٍ فِي حَدِّ حَضْرَمَوْتَ الْجَنُوبِيِّ الْغَرْبِيِّ.
lines.en: ʿAyn Bāmaʿbad: it is like a small village, lying on the south-western border of Ḥaḍramawt.
lines.ar_bare: عين بامعبد: هي كقرية صغيرة واقعة في حد حضرموت الجنوبي الغربي.

lines.ar: وَفِي عَيْنِ بَامَعْبَدٍ عُيُونُ مَاءٍ عَلَيْهَا نَخْلٌ كَثِيرٌ.
lines.en: In ʿAyn Bāmaʿbad there are springs of water with many date palms on them.
lines.ar_bare: وفي عين بامعبد عيون ماء عليها نخل كثير.

lines.ar: وَسُكَّانُهَا الْآنَ – مِنَ الرِّجَالِ – نَحْوُ الْمِائَتَيْنِ، مِنْ آلِ بَامَعْبَدٍ وَآلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ.
lines.en: Its inhabitants now, of men, are about two hundred, from the Bāmaʿbad and ʿAbd Allāh families and others.
lines.ar_bare: وسكانها الآن – من الرجال – نحو المائتين، من آل بامعبد وآل عبد الله وغيرهم.

lines.ar: وَهِيَ تَبْعُدُ مِنَ السَّاحِلِ بِنَحْوِ أَرْبَعِ سَاعَاتٍ لِلْمَاشِي.
lines.en: It is about four hours' walk from the coast.
lines.ar_bare: وهي تبعد من الساحل بنحو أربع ساعات للماشي.

glossary.en: is far, lies at a distance

passages.ar: عَيْنُ بَامَعْبَدٍ: هِيَ كَقَرْيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ وَاقِعَةٍ فِي حَدِّ حَضْرَمَوْتَ الْجَنُوبِيِّ الْغَرْبِيِّ. وَفِي عَيْنِ بَامَعْبَدٍ عُيُونُ مَاءٍ عَلَيْهَا نَخْلٌ كَثِيرٌ. وَسُكَّانُهَا الْآنَ – مِنَ الرِّجَالِ – نَحْوُ الْمِائَتَيْنِ، مِنْ آلِ بَامَعْبَدٍ وَآلِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ. وَهِيَ تَبْعُدُ مِنَ السَّاحِلِ بِنَحْوِ أَرْبَعِ سَاعَاتٍ لِلْمَاشِي.
passages.en: ʿAyn Bāmaʿbad: it is like a small village, lying on the south-western border of Ḥaḍramawt. In ʿAyn Bāmaʿbad there are springs of water with many date palms on them. Its inhabitants now, of men, are about two hundred, from the Bāmaʿbad and ʿAbd Allāh families and others. It is about four hours' walk from the coast.

lines.ar: إِلَى النَّحْلِ
وَأَوْحَىٰ رَبُّكَ
مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا
وَمِنَ الشَّجَرِ
يَخْرُجُ مِن بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ
فِيهِ شِفَآءٌ لِّلنَّاسِ

passages.ar: إِلَى النَّحْلِ وَأَوْحَىٰ رَبُّكَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا وَمِنَ الشَّجَرِ يَخْرُجُ مِن بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ فِيهِ شِفَآءٌ لِّلنَّاسِ

passages.intro_en: A page of an encyclopaedia. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (written for Lesson 94 in the register of a school encyclopaedia; generic: it names no real place).

lines.ar: الْوَادِي: هُوَ مَكَانٌ بَيْنَ جَبَلَيْنِ، وَيَنْزِلُ إِلَيْهِ مَاءُ الْمَطَرِ.
lines.en: The wadi: it is a place between two mountains, and the water of the rain comes down into it.
lines.ar_bare: الوادي: هو مكان بين جبلين، وينزل إليه ماء المطر.

lines.ar: وَفِي الْوَادِي قَرْيَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ وَعُيُونٌ كَثِيرَةٌ.
lines.en: In the wadi there is a small village and many springs.
lines.ar_bare: وفي الوادي قرية صغيرة وعيون كثيرة.

lines.ar: وَالنَّخْلُ كَثِيرٌ فِي الْوَادِي لِأَنَّ الْمَاءَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْهُ.
lines.en: Palm trees are many in the wadi, because the water is near them.
lines.ar_bare: والنخل كثير في الوادي لأن الماء قريب منه.

lines.ar: وَالنَّخْلَةُ شَجَرَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ، ثَمَرُهَا التَّمْرُ، وَهُوَ طَعَامٌ جَيِّدٌ لِلصَّغِيرِ وَالْكَبِيرِ.
lines.en: The palm is a good tree; its fruit is the date, and it is good food for the small and the big.
lines.ar_bare: والنخلة شجرة طيبة، ثمرها التمر، وهو طعام جيد للصغير والكبير.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدَ الْمَطَرِ يَصِيرُ الْوَادِي جَمِيلًا، وَيَذْهَبُ النَّاسُ إِلَى النَّخْلِ وَالْعُيُونِ.
lines.en: After the rain the wadi becomes beautiful, and the people go to the palms and the springs.
lines.ar_bare: وبعد المطر يصير الوادي جميلا، ويذهب الناس إلى النخل والعيون.

lines.ar: وَفِي الْقَرْيَةِ نَحْوُ خَمْسِينَ بَيْتًا وَنَحْوُ مِائَةِ نَخْلَةٍ.
lines.en: In the village there are about fifty houses and about a hundred palm trees.
lines.ar_bare: وفي القرية نحو خمسين بيتا ونحو مائة نخلة.

passages.ar: الْوَادِي: هُوَ مَكَانٌ بَيْنَ جَبَلَيْنِ، وَيَنْزِلُ إِلَيْهِ مَاءُ الْمَطَرِ. وَفِي الْوَادِي قَرْيَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ وَعُيُونٌ كَثِيرَةٌ. وَالنَّخْلُ كَثِيرٌ فِي الْوَادِي لِأَنَّ الْمَاءَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْهُ. وَالنَّخْلَةُ شَجَرَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ، ثَمَرُهَا التَّمْرُ، وَهُوَ طَعَامٌ جَيِّدٌ لِلصَّغِيرِ وَالْكَبِيرِ. وَبَعْدَ الْمَطَرِ يَصِيرُ الْوَادِي جَمِيلًا، وَيَذْهَبُ النَّاسُ إِلَى النَّخْلِ وَالْعُيُونِ. وَفِي الْقَرْيَةِ نَحْوُ خَمْسِينَ بَيْتًا وَنَحْوُ مِائَةِ نَخْلَةٍ.
passages.en: The wadi: it is a place between two mountains, and the water of the rain comes down into it. In the wadi there is a small village and many springs. Palm trees are many in the wadi, because the water is near them. The palm is a good tree; its fruit is the date, and it is good food for the small and the big. After the rain the wadi becomes beautiful, and the people go to the palms and the springs. In the village there are about fifty houses and about a hundred palm trees.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 174-175 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الْوَادِي فَرَأَى نَخْلًا كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: The boy went with his father to the wadi and saw many date palms.

lines.ar: وَالنَّخْلَةُ شَجَرَةٌ ثَمَرُهَا طَيِّبٌ، وَعِنْدَهَا عَيْنُ مَاءٍ.
lines.en: The date palm is a tree whose fruit is good, and by it is a spring of water.

passages.ar: ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الْوَادِي فَرَأَى نَخْلًا كَثِيرًا. وَالنَّخْلَةُ شَجَرَةٌ ثَمَرُهَا طَيِّبٌ، وَعِنْدَهَا عَيْنُ مَاءٍ.
passages.en: The boy went with his father to the wadi and saw many date palms. The date palm is a tree whose fruit is good, and by it is a spring of water.
