questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: ʿAyn Bāmaʿbad: it is like a small village, lying on the south-western border of Ḥaḍramawt.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A reference entry (a gazetteer, a book of places): the place name, a colon, then هِيَ and a description, followed by facts and numbers.

questions.q: Which words does line 1 define, and what shows it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ يُعَرِّفُهَا السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ؟ وَمَا الدَّلِيلُ؟
questions.a: عَيْنُ بَامَعْبَدٍ: they stand before the colon and هِيَ follows.

questions.q: Why هِيَ and not هُوَ?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا «هِيَ» وَلَيْسَ «هُوَ»؟
questions.a: Because عَيْن (the place) is feminine.

questions.q: Where does the place lie?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ تَقَعُ الْقَرْيَةُ؟
questions.a: On the south-western border of Ḥaḍramawt.

questions.q: What is found in the place? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فِي الْقَرْيَةِ؟
questions.a: Springs of water with many palm trees on them.

questions.q: How many men live there, and which word tells you the number is not exact?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ رَجُلًا يَسْكُنُ هُنَاكَ؟ وَمَا الْكَلِمَةُ الَّتِي تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الْعَدَدَ تَقْرِيبِيٌّ؟
questions.a: About two hundred; the word is نَحْوُ (“about”).

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: And it is about four hours’ walk from the coast.

questions.q: True or false: the place is right next to the coast.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: الْقَرْيَةُ بِجَانِبِ السَّاحِلِ.
questions.a: False. It is about four hours’ walk from it.

questions.q: Both words end in ـِيِّ. What is this ending called, and what does it do?
questions.q_ar: كِلْتَا الْكَلِمَتَيْنِ تَنْتَهِي بِـ ـِيِّ. مَا اسْمُ هَذِهِ النِّهَايَةِ؟ وَمَاذَا تَفْعَلُ؟
questions.a: The nisba: it turns “south” and “west” into “of the south”, “of the west”: south-western.

questions.q: The entry counts only the men. What should a careful reader say about the whole population?
questions.q_ar: يَعُدُّ الْكَاتِبُ الرِّجَالَ فَقَطْ. مَاذَا يَقُولُ الْقَارِئُ الْحَذِرُ عَنْ جَمِيعِ السُّكَّانِ؟
questions.a: Only that the text counts men: it does not say how many people live there. A careful reader says what the text says and no more.

questions.q: The entry fixes the place in two ways: by its border and by a walking distance. Why does a traveller need both?
questions.q_ar: يُحَدِّدُ الْكَاتِبُ الْمَكَانَ بِطَرِيقَتَيْنِ: بِالْحَدِّ وَبِمَسَافَةِ الْمَشْيِ. لِمَاذَا يَحْتَاجُ الْمُسَافِرُ إِلَيْهِمَا مَعًا؟
questions.a: The border tells where in Ḥaḍramawt it lies; the hours on foot tell how far it is from the coast. A place is fixed by direction and by distance.

questions.q: Which small creature is named here?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ مَخْلُوقٍ صَغِيرٍ يُذْكَرُ هُنَا؟
questions.a: The bee (النَّحْلُ).

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: And your Lord inspired…

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: …among the mountains, houses…

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: …and among the trees.

questions.q: Translate.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ.
questions.a: There comes out of their bellies a drink…

questions.q: Translate. Who is it good for?
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمْ. لِمَنْ هُوَ؟
questions.a: In it is healing for people. It is for the people (النَّاسِ).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how can you tell it is not an encyclopaedia entry?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ تَعْرِفُ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ مَقَالَةً فِي مَوْسُوعَةٍ؟
questions.a: A verse of the Qur’an: it is fully vowelled, it speaks to the bee, and it has no “word, colon, هُوَ” frame.

questions.q: The encyclopaedia says what honey IS; the verse says what it DOES. Put the difference in one sentence.
questions.q_ar: تَقُولُ الْمَوْسُوعَةُ مَا هُوَ الْعَسَلُ، وَتَقُولُ الْآيَةُ مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ. اُكْتُبِ الْفَرْقَ فِي جُمْلَةٍ.
questions.a: A reference entry defines (what the thing is); the verse speaks of the bee and of what comes out of it for people (its use and its sign).

questions.q: Which word is being defined in line 1, and how can you tell?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ يُعَرِّفُهَا السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: الْوَادِي: it stands before the colon and هُوَ follows it.

questions.q: Where does the rain water go?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ يَنْزِلُ مَاءُ الْمَطَرِ؟
questions.a: Down into the wadi.

questions.q: What is in the wadi besides palms? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فِي الْوَادِي غَيْرُ النَّخْلِ؟
questions.a: A small village and many springs.

questions.q: Why are there many palms in the wadi? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا النَّخْلُ كَثِيرٌ فِي الْوَادِي؟
questions.a: Because the water is near them.

questions.q: What does وَهُوَ stand for in line 4?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَاذَا يَرْجِعُ ضَمِيرُ «وَهُوَ»؟
questions.a: The date (التَّمْرُ), not the tree.

questions.q: True or false: dates are good only for the big.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: التَّمْرُ جَيِّدٌ لِلْكَبِيرِ فَقَطْ.
questions.a: False: they are good for the small and the big.

questions.q: Translate line 5.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْخَامِسَ.
questions.a: After the rain the wadi becomes beautiful, and the people go to the palms and the springs.

questions.q: Translate line 6.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ السَّادِسَ.
questions.a: In the village there are about fifty houses and about a hundred palm trees.

questions.q: Does the writer say there are exactly fifty houses?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ يَقُولُ الْكَاتِبُ إِنَّ الْبُيُوتَ خَمْسُونَ بِالضَّبْطِ؟
questions.a: No. نَحْوُ means “about”.

questions.q: Line 3 gives a reason (لِأَنَّ). Why is a reason useful in a reference entry?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّالِثِ سَبَبٌ (لِأَنَّ). لِمَاذَا يَنْفَعُ السَّبَبُ فِي كِتَابِ مَعْلُومَاتٍ؟
questions.a: It turns a bare fact into an explanation: the reader learns why palms are many here, not only that they are.

questions.q: Line 4 defines the palm inside a longer entry. How is it built, compared with the frame “word, colon, هُوَ”?
questions.q_ar: يُعَرِّفُ السَّطْرُ الرَّابِعُ النَّخْلَةَ دَاخِلَ مَقَالَةٍ أَطْوَلَ. كَيْفَ بُنِيَ مُقَارَنَةً بِقَالَبِ «الْكَلِمَةُ، نُقْطَتَانِ، هُوَ»؟
questions.a: Word + noun + adjective, then “its fruit is…”: the same ingredients as the frame, joined to the rest by وَ instead of a colon.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy went with his father to the wadi and saw many date palms. The date palm is a tree whose fruit is good, and by it is a spring of water.

questions.q: Which word means date palms as a group, and which means one date palm?
questions.a: نَخْلًا (date palms) and النَّخْلَةُ (one date palm)

questions.q: What does عَيْنُ مَاءٍ mean here? (It is not “eye”.)
questions.a: A spring of water.

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The date palm is a tree.
questions.a: النَّخْلَةُ شَجَرَةٌ.

translate.ar: النَّخْلَةُ شَجَرَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ، وَثَمَرُهَا طَعَامٌ جَيِّدٌ لِلنَّاسِ.
translate.en: The palm is a good tree, and its fruit is good food for people.

translate.ar: الْعَسَلُ طَعَامٌ طَيِّبٌ، وَالنَّحْلُ يَأْخُذُ طَعَامَهُ مِنَ النَّبَاتِ.
translate.en: Honey is a good food, and the bees take their food from plants.

translate.ar: الْعَيْنُ مَكَانٌ يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ، وَفِي الْقَرْيَةِ عَيْنٌ كَبِيرَةٌ.
translate.en: A spring is a place from which water comes out, and in the village there is a big spring.

translate.ar: يَسْكُنُ فِي الْقَرْيَةِ نَحْوُ مِائَةِ رَجُلٍ مِنَ الطُّلَّابِ وَالْعُلَمَاءِ.
translate.en: About a hundred men, students and scholars, live in the village.

translate.ar: الْوَادِي الْجَنُوبِيُّ بَعِيدٌ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ، وَالْوَادِي الْغَرْبِيُّ قَرِيبٌ مِنْهَا.
translate.en: The southern wadi is far from the city, and the western wadi is near it.

translate.ar: إِذَا نَزَلَ الْمَطَرُ فِي الْجَبَلِ جَاءَ الْمَاءُ إِلَى الْوَادِي.
translate.en: When the rain comes down on the mountain, water comes to the wadi.

translate.ar: سَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ الْمُعَلِّمَ: مَا النَّخْلُ؟ فَقَالَ: النَّخْلُ شَجَرٌ ثَمَرُهُ التَّمْرُ.
translate.en: The boy asked the teacher: What are date palms? He said: Date palms are trees whose fruit is the date.

translate.ar: لَا يُوجَدُ النَّخْلُ فِي كُلِّ مَكَانٍ، لَكِنَّهُ كَثِيرٌ فِي الْوَادِي.
translate.en: Palms are not found in every place, but they are many in the wadi.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ تَعْرِيفَ الْعَسَلِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ ثُمَّ كَتَبَهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ.
translate.en: Ahmad read the definition of honey in the dictionary and then wrote it in his book.

translate.source: Ibn al-Wardī, Kharīdat al-ʿAjāʾib wa-Farīdat al-Gharāʾib, the entry on the date palm

lines.ar: النَّخْلُ: هُوَ أَوَّلُ شَجَرَةٍ اسْتَقَرَّتْ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ، وَهِيَ شَجَرَةٌ مُبَارَكَةٌ لَا تُوجَدُ فِي كُلِّ مَكَانٍ.
lines.en: The date palm: it is the first tree that settled on the face of the earth, and it is a blessed tree not found everywhere.

lines.ar: وَالْجُمَّارُ مِنَ النَّخْلَةِ كَالْمُخِّ مِنَ الْإِنْسَانِ، وَعَلَيْهَا اللِّيفُ كَشَعْرِ الْإِنْسَانِ.
lines.en: The pith of the palm is like the brain in a person, and fibre covers it like a person's hair.

translate.ar: النَّخْلُ: هُوَ أَوَّلُ شَجَرَةٍ اسْتَقَرَّتْ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْأَرْضِ، وَهِيَ شَجَرَةٌ مُبَارَكَةٌ لَا تُوجَدُ فِي كُلِّ مَكَانٍ. وَالْجُمَّارُ مِنَ النَّخْلَةِ كَالْمُخِّ مِنَ الْإِنْسَانِ، وَعَلَيْهَا اللِّيفُ كَشَعْرِ الْإِنْسَانِ.
translate.en: The date palm: it is the first tree that settled on the face of the earth, and it is a blessed tree not found everywhere. The pith of the palm is like the brain in a person, and fibre covers it like a person's hair.

glossary.en: the pith, the heart of the palm

translate.en: The date palm: it is a big tree.
The spring: it is a place from which the water comes out.
translate.ar: الْعَيْنُ: هِيَ مَكَانٌ يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ.

translate.en: Honey: it is a good food.
The wadi: it is a place between two mountains.
The village: it is a small place, and about fifty men live in it.
translate.ar: الْقَرْيَةُ: هِيَ مَكَانٌ صَغِيرٌ، وَيَسْكُنُ فِيهَا نَحْوُ خَمْسِينَ رَجُلًا.
alt: الْقَرْيَةُ: هِيَ مَكَانٌ صَغِيرٌ يَسْكُنُ فِيهِ نَحْوُ خَمْسِينَ رَجُلًا.

translate.en: The village is in the southern wadi.
Bees: they are small animals, and their honey is good food.
translate.ar: النَّحْلُ: هُوَ حَيَوَانٌ صَغِيرٌ، وَعَسَلُهُ طَعَامٌ طَيِّبٌ.
alt: النَّحْلُ: حَيَوَانٌ صَغِيرٌ، وَعَسَلُهُ طَعَامٌ طَيِّبٌ.

translate.en: The Hadrami palms are many in the wadi.
Between the village and the city there are four hours.
Tarim: it is a city in Ḥaḍramawt.

readings.title_en: Biography and history
readings.question_en: How do I read a history or a life: what happened, in what order, and why?
readings.question_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ تَارِيخًا أَوْ سِيرَةَ إِنْسَانٍ: مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟ وَبِأَيِّ تَرْتِيبٍ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟

passages.intro_en: The founding of a city. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.source: Munīr b. Sālim Bāzuhayr, Minḥat al-Karīm bi-Dhikr Khulāṣa min Tārīkh Madīnat Tarīm (Tarīm, 2017), p. 11
passages.cite: Munīr b. Sālim b. Saʿd Bāzuhayr, Minḥat al-Karīm bi-Dhikr Khulāṣa min Tārīkh Madīnat Tarīm, Maktabat Tarīm al-Ḥadītha li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr wa-l-Tawzīʿ, Tarīm (Ḥaḍramawt), 1st ed. 1438 H / 2017 (title page read on the PDF image; TLNOOR 673, 81 pp), printed p. 11 (al-Maṭlab al-awwal: 'fī tārīkh taʾsīs madīnat Tarīm'). In copyright (2017): four print lines only, cited. The 2nd line is the last clause of the same paragraph (elided: the intervening sentences on the Sabaean dynasty and Ibn Bilfaqīh). Two print lines only (in copyright); vowels added by the course (vowelled for learners).

lines.ar: اتَّفَقَ مُؤَرِّخُو الْعَرَبِ قَبْلَ الْإِسْلَامِ عَلَى أَنَّ تَأْسِيسَ مَدِينَةِ (تَرِيمَ) وَاخْتِطَاطَهَا كَانَ فِي عَهْدِ الدَّوْلَةِ السَّبَئِيَّةِ، الَّتِي امْتَدَّتْ مِنَ الْقَرْنِ الرَّابِعَ عَشَرَ قَبْلَ الْمِيلَادِ إِلَى الْقَرْنِ السَّادِسِ بَعْدَهُ.
lines.en: The historians of the Arabs before Islam agreed that the founding and laying-out of the city of Tarīm took place in the time of the Sabaean state, which extended from the fourteenth century BC to the sixth century after it.
lines.ar_bare: اتفق مؤرخو العرب قبل الإسلام على أن تأسيس مدينة (تريم) واختطاطها كان في عهد الدولة السبئية، التي امتدت من القرن الرابع عشر قبل الميلاد إلى القرن السادس بعده.

lines.ar: وَأَنَّ تَرِيمَ أَحَدُ أَوْلَادِ سَبَأٍ الْأَصْغَرِ، نَزَلَ حَضْرَمَوْتَ وَأَسَّسَ مَدِينَةَ تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: And that Tarīm, one of the children of Saba the Younger, settled in Ḥaḍramawt and founded the city of Tarīm.
lines.ar_bare: وأن تريم أحد أولاد سبأ الأصغر، نزل حضرموت وأسس مدينة تريم.

passages.ar: اتَّفَقَ مُؤَرِّخُو الْعَرَبِ قَبْلَ الْإِسْلَامِ عَلَى أَنَّ تَأْسِيسَ مَدِينَةِ (تَرِيمَ) وَاخْتِطَاطَهَا كَانَ فِي عَهْدِ الدَّوْلَةِ السَّبَئِيَّةِ، الَّتِي امْتَدَّتْ مِنَ الْقَرْنِ الرَّابِعَ عَشَرَ قَبْلَ الْمِيلَادِ إِلَى الْقَرْنِ السَّادِسِ بَعْدَهُ. وَأَنَّ تَرِيمَ أَحَدُ أَوْلَادِ سَبَأٍ الْأَصْغَرِ، نَزَلَ حَضْرَمَوْتَ وَأَسَّسَ مَدِينَةَ تَرِيمَ.
passages.en: The historians of the Arabs before Islam agreed that the founding and laying-out of the city of Tarīm took place in the time of the Sabaean state, which extended from the fourteenth century BC to the sixth century after it. And that Tarīm, one of the children of Saba the Younger, settled in Ḥaḍramawt and founded the city of Tarīm.

passages.intro_en: The life of a physician. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text (written for Lesson 95 in the register of a short biography; the person and the years are made up).

lines.ar: وُلِدَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ سَالِمٍ فِي قَرْيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ فِي الْوَادِي سَنَةَ ١٣٠٠ هـ.
lines.en: ʿAlī b. Sālim was born in a small village in the wadi in the year 1300 AH.
lines.ar_bare: ولد علي بن سالم في قرية صغيرة في الوادي سنة ١٣٠٠ ه.

lines.ar: وَنَشَأَ فِي بَيْتِ عَمِّهِ، لِأَنَّ أَبَاهُ تُوُفِّيَ وَهُوَ صَغِيرٌ.
lines.en: And he grew up in his uncle’s house, because his father died when he was small.
lines.ar_bare: ونشأ في بيت عمه، لأن أباه توفي وهو صغير.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ دَرَسَ فِي مَدْرَسَةِ الْقَرْيَةِ، وَكَانَ يَقْرَأُ الْكُتُبَ بَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ.
lines.en: Then he studied in the village school, and he used to read books after the lesson.
lines.ar_bare: ثم درس في مدرسة القرية، وكان يقرأ الكتب بعد الدرس.

lines.ar: وَفِي سَنَةِ ١٣٢٠ هـ سَافَرَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لِيَصِيرَ طَبِيبًا.
lines.en: And in the year 1320 AH he travelled to the city to become a physician.
lines.ar_bare: وفي سنة ١٣٢٠ ه سافر إلى المدينة ليصير طبيبا.

lines.ar: وَبَعْدَ سَنَتَيْنِ رَجَعَ إِلَى الْوَادِي طَبِيبًا.
lines.en: And after two years he returned to the wadi a physician.
lines.ar_bare: وبعد سنتين رجع إلى الوادي طبيبا.

passages.ar: وُلِدَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ سَالِمٍ فِي قَرْيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ فِي الْوَادِي سَنَةَ ١٣٠٠ هـ. وَنَشَأَ فِي بَيْتِ عَمِّهِ، لِأَنَّ أَبَاهُ تُوُفِّيَ وَهُوَ صَغِيرٌ. ثُمَّ دَرَسَ فِي مَدْرَسَةِ الْقَرْيَةِ، وَكَانَ يَقْرَأُ الْكُتُبَ بَعْدَ الدَّرْسِ. وَفِي سَنَةِ ١٣٢٠ هـ سَافَرَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ لِيَصِيرَ طَبِيبًا. وَبَعْدَ سَنَتَيْنِ رَجَعَ إِلَى الْوَادِي طَبِيبًا.
passages.en: ʿAlī b. Sālim was born in a small village in the wadi in the year 1300 AH. And he grew up in his uncle’s house, because his father died when he was small. Then he studied in the village school, and he used to read books after the lesson. And in the year 1320 AH he travelled to the city to become a physician. And after two years he returned to the wadi a physician.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 176-177 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ كِتَابَ تَارِيخٍ عَنْ تَأْسِيسِ تَرِيمَ.
lines.en: The boy read a history book about the founding of Tarim.

lines.ar: وَقَرَأَ: أُسِّسَتْ تَرِيمُ قَبْلَ وَقْتٍ طَوِيلٍ.
lines.en: And he read: Tarim was founded a long time ago.

passages.ar: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ كِتَابَ تَارِيخٍ عَنْ تَأْسِيسِ تَرِيمَ. وَقَرَأَ: أُسِّسَتْ تَرِيمُ قَبْلَ وَقْتٍ طَوِيلٍ.
passages.en: The boy read a history book about the founding of Tarim. And he read: Tarim was founded a long time ago.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: The historians of the Arabs before Islam agreed that the founding and laying-out of the city of Tarīm took place in the time of the Sabaean state, which extended from the fourteenth century BC to the sixth century after it.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: And that Tarīm, one of the children of Saba the Younger, settled in Ḥaḍramawt and founded the city of Tarīm.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A history of a city: it speaks of founding, of an era and of centuries, and it gives the historians as its authority (the historians “agreed”).

questions.q: Who agreed, and what did they agree on? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّفَقُوا؟ وَعَلَى مَاذَا؟
questions.a: The historians of the Arabs before Islam agreed that Tarim was founded in the time of the Sabaean state.

questions.q: Which word means “founding”? Which verb in line 2 has the same root?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «التَّأْسِيسَ»؟ وَأَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي مِنْ جَذْرِهَا؟
questions.a: تَأْسِيس; the verb أَسَّسَ (root أ س س).

questions.q: In which time was the city founded, according to line 1?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ عَهْدٍ تَأَسَّسَتِ الْمَدِينَةُ؟
questions.a: In the time of the Sabaean state.

questions.q: Which centuries does the Sabaean state cover?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ قُرُونٍ تَشْمَلُ الدَّوْلَةُ السَّبَئِيَّةُ؟
questions.a: From the fourteenth century BC to the sixth century AD.
questions.ref_ar: مِنَ الْقَرْنِ الرَّابِعَ عَشَرَ قَبْلَ الْمِيلَادِ

questions.q: Who founded the city, according to line 2?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ أَسَّسَ الْمَدِينَةَ؟
questions.a: Tarim, one of the children of Saba the Younger.

questions.q: True or false: Tarim stayed in Saba and never went to Ḥaḍramawt.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: بَقِيَ تَرِيمُ فِي سَبَأٍ وَلَمْ يَذْهَبْ إِلَى حَضْرَمَوْتَ.
questions.a: False: he settled in Ḥaḍramawt (نَزَلَ حَضْرَمَوْتَ) and founded the city there.

questions.q: Which little words introduce what the historians agreed on?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ صَغِيرَةٍ تُقَدِّمُ مَا اتَّفَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْمُؤَرِّخُونَ؟
questions.a: عَلَى أَنَّ (“that”), repeated in line 2 as وَأَنَّ.

questions.q: The historians “agreed”. Does that make the event certain? How should a careful reader report it?
questions.q_ar: اتَّفَقَ الْمُؤَرِّخُونَ. هَلْ يَجْعَلُ هَذَا الْحَدَثَ يَقِينًا؟ كَيْفَ يَنْقُلُهُ الْقَارِئُ الْحَذِرُ؟
questions.a: It tells us what the historians report and that they agree, not that the event is proved. A careful reader says “according to the historians”.

questions.q: Line 1 is one long sentence. Where would you cut it into three pieces?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ الْأَوَّلُ جُمْلَةٌ طَوِيلَةٌ. أَيْنَ تَقْطَعُهَا إِلَى ثَلَاثَةِ أَجْزَاءٍ؟
questions.a: (1) The historians agreed that (2) the founding of Tarim took place in the time of the Sabaean state, (3) which extended from the fourteenth century BC to the sixth AD.

questions.q: Who is the text about, and where was he born? (line 1)
questions.q_ar: عَنْ مَنْ هَذَا النَّصُّ؟ وَأَيْنَ وُلِدَ؟
questions.a: ʿAlī b. Sālim, born in a small village in the wadi.

questions.q: In which year was he born?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ سَنَةٍ وُلِدَ؟
questions.a: In the year 1300 AH.

questions.q: Why did he grow up in his uncle’s house? (line 2)
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا نَشَأَ فِي بَيْتِ عَمِّهِ؟
questions.a: Because his father died when he was small.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: Then he studied in the village school, and he used to read books after the lesson.

questions.q: Where did he study? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ دَرَسَ؟
questions.a: In the village school.

questions.q: Which word shows that studying came after growing up?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الدِّرَاسَةَ جَاءَتْ بَعْدَ النَّشْأَةِ؟
questions.a: ثُمَّ (“then”).

questions.q: Where did he travel in 1320, and why? (line 4)
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ سَافَرَ سَنَةَ ١٣٢٠؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: To the city, to become a physician.

questions.q: What does لِـ at the start of لِيَصِيرَ tell you?
questions.q_ar: عَلَامَ تَدُلُّ «لِـ» فِي أَوَّلِ «لِيَصِيرَ»؟
questions.a: His purpose: he travelled so that he would become a physician.

questions.q: Translate line 5.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْخَامِسَ.
questions.a: And after two years he returned to the wadi a physician.

questions.q: How long after did he return? (line 5)
questions.q_ar: بَعْدَ كَمْ سَنَةً رَجَعَ؟
questions.a: After two years.

questions.q: True or false: he stayed in the city all his life.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: بَقِيَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ طُولَ حَيَاتِهِ.
questions.a: False: he returned to the wadi.

questions.q: Which line gives a cause, not only an event? Which word shows it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ يُعْطِي سَبَبًا لَا حَدَثًا فَقَطْ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ؟
questions.a: Line 2: لِأَنَّ introduces the cause of growing up in his uncle’s house.

questions.q: How many years lie between the dates of line 1 and line 4? What does it tell you about his age?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ سَنَةً بَيْنَ تَارِيخِ السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ وَتَارِيخِ السَّطْرِ الرَّابِعِ؟ مَاذَا يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ عَنْ عُمْرِهِ؟
questions.a: Twenty years: he was about twenty when he travelled.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy read a history book about the founding of Tarim. And he read: Tarim was founded a long time ago.

questions.q: Which verb is passive (we are not told who did it)?
questions.a: أُسِّسَتْ (it was founded)

questions.q: What does قَبْلَ وَقْتٍ طَوِيلٍ mean?
questions.a: A long time ago (literally: before a long time).

questions.q: Write in Arabic: The boy read a history book.
questions.a: قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ كِتَابَ تَارِيخٍ.

translate.ar: بُنِيَ الْمَسْجِدُ قَبْلَ مِائَةِ سَنَةٍ، ثُمَّ أُسِّسَتِ الْمَدْرَسَةُ بَعْدَ سَنَتَيْنِ.
translate.en: The mosque was built a hundred years ago, then the school was founded two years later.

translate.ar: وُلِدَ الْعَالِمُ فِي قَرْيَةٍ سَنَةَ ١٣٠٠ هـ، وَتُوُفِّيَ فِيهَا سَنَةَ ١٣٧٠ هـ.
translate.en: The scholar was born in a village in the year 1300 AH and died there in the year 1370 AH.

translate.ar: كَانَ الْمَاءُ قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْقَرْيَةِ، فَسَكَنَ النَّاسُ هُنَاكَ.
translate.en: The water was near the village, so the people settled there.

translate.ar: أُسِّسَتِ الْمَكْتَبَةُ لِأَنَّ الطُّلَّابَ كَانُوا كَثِيرِينَ، وَلِذَلِكَ جَاءَ إِلَيْهَا النَّاسُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ.
translate.en: The library was founded because the students were many, and so the people came to it from every place.

translate.ar: السَّبَبُ هُوَ الْمَطَرُ، وَالنَّتِيجَةُ أَنَّ الْوَادِي صَارَ جَمِيلًا.
translate.en: The cause is the rain, and the result is that the wadi became beautiful.

translate.ar: قَرَأَ أَحْمَدُ خَبَرًا عَنْ تَأْسِيسِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
translate.en: Ahmad read a report about the founding of the city.

translate.ar: بُنِيَتْ مَدْرَسَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ لِأَنَّ الْمَدْرَسَةَ الْقَدِيمَةَ كَانَتْ صَغِيرَةً.
translate.en: A new school was built because the old school was small.

translate.ar: تَأْسِيسُ الدَّوْلَةِ حَدَثٌ كَبِيرٌ فِي تَارِيخِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
translate.en: The founding of the state is a big event in the history of the city.

translate.ar: اتَّفَقَ الْمُؤَرِّخُونَ عَلَى أَنَّ الْمَدِينَةَ قَدِيمَةٌ جِدًّا.
translate.en: The historians agreed that the city is very old.

lines.ar: وَفِي سَنَةِ ١٣٢٦ هـ بُنِيَ لَهُ بَيْتٌ صَغِيرٌ لِلدَّوَاءِ فِي الْقَرْيَةِ، فَجَاءَ إِلَيْهِ النَّاسُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ.
lines.en: And in the year 1326 AH a small house for medicine was built for him in the village, and the people came to it from every place.

lines.ar: وَبِسَبَبِ عَمَلِهِ الْجَيِّدِ كَانَ النَّاسُ يَشْكُرُونَهُ.
lines.en: And because of his good work the people used to thank him.

lines.ar: وَتُوُفِّيَ سَنَةَ ١٣٧٠ هـ، وَدُفِنَ فِي قَرْيَتِهِ.
lines.en: He died in the year 1370 AH, and was buried in his village.

translate.ar: وَفِي سَنَةِ ١٣٢٦ هـ بُنِيَ لَهُ بَيْتٌ صَغِيرٌ لِلدَّوَاءِ فِي الْقَرْيَةِ، فَجَاءَ إِلَيْهِ النَّاسُ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ. وَبِسَبَبِ عَمَلِهِ الْجَيِّدِ كَانَ النَّاسُ يَشْكُرُونَهُ. وَتُوُفِّيَ سَنَةَ ١٣٧٠ هـ، وَدُفِنَ فِي قَرْيَتِهِ.
translate.en: And in the year 1326 AH a small house for medicine was built for him in the village, and the people came to it from every place. And because of his good work the people used to thank him. He died in the year 1370 AH, and was buried in his village.
The mosque was built a hundred years ago.
The school was founded in the year 1350 AH.
The scholar was born in Tarim, then he studied in the ribāṭ.
translate.ar: وُلِدَ الْعَالِمُ فِي تَرِيمَ ثُمَّ دَرَسَ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.

translate.en: The rain came down, so the wadi became beautiful.
alt: نَزَلَ الْمَطَرُ، وَلِذَلِكَ صَارَ الْوَادِي جَمِيلًا.

translate.en: The library was founded because the students were many.
translate.ar: أُسِّسَتِ الْمَكْتَبَةُ لِأَنَّ الطُّلَّابَ كَانُوا كَثِيرِينَ.

translate.en: He died after two years.
A big house was built for the books.
The cause was the rain, and the result was much water.
translate.ar: السَّبَبُ هُوَ الْمَطَرُ، وَالنَّتِيجَةُ مَاءٌ كَثِيرٌ.

translate.en: He was born in the year 1300 AH and died in the year 1370 AH.
translate.ar: وُلِدَ سَنَةَ ١٣٠٠ هـ وَتُوُفِّيَ سَنَةَ ١٣٧٠ هـ.

translate.en: The state was founded after a long time.

readings.title_en: The travel narrative
readings.question_en: Who is travelling, from where to where, and how long did it take?
readings.question_ar: مَنْ يُسَافِرُ؟ مِنْ أَيْنَ؟ إِلَى أَيْنَ؟ وَكَمْ يَوْمًا؟

passages.intro_en: A traveller sails to the coast of Ẓafār. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa, Riḥlat Ibn Baṭṭūṭa (Tuḥfat al-Nuẓẓār fī Gharāʾib al-Amṣār wa-ʿAjāʾib al-Asfār), Shamela 3.28 id 5997 (the card names no publisher; 'auto-numbered, not matching the print'), digital pp. 122–123 of the copy. The same passage is in the Master Library copy [40250] 'رحلة ابن بطوطة ط دار الشرق العربي' (digital p. 199; with misprint ستة وعشر), and the book's Rabat Academy edition ([40240], ed. ʿAbd al-Hādī al-Tāzī, 1997) is a third witness: no printed page is claimed. IMPORTANT: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa never visited Ḥaḍramawt; he mentions it only as a distance (this passage) and the tomb of Hūd near Ẓafār (digital p. 41); the 'رحلة مغربي إلى حضرموت' is a modern fabrication, as the editor's introduction to the Academy edition notes (copy [40240], p. 117). Lines 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the five in the research file (line 3, on crops and wells, left out). Vowelled for learners (the printed copy is unvowelled).

lines.ar: وَرَكِبْنَا الْبَحْرَ مِنْ كِلْوَا إِلَى مَدِينَةِ ظَفَارِ الْحُمُوضِ «وَضُبِطَ اسْمُهَا بِفَتْحِ الظَّاءِ الْمُعْجَمِ وَالْفَاءِ وَآخِرُهُ رَاءٌ مَبْنِيَّةٌ عَلَى الْكَسْرِ»، وَهِيَ آخِرُ بِلَادِ الْيَمَنِ عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ الْهِنْدِيِّ، وَمِنْهَا تُحْمَلُ الْخَيْلُ الْعِتَاقُ إِلَى الْهِنْدِ.
lines.en: We sailed from Kilwa to the city of Ẓafār al-Ḥumūḍ («its name is spelt with fatḥa on the dotted ẓāʾ and on the fāʾ, and ends in a rāʾ built on kasra»); it is the last of the lands of Yemen on the coast of the Indian Ocean, and from it the thoroughbred horses are shipped to India.
lines.ar_bare: وركبنا البحر من كلوا إلى مدينة ظفار الحموض «وضبط اسمها بفتح الظاء المعجم والفاء وآخره راء مبنية على الكسر»، وهي آخر بلاد اليمن على ساحل البحر الهندي، ومنها تحمل الخيل العتاق إلى الهند.

lines.ar: وَبَيْنَ ظَفَارَ وَعَدَنَ فِي الْبَرِّ مَسِيرَةُ شَهْرٍ فِي صَحْرَاءَ.
lines.en: Between Ẓafār and Aden by land is a month's journey through desert.
lines.ar_bare: وبين ظفار وعدن في البر مسيرة شهر في صحراء.

lines.ar: وَبَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَضْرَمَوْتَ سِتَّةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا، وَبَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ عُمَانَ عِشْرُونَ يَوْمًا.
lines.en: Between it and Ḥaḍramawt are sixteen days, and between it and Oman twenty days.
lines.ar_bare: وبينها وبين حضرموت ستة عشر يوما، وبينها وبين عمان عشرون يوما.

lines.ar: وَهُمْ أَهْلُ تِجَارَةٍ لَا عَيْشَ لَهُمْ إِلَّا مِنْهَا.
lines.en: They are people of trade, with no living except from it.
lines.ar_bare: وهم أهل تجارة لا عيش لهم إلا منها.

lines.ar: وَهُمْ أَهْلُ تَوَاضُعٍ وَحُسْنِ أَخْلَاقٍ وَفَضِيلَةٍ وَمَحَبَّةٍ لِلْغُرَبَاءِ، وَلِبَاسُهُمُ الْقُطْنُ، وَهُوَ يُجْلَبُ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ بِلَادِ الْهِنْدِ.
lines.en: They are people of humility, good character, virtue and love of strangers; their clothing is cotton, which is brought to them from India.
lines.ar_bare: وهم أهل تواضع وحسن أخلاق وفضيلة ومحبة للغرباء، ولباسهم القطن، وهو يجلب إليهم من بلاد الهند.

passages.ar: وَرَكِبْنَا الْبَحْرَ مِنْ كِلْوَا إِلَى مَدِينَةِ ظَفَارِ الْحُمُوضِ «وَضُبِطَ اسْمُهَا بِفَتْحِ الظَّاءِ الْمُعْجَمِ وَالْفَاءِ وَآخِرُهُ رَاءٌ مَبْنِيَّةٌ عَلَى الْكَسْرِ»، وَهِيَ آخِرُ بِلَادِ الْيَمَنِ عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ الْهِنْدِيِّ، وَمِنْهَا تُحْمَلُ الْخَيْلُ الْعِتَاقُ إِلَى الْهِنْدِ. وَبَيْنَ ظَفَارَ وَعَدَنَ فِي الْبَرِّ مَسِيرَةُ شَهْرٍ فِي صَحْرَاءَ. وَبَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَضْرَمَوْتَ سِتَّةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا، وَبَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ عُمَانَ عِشْرُونَ يَوْمًا. وَهُمْ أَهْلُ تِجَارَةٍ لَا عَيْشَ لَهُمْ إِلَّا مِنْهَا. وَهُمْ أَهْلُ تَوَاضُعٍ وَحُسْنِ أَخْلَاقٍ وَفَضِيلَةٍ وَمَحَبَّةٍ لِلْغُرَبَاءِ، وَلِبَاسُهُمُ الْقُطْنُ، وَهُوَ يُجْلَبُ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ بِلَادِ الْهِنْدِ.
passages.en: We sailed from Kilwa to the city of Ẓafār al-Ḥumūḍ («its name is spelt with fatḥa on the dotted ẓāʾ and on the fāʾ, and ends in a rāʾ built on kasra»); it is the last of the lands of Yemen on the coast of the Indian Ocean, and from it the thoroughbred horses are shipped to India. Between Ẓafār and Aden by land is a month's journey through desert. Between it and Ḥaḍramawt are sixteen days, and between it and Oman twenty days. They are people of trade, with no living except from it. They are people of humility, good character, virtue and love of strangers; their clothing is cotton, which is brought to them from India.

passages.intro_en: A short travel diary. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ بَعْدَ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ، أَنَا وَأَبِي وَعُمَرُ.
lines.en: We left Tarim after the dawn prayer, my father, Umar and I.
lines.ar_bare: خرجنا من تريم بعد صلاة الفجر، أنا وأبي وعمر.

lines.ar: رَكِبْنَا السَّيَّارَةَ وَنَظَرْنَا إِلَى الْوَادِي وَالْجَبَلِ.
lines.en: We got into the car and looked at the wadi and the mountain.
lines.ar_bare: ركبنا السيارة ونظرنا إلى الوادي والجبل.

lines.ar: سَافَرْنَا يَوْمَيْنِ، وَكَانَ الطَّرِيقُ طَوِيلًا وَجَمِيلًا.
lines.en: We travelled two days, and the road was long and beautiful.
lines.ar_bare: سافرنا يومين، وكان الطريق طويلا وجميلا.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الشِّحْرِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ، وَهِيَ مَدِينَةٌ عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ.
lines.en: Then we reached al-Shiḥr in the evening; it is a city on the coast of the sea.
lines.ar_bare: ثم وصلنا إلى الشحر في المساء، وهي مدينة على ساحل البحر.

lines.ar: أَقَمْنَا فِي بَيْتِ صَدِيقِ أَبِي ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ.
lines.en: We stayed in the house of my father’s friend for three days.
lines.ar_bare: أقمنا في بيت صديق أبي ثلاثة أيام.

lines.ar: وَفِي الصَّبَاحِ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمِينَاءِ وَنَظَرْنَا إِلَى الْبَحْرِ طَوِيلًا.
lines.en: In the morning we went to the port and looked at the sea for a long time.
lines.ar_bare: وفي الصباح ذهبنا إلى الميناء ونظرنا إلى البحر طويلا.

lines.ar: ثُمَّ رَكِبْنَا السَّيَّارَةَ إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ كَبِيرَةٍ عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَوَصَلْنَا قَبْلَ اللَّيْلِ.
lines.en: Then we rode the car to a big city on the coast and arrived before night.
lines.ar_bare: ثم ركبنا السيارة إلى مدينة كبيرة على الساحل ووصلنا قبل الليل.

lines.ar: وَأَقَمْنَا فِي تِلْكَ الْمَدِينَةِ يَوْمًا وَاحِدًا، ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَا إِلَى تَرِيمَ وَحَمِدْنَا اللَّهَ.
lines.en: We stayed in that city one day, then we returned to Tarim and praised God.
lines.ar_bare: وأقمنا في تلك المدينة يوما واحدا، ثم رجعنا إلى تريم وحمدنا الله.

passages.ar: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ بَعْدَ صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ، أَنَا وَأَبِي وَعُمَرُ. رَكِبْنَا السَّيَّارَةَ وَنَظَرْنَا إِلَى الْوَادِي وَالْجَبَلِ. سَافَرْنَا يَوْمَيْنِ، وَكَانَ الطَّرِيقُ طَوِيلًا وَجَمِيلًا. ثُمَّ وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الشِّحْرِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ، وَهِيَ مَدِينَةٌ عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ. أَقَمْنَا فِي بَيْتِ صَدِيقِ أَبِي ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ. وَفِي الصَّبَاحِ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمِينَاءِ وَنَظَرْنَا إِلَى الْبَحْرِ طَوِيلًا. ثُمَّ رَكِبْنَا السَّيَّارَةَ إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ كَبِيرَةٍ عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَوَصَلْنَا قَبْلَ اللَّيْلِ. وَأَقَمْنَا فِي تِلْكَ الْمَدِينَةِ يَوْمًا وَاحِدًا، ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَا إِلَى تَرِيمَ وَحَمِدْنَا اللَّهَ.
passages.en: We left Tarim after the dawn prayer, my father, Umar and I. We got into the car and looked at the wadi and the mountain. We travelled two days, and the road was long and beautiful. Then we reached al-Shiḥr in the evening; it is a city on the coast of the sea. We stayed in the house of my father’s friend for three days. In the morning we went to the port and looked at the sea for a long time. Then we rode the car to a big city on the coast and arrived before night. We stayed in that city one day, then we returned to Tarim and praised God.

passages.intro_en: The story strip, new lines 178-179 (the boy and the Habib; it continues from lesson to lesson).

lines.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي رِحْلَتِهِ: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ مَعَ أَبِي وَعُمَرَ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى الشِّحْرِ.
lines.en: The boy wrote on his journey: We left Tarim with my father and Umar, and we arrived at al-Shiḥr.

lines.ar: أَقَمْنَا أَيَّامًا عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَرَأَيْنَا الْمِينَاءَ.
lines.en: We stayed some days on the coast, and we saw the port.

passages.ar: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي رِحْلَتِهِ: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ مَعَ أَبِي وَعُمَرَ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى الشِّحْرِ. أَقَمْنَا أَيَّامًا عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَرَأَيْنَا الْمِينَاءَ.
passages.en: The boy wrote on his journey: We left Tarim with my father and Umar, and we arrived at al-Shiḥr. We stayed some days on the coast, and we saw the port.

questions.q: Translate line 1.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: We sailed from Kilwa to the city of Ẓafār al-Ḥumūḍ («its name is spelt with fatḥa on the dotted ẓāʾ and on the fāʾ, and ends in a rāʾ built on kasra»); it is the last of the lands of Yemen on the coast of the Indian Ocean, and from it the thoroughbred horses are shipped to India.

questions.q: Translate line 2.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: Between Ẓafār and Aden by land is a month's journey through desert. Between it and Ḥaḍramawt are sixteen days, and between it and Oman twenty days.

questions.q: Translate line 3.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّالِثَ.
questions.a: They are people of trade, with no living except from it.

questions.q: Translate line 4.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
questions.a: They are people of humility, good character, virtue and love of strangers; their clothing is cotton, which is brought to them from India.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A travel narrative: an account of a journey by the traveller Ibn Baṭṭūṭa, from his Riḥla.

questions.q: Line 1: who is “we”? How do you know?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَنْ «نَحْنُ»؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: The writer and his companions. The ending ـنَا in رَكِبْنَا.

questions.q: Line 1: from where to where did they sail?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مِنْ أَيْنَ إِلَى أَيْنَ رَكِبُوا الْبَحْرَ؟
questions.a: From Kilwa to the city of Ẓafār.

questions.q: Line 1: what is Ẓafār, and where is it?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَا ظَفَارُ؟ وَأَيْنَ هِيَ؟
questions.a: The last of the lands of Yemen, on the coast of the Indian Ocean.

questions.q: Line 1: what is shipped from Ẓafār to India?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَاذَا يُحْمَلُ مِنْ ظَفَارَ إِلَى الْهِنْدِ؟
questions.a: Thoroughbred horses.

questions.q: Line 1: find the word that means “coast”.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَدُلُّ عَلَى شَاطِئِ الْبَحْرِ.
questions.a: سَاحِل (in عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ).

questions.q: Line 2: how far is Ẓafār from Aden by land?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: كَمْ بَيْنَ ظَفَارَ وَعَدَنَ؟
questions.a: A month’s journey, through desert.

questions.q: Line 2: which is farther from Ẓafār, Ḥaḍramawt or Oman?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: أَيُّهُمَا أَبْعَدُ عَنْ ظَفَارَ: حَضْرَمَوْتُ أَمْ عُمَانُ؟
questions.a: Oman: twenty days, against sixteen days to Ḥaḍramawt.

questions.q: True or false: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa says here that he went to Ḥaḍramawt.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَقُولُ ابْنُ بَطُّوطَةَ هُنَا إِنَّهُ ذَهَبَ إِلَى حَضْرَمَوْتَ.
questions.a: False. He only gives a distance: sixteen days from Ẓafār. He never visited Ḥaḍramawt.
questions.ref_ar: بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَضْرَمَوْتَ سِتَّةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا

questions.q: Line 3: what is the living of the people of Ẓafār?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مِنْ أَيْنَ عَيْشُ أَهْلِ ظَفَارَ؟
questions.a: Trade: they have no living except from it.

questions.q: Line 4: name the four good qualities of the people.
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: اُذْكُرِ الصِّفَاتِ الطَّيِّبَةَ الْأَرْبَعَ لِلنَّاسِ.
questions.a: Humility, good character, virtue and love of strangers.

questions.q: Line 4: what do they wear, and where does it come from?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٤: مَاذَا يَلْبَسُونَ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ يَأْتِي؟
questions.a: Cotton, brought to them from India.

questions.q: Line 1 has a note between « ». What is it for, and may you skip it when you read the story?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ١ كَلَامٌ بَيْنَ « ». لِمَاذَا يُكْتَبُ؟ وَهَلْ تَتْرُكُهُ فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ؟
questions.a: It tells how to spell and vowel the name Ẓafār (the editor’s note). It is an aside: the story reads on without it.

questions.q: Ḥaḍramawt is named in line 2 only as a distance. Why must a reader tell “what the traveller saw” from “what he reports”?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ مَا رَآهُ الرَّحَّالَةُ وَمَا يَنْقُلُهُ فَقَطْ؟
questions.a: Because a place named as a distance has not been visited. The traveller reached Ẓafār and reports the lands beyond it: the reader must not say he went there.

questions.q: Who travelled?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ سَافَرَ؟
questions.a: The writer, his father and Umar.

questions.q: When did they leave, and from where?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى خَرَجُوا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ؟
questions.a: After the dawn prayer, from Tarim.

questions.q: How did they travel?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ سَافَرُوا؟
questions.a: By car.

questions.q: What did they look at on the way?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى مَاذَا نَظَرُوا فِي الطَّرِيقِ؟
questions.a: The wadi and the mountain.

questions.q: How many days did the journey to al-Shiḥr take?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ يَوْمًا دَامَ السَّفَرُ إِلَى الشِّحْرِ؟
questions.a: Two days.

questions.q: What was the road like?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ كَانَ الطَّرِيقُ؟
questions.a: Long and beautiful.

questions.q: What is al-Shiḥr, and when did they arrive?
questions.q_ar: مَا الشِّحْرُ؟ وَمَتَى وَصَلُوا؟
questions.a: A city on the coast of the sea; they arrived in the evening.

questions.q: Where did they stay in al-Shiḥr, and for how long?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ أَقَامُوا فِي الشِّحْرِ؟ وَكَمْ يَوْمًا؟
questions.a: In the house of a friend of the writer’s father, three days.

questions.q: What did they do at the port?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا فَعَلُوا فِي الْمِينَاءِ؟
questions.a: They looked at the sea for a long time.

questions.q: Where did they go next? When did they arrive?
questions.q_ar: إِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبُوا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ؟ وَمَتَى وَصَلُوا؟
questions.a: To a big city on the coast, by car; they arrived before night.

questions.q: True or false: they stayed a week in the second city.
questions.q_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: أَقَامُوا أُسْبُوعًا فِي الْمَدِينَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ.
questions.a: False. They stayed one day.
questions.ref_ar: أَقَمْنَا فِي تِلْكَ الْمَدِينَةِ يَوْمًا وَاحِدًا

questions.q: Find the word that means “we stayed”.
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْفِعْلَ الَّذِي يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْإِقَامَةِ.
questions.a: أَقَمْنَا (lines 5 and 8).

questions.q: Put in order: they praised God · they arrived at al-Shiḥr · they left Tarim · they stayed one day in the second city.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ.
questions.a: They left Tarim, arrived at al-Shiḥr, stayed one day in the second city, praised God.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
questions.a: A travel narrative: “we” verbs in the past (خَرَجْنَا، وَصَلْنَا، أَقَمْنَا), place names, and time markers.

questions.q: The diary ends with “we praised God”. What does that ending do for the journey?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ الْخَاتِمَةُ «وَحَمِدْنَا اللَّهَ» فِي الرِّحْلَةِ؟
questions.a: It closes the journey: the travellers thank God for it when they come home.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy wrote on his journey: We left Tarim with my father and Umar, and we arrived at al-Shiḥr. We stayed some days on the coast, and we saw the port.

questions.q: Which verbs say “we left”, “we arrived”, “we stayed”?
questions.a: خَرَجْنَا، وَصَلْنَا، أَقَمْنَا

questions.q: Which ending shows “we” on these verbs?
questions.a: ـنَا

questions.q: Write in Arabic: We arrived at al-Shiḥr.
questions.a: وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الشِّحْرِ.

translate.ar: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْوَادِي بَعْدَ سَاعَتَيْنِ.
translate.en: We left Tarim in the morning and reached the wadi after two hours.

translate.ar: رَكِبْنَا الْبَحْرَ مِنَ الْمِينَاءِ وَنَزَلْنَا عَلَى سَاحِلٍ بَعِيدٍ.
translate.en: We sailed from the port and landed on a distant coast.

translate.ar: أَقَمْنَا فِي تِلْكَ الْمَدِينَةِ شَهْرًا وَسَأَلْنَا عَنْ عُلَمَائِهَا.
translate.en: We stayed in that city a month and asked about its scholars.

translate.ar: بَيْنَ الْمَدِينَةِ وَالْبَحْرِ مَسِيرَةُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي صَحْرَاءَ وَاسِعَةٍ.
translate.en: Between the city and the sea is a three days’ journey through a wide desert.

translate.ar: وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الشِّحْرِ قَبْلَ الْمَسَاءِ، وَهِيَ مِينَاءٌ قَدِيمٌ عَلَى سَاحِلِ الْبَحْرِ.
translate.en: We reached al-Shiḥr before evening; it is an old port on the sea coast.

translate.ar: فِي الْمِينَاءِ سَمِعْنَا كَلَامًا كَثِيرًا عَنِ الْبَحْرِ.
translate.en: In the port we heard a great deal of talk about the sea.

translate.ar: ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَا إِلَى بَيْتِنَا وَشَكَرْنَا اللَّهَ عَلَى هَذَا السَّفَرِ.
translate.en: Then we returned to our house and thanked God for this journey.

translate.ar: كَانَ السَّفَرُ طَوِيلًا، لَكِنَّ الْمِينَاءَ كَانَ جَمِيلًا.
translate.en: The journey was long, but the port was beautiful.

translate.ar: سَافَرَ الرَّحَّالَةُ مِنْ مَكَّةَ إِلَى بِلَادٍ بَعِيدَةٍ وَكَتَبَ عَنْهَا كِتَابًا.
translate.en: The traveller journeyed from Mecca to distant lands and wrote a book about them.

translate.ar: خَرَجْنَا مِنَ الْبَيْتِ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمِينَاءِ. وَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ رَكِبْنَا الْبَحْرَ، وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى مَدِينَةٍ عَلَى السَّاحِلِ عِنْدَ الْمَسَاءِ.
translate.en: We left the house before dawn and went to the port. After an hour we embarked, and we reached a city on the coast at evening.

translate.ar: فَفِي يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ الثَّالِثَ عَشَرَ مِنْ رَبِيعٍ الثَّانِي سَنَةَ ١٣٨٧ هـ، تَشَرَّفَ وَادِي حَضْرَمَوْتَ وَأَهْلُهُ بِوُصُولِ الْحَبِيبِ الْإِمَامِ الْعَلَّامَةِ سَيِّدِي عُمَرَ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ سُمَيْطٍ، قَاصِدًا زِيَارَةَ أَهْلِ الْوَادِي مِنَ الْأَحْيَاءِ وَأَهْلِ الْبَرْزَخِ، قَادِمًا مِنَ الشِّحْرِ، تَوَجَّهَ مِنْهَا بِالسَّيَّارَةِ فَجْرَ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ الْمَذْكُورِ.
translate.en: On Friday the thirteenth of Rabīʿ al-Thānī 1387 AH, the Valley of Ḥaḍramawt and its people were honoured by the arrival of al-Ḥabīb, the learned Imām, my master ʿUmar b. Aḥmad b. Abī Bakr b. Sumayṭ, intending to visit the people of the valley, living and in the barzakh, coming from al-Shiḥr; he set out from there by car at dawn on the said Friday.

translate.ar: فَفِي يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ الثَّالِثَ عَشَرَ مِنْ رَبِيعٍ الثَّانِي سَنَةَ ١٣٨٧ هـ، تَشَرَّفَ وَادِي حَضْرَمَوْتَ وَأَهْلُهُ بِوُصُولِ الْحَبِيبِ الْإِمَامِ الْعَلَّامَةِ سَيِّدِي عُمَرَ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ سُمَيْطٍ، قَاصِدًا زِيَارَةَ أَهْلِ الْوَادِي مِنَ الْأَحْيَاءِ وَأَهْلِ الْبَرْزَخِ، قَادِمًا مِنَ الشِّحْرِ، تَوَجَّهَ مِنْهَا بِالسَّيَّارَةِ فَجْرَ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ الْمَذْكُورِ.
translate.en: Al-Ḥabīb ʿUmar b. Sumayṭ arrives in the valley of Ḥaḍramawt, coming from al-Shiḥr; he set out by car at dawn.
We left the house after dawn.
We got into the car and travelled two days.
We arrived at the port in the evening.
We stayed in the city three days.
Then we returned to our land.
Between the house and the sea is a day’s journey.
alt: بَيْنَ الْبَيْتِ وَالْبَحْرِ مَسِيرَةُ يَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ.

translate.en: We looked at the sea for a long time.
We left Tarim and arrived at the coast after four days.
translate.ar: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى السَّاحِلِ بَعْدَ أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ.

translate.en: We stayed in the house of a friend.
The road was long and beautiful.
We asked about the road and went to the port.
translate.ar: سَأَلْنَا عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ وَذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمِينَاءِ.

translate.en: After two days we sailed from the port.
translate.ar: بَعْدَ يَوْمَيْنِ رَكِبْنَا الْبَحْرَ مِنَ الْمِينَاءِ.

translate.en: We arrived before night and thanked God.
Write the first line of your own travel diary: from where you left, when, and where you arrived.
translate.ar: خَرَجْنَا مِنَ الْبَيْتِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ بَعْدَ سَاعَتَيْنِ.
alt: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْوَادِي بَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ.

readings.title_en: The interview and the dialect

readings.question_ar: مَنْ يَسْأَلُ؟ وَمَنْ يُجِيبُ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ مَحَلِّيَّةٌ؟

passages.intro_en: An interview with a craftsman of Tarim. Read it aloud, then answer.
passages.cite: Course text

lines.ar: أَحْمَدُ: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ.
lines.en: Ahmad: Peace be upon you.
lines.ar_bare: أحمد: السلام عليكم.

lines.ar: كَيْفَ بَدَأْتَ هَذِهِ الْحِرْفَةَ؟
lines.en: How did you begin this craft?
lines.ar_bare: كيف بدأت هذه الحرفة؟

lines.ar: الْخَزَّافُ: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ.
lines.en: The potter: And upon you be peace.
lines.ar_bare: الخزاف: وعليكم السلام.

lines.ar: بَدَأْتُ وَأَنَا وَلَدٌ صَغِيرٌ، وَكَانَ أَبِي خَزَّافًا.
lines.en: I began when I was a small boy, and my father was a potter.
lines.ar_bare: بدأت وأنا ولد صغير، وكان أبي خزافا.

lines.ar: أَحْمَدُ: مَاذَا تَعْمَلُ الْيَوْمَ؟
lines.en: Ahmad: What do you make today?
lines.ar_bare: أحمد: ماذا تعمل اليوم؟

lines.ar: الْخَزَّافُ: أَعْمَلُ الزِّيرَ لِلْمَاءِ، وَأَعْمَلُ الْجَحْلَةَ (أَيِ الزِّيرَ الْكَبِيرَ) لِحِفْظِ التَّمْرِ.
lines.en: The potter: I make the zīr for water, and I make the jaḥla (that is, the large zīr) for storing dates.
lines.ar_bare: الخزاف: أعمل الزير للماء، وأعمل الجحلة (أي الزير الكبير) لحفظ التمر.

lines.ar: أَحْمَدُ: مِنْ أَيْنَ تَأْخُذُ الطِّينَ؟
lines.en: Ahmad: Where do you take the clay from?
lines.ar_bare: أحمد: من أين تأخذ الطين؟

lines.ar: وَكَمْ يَوْمًا تَعْمَلُ فِي الزِّيرِ الْوَاحِدِ؟
lines.en: And how many days do you work on one zīr?
lines.ar_bare: وكم يوما تعمل في الزير الواحد؟

lines.ar: الْخَزَّافُ: آخُذُ الطِّينَ مِنَ الْوَادِي، ثُمَّ أَعْمَلُ بِهِ بِيَدِي ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ.
lines.en: The potter: I take the clay from the wadi, then I work with it by hand for three days.
lines.ar_bare: الخزاف: آخذ الطين من الوادي، ثم أعمل به بيدي ثلاثة أيام.

lines.ar: أَحْمَدُ: مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي هَذِهِ الْحِرْفَةِ الْيَوْمَ؟
lines.en: Ahmad: What do you think of this craft today?
lines.ar_bare: أحمد: ما رأيك في هذه الحرفة اليوم؟

lines.ar: الْخَزَّافُ: هِيَ حِرْفَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ، وَلَكِنَّ النَّاسَ الْيَوْمَ يَطْلُبُونَ الْجَدِيدَ.
lines.en: The potter: It is an old, beautiful craft, but people today ask for what is new.
lines.ar_bare: الخزاف: هي حرفة قديمة جميلة، ولكن الناس اليوم يطلبون الجديد.

lines.ar: أَحْمَدُ: هَلْ تُعَلِّمُ أَوْلَادَكَ؟
lines.en: Ahmad: Do you teach your sons?
lines.ar_bare: أحمد: هل تعلم أولادك؟

lines.ar: الْخَزَّافُ: نَعَمْ، وَهُمْ يَعْمَلُونَ مَعِي كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
lines.en: The potter: Yes, and they work with me every morning.
lines.ar_bare: الخزاف: نعم، وهم يعملون معي كل صباح.

lines.ar: أَحْمَدُ: شُكْرًا لَكَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْمُقَابَلَةِ.
lines.en: Ahmad: Thank you for this interview.
lines.ar_bare: أحمد: شكرا لك على هذه المقابلة.

glossary.en: jaḥla (a local word for a big jar)

passages.ar: أَحْمَدُ: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. كَيْفَ بَدَأْتَ هَذِهِ الْحِرْفَةَ؟ الْخَزَّافُ: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. بَدَأْتُ وَأَنَا وَلَدٌ صَغِيرٌ، وَكَانَ أَبِي خَزَّافًا. أَحْمَدُ: مَاذَا تَعْمَلُ الْيَوْمَ؟ الْخَزَّافُ: أَعْمَلُ الزِّيرَ لِلْمَاءِ، وَأَعْمَلُ الْجَحْلَةَ (أَيِ الزِّيرَ الْكَبِيرَ) لِحِفْظِ التَّمْرِ. أَحْمَدُ: مِنْ أَيْنَ تَأْخُذُ الطِّينَ؟ وَكَمْ يَوْمًا تَعْمَلُ فِي الزِّيرِ الْوَاحِدِ؟ الْخَزَّافُ: آخُذُ الطِّينَ مِنَ الْوَادِي، ثُمَّ أَعْمَلُ بِهِ بِيَدِي ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ. أَحْمَدُ: مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي هَذِهِ الْحِرْفَةِ الْيَوْمَ؟ الْخَزَّافُ: هِيَ حِرْفَةٌ قَدِيمَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ، وَلَكِنَّ النَّاسَ الْيَوْمَ يَطْلُبُونَ الْجَدِيدَ. أَحْمَدُ: هَلْ تُعَلِّمُ أَوْلَادَكَ؟ الْخَزَّافُ: نَعَمْ، وَهُمْ يَعْمَلُونَ مَعِي كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ. أَحْمَدُ: شُكْرًا لَكَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْمُقَابَلَةِ.
passages.en: Ahmad: Peace be upon you. How did you begin this craft? The potter: And upon you be peace. I began when I was a small boy, and my father was a potter. Ahmad: What do you make today? The potter: I make the zīr for water, and I make the jaḥla (that is, the large zīr) for storing dates. Ahmad: Where do you take the clay from? And how many days do you work on one zīr? The potter: I take the clay from the wadi, then I work with it by hand for three days. Ahmad: What do you think of this craft today? The potter: It is an old, beautiful craft, but people today ask for what is new. Ahmad: Do you teach your sons? The potter: Yes, and they work with me every morning. Ahmad: Thank you for this interview.
