questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: The Qur’an: Sūrat al-Sharḥ (94), verses 5 and 6.

questions.q: Which two words are opposites?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ مُتَضَادَّتَانِ؟
questions.a: الْعُسْرِ (hardship) and يُسْرًا (ease).

questions.q: Which little word says that the ease comes with the hardship, and not after it?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الْيُسْرَ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ لَا بَعْدَهُ؟
questions.a: مَعَ (“with”).

questions.q: The same sentence comes in verse 5 and in verse 6. What does the repeating do?
questions.q_ar: تَتَكَرَّرُ الْجُمْلَةُ فِي الْآيَتَيْنِ. مَاذَا يُفِيدُ التَّكْرَارُ؟
questions.a: It makes the promise firm; the reader is meant to hear it twice.

questions.q: What does this text want from the reader? Say it in one line.
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُرِيدُ النَّصُّ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟ قُلْهُ فِي سَطْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.
questions.a: It comforts: do not lose hope in hardship, for ease comes with it.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A ḥadīth, from Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī (no. 6307), narrated by Abū Hurayra.

questions.q: Who is speaking? (Look at the source line.)
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الْمُتَكَلِّمُ؟ (اُنْظُرْ إِلَى سَطْرِ الْمَصْدَرِ.)
questions.a: The Prophet ﷺ; Abū Hurayra reports his words.

questions.q: How many times a day? Find the words.
questions.q_ar: كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْمِ؟ جِدِ الْكَلِمَاتِ.
questions.a: More than seventy times: أَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً.

questions.q: What do the two verbs mean, and what is the difference?
questions.q_ar: مَا مَعْنَى الْفِعْلَيْنِ؟ وَمَا الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَهُمَا؟
questions.a: أَسْتَغْفِرُ: I ask forgiveness (root غ ف ر); أَتُوبُ: I turn back in repentance (root ت و ب). The first asks; the second returns.

questions.q: What does this ḥadīth want from the reader? Say it in one line.
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُرِيدُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟ قُلْهُ فِي سَطْرٍ.
questions.a: It teaches by example: ask God’s forgiveness and turn back to Him many times a day.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and which book is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيِّ كِتَابٍ؟
questions.a: A matn (a short text of fiqh, to be learned by heart): Safīnat al-Najā of Sālim b. Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī.

questions.q: Line 1: what are the two excuses for the prayer?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَا الْعُذْرَانِ لِلصَّلَاةِ؟
questions.a: Sleep and forgetting (النَّوْمُ وَالنِّسْيَانُ).

questions.q: Line 2: how many kinds of ḥadath (impurity) are there, and which?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: كَمْ نَوْعًا لِلْحَدَثِ؟ وَمَا هِيَ؟
questions.a: Two: the minor (أَصْغَرُ) and the major (أَكْبَرُ).

questions.q: Line 3: which kind requires wuḍūʾ, and which requires the full wash?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ يُوجِبُ الْوُضُوءَ؟ وَأَيُّ نَوْعٍ يُوجِبُ الْغُسْلَ؟
questions.a: The minor requires wuḍūʾ; the major requires the full wash (الْغُسْلَ).

questions.q: Lines 1 and 2 have the same frame. Write it down.
questions.q_ar: لِلسَّطْرَيْنِ ١ وَ٢ قَالَبٌ وَاحِدٌ. اُكْتُبْهُ.
questions.a: Heading + number + colon + the items: أَعْذَارُ الصَّلَاةِ اثْنَانِ: … · الْأَحْدَاثُ اثْنَانِ: …

questions.q: Why is a matn so short, and where does the explanation come from?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا الْمَتْنُ قَصِيرٌ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ يَأْتِي الشَّرْحُ؟
questions.a: A matn is short so that it can be learned by heart; the explanation is in a commentary (sharḥ) read with a teacher.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Counsel (a ḥikma, a short saying of wisdom), from Kitāb al-Ḥikam of Imam ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād.

questions.q: Who are the two men in the line?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الرَّجُلَانِ فِي السَّطْرِ؟
questions.a: The one who puts wealth where it does not belong (وَاضِعُ الْمَالِ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ) and the one who holds it back from its due (مَاسِكُهُ عَنْ حَقِّهِ).

questions.q: Which word means “sin”, and which means “less”?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «الذَّنْبَ»؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «أَدْنَى»؟
questions.a: إِثْمًا (sin); أَقَلَّ (less).

questions.q: Does the line praise the one who withholds wealth, or the one who puts it in the wrong place?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ يَمْدَحُ السَّطْرُ مَنْ يُمْسِكُ الْمَالَ أَمْ مَنْ يَضَعُهُ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ؟
questions.a: Neither: it blames both. The first is “not less sinful” than the second.

questions.q: How does لَيْسَ work here? Why is there a بِ before أَقَلَّ?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُ «لَيْسَ» هُنَا؟ لِمَاذَا جَاءَتِ الْبَاءُ قَبْلَ «أَقَلَّ»؟
questions.a: لَيْسَ takes بِ before its predicate. “X is not less sinful than Y” (أَقَلَّ إِثْمًا مِنْ): a negated comparison.

questions.q: What does the line want from the reader? Say it in one line.
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُرِيدُ السَّطْرُ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟ قُلْهُ فِي سَطْرٍ.
questions.a: Put wealth where it belongs: do not waste it and do not hold it back.

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: A bayt of poetry (two halves) by al-Mutanabbī, from his Dīwān.

questions.q: Translate the first half.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الشَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
questions.a: Not everything a man wishes for does he reach;

questions.q: Translate the second half.
questions.q_ar: تَرْجِمِ الشَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
questions.a: the winds blow in ways the ships do not desire.

questions.q: In the picture, who are the ships and what are the winds?
questions.q_ar: فِي الصُّورَةِ: مَنِ السُّفُنُ؟ وَمَا الرِّيَاحُ؟
questions.a: The ships are people with their wishes; the winds are what happens, which does not follow their wishes.

questions.q: Which half carries the rhyme? How can you tell this is verse and not prose?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الشَّطْرَيْنِ فِيهِ الْقَافِيَةُ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ أَنَّهُ شِعْرٌ لَا نَثْرٌ؟
questions.a: The second half ends in السُّفُنُ (rhyme: nūn). It is one line in two halves, built on a picture, not a report.

questions.q: What does the line want from the reader? Say it in one line.
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُرِيدُ الْبَيْتُ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟ قُلْهُ فِي سَطْرٍ.
questions.a: It teaches calm: things do not always go as we wish, and that is part of life.

questions.q: Line 1: what did God send us, and what did He make a blessing?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ١: مَاذَا أَرْسَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْنَا؟ وَمَاذَا جَعَلَ نِعْمَةً؟
questions.a: He sent us His Prophet as a mercy, and made remembering him a blessing for hearts.

questions.q: Line 2: what do we ask God for?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَاذَا نَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ؟
questions.a: To send blessings and peace upon our master Muḥammad ﷺ, by which He forgives our sins and brings hearts together.

questions.q: Line 3: what do the people do on the night of the mawlid?
questions.q_ar: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ النَّاسُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ؟
questions.a: They gather with their brothers: they read, listen and remember their Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: Find the words that end alike in lines 1 and 2. What is this style called?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْكَلِمَاتِ الَّتِي تَنْتَهِي بِصَوْتٍ وَاحِدٍ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ١ وَ٢. مَا اسْمُ هَذَا الْأُسْلُوبِ؟
questions.a: رَحْمَةً / نِعْمَةً and الذُّنُوبَ / الْقُلُوبَ: rhymed prose (sajʿ), the style of mawlid texts.

questions.q: Say the whole text in one line.
questions.q_ar: قُلِ النَّصَّ كُلَّهُ فِي سَطْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.
questions.a: It praises God for sending the Prophet ﷺ as a mercy, asks for blessings upon him, and tells of the gathering of the night of the mawlid.

questions.q: Who writes to whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ يَكْتُبُ إِلَى مَنْ؟
questions.a: Sālim (the uncle) writes to his nephew Aḥmad.

questions.q: Which line is the greeting, and which words begin the message itself?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ هُوَ التَّحِيَّةُ؟ وَبِأَيِّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَبْدَأُ الرِّسَالَةُ؟
questions.a: Line 3 is the greeting; the message begins after أَمَّا بَعْدُ.

questions.q: What did the uncle receive, and what does he send?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا وَصَلَ الْعَمَّ؟ وَمَاذَا يُرْسِلُ؟
questions.a: He received Aḥmad’s letter and is happy with it; he sends a new book.

questions.q: What three things does the uncle ask of Aḥmad?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْأُمُورُ الثَّلَاثَةُ الَّتِي يَطْلُبُهَا الْعَمُّ؟
questions.a: To read the book with ʿUmar, to strive in his lesson, and to write to him every month.

questions.q: Name three signs that this is a letter.
questions.q_ar: اُذْكُرْ ثَلَاثَ عَلَامَاتٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ النَّصَّ رِسَالَةٌ.
questions.a: The basmala; “from … to …”; the greeting and أَمَّا بَعْدُ; the closing وَالسَّلَامُ and the signature.

questions.q: What is the headline about?
questions.q_ar: عَنْ مَاذَا الْعُنْوَانُ؟
questions.a: A trip for the school’s students to the coast.

questions.q: When was it announced, and on which day is the trip?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى أُعْلِنَ الْخَبَرُ؟ وَفِي أَيِّ يَوْمٍ الرِّحْلَةُ؟
questions.a: It was announced yesterday; the trip is on Sunday.

questions.q: At what time does the car leave, and from where?
questions.q_ar: فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ تَخْرُجُ السَّيَّارَةُ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ؟
questions.a: At 6:30 in the morning, from in front of the school.

questions.q: What must every student carry, and when does the trip return?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَحْمِلُ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ؟ وَمَتَى تَرْجِعُ الرِّحْلَةُ؟
questions.a: Water; after the afternoon (after ʿaṣr).

questions.q: Is أُعْلِنَ active or passive? Why does a news report often use it?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ «أُعْلِنَ» مَعْلُومٌ أَمْ مَجْهُولٌ؟ لِمَاذَا يَكْثُرُ فِي الْأَخْبَارِ؟
questions.a: Passive: “it was announced”. The announcer is not named; the news is the point.

questions.q: What does the report want from its readers?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يُرِيدُ الْخَبَرُ مِنَ الْقُرَّاءِ؟
questions.a: That the students and their families know the day and the time, and bring water.

questions.q: What is this form for?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا هَذِهِ الِاسْتِمَارَةُ؟
questions.a: Registering at the library.

questions.q: Which lines must you fill in? Name three.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الْأَسْطُرِ تَمْلَؤُهَا؟ اُذْكُرْ ثَلَاثَةً.
questions.a: Any three of: the name, the address, the appointment (day and time), the signature.

questions.q: What does this line ask of you?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَطْلُبُ هَذَا السَّطْرُ مِنْكَ؟
questions.a: Please write the name and the address clearly.
questions.ref_ar: يُرْجَى كِتَابَةُ الِاسْمِ وَالْعُنْوَانِ كِتَابَةً وَاضِحَةً

questions.q: What does this sign say? What kind of word is مَمْنُوعٌ?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا تَقُولُ هَذِهِ اللَّافِتَةُ؟ وَمَا نَوْعُ كَلِمَةِ «مَمْنُوعٌ»؟
questions.a: Playing in the library is forbidden. مَمْنُوعٌ is “forbidden”, the usual word of signs (a passive participle of the root م ن ع).

questions.q: Which three of the ten questions does the form ask you? Say which line answers each.
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ ثَلَاثَةِ أَسْئِلَةٍ مِنَ الْعَشَرَةِ تَسْأَلُكَ الِاسْتِمَارَةُ؟
questions.a: Who (the name), where (the address), when (the appointment).

questions.q: What are the ingredients?
questions.q_ar: مَا الْمَقَادِيرُ؟
questions.a: A cup of milk, three dates and a spoon of honey.

questions.q: How many steps are there, and how are they marked?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ خُطْوَةً؟ وَكَيْفَ رُقِّمَتْ؟
questions.a: Three, marked with the digits ١ ٢ ٣.

questions.q: In step 2, how long do you leave it?
questions.q_ar: فِي الْخُطْوَةِ ٢: كَمْ تَتْرُكُهُ؟
questions.a: Two minutes (دَقِيقَتَيْنِ).

questions.q: How can you tell that every step is a command to one person?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ تَعْرِفُ أَنَّ كُلَّ خُطْوَةٍ أَمْرٌ لِشَخْصٍ وَاحِدٍ؟
questions.a: Each step begins with a command verb with no doer written: اِغْسِلْ، اِخْلِطْ، أَضِفْ، اُتْرُكْ، اِشْرَبْ. It speaks to “you”.

questions.q: Say the recipe in one line.
questions.q_ar: قُلِ الطَّرِيقَةَ كُلَّهَا فِي سَطْرٍ.
questions.a: Mix washed dates with honey, add milk, wait two minutes and drink it cold.

questions.q: Who are the two friends, and where do they live?
questions.q_ar: مَنِ الصَّدِيقَانِ؟ وَأَيْنَ يَسْكُنَانِ؟
questions.a: A tortoise and a monkey, in the wadi.

questions.q: Why did the monkey laugh at the tortoise?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا ضَحِكَ الْقِرْدُ مِنْهَا؟
questions.a: Because she walks little by little.

questions.q: What did the tortoise propose? (line 3)
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا اقْتَرَحَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ؟
questions.a: To go to the spring and see who arrives first.

questions.q: Who arrived first, and why?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ وَصَلَ أَوَّلًا؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: The tortoise: the monkey slept under a tree.

questions.q: Find the moral. What is it?
questions.q_ar: جِدِ الْعِبْرَةَ. مَا هِيَ؟
questions.a: مَنْ صَبَرَ وَصَلَ: whoever is patient arrives.

questions.q: Which first words tell you this is a tale and not a news report?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ فِي أَوَّلِ النَّصِّ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّهُ حِكَايَةٌ لَا خَبَرٌ؟
questions.a: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ: “they say that …” (once upon a time).

questions.q: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
questions.q_ar: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
questions.a: Proverbs (أَمْثَال), from Majmaʿ al-Amthāl of al-Maydānī.

questions.q: Which proverb tells you to choose the neighbour before the house?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ مَثَلٍ يَأْمُرُكَ بِاخْتِيَارِ الْجَارِ قَبْلَ الدَّارِ؟
questions.a: Line 1: الْجَارَ ثُمَّ الدَّارَ (the neighbour, then the house).

questions.q: Which proverb gives hope in a hard time?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ مَثَلٍ يُعْطِي الْأَمَلَ فِي الشِّدَّةِ؟
questions.a: Line 2: الصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَرَجِ (patience is the key to relief).

questions.q: In line 3, whose friend is called “an uncle”?
questions.q_ar: فِي السَّطْرِ ٣: صَدِيقُ مَنْ يُسَمَّى «عَمًّا»؟
questions.a: The father’s friend is called the child’s uncle.

questions.q: Do these lines have verbs? What does that tell you about proverbs?
questions.q_ar: هَلْ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَسْطُرِ أَفْعَالٌ؟ مَاذَا يَقُولُ هَذَا عَنِ الْأَمْثَالِ؟
questions.a: None has a verb. Proverbs are short two-part statements (topic + statement), easy to remember.

questions.q: Which proverb would you tell to a friend who is losing hope? Say why in one line.
questions.q_ar: أَيَّ مَثَلٍ تَقُولُ لِصَدِيقٍ يَفْقِدُ الْأَمَلَ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
questions.a: الصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَرَجِ: it says that waiting patiently opens the way out.

questions.q: What is being defined?
questions.q_ar: مَا الَّذِي يُعَرَّفُ؟
questions.a: The bee (النَّحْلُ).

questions.q: Where do bees live?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ يَسْكُنُ النَّحْلُ؟
questions.a: In many houses (hives) on trees and in the mountain.

questions.q: What do bees make, and from what?
questions.q_ar: مَاذَا يَصْنَعُ النَّحْلُ؟ وَمِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ؟
questions.a: Honey, from the flowers of plants.

questions.q: How does the entry begin, and which word marks a definition?
questions.q_ar: كَيْفَ يَبْدَأُ الْمَدْخَلُ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّعْرِيفِ؟
questions.a: Headword + colon + هُوَ + what it is: النَّحْلُ: هُوَ حَيَوَانٌ صَغِيرٌ. The word هُوَ marks the definition.

questions.q: Say the entry in one line.
questions.q_ar: قُلِ الْمَدْخَلَ فِي سَطْرٍ.
questions.a: The bee is a small animal that lives in hives and makes honey, a sweet food.

questions.q: When did they leave, and how?
questions.q_ar: مَتَى خَرَجُوا؟ وَكَيْفَ؟
questions.a: In the morning, by car.

questions.q: How long was the road to the coast?
questions.q_ar: كَمْ سَاعَةً بَيْنَ الْمَدِينَةِ وَالسَّاحِلِ؟
questions.a: Three hours.

questions.q: Where did they stay, and for how long?
questions.q_ar: أَيْنَ أَقَامُوا؟ وَكَمْ يَوْمًا؟
questions.a: In the port, for two days.

questions.q: Which verbs end in نَا, and whom does the ending stand for?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ الْأَفْعَالِ تَنْتَهِي بِـ «نَا»؟ وَإِلَى مَنْ تَعُودُ؟
questions.a: خَرَجْنَا، رَكِبْنَا، وَصَلْنَا، أَقَمْنَا: all say “we”.

questions.q: Put the journey in order, in four words.
questions.q_ar: رَتِّبِ الرِّحْلَةَ فِي أَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ.
questions.a: Left, arrived, stayed, embarked (by sea).

questions.q: Who sold what to whom?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ بَاعَ مَاذَا لِمَنْ؟
questions.a: ʿAlī sold this book to ʿUmar.

questions.q: At what price?
questions.q_ar: بِكَمِ الثَّمَنُ؟
questions.a: Ten riyals (عَشَرَةُ رِيَالَاتٍ).

questions.q: Who witnessed it?
questions.q_ar: مَنْ شَهِدَ؟
questions.a: Sālim and Aḥmad.

questions.q: Which words give the sale formula, and which give the amount?
questions.q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَاتٍ هِيَ صِيغَةُ الْبَيْعِ؟ وَأَيْنَ الْمَبْلَغُ؟
questions.a: بَاعَ … بِثَمَنٍ قَدْرُهُ …: the sale formula. The amount comes after قَدْرُهُ: عَشَرَةُ رِيَالَاتٍ.

questions.q: Why does a contract name the seller, the buyer, the price and the witnesses?
questions.q_ar: لِمَاذَا يَذْكُرُ الْعَقْدُ الْبَائِعَ وَالْمُشْتَرِيَ وَالثَّمَنَ وَالشُّهُودَ؟
questions.a: So that no one can later dispute the sale: each of these is a point the contract has to settle.

questions.q: Translate the two new lines into English.
questions.a: The boy returned to Tarim and sat with a little boy in the mosque. And he taught him the first lesson: Read and understand.

questions.q: What is the first lesson he teaches?
questions.a: اِقْرَأْ وَافْهَمْ: read and understand.

questions.q: Read the whole Story Strip once more. Where did the boy begin, and where does he end?
questions.a: He began as a small boy going to a mosque with a muṣḥaf; he ends as a student who teaches a younger boy: “Read and understand.”

questions.q: Write in Arabic: Read and understand!
questions.a: اِقْرَأْ وَافْهَمْ.

translate.en: Indeed, with hardship comes ease.

translate.ar: وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ فِي الْيَوْمِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً
translate.en: By God, I ask God’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.

translate.ar: فَالْأَصْغَرُ مَا أَوْجَبَ الْوُضُوءَ، وَالْأَكْبَرُ مَا أَوْجَبَ الْغُسْلَ.
translate.en: The minor is what requires wuḍūʾ, and the major is what requires the full wash.

translate.ar: لَيْسَ وَاضِعُ الْمَالِ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ بِأَقَلَّ إِثْمًا مِنْ مَاسِكِهِ عَنْ حَقِّهِ.
translate.en: One who puts wealth where it does not belong is no less sinful than one who withholds it from its due.

translate.ar: تَجْرِي الرِّيَاحُ بِمَا لَا تَشْتَهِي السُّفُنُ
translate.en: The winds blow in ways the ships do not desire.

translate.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْنَا نَبِيَّهُ رَحْمَةً.
translate.en: Praise be to God, who sent us His Prophet as a mercy.

translate.ar: وَأَنَا أُرْسِلُ إِلَيْكَ كِتَابًا جَدِيدًا، فَاقْرَأْهُ مَعَ عُمَرَ.
translate.en: I am sending you a new book; read it with ʿUmar.

translate.ar: أُعْلِنَ أَمْسِ عَنْ رِحْلَةٍ لِطُلَّابِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ إِلَى السَّاحِلِ يَوْمَ الْأَحَدِ.
translate.en: It was announced yesterday that there will be a trip for the school’s students to the coast on Sunday.

translate.ar: يُرْجَى كِتَابَةُ الِاسْمِ وَالْعُنْوَانِ كِتَابَةً وَاضِحَةً.
translate.en: Please write the name and the address clearly.
2. Add the milk, then leave it for two minutes.

translate.ar: فَذَهَبَ الْقِرْدُ وَنَامَ تَحْتَ شَجَرَةٍ، وَذَهَبَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ إِلَى الْعَيْنِ.
translate.en: The monkey went and slept under a tree, and the tortoise went little by little until she reached the spring.
Patience is the key to relief.

translate.ar: وَيَصْنَعُ النَّحْلُ الْعَسَلَ مِنْ أَزْهَارِ النَّبَاتِ.
translate.en: And the bees make honey from the flowers of plants.

translate.ar: وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى السَّاحِلِ بَعْدَ ثَلَاثِ سَاعَاتٍ، وَأَقَمْنَا فِي الْمِينَاءِ يَوْمَيْنِ.
translate.en: We arrived at the coast after three hours, and stayed in the port for two days.

translate.ar: بَاعَ عَلِيٌّ لِعُمَرَ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ بِثَمَنٍ قَدْرُهُ عَشَرَةُ رِيَالَاتٍ.
translate.en: ʿAlī sold this book to ʿUmar for a price amounting to ten riyals.

translate.ar: الْمَكْتَبَةُ مُغْلَقَةٌ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ. مَفْتُوحَةٌ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ. الرَّجَاءُ عَدَمُ الْكَلَامِ.
translate.en: The library is closed on Friday. Open after the afternoon. Please do not talk.
The Qur’an: “Indeed, with hardship comes ease.” Write the verse (you read it in section A).
A ḥadīth-style clause: I ask God’s forgiveness, and I turn back to Him.
A matn: The pillars of Islam are five.
Counsel to a friend: Seek knowledge, and be patient.
A line of verse: The winds blow and the ships go.
Mawlid prose: O God, send blessings and peace upon our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
translate.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.

translate.en: The opening of a letter: Peace be upon you. To proceed: I am well, praise be to God.
translate.ar: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ، أَمَّا بَعْدُ: فَأَنَا بِخَيْرٍ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.

translate.en: A news headline: A new library has been opened.
The labels of a form: name, address, signature.
A recipe, step 1: Wash the dates, then mix them with the honey.
The opening of a fable: They claim that a monkey lived in the wadi.
translate.ar: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ يَسْكُنُ فِي الْوَادِي.

translate.en: A saying: Knowledge is light.
An encyclopaedia definition: The date palm: it is a tree.
A travel line: We went out in the morning and arrived at the port.
translate.ar: خَرَجْنَا فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْمِينَاءِ.

translate.en: A contract: Sālim sold this house to ʿAlī for a price amounting to ten riyals.
translate.ar: بَاعَ سَالِمٌ هَذَا الْبَيْتَ لِعَلِيٍّ بِثَمَنٍ قَدْرُهُ عَشَرَةُ رِيَالَاتٍ.
